title: Comparison categories: the normal form and the regularity of comparison data
abstract: There are many types of equivalence relations in mathematics, each one enjoying its own defnition, but many of them can also be defined by transformations of morphisms: Green's relations, orbit relations, conjugacy, equality of orbit closures, equivalence of Cauchy sequences, stable isomorphism. We unify them through the comparison category of a comparison datum, read at levels $-1,0,1,2,\dots$ (comparisons in both directions, connected components, homotopy groups). Its normal form is a full subcategory of a Grothendieck construction $\int_VH$ cut out by a map $s$; the classical relations are traced back to it by restriction along $s$, enrichment by a cost (limit relations) and filtered colimits (stabilization). If the map $σ$ transporting morphisms into a $2$-category is arbitrary, every relation occurs, so the constraint is the regularity of $σ$. We grade data along seven regularity classes. The rigid and diagonal classes are classified completely (on finite groups, by the double coset relations); completely functorial data contain conjugacy and obey a dichotomy on nil monoids. Whether every relation on a monoid is level $0$ of a completely functorial datum is open.

title: Strong stable sets and asymptotic fineness
abstract: We investigate the strong stable sets of the geodesic flow on hyperbolic surfaces and their relation to the injectivity radius. We prove that the strong stable set of a vector does not coincide with its stable horocycle if and only if the injectivity radius along the associated geodesic ray is not bounded away from zero and the ray does not diverge through a cusp. In that case, the strong stable set is an uncountable union of stable horocycles. In previous works, we considered the particular cases where the ray meets arbitrarily short closed geodesics or closed horocycles. Here we complete the study by treating the third possible case, where the ray meets closed hypercycles of arbitrarily small length.

title: TensorSpectra: Bridging the Spectral and Tensor Worlds for High-Dimensional PDEs
abstract: High-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) remain challenging for spectral methods due to the exponential growth of multidimensional coefficient spaces. We propose TensorSpectra, a low-rank spectral framework that directly parameterizes spectral coefficient tensors in canonical polyadic (CP) form, reducing representation complexity from $\mathcal{O}(N^d)$ to $\mathcal{O}(dNr)$. TensorSpectra combines structure-preserving spectral calculus, de-aliased nonlinear interactions, operator-aware residual weighting, and progressive low-rank corrections to enable efficient PDEs solving in compressed coefficient space. We further establish a theoretical framework connecting spectral truncation, low-rank approximation, and optimization errors. Extensive experiments across five PDE families and 24 benchmark configurations demonstrate State-Of-The-Art accuracy among five representative baselines, with TensorSpectra consistently achieving the lowest relative $L^2$ errors. More broadly, our findings offer a new perspective on high-dimensional PDEs solving, suggesting that exploiting intrinsic low-rank structure in spectral coefficient space provides a viable alternative to conventional physical-space approaches.

title: Determining norm-Euclidean complex cubic fields
abstract: We prove that Cavallar and Lemmermeyer's list of $58$ norm-Euclidean complex cubic fields is complete. The proof combines a classical discriminant bound with exact certificates of non-Euclideanity. The unit action reduces their verification to finite lattice enumeration with rigorous interval arithmetic. An independent covering computation confirms norm-Euclideanity for the $58$ fields.

title: An Energy-based discontinuous Galerkin method for the Westervelt equation with absorbing boundary conditions
abstract: This paper develops and analyzes an energy-based discontinuous Galerkin method for the Westervelt equation in the acoustic-velocity-potential formulation with spatially varying material parameters and nonlinear absorbing boundary conditions. The semi-discrete scheme is constructed from the underlying energy balance and incorporates an additional consistent term to accommodate the strong damping operator within the discrete energy framework. Numerical fluxes are designed at both interelement and physical boundaries to provide a unified treatment of interior and boundary dissipation. For the nonlinear analysis, we study an auxiliary variable-coefficient linearized problem and establish stability and a priori error estimates, including the additional terms induced by the solution-dependent absorbing boundary flux. These estimates are combined with a fixed-point argument to prove existence, uniqueness, and convergence of the nonlinear semi-discrete approximation under suitable regularity, smallness, and nondegeneracy assumptions. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical convergence results and illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

title: On the $b$-Symbol Weight Distribution of Dual Melas Codes and a Poisson Randomness Postulate
abstract:
We prove a new lower bound on the $b$-symbol weight of codewords in dual Melas codes, which is strictly better than known results. We employ a new strategy that translates a pattern counting problem in linear-feedback shift register sequences to a problem on orbits of binary polynomials under a certain action. We use the same techniques to provide an improved lower bound on the burst-covering radius of Melas codes and a new upper bound on the critical exponent of dual Melas codes.
  We then define a new randomness postulate on (families of) binary sequences, based on the definition of infinite Poisson generic sequences. We conjecture that codewords in the dual Melas code satisfy this postulate, and we show partial progress in establishing this conjecture. We also show how a relaxed version of the problem can be completely resolved, and relate the conjecture to the first part of the paper, giving a justification of why the improved bounds on the $b$-symbol weight were somewhat to be expected.

title: Pooled Testing under Congestion: Operational Scaling Laws for Pool-Size Selection
abstract:
Classical pooled-testing rules choose pool sizes to reduce the number of tests. In practice, however, samples arrive over time, pools take time to form, testing capacity is finite, and positive pools create bursts of follow-up work. These operational features can make the test-efficient pool size far from the delay-efficient one.
  We formulate pooled testing with stochastic arrivals and finite testing capacity as a queueing system, and derive exact performance representations and asymptotic scaling laws for fixed-batch Dorfman testing and a dynamic two-threshold policy. The analysis reveals three distinct design regimes. When test usage is the main concern, the classical Dorfman rule is recovered and the optimal pool size scales with the inverse square root of prevalence. When delay accumulated while the laboratory is busy testing another batch matters, positive pools create service-time variability that grows more rapidly with pool size than the mean retesting burden, and the optimal scale shifts to the inverse cube root of prevalence. When waiting to assemble a pool is itself costly, the optimal fixed pool size remains bounded even as prevalence becomes very small. Under severe capacity scarcity, congestion remains relevant at the classical Dorfman scale: the square-root law survives, but with a capacity-dependent constant.
  Dynamic pooling separates two operational decisions that fixed pool sizes conflate. A lower threshold determines when routine testing should begin, while an upper threshold limits pooling when backlog is high. The lower threshold follows the cube-root scale, whereas the upper threshold primarily acts as congestion control. The results show how prevalence, capacity, and delay jointly determine pooling decisions and explain why operationally optimal pools can be much smaller than those suggested by test-efficiency calculations alone.

title: Invariance in half-space last passage percolation and directed polymers
abstract: We prove various invariance properties for half-space geometric and exponential last passage percolation and the half-space log-gamma polymer, analogous to the full-space invariances proved by Dauvergne. We use the RSK and geometric RSK correspondences to establish a conditional distributional identity between the half-space models and the corresponding full-space models, which allows us to directly transfer the invariance results in the full space to the half space.

title: Kernel representations of fractional gradient bilinear forms. Part II. Variable coefficients
abstract: This paper investigates the existence and properties of interaction kernels representing nonlocal energies associated with the Riesz fractional gradient and variable, uniformly elliptic matrix fields $A(x)$. Building on our previous analysis of constant matrices in [DSV26], we establish necessary conditions on the singularity and decay of such kernels, derive an explicit representation formula under suitable regularity assumptions, and prove uniqueness of the kernel representation. We also obtain sharp asymptotics and positivity criteria near the diagonal, averaged decay estimates at infinity, and characterize the divergence free property of $A(x)$ through the decay of the kernel. Finally, we show that the associated energy may fail the truncation property and that arbitrarily small smooth perturbations of constant matrices can destroy the nonnegativity of the representing kernel. These results provide negative answers to both [SS18, Open Problems 1.9 and 1.10].

title: Symmetry-resolved periods in a cyclic-dominance automaton: separating intrinsic from lattice-induced periodicity
abstract: Periodic attractors of spatially extended systems possess not one period but a hierarchy of periods, one for each level of observation and symmetry quotient, and this hierarchy separates how a pattern evolves from how it fits the finite domain. For a synchronous threshold model of cyclic dominance on an $L\times L$ torus, equivalent to the three-color cyclic cellular automaton of Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath, we measure for every attractor a \emph{tuple} of periods: that of the populations ($\Tpop$), of the full configuration ($\Tst$), and of the configuration up to color rotations ($\Tcol$), lattice symmetries ($\Tgeo$) and the full space--color group ($\TG$). Equivariance implies exact divisibility relations and the factorization $\Tst=\TG\,m$, where $m$ counts the applications of the symmetry $h$ that maps the configuration onto itself after $\TG$ steps: $\TG$ and the type of $h$ belong to the pattern, $m$ to the lattice, and the attractors are relative periodic orbits whose full period emerges from the interaction between the intrinsic dynamics and the lattice symmetries. A family of attractors built around a pair of counter-rotating spirals, with $\Tpop=24$ and $\TG=8$, persists from $L=9$ to $L=40$ while $\Tst$ takes values from 24 to 960, given in every case by the order of $h$; on a rectangular $9\times12$ torus it takes the value 48, absent from all square tori. With more than $4.5\times10^5$ runs at each of $L=8$ and $L=9$ we estimate the basins of attraction: fixed points take 95--97\% of the configuration space, and no single period is enough to tell the oscillating attractors apart. The same analysis locates local diversity: it is balanced whenever the cycle has a color symmetry and, on large lattices, it is concentrated at the spiral cores.

title: On the cohomological dimension of Henselian valued fields
abstract: Let $(K,v)$ be a Henselian valued field of rank one and of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with value group $Γ$ dense in $\mathbb{R}$ and residue field $k$. We compute all the graded pieces of the filtration induced by $v$ on the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ of $K$, in terms of the exterior powers of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector space $Γ/pΓ$ and of the modules of differential forms of $k$. This extends to the non-discrete setting a classical theorem of Kato concerning complete discretely valued fields. We also prove that, when $(K,v)$ is maximally complete, no class escapes this filtration by accumulating at a limit. As an application, we prove the inequality $\dim_p(K)\geq\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}(Γ/pΓ)+\dim_p(k)$ between Kato's $p$-dimensions, and we show that it becomes an equality as soon as $(K,v)$ is maximally complete.

title: Torsion Theories in a non-pointed Context II: iterated torsion theories
abstract: Generalizing a known result in the context of homological categories, we show that, in a regular protomodular category $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a posetal, monocoreflective subcategory whose coreflector inverts monomorphisms, every torsion theory, in a non-pointed sense, satisfying suitable properties gives rise to a torsion theory in the category $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ of arrows in $\mathcal{C}$. Moreover, we show that the induced torsion theory in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ satisfies the same good properties of the original one in $\mathcal{C}$, allowing to iterate the process. Examples of this situation can be found in protomodular varieties of universal algebras with more than one constant or in duals of elementary toposes.

title: An Introduction to the Obstacle Problem
abstract: We give a self-contained account of the classical obstacle problem, written for graduate students who wish to enter the field of free boundary problems. Starting from a one-dimensional model and an explicit radially symmetric example, we set up the variational problem, show that minimizers exist and are unique, and prove interior $W^{2,p}$-regularity as well as the optimal $C^{1,1}$-regularity. The second half of the notes is devoted to the free boundary: we prove that it is porous, introduce blow-up limits, and use the Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman monotonicity formula to show that every free boundary point is either regular or singular. These notes grew out of a mini-course at the Rio Summer School on PDEs in 2020, and they are meant to be read alongside, not instead of, the monograph by Petrosyan, Shahgholian, and Uraltseva.

title: Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals: Absorption Probabilities and Conic Intrinsic Volumes
abstract:
Let $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process in $\mathbb R^d$ whose coordinate processes $(U_t^{(i)})_{t\in\mathbb R}$, $1\le i\le d$, are independent, centered, and have covariance function $\mathbb E [U_s^{(i)}U_t^{(i)}]=e^{-|t-s|/2}$.
  For every $T>0$, we obtain an explicit formula for the probability that the convex hull $\mathrm{conv}\{U_t:0\le t\le T\}$ contains the origin. We obtain a similar formula for a circular Ornstein--Uhlenbeck loop whose covariance is the normalized $T$-periodization of this kernel.
  For each fixed dimension $d$, we determine the precise long-time asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities, which decay as explicit constants times $T^{d-1} e^{-T/2}$ as $T\to\infty$. We also show that, as $d\to\infty$, the absorption probabilities in both models undergo a transition from $0$ to $1$ around $T=2d$, with a common Gaussian limiting profile on the scale $\sqrt d$.
  We also obtain explicit formulas for the probability that $σZ$ belongs to the convex hull of Brownian motion or Brownian bridge on $[0,1]$ in $\mathbb R^d$, where $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector and $σ\ge0$. The large-$σ$ asymptotics recover the known formulas for the expected volumes of these convex hulls.
  Finally, we compute the conic intrinsic volumes of the closed positive hulls of deterministic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals and their circular analogues in Hilbert spaces. Their Grassmann angles coincide with the corresponding Ornstein--Uhlenbeck absorption probabilities. After suitable rescaling, the small-time limits of these conic intrinsic volumes recover the formulas of Gao--Vitale and Gao for the intrinsic volumes of the Brownian body and its Brownian-bridge analogue.

title: Algebraic Quantum Field Theory
abstract: Algebraic quantum field theory describes a quantum system through its observables, their localisation in spacetime, and the states that assign them expectation values. The separation of the specification of observables from the choice of a state makes it possible to compare vacuum, thermal and charged representations without assuming that they share a preferred Hilbert space. We develop the framework from familiar quantum mechanics, construct the free scalar field, and explain how causality and positive energy constrain local measurements. The Reeh--Schlieder theorem, the structure of local von Neumann algebras and the split property reveal key differences between quantum theory in the continuum (i.e. QFT) and ordinary quantum mechanics with finitely many degrees of freedom. Superselection theory relates observable charges to statistics and internal symmetries. Finally, local covariance and perturbative and homological methods extend the discussion to curved spacetime, interactions and gauge theories. We also discuss measurement theory and quantum information aspects of AQFT.

title: An alternative variational approach to constrained critical points for nonlinear Schrödinger equations with combined nonlinearities
abstract: We introduce a new variational framework for the study of standing waves for nonlinear Schrödinger equations with combined power nonlinearities. The approach is based on minimizing the mass functional over a set defined by an upper bound on the energy and a lower bound on a nonlinear potential term, rather than minimizing the energy at prescribed mass. This yields a new characterization of the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg optimizer through purely variational constraints. As a consequence, we establish the existence of minimizers for all energy levels below a critical threshold and derive the corresponding Euler--Lagrange equations. These minimizers give rise to standing-wave solutions of the nonlinear Schröedinger equation

title: Symplectomorphism invariance of the wrapped Fukaya category
abstract: An exact symplectomorphism of finite type Liouville manifolds is called 'strict' if it has bounded primitive; such symplectomorphisms are well known to induce deformation equivalences and hence equivalences of wrapped Fukaya categories. Here we note that an arbitrary symplectomorphism of Weinstein manifolds, with no assumptions at infinity, can be used to construct an equivalence of Fukaya categories. We combine this with a pointwise criterion for constructing such symplectomorphisms to improve two statements in the mirror symmetry literature -- for very affine hypersurfaces and multiplicative hypertoric varieties -- where Fukaya categories were calculated for a Liouville form not known to be strictly exact symplectomorphic to the natural Kähler Liouville form on the space in question. All results are obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

title: Moment Polyptychs and the Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties
abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric variety of complex dimension $2n$ using symplectic cutting. When the defining arrangement is cooriented so that its base region is non-empty and bounded, fibre rotation has proper moment map and produces compact Kähler orbifold cuts carrying the residual torus action. We introduce the moment polyptych of such a cut, a polytopal complex assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and show that its vertices and local lattice data determine the fixed points, tangent weights, and finite orbifold groups required for equivariant orbifold Riemann-Roch localisation. Even for a smooth hypertoric manifold, a reducible core forces every cut in the outer cut chamber to have non-trivial cyclic isotropy, while the cuts are smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety, which is then a product of projective spaces. For a positive regular integral level $d$ in the outer cut chamber, algebraic cutting identifies the cut's quantisation with a finite filtration piece of the circle-graded quantisation of the original hypertoric variety, whose successive quotients recover the individual circle-weight spaces. We prove that the higher cohomology of the pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes at every such level, so that the localised index is the character of the actual space of sections. Finally, a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is the arrangement slack function, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. Thus, each finite stage admits a weighted lattice-point description whose multiplicity function is supported on the lattice points in the support of the level-$d$ moment polyptych.

title: Jacob's ladders and wander from Hardy-Littlewood integral (1918) to the $ζ$-Platonic cube form of equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem
abstract: In this paper we obtain $ζ$-Platonic cube form of our almost linear formula. From this follows, for example, the $ζ$-Platonic equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem. The last result represents the point of contact between the Hardy-Littlewood integral and the Fermat-Wiles theorem and also with one of the Platonic solid - cube.

title: Local-to-Global Theorems Based on Cones with Applications to Graph Coloring
abstract:
Local-to-Global theorems are a cornerstone of many of recent developments in theoretical computer science from coding theory and PCPs all the way to analyzing mixing time of Markov chains. Building on trickledown theorems on simplicial complexes, several techniques have been established to obtain tighter local-to-global theorems to analyze the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics, namely matrix trickledown, ${\mathcal C}$-Lorentzian polynomials and more recently Bochner type inequalities.
  In this paper, we adopt non-local local-to-global/Bochner type inequalities on "cones", corresponding to the local neighborhood of a given vertex, to show that the Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time to sample proper colorings of maximum degree $Δ$ graphs as long as $q\geq 1.7408Δ$.

title: Diagrams for Roots and Quiver Representations in the context of the Gabriel-Kac Theorem
abstract: Using the data of the Dynkin diagrams, we build graphical calculi for representing the positive roots of Kac-Moody algebras and the representations of quivers. Once developed, we use these to analyze the asymptotic size of the root and representation spaces, and discuss how this relates to the Gabriel-Kac theorem, the correspondence between these two structures. We give a refinement of this correspondence in terms of the trichotomy of growth rates for Kac-Moody algebras depending on if they are of finite, affine, or indefinite type, which is done in terms of what we call ``tree like" representations.

title: A Stochastic LineseArch Method (SLAM) for Minimizing Expectation Residuals: Weakening Boundedness of Gradient
abstract: We establish convergence guarantees for the Stochastic LineseArch Method (SLAM) proposed and analyzed in Wang et al. (arXiv:2512.14979) for nonconvex composite stochastic optimization, retaining the iteration and sample complexity orders of the original analysis assuming neither the boundedness of true gradients nor the Lipschitz continuity of the convex nonsmooth term $r$. ChatGPT was used to assist in developing a key intermediate result. Under uniformly Lipschitz continuous and unbiased sampled gradients with uniformly bounded variance with mini-batch sizes proportional to the iteration budget, SLAM achieves an iteration complexity $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ and a sample complexity $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$ for obtaining an iterate whose expected proximal-gradient residual norm is at most $ε$.

title: Van der Waerden's Problem for Cubic Surfaces
abstract:
For a smooth cubic surface $S/\mathbb{Q}$, the absolute Galois group acts on the $27$ lines of $S_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$, giving a subgroup \[ G_S\subseteq W(E_6). \] We study the distribution of $G_S$ when the twenty coefficients of a defining cubic form are chosen independently from a large interval $[-H,H]$.
  We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the number of smooth integral cubic forms of height at most $H$ for which \[ G_S\neq W(E_6) \] is \[ O_\varepsilon\!\left(H^{19+1/21+\varepsilon}\right). \] The principal obstruction is the unique subgroup $W(E_6)^+$ of index $2$. By a theorem of Saito, membership in this subgroup is equivalent to the signed discriminant of the cubic surface being a square. A recent square-value estimate of Bonolis, Pierce, and Woo then gives the exponent $19+1/21$. For each of the other five conjugacy classes of maximal subgroups of $W(E_6)$, recent results on rational points in projective thin sets give the sharper bound $O(H^{19})$.
  We also prove the lower bound \[ N_{\mathrm{exc}}(H)\gg H^{16} \] by counting cubic surfaces containing a fixed rational line, and exhibit an $H^{14}$-sized exceptional family with no rational line, arising from rational Eckardt points. These examples lead us to conjecture that \[ N_{\mathrm{exc}}(H)=H^{16+o(1)}. \]
  Finally, we investigate whether Bhargava's proof of van der Waerden's conjecture for $S_n$ can be adapted to the index-$2$ $E_6$-problem. A double-discriminant argument gives the desired $H^{19+\varepsilon}$ bound whenever the product of the strongly square-dividing primes is sufficiently large. The remaining difficulty comes from weak square divisibility.

title: Generalised hyperbolic polynomials: combinatorial interpretation and real-rootedness
abstract: For $p,q$ natural numbers, define $Δ^{\langle p,q \rangle}:=x^{p-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y} + y^{q-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial x}$, and consider the sequence of polynomials $\biggl((Δ^{\langle p,q \rangle})^n \cdot x\biggr)_{n\geq 0}$; we call these the generalised hyperbolic polynomials. In this paper, we provide a simple combinatorial interpretation for these polynomials. As special cases, we obtain combinatorial interpretations for the coefficients of the analogs of sinh and cosh corresponding to the curve $x^p- p y^q/q=1$; on setting $p=q=3$, we obtain Conrad and Flajolet's tree interpretation for the coefficients of the Dixonian elliptic functions (2006) as a special case. Finally, we show that for any $p,q\geq 3$, after suitably normalising followed by substituting $y=1$, we obtain a sequence of univariate polynomials which are real-rooted.

title: Hierarchical Laminates Cannot Reproduce All Effective Properties of Planar Two-Phase Composites: A Counterexample with a 16-Component Potential
abstract: Designing a composite requires understanding which effective properties can be achieved through varying its microstructure, i.e., the spatial arrangement of given constituent materials. Hierarchical laminates, created by successive layering, reach many known limits on these properties, making it natural to ask whether they can reproduce every effective response obtainable from the same constituents. We answer this question negatively for planar two-phase composites governed by linear systems whose potentials have 16 or more components. We construct constituent material properties and, at any prescribed nontrivial phase fraction, periodic microstructures whose effective properties cannot be approximated by hierarchical laminates, even when layer directions, proportions, and the number of layering steps are unrestricted. We design the constituents so that all hierarchical laminates have equal effective energies at two prescribed mean gradients. The key step is to construct a medium whose local properties are those of horizontal laminates with smoothly varying phase fractions, but whose effective energies violate this equality. Approximating these energies with sufficiently fine periodic stripes of the original constituents yields the two-phase counterexample. This construction also gives a negative answer to the two-well relaxation problem: the minimum of two positive-definite homogeneous quadratic forms on $\mathbb{R}^{2\times32}$ can have distinct quasiconvex and rank-one convex envelopes. The counterexample and the strict inequality between the envelopes are formally verified in Lean 4.

title: Sobolev Inequalities Relating Rough Riemannian Metrics to their Distance Functions
abstract: In previous papers, the first named author and E. Bryden explored Sobolev like inequalities relating the norm of a Riemmanian metric $g_1$, in terms of a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, in order to estimate the distance function $d_{g_1}$. Although $|g_1|_{g_0}$ is not the gradient of the distance function $d_{g_1}$, it was shown that a Morrey and Sobolev inequalities hold in their appropriate domains. In this paper we see that these results can be extended to the case where $g_1$ is a Rough Riemannian metric, something roughly analogous to an $L^{\infty}$ metric. We show that the proof of the Morrey and Sobolev inequality go through, with appropriate adjustments, as well as convergence results. We also adapt previous examples from the literature to the rough Riemannian metric case which show the hypotheses from the main theorems are necessary.

title: Width and amplitude inequalities over DG-rings
abstract: We study width over commutative noetherian local differential graded (DG) rings with bounded homology. We establish a derived width formula and prove amplitude inequalities for the derived completion of derived Hom and tensor products. As applications, we obtain Iversen's amplitude inequality and a criterion ensuring that regular sequences on a DG-module are regular on the DG-ring. These applications recover results for DG-modules with finitely generated homology and also hold for derived complete DG-modules. Finally, we characterize Cohen--Macaulay DG-rings by the existence of a bounded derived complete DG-module of finite injective dimension whose amplitude equals that of the DG-ring. This provides a version of Bass' conjecture for derived complete DG-modules.

title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of oriented $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$
abstract: We prove a uniqueness theorem for stationary integral $n$-cycles asymptotic to a pair of n-planes satisfying the symmetric angle condition. For the general angle condition, we obtain a classification for complete smooth embedded oriented minimal submanifolds with vanishing first de Rham cohomology that are asymptotic to a pair of $n$-planes.

title: Uniqueness of the weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow in four dimensions
abstract: We improve a parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem for the Yang-Mills flow. This allows us to prove new existence of weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow having with better properties than Struwe's weak solution on four manifolds in \cite {St2}. Finally, we apply the new parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem to solve the Struwe problem in \cite {St2} and prove uniqueness of weak solutions to the Yang-Mills flow on compact four-manifolds with initial value $A_0 \in W^{1, 2}(M)$.

title: The Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over higher dimensional Riemannian manifolds
abstract: We develop a parabolic formulation of the Uhlenbeck gauge fixing theorem and use it to prove the maximal existence of the Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over compact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds for $n \geq 4$. We apply Moser's iteration technique \cite{Mo1} to give a new proof of the bound of the curvature. Using an idea of Hamilton on the Ricci flow \cite{Ha}, we also provide a new proof on uniform estimates of higher order derivatives. Furthermore, we investigate the blow-up of the Yang-Mills flow at the maximal existence time and improve an asymptotical result of Hong-Tian \cite{HT1}.

title: Boxing Problem
abstract: We study the \textit{Boxing Problem}, which seeks a subset of points in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) maximizing the total reward of a selection of points minus the width of its axis-aligned bounding box. We also investigate the associated \textit{Boxing Set}, defined by the epigraph of the width function over binary selection variables. Although the width function is not submodular in general, we restore submodularity by fixing an anchor point. After anchoring, we establish a connection to the intersection of mixing sets with a linking constraint, which yields a polynomial-time optimization algorithm and a polynomial-size extended formulation. We then study the polyhedral structure of the Boxing Set and show that its facets admit laminar families of tight sets and can be obtained by sequential lifting. For the one-dimensional case, we provide a complete description of facet-defining inequalities together with a strongly polynomial-time separation algorithm.

title: Loop Space Models and Integral Homology of Connected Quandles
abstract: We construct a marked integral delooping of a connected quandle's covering monoid, realizing its rack space as a homotopy fiber. For finite connected quandles at primes $p$ not dividing a point-stabilizer order, we determine the local $A_\infty$ type and the ordinary rack cohomology shuffle algebra over fields of characteristic $p$. We compute integral quandle homology in all positive degrees for finite connected regular cyclic Alexander quandles and the tetrahedral quandle. At such primes dividing the quandle order, rack-space homotopy groups have exponentially many cyclic direct summands of fixed $p$-power order in each sufficiently large degree.

title: Conformal Predictive Distributions for Contextual Order Fulfillment Optimization
abstract: Ship-to-home fulfillment requires a retailer to select a fulfillment location and carrier before the delivery time is known. These decisions often rely on static transit-time estimates, which cannot represent how delivery-time uncertainty varies across orders and fulfillment options. This paper constructs conformal predictive distributions (CPDs) using Conformal Predictive Systems (CPS) for regression and the cross Venn-Abers predictor (CVAP) for multiclass classification, and uses them in a contextual optimization model for fulfillment decisions. The model is solved by contextual sample-average approximation (C-SAA). The regret of each fulfillment decision, its expected cost above that of the best decision, is bounded by forecast error, scenario-evaluation error, and the candidate-generation gap. The forecast term depends on how well calibration residuals or class probabilities represent the current order. On more than five million proprietary order records, CVAP raises exact-day accuracy from 49.5% for the rule-based estimate to 64.1%. Paired with a decision rule that selects a quantile weighting late errors more heavily, the split CPS (SCPS) gives a point estimate that raises late-delivery detection from 3.8% to 79.4%. Residual-based CPS distributions also meet or slightly exceed nominal interval-coverage targets. In decision experiments with a JD.com simulator over six test dates, C-SAA with CVAP lowers mean total cost by 7.1% and C-SAA with the Mondrian CPS (MCPS) lowers it by 6.7%, relative to C-SAA with the original nonconformal forecast. Both cut the late-delivery rate from 5.7% to below 4.0%.

title: Convergence analysis of an augmented dual-mixed fnite element method with skew-symmetric Nitsche stabilization for the generalized Oseen equations with mixed boundary conditions
abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze a new skew-symmetric Nitsche-augmented mixed scheme for the generalized Oseen equations with non-solenoidal convective fields, subject to mixed boundary conditions. The scheme is based on a continuous pseudostress-velocity augmented dual-mixed finite element formulation, in which the Dirichlet datum is imposed naturally, whereas the prescribed normal trace of the pseudostress is incorporated into the $H(div,)$ stress space. We establish the well-posedness of the continuous formulation by means of a classical lifting argument and its corresponding homogeneous problem. The essential boundary condition is then weakly enforced in the discrete scheme through suitable stabilizing Nitsche terms. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the discrete scheme, allowing the use of general conforming approximation spaces for both the pseudostress and the velocity. Moreover, in the case of homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and general Neumann data, we establish the stability of the Nitsche scheme. Under mild regularity assumptions on the exact solution, we prove optimal convergence rates in an energy norm. Finally, numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the theoretical convergence rates and assess the performance of the proposed scheme for non-solenoidal convective fields and solutions exhibiting boundary layers.

title: Maximum Diversity and Support Transitions on Disks and Three-Dimensional Balls
abstract: For the similarity kernel $e^{-|x-y|}$, we determine the probability measure of maximum diversity on every planar disk and three-dimensional ball, answering a question of Leinster and Roff. In each dimension the measure is uniform on the boundary up to a threshold. Above it, the support is a closed central ball and the outer sphere, separated by a mass-free annulus. In dimensions two and three, their conjecture of finitely many supporting spheres therefore holds only up to the respective threshold. We obtain the measure explicitly up to one scalar root in three dimensions and through Fredholm integral equations and a scalar contact equation in the plane. Computations in dimensions four and five suggest that interior supporting spheres appear one at a time.

title: Pointed Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
abstract: We study the geometry of Hurwitz--Brill--Noether spaces with vanishing conditions at a totally ramified point. Degeneration to a curve with an elliptic tail simplifies the combinatorics of Larson, Larson--Larson--Vogt, and Aggarwal, giving inductive proofs of Aggarwal's results in the one-point setting, and yields an efficient recursion for the algebraic Euler characteristics. Finally, when the expected dimension is negative, we give a numerical criterion ensuring the universal Hurwitz--Brill--Noether locus admits a component of expected relative dimension, generically finite over its image in the Hurwitz space, analogous to the existing results of Pflueger and Teixidor i Bigas for classical Brill--Noether loci.

title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
abstract: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. The values for n <= 5 are classical. We prove D_6 = 107/312, attained only by permutations of (12, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2), and D_7 = 73/180, attained only by permutations of (11, 10, 8, 7, 4, 3, 1). The proof reduces the supremum to a finite search. The key facts are an exact lower bound d_n(v) >= delta^2_U for every rational subspace U perpendicular to v, a matching fiber upper bound, and Banaszczyk's transference theorem, applied along the Korkine-Zolotarev flag of the dual lattice v^perpendicular intersection Z^n. The search is quotiented by signed coordinate permutations and carried out entirely in exact rational arithmetic. It terminates with a certificate: no node of the search is left unresolved, and every surviving candidate is evaluated exactly. The method also recovers the known values for n = 3, 4, 5.

title: Simple Torsion-Free Linear Groups from Global Division Algebras
abstract: We investigate the reduced norm-one group $\mathrm{SL}_1(D)$ of a central division algebra $D$ of odd degree over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using the Brauer-Hasse-Noether theorem and the Margulis-Platonov theorem, we derive a criterion for abstract simplicity in terms of local division completions. For a division algebra of degree $15$ with local invariants $1/3$, $-1/3$, $1/5$, and $-1/5$, the construction yields a candidate example of an infinite, torsion-free, nonabelian simple linear group. This would provide an affirmative answer to Problem 16.78 of the Kourovka Notebook. The argument was generated using an AI system and has not yet been independently verified by human mathematicians.

title: Cohomological change of coefficients for noncocommutative Hopf algebras
abstract: Let $A$ be a finite Hopf algebra over a Noetherian commutative ring $R$. For any map $f : R \to k$ where $k$ is a field, there is a natural map on the cohomology of $A$ under this change of coefficients $H^\ast(f): H^\ast(A, R) \otimes_R k \to H^\ast(A_k, k)$. In this paper we examine this map for $R = \mathbb Z[ζ]$ the cyclotomic integers with $ζ$ an $\ell$th root of unity. We show that under a finite generation assumption, the induced map gives a homeomorphism on the spectra of the two cohomology rings. Finally, we turn to small quantum groups defined over $\mathbb Z[ζ]$ and show that, with mild restrictions on $\ell$, every fiber map whose residue field has a good prime characteristic induces an isomorphism on cohomology.

title: Randomized algorithms in numerical linear algebra for scientific computing
abstract: Randomized numerical linear algebra (RNLA) has fundamentally changed the landscape of scientific computing over the last twenty to thirty years. While early breakthroughs focused primarily on low-rank approximation and least-squares problems, randomized techniques are now used to solve a broad range of linear algebra problems, supporting applications spanning data science, optimization, and computational engineering. This paper surveys some of the main ideas of RNLA, focusing on methods that are effective in practice and on simple theoretical bounds that can be used to understand them. We highlight the core benefits of randomization: improved scalability, algorithmic simplicity, and---contrary to what the name may suggest---remarkable reliability and numerical stability. Topics include sketching, low-rank approximation, least squares, orthogonalization and approximate orthogonalization, randomized Krylov subspace methods, preconditioning, trace and spectral density estimation, row and column selection algorithms, posterior error estimation, randomized regularization, and tensor-structured randomness.

title: New structure for Villadsen algebras of the first type
abstract: In this paper we establish two main results concerning the comparison theory of positive elements in approximately homogeneous $C^{*}$-algebras with diagonal maps. The first is an existence theorem which interfaces with the rank problem; given a Villadsen algebra $A$, we construct a convex cone that induces an embedding of a semigroup into $Cu(A)$. This semigroup is identified with the set of strictly positive, lower-semicontinuous affine maps on the trace simplex of $A$. The second is a construction of an AH algebra that produces an obstacle to classifying the approximate unitary orbits of positive elements in terms of their spectral data. Our counterexample sheds light on a critical topological obstruction when attempting to understand equivalence classes of $*$-homomorphisms from $C_{0}((0,1])$ to an arbitrary $C^{*}$-algebra of stable rank one.

title: Non-associative Hopf Algebra on Dyck Paths Arising from the Shuffle-insertion Product
abstract: In this paper, we define a shuffle-insertion product and a cut-box coproduct on the vector space spanned by Dyck paths, where the product is commutative but non-associative. We prove that the product and coproduct are compatible, making the space a non-associative bialgebra. This bialgebra is connected and bigraded by path degree and peak number, and hence is a non-associative Hopf algebra. Its primitive subspace is spanned by atoms, and associators of primitive elements are primitive. Furthermore, we provide closed-form formulas for its left and right antipodes. We also define the convolution product on the space of linear transformations of the non-associative Hopf algebra, which equips this space with a non-associative algebra structure. Finally, we construct a one-parameter deformation preserving the cut-box coproduct. Its zero specialization is the ordinary shuffle Hopf algebra, which is also the associated graded algebra for the atom filtration, while every nonzero specialization is isomorphic to the shuffle-insertion algebra.

title: Geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack
abstract: The analytic Emerton-Gee stack is a rigid analytic moduli stack of $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules over the Robba ring, and is expected to play a fundamental role in the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for locally analytic representations. In this paper, we establish the fundamental geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack: it is a rigid analytic Artin stack, normal, a local complete intersection, and equidimensional of the expected dimension. As an application, our normality result removes the reducedness hypothesis in the paper of Le, Strauch, and Wang, thereby yielding an unconditional proof of the conjecture on the global sections of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack formulated by Emerton, Gee, and Hellmann.

title: New Explicit Examples of Mannheim Pairs in $\mathbb{R}^3$
abstract: In this paper, we construct new explicit parametrizations of Mannheim pairs in Euclidean 3-space. Unlike the known examples in the literature, which are essentially slant helices or general helices, the curve presented here is neither a helix nor a slant helix. We provide the full Frenet apparatus, the explicit Cartesian coordinates expressed in terms of elementary functions, and the corresponding Mannheim partner curve. The construction is based on a specific choice of the angular function that governs the curve's tangent indicatrix, leading to integrable expressions.

title: Safety of layered control systems via control barrier morphisms
abstract: Layered control architectures provide a powerful paradigm for synthesizing controllers for complex systems. Yet, translating guarantees at each layer to system-level guarantees is challenging due to the interactions between layers. To address this problem, this paper presents a categorical perspective on layered control architectures. Individual systems are represented as control coalgebras, their interactions are specified as morphisms to mediators, and system-level behaviors are obtained via composition defined categorically as a pullback. To analyze the safety of these systems, we formulate control barrier morphisms (CBMs), the categorical generalization of control barrier functions. We prove that feedback controllers satisfying a CBM condition render the associated safe subobject forward invariant. It is through CBMs that we can establish the safety of layered systems: given a CBM at each layer subject to compatibility conditions, the universal property of the pullback implies the existence of a CBM for the composed system. Safety of a full-order model being safety filtered by a reduced-order model is recovered as a specialization of the categorical framework.

title: Sharp Adams inequality for Critical Biharmonic Equations with Hardy--Hénon Weights in $\mathbb{R}^4$
abstract: We study a class of weighted fourth-order elliptic problems in \(\mathbb{R}^4\) driven by the biharmonic operator and involving Hardy--Hénon type potentials. The nonlinear term has critical exponential growth in the sense of an Adams-type inequality. The weights \(|x|^a\) and \(|x|^b\) allow us to incorporate singular, vanishing, and unbounded effects in a unified variational framework. We introduce a suitable weighted function space, establish Sobolev-type embeddings, and prove an Adams-type inequality adapted to this setting. Under appropriate structural assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove the existence of nontrivial weak solutions. We also obtain regularity properties and derive a Pohozaev identity, which leads to a nonexistence result.

title: Neural Stream Function Method for Electrical Impedance Tomography with Lipschitz Conductivities
abstract: Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) reconstructs the conductivity inside an object from voltage and current measurements on its boundary. The resulting inverse problem is nonlinear and severely ill-posed. Neural networks offer a flexible computational approach, but training physics informed neural networks for EIT and relating their training loss to reconstruction accuracy remain challenging. We develop a novel constrained neural stream function method for planar EIT with Lipschitz conductivities. The method builds the conductivity constraints and prescribed boundary voltages into the neural trial functions and replaces the second order conductivity equation with a first order system in strong form. The measured current is also used to construct a fixed baseline for the stream function. For this formulation, we derive error estimates that relate the sampled neural objective to errors in the physical boundary currents and the reconstructed conductivity. The error estimates separate the contributions from neural approximation, measurement noise, and sampling. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high reconstruction accuracy with both exact and noisy boundary data.

title: Bore wave solutions to the viscous Saint-Venant system with capillarity
abstract: We study a traveling wave formulation of the viscous Saint-Venant system in one spatial dimension with capillarity, which can be reduced to an equivalent nonlinear third order ODE. We construct heteroclinic orbits for small positive capillarity, for arbitrary positive capillarity under an explicit small Froude number condition, and in a small-amplitude regime away from the critical Froude number. These then give rise to smooth traveling bore wave solutions to the viscous Saint-Venant system.

title: Optimality of Threshold Policies for Heat Storage Optimization and a Policy Gradient Algorithm
abstract:
We study the optimal control of a stylized finite-horizon heat-storage system operated by a prosumer who can buy heat from and sell heat to a district heating network. Heat production and consumption are uncertain, and charging and discharging decisions have to be taken before the subsequent heat balance is observed. The resulting problem is formulated as a Markov decision process with continuous state and action spaces. We first establish a structural characterization of the optimal policy as a two-parameter threshold policy. Under additional regularity assumptions, we prove differentiability and Lipschitz properties of the value functions.
  Exploiting the threshold structure, we parameterize the policy by the time-dependent lower and upper thresholds and derive a pathwise stochastic-gradient estimator. We then propose a projected stochastic policy-gradient algorithm, establish a constrained Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz inequality and derive global finite-sample bounds for both the objective optimality gap and the distance to the optimal threshold vector. Finally, numerical experiments for a non-stationary heat-balance process illustrate the evolution of the threshold parameters.

title: Spectrahedral relaxations and tightenings of rigidly convex sets
abstract: We construct a natural spectrahedral relaxation of a rigidly convex set (rcs) that depends only on the cubic part and on the degree of the defining real zero polynomial. For quadratic polynomials, we prove exactness and for a product of linear polynomials, we show that a higher order version of our relaxation is exact. We also establish a way of tightening the relaxation by moving the origin inside the rcs, and that the rcs is recovered by sweeping the origin over its interior. To obtain all these results we use a linear form that is closely connected to the zeros of a given real zero polynomial. We also prove that any rcs can be written as an affine linear slice of the cone of non-negative polynomials. Using this, we can define a hierarchy of tightenings that are spectrahedral shadows. We can show that this tightening is exact if the given polynomial admits a determinantal representation. This tightening is similar to a tightening of a hyperbolicity cone due to Kummer, Plaumann, and Vinzant.

title: Stable limits for the clone-mutant chain with mother-dependent mutation
abstract: We consider the general mother-dependent neutral mutation model defined in Blancas, Fittipaldi and Hernández-Torres (2026), consisting of a multitype branching process in which every individual carries one of $d$ alleles and each mutant child acquires a type different from that of its mother, according to a prescribed distribution. We assume that the total offspring distribution is critical and belongs to the domain of attraction of an $α$-stable law, with $α\in(1,2)$, while mutations are rare. Extending the results of Blancas and Rivero (2018), we prove the finite-dimensional convergence of the rescaled Markov chain that records, in each allelic generation, the sizes of the type-specific clone subfamilies and the mutant populations they produce. The limiting clone masses form a multitype Jiřina process driven by stable subordinators with drift, whose branching mechanism combines the stable reproduction law with the mother-dependent mutation matrix.

title: Characteristic identities for orthogonal quantum matrices: examples
abstract:
In this note, we illustrate our recent results regarding structure theory of orthogonal Quantum Matrix algebras \cite{OP-BMW,OP-reciprocal,OP-ortho} using the simplest nontrivial example: the RTT-algebra associated with the canonical orthogonal R-matrix of type $O(3)$ (see, e.g., \cite{FRT}). By introducing a suitable linear order on the set of generators, we obtain a set of quadratic relations defining the algebra. Next, we investigate relations among its higher-degree polynomials. As a result, we verify `in components' the Cayley-Hamilton and the reciprocal relations, obtained earlier with the use of the R-matrix techniques. We explicitly calculate the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of quantum matrices and propose a
  conjecture regarding the form of the Hilbert-Poincaré series for the RTT-algebra.

title: The Interference-Conjugate Transform: The Tightest Interference-Linear Surrogate for Power Control, Scheduling and Beamforming in Wireless Networks
abstract: Closed-form fractional programming (FP), weighted MMSE (WMMSE), and the 2026 surrogate-enhanced methods SEFP and XMMSE all maximize the weighted sum rate by iteratively maximizing a surrogate linear in the interference power. We show that this family admits a unique best member: the interference-conjugate transform (ICT), which replaces each rate term $\log(1+a/b)$ by $\max_{κ\ge0}[Ω(κa)-κb]$, where $Ω$ is the closed-form partial convex conjugate of the rate in the interference variable and the optimal multiplier is the interference price $a/(b(a+b))$. We prove that, for any fixed price, $Ω(κ\,\cdot)$ is the pointwise largest own-signal function compatible with a valid interference-linear lower bound, and that tightness at an anchor forces the price. Hence all four benchmark surrogates, which share this price and differ only in their own-signal term, are dominated pointwise by ICT. At SINR $γ$, the benchmarks' own-signal curvature exceeds the true curvature by factors behaving as $γ/2$ (FP/WMMSE) and $(\logγ)/2$ (SEFP/XMMSE), against $1+1/(γ(γ+2))$ for ICT, and this ordering carries over to the certified ascent per iteration and the asymptotic linear convergence rate. ICT yields closed-form updates at the benchmarks' per-iteration cost for single-antenna power control, uplink joint scheduling and power control, and multi-cell MISO beamforming, and the first solver-free algorithm for sum-least-$q$th-percentile rate maximization, via a $K$-dimensional convex dual with closed-form gradient and Hessian and a certified duality gap. In uplink scheduling, ICT improves proportional-fairness utility over FP by +7.03 and over SEFP by +3.35 (60/60 drops) using 18.7 iterations per slot vs. 49.7 and 38.0; in MISO beamforming with $M=8$, it reaches 99.9% of its final value in a median of 9 iterations vs. 16 (XMMSE) and 1160 (FP/WMMSE).

title: Maximal Curves with Few Automorphisms
abstract: We consider the problem of constructing maximal curves with few automorphisms over finite fields. Our main ingredient is the determination of the \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\!\left(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\right)\)-stabilizer of the roots of the Chebyshev polynomials, apart from two exceptional cases already treated in the literature. We prove that, in all other cases, the only nontrivial Möbius symmetry is the sign involution. This settles the general case for the automorphism groups of the corresponding Chebyshev curves. We further construct an infinite family of maximal curves of unbounded genus whose only nontrivial automorphism is the hyperelliptic involution. This reveals a contrasting phenomenon to the common heuristic that curves with many rational points tend to have large automorphism groups.

title: Uniqueness and comparison principle for Trudinger's parabolic equation with Hölder continuous boundary values
abstract:
For every $p > 1$, we establish uniqueness and comparison principle for Trudinger's parabolic equation \[
  \partial_t (|u|^{p-2}u) = \text{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u) \quad \text{in } Ω\times (0,\text{T}), \] assuming suitable Hölder regularity for the boundary values. Our comparison principle applies to sign-changing weak sub- and supersolutions. As an application, we obtain uniqueness of weak solutions to Cauchy--Dirichlet problems when the lateral boundary data is suitably Hölder continuous in time. In particular, Lipschitz continuous boundary values are covered.

title: Fisher Geometry of Circular Wrapped Normals: Completion and Curvature
abstract: We determine the intrinsic Fisher geometry of the two-parameter circular wrapped normal family. Although its finite parameters form a cylinder, its metric completion is a disk: adjoining the uniform law extends the Fisher metric to a positive-definite real-analytic metric. The Gaussian curvature vanishes at the added point, is positive nearby, and tends to $-1/2$ as the underlying standard deviation tends to zero. We prove that the curvature has exactly one nonuniform zero radius and exactly one critical radius, the latter a nondegenerate positive maximum. Opposite points sufficiently close to uniformity are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic through the uniform law, so their intrinsic distance is not attained inside the nonuniform family. In contrast, identifying the means of real normal distributions modulo a period retains a complete hyperbolic cylinder with an infinitely distant cusp. Wrapping strictly decreases Fisher information in every nonzero tangent direction, while the information deficit and its fixed-order derivatives are exponentially small as the standard deviation tends to zero. The curvature theorem is proved by convergent series and explicit analytic remainder estimates; numerical figures serve only as illustrations.

title: A Poisson Transition and Bias Law for KSG Mutual-Information Estimation
abstract: We quantify the error of the strict-radius Kraskov--Stögbauer--Grassberger (KSG-1) mutual-information estimator on a Gaussian channel as the sample size \(n\) grows and the channel becomes nearly deterministic. For fixed dimension \(p\) and neighbor index \(k\), we define the resolution parameter \(u_n=ne^{-I_n}\), where \(I_n\) is the true mutual information in nats. When \(u_n\to u\in(0,\infty)\), we prove that the estimation error converges in mean square to a computable deterministic bias \(B_{p,k}(u)\). Sampling fluctuations therefore vanish, while an additive bias can persist. We derive this bias from an explicit marked-Poisson law for the neighborhood counts, characterize its small-\(u\) asymptotics, and show that it tends to zero as \(u\to\infty\). The same law describes how often neighborhoods saturate, meaning that they make the largest possible contribution to the estimate. The limiting saturation probability decreases continuously and strictly from one to zero, allowing a Gaussian-model bias correction on fixed critical intervals. Finite-sample experiments show substantial bias even when the true information lies below the estimator's logarithmic ceiling and saturated neighborhoods are rare. Saturation-based correction reduces estimation error in these experiments, though recovering the resolution parameter from the observed saturation fraction can remain difficult when saturation is rare.

title: High-chromatic tournament parts without a complete pair of cyclic triangles
abstract: Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour conjectured that any two disjoint subtournaments of sufficiently large chromatic number contain cyclic triangles, one in each subtournament, with all edges between them oriented in the same direction. We disprove this conjecture by constructing, for every positive integer $d$, a tournament $T$ with a vertex partition $(X,Y)$ such that $χ(T[X]),χ(T[Y])\ge d$, but no cyclic triangle in either part is complete to a cyclic triangle in the other. Our construction combines a graph of large girth and large chromatic number with a variant of Kneser graphs defined in terms of binary functions. We give two proofs of the required chromatic lower bound, one using the Borsuk--Ulam theorem and the other using the octahedral form of Tucker's lemma.

title: Lie (super)algebras generated by reflections in finite reflection groups of exceptional type
abstract: Using a mixture of theoretical tools and computer calculations, we describe the Lie subalgebras and the Lie sub-superalgebras generated by the sets of reflections in the group algebras of the exceptional finite reflection groups.

title: The generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture
abstract: We establish the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, including rigidity in the equality case. As a corollary, we obtain that isoperimetric regions are bounded. We prove the conjecture for Alexandrov spaces with two sided curvature bounds as well. A sharp Michael-Simon-type inequality for hypersurfaces in these spaces is also shown.

title: Sharp $L^4$ Strichartz estimate for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$
abstract: We prove the local $L^4$ Strichartz estimate without derivative loss for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov flow on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$. This reaches the sharp spatial regularity endpoint and implies the embedding $X^{0,b}\hookrightarrow L^4$ for every $b>1/2$. The proof reduces the estimate to a semi-algebraic mixed-measure estimate.

title: Homogenization theory of topological Anderson insulators: genuine gaps and pseudo-gaps
abstract: A topological Anderson insulator is an insulator whose non-trivial topological phase is induced by disorder. We develop a homogenization theory of this phenomenon for constant-coefficient elliptic systems perturbed by fluctuations oscillating at scale $\varepsilon$. Periodic fluctuations of every order below that of the operator, with appropriate amplitudes, do not average out: they produce an order-one correction $M$ given by a second-order (Born) formula, and the operator converges in the norm-resolvent sense to its homogenized limit. In particular, electric potentials and magnetic fields of zero mean, usually regarded as topologically trivial perturbations, generate corrections $M$ that change the topological phase. Fluctuations confined to a half-plane create an interface that carries the bulk-difference invariant of the homogenized operator for all $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small, a property that is stable under local defects. For random fluctuations, rare regions typically fill the homogenized gap, which becomes a pseudo-gap, and the standard interface index need no longer be defined. We define an index along cuts deformed so as to avoid the rare regions, and prove that it equals almost surely the bulk-difference invariant of the operator homogenized in the Born approximation, for first-order alloys with vanishing low moments and for a class of second-order systems with scalar disorder at criticality that includes the BHZ model.

title: Exponential decay of threshold correlations for symmetric periodic functions
abstract:
We study how often $n$ distinct integer dilates of a periodic function can all lie above a fixed threshold or all lie below its negative. We consider continuous functions $f:\mathbb R\to[-1,1]$ that are $1$-periodic, even, strictly decreasing on $[0,1/2]$, and satisfy $f(0)=1$ and $f(t+1/2)=-f(t)$. This class includes the cosine and the triangle wave. For $0\leqα<1$, let $ρ_α\in(0,1/4]$ be determined by $f(ρ_α)=α$, and let $F_α(n)$ denote the infimum of these proportions over all sets of $n$ distinct positive integer frequencies.
  We prove that $F_α(n)\geq 4ρ_α^n$ and that the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}F_α(n)^{1/n}$ exists for every threshold. When $ρ_α^{-1}$ is an integer, we obtain \begin{align} F_α(n) &\leq C_αn^{\log_2((1-ρ_α)/(1-2ρ_α))}ρ_α^n, \end{align} and hence the limit equals $ρ_α$. Otherwise, the limit belongs to the interval $[ρ_α,\lfloorρ_α^{-1}\rfloor^{-1}]$.
  The upper bound in the reciprocal case uses a cyclic covering construction previously studied in the context of circular graphs. We give a self-contained proof of the corresponding optimal modulus.

title: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program
abstract: Solving large-scale multiparametric quadratic programs (mpQPs) in real time often requires thousands of iterative optimization updates, creating a major computational bottleneck in model predictive control and learning-enabled systems. This paper proposes TQPNet, a self-supervised neural compression framework that learns to compress long ADMM optimization trajectories into a compact neural warm start followed by a few refinement iterations. We derive a low-dimensional ADMM scheme operating on the primal-dual variables $(x,β)$ and show that its iteration admits an equivalent ReLU-layer representation, termed ADMM(ReLU). Building on this insight, TQPNet combines a multilayer perceptron with ReLU activations (MLP(ReLU)) and a small number of unrolled ADMM(ReLU) refinement layers. The network is trained offline using an optimality-condition-informed residual loss, eliminating the need for solver-generated labels. The proposed residual-based framework enables both self-supervised training and online solution certification through adaptive ADMM(ReLU) refinement. Experiments on large-scale mpQPs and real-time MPC applications demonstrate that TQPNet achieves high accuracy, strong generalization, and substantially faster inference than conventional optimization-based methods.

title: Trajectory-Planning Attitude Control System for Satellites with Magnetic Attitude Control and One Reaction Wheel
abstract: Selecting attitude actuators for spacecraft in low earth orbit (LEO) often involves a trade between reaction wheels and magnetorquers. Reaction wheels generally have higher size, weight and power as well as cost, compared with magnetorquers, but have performance advantages. We consider a hybrid system relying on a single reaction wheel and three magnetorquers, using a trajectory planning control method that focuses on meeting pointing goals and minimizing the need to desaturate the reaction wheel. The use of planning allows for intelligent use of the reaction wheel and accommodates time-changing goals and orbit-varying magnetic fields. Preliminary results show trajectories with fractional-degree-accuracy, as well as management of reaction wheel momentum and avoidance of stiction. We also compare to a magnetorquer-only planning-based control system and show better convergence and faster slews.

title: An Improved Johnson Bound for List-Decoding with Hints
abstract:
This paper studies when list-decodability guarantees for error-correcting codes of good distance can go beyond the classical Johnson radius and gives a corresponding efficient list-decoding algorithm for Reed-Solomon codes up to this new radius. The Johnson bound shows that any error-correcting code with distance $δ$ is automatically list-decodable with small list size up to a certain radius $J(δ)$ around any received word $r$. We show that if the received word $r$ is known to have some codewords that are somewhat close to it (we call these ``hints"), then $C$ is list-decodable with small list size up to an even larger radius around $r$.
  We determine the optimal list-decoding radius in this setting for single and multiple hints over both large and small alphabets and show that this radius is the optimum of a natural convex program. Remarkably, even a single hint that is $(J(δ)-ε)$-close to $r$ improves the list-decoding radius around $r$ to $J(δ)+ε'$.
  Finally, we give an efficient algorithm, based on the weighted Guruswami-Sudan decoder, that list-decodes Reed-Solomon codes up to this optimal radius.

title: Regularizing the Navier-Stokes Equations via Additive Type Noise plus Small Linear Multiplicative Noise
abstract: We derive a series of ``regularization by noise in high probability" results for incompressible Navier-Stokes equations $(d\geq3)$, via a new mechanism based on fixed point argument: For initial values in critical Besov space $\dot{B}_{q,\infty}^{-1+d/q}~ (1\leq q<\infty)$, we can expect unique global solutions with $C_{w^*,loc}\big([0,\infty);\dot{B}_{q,\infty}^{-1+d/q}\big)$-paths in high probability if the equations are perturbed by well-constructed additive type noise; for initial values in the ``end-point space" $\dot{B}_{\infty,\infty}^{-1}$ where the equations are locally ill-posed in deterministic setting \cite{BP08}, we can still expect unique solutions on $[0,T]$ (with ``modified" $*$-weak continuous paths) in high probability for large enough $T>0$, if the equations are perturbed by a well-constructed additive type noise plus a ``small" linear multiplicative noise. This means that the regularizing effect can be strengthen by small additional linear multiplicative noise in the sense that the Picard iteration remains effective for values in the largest critical space $\dot{B}_{\infty,\infty}^{-1}$. This work has nothing to do with AI models.

title: Inexact PDHG for Large-Scale Semidefinite Programming
abstract: First-order methods, such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method, have recently been explored for large-scale semidefinite programming (SDP). However, exact projections can be computationally prohibitive, motivating inexact projections using conditional gradient methods. Although computationally cheap and projection-free, these methods typically converge sublinearly. Recent variants, such as Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe (Garber, 2026), achieve linear convergence in expectation near the optimal face of the spectrahedron. We develop an inexact PDHG framework with tractable spectrahedral projections using two techniques: (i) adaptive error tolerances that avoid unnecessary inner iterations while guaranteeing convergence, and (ii) a heuristic spectral warm start based on the Lanczos algorithm that accelerates Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe by initializing near the optimal face. We establish an O(1/t) convergence rate for PDHG in the presence of projection errors and estimate the total number of inner iterations required for convergence. Experiments on large-scale SDP instances demonstrate that combining spectral warm starts with Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe outperforms Lanczos-based inexact projections.

title: Nonlinear springs with orbits in radicals: a solvability criterion
abstract: An odd polynomial oscillator has a periodic orbit given by a quadrature. When the zeros of the energy polynomial are all simple or all of even multiplicity, that quadrature is elementary exactly when the polynomial is a perfect square, and the time is a sum of inverse tangents. Recovering the displacement inverts that relation, algebraic when their coefficients are commensurate, making a closed form a Galois question. This paper identifies the group as the monodromy group of a rational map, computes its branch data from the parameters, and shows the branch value at the phase-angle singularity never vanishes, so every decomposition pairs the amplitudes reciprocally. In the commensurate family with distinct real factors, the orbit is radical exactly when the primitive inversion degree is at most four, or when reciprocal pairs leave a reduced spring of that degree. Radical orbits occur at the fifth, ninth, thirteenth and seventeenth force orders, the last only for reciprocal members, an expression recorded for each. The multiplicity hypothesis cannot be dropped. Factoring the energy polynomial into square and squarefree parts turns the quadrature into a differential of the third kind on a hyperelliptic curve, where elementarity is a torsion condition on the divisor of its poles with a vanishing holomorphic remainder. The first nonsquare elementary member appears at the ninth force order, and the power pullback inverts in closed form at every such order, giving a radical orbit for a confining spring of arbitrarily high degree with a sufficient condition for positive coefficients.

title: The NWU ageing property of the gamma-gamma distribution
abstract: Baricz et al. [BPV2011] posed the question of whether the $K$-distribution (or gamma-gamma distribution) satisfies the ageing property known as the new is better than used (NBU) property. In this paper we address this question by establishing that, under certain parameter conditions, the gamma-gamma distribution satisfies the new is worse than used (NWU) property rather than the NBU property. For the remaining parameter ranges, we show that the gamma-gamma distribution is neither NBU nor NWU. The proofs rely on tools from the theory of stochastic orders of random variables. Moreover, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the $K$-distribution is actually the product of two independent gamma random variables, we obtain alternative proofs of our results. Similarly, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the beta-prime distribution is actually the quotient of two independent gamma random variables, we establish analogous NBU/NWU properties for this distribution. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the product of two independent positive random variables possesses the NWU and decreasing failure rate (DFR) properties. On the other hand, we show that the survival function of the $K$-distribution is hyperbolically completely monotone by representing it as the Laplace transform of a random variable belonging to the class of generalized gamma convolutions. As a consequence, we establish some monotonicity properties of the Mills ratio and hazard rate function of the $K$-distribution. These results provide further insight into the ageing and monotonicity properties of the gamma-gamma distribution. In addition, we derive a new integral representation and two new series representations, as well as bounds, for the survival function of the $K$-distribution.

title: A short proof of the universality of the fundamental shadow links
abstract: We give a constructive three-dimensional proof of Costantino and Thurston's universality theorem for fundamental shadow links. More precisely, every compact connected oriented three-manifold with empty or toroidal boundary can be obtained by integral Dehn filling along a subset of the boundary components of a fundamental shadow link exterior.

title: Spine extremality and its frequency in critical branching random walks
abstract: We study the generations at which the distinguished spine of a critical branching random walk occupies the spatial minimum. Under finite positive offspring variance and any nonconstant law of independent real edge increments, their number up to generation $N$ is $(\log N)^{1+o(1)}$ almost surely and has order $\log N$ in probability, with ties included. The same conclusions hold for the unique-minimum event. No spatial moment assumption is needed. The proof combines counting estimates from the spine decomposition with uniform control of extremal multiplicity in an ordinary surviving tree. For a selected minimizer, its one-time probability is the ordinary survival probability $q_n$, and recurrence is equivalent to $\sum_nq_n=\infty$. We also exhibit a critical infinite-variance offspring family for which the weak-minimum event occurs only finitely often, for every nonconstant increment law. We determine the polynomial order of its last occurrence and, for Gaussian or Laplace increments, prove quantitative eventual separation of the spine from the minimum. The sharp frequency constant and limiting distribution in the nonconstant finite-variance model remain undetermined.

title: Explicit matrix hitting points for noncommutative algebraic branching programs
abstract:
We give a deterministic polynomial-resource black-box identity test for noncommutative algebraic branching programs (ABPs), using ordinary matrix evaluations of the output polynomial. Given an alphabet of size $m\ge1$ and an ABP vertex bound $S\ge1$, we construct one fixed tuple of integer matrices of order $R=(m+2)d(d+1)/2$, where $d=(m+2)S$, with entry bit length $O(d\log(d+1))$. Every nonzero polynomial computed by an ABP with at most $S$ vertices has a nonzero evaluation at this tuple. The construction accesses neither the hidden ABP nor its intermediate gates. A rectangular variant improves the order to $O(m^{3/2}S^2)$. Matrix order, description length, and all returned entries are counted; the total resources are polynomial. The result holds in characteristic zero and in characteristic $p>\binom d2$.
  The main ingredient is a fixed polynomial frame spanning the joint cyclic module of every matrix tuple from every prescribed vector. A compensating block makes a tagged encoding nilpotent of index at most three, while preserving the original cyclic module. A differential exterior-vector argument then gives a single triangular recurrence with polynomially many outputs. Its shared left-linear circuit is converted into actual integer query matrices by coefficient duality. Two-sided pairing further gives deterministic nonadaptive reconstruction of an equivalent ABP from polynomially many output-only matrix queries. The same frame gives polynomial-cardinality explicit trace separators for simultaneous-conjugation orbit closures, and a fixed nilpotent substitution for bounded-dimensional recognizable series. The latter also tests rational formulas whose given syntax is defined at the scalar origin. We provide complete proofs, construction costs, and exact implementation checks.

title: On End-Semidualizing Modules
abstract: We introduce and study the notion of End-semidualizing modules which are generalizations of semidualizing modules in the classical sense, and also extend the notion of $S-R$ semidualizing bimodules studied by Holm-White and Wakamatsu. By constrast with these notions, End-semidualizing modules exist abundantly.
