We characterize these modules by the inclusion of projective and flat modules in their Auslander class, or injective modules in their Bass class, and give criteria for when these Foxby classes satisfy the two-out-of-three property. Over commutative Noetherian rings, we prove base-change and duality results, and characterize local depth inequalities by the inclusion of all modules of finite flat or injective dimension in the corresponding classes.

title: Diffraction of rotated measures
abstract: Consider a translation-bounded measure on the line. We can rotate the measure, distributing the mass proportionally to the area, to create a two-dimensional rotationally invariant translation-bounded measure. We show that the diffraction of the two-dimensional object is the normalised rotation of the diffraction of the original measure. We discuss some examples and generalisation beyond $d=2$.

title: Novel properties of polynomials
abstract: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a complex polynomial to have a prescribed multiset of roots, expressed in terms of its coefficients and complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials. These conditions extend the classical Vieta formulas and yield explicit formulas for the coefficients of the corresponding quotient. We apply our results to obtain characterizations of Kronecker polynomials through identities involving symmetric polynomials and construct Borwein multiples of products of cyclotomic polynomials.

title: On the convexity of the fundamental domain of binary cyclotomic forms
abstract: Denote by $Φ_m(X,Y)\in\Z[X,Y]$, $m\geqslant 1$ the sequence of binary cyclotomic forms, so that $Φ_m(T,1)\in\Z[T]$, $m\geqslant 1$ is the sequence of cyclotomic polynomials. We prove that, for $m\geqslant 3$, the fundamental domain $ \cal{O}_m:= \{ (x,y)\in\R^2\; \mid \; Φ_m(x,y)\leqslant 1\} $ of $Φ_m$ is a convex subset of $\R^2$ if and only if $m$ is equal to $p$, $2p$ or $2^k$ with $p$ an odd prime and $k\geqslant 2$. Finally we investigate the convexity of the fundamental domains attached to some products of binary forms $Φ_m$.

title: Nijenhuis Lie $n$-algebras
abstract:
We introduce a homotopical framework for Nijenhuis operators on semistrict Lie $n$-algebras ($n$-term $L_\infty$-algebras) for every $n \ge 1$ and, more generally, on arbitrary $L_\infty$-algebras. A Nijenhuis operator is defined as a family $N = (N_q)_{q \ge 1}$ of multilinear maps, with $N_1$ linear, realizing an $L_\infty$-morphism from an $N$-twisted copy of the structure to the original one. We prove that this condition is equivalent to the vanishing, at every arity $m$, of the $m$-th Nijenhuis torsion up to a correction term $Λ^N_m$ formed by higher-component substitutions, and we provide a closed combinatorial formula for $Λ^N_m$ as a sum over set partitions. Along the way, we show that the arity-$k$ Nijenhuis torsion factors canonically as a composite of $k$ commuting elementary slot deformations.
  The resulting objects form a category $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$; we establish that $\mathbf{NijLie}_m$ embeds as the full subcategory of $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$ on objects concentrated in the bottom
  $m$ degrees for all $m \le n$. These levels assemble into a tower whose first three stages are classical Nijenhuis Lie algebras, the Nijenhuis Lie $2$-algebras of Das, and the newly introduced Nijenhuis Lie $3$-algebras. We characterize the strict and skeletal objects at every level, introduce $n$-term representations up to homotopy of a Nijenhuis Lie algebra,
  and prove that the semidirect product construction establishes an equivalence between the category of such representations and split abelian $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$-extensions.
  Finally, two corrections to published level-three identities are documented, and all component identities up to arity five are verified via computer algebra.

title: Residual-based Adaptive Refinement of hp-Variational PINNs for elliptic PDEs with geometric singularities and localized features
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks approximate the solution of boundary value problems by minimizing the strong-form residual, their accuracy is often limited near corner and crack singularities, sharp layers and localized features and the enforcement of Neumann boundary conditions remains challenging. In hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks, the problem is formulated in a Petrov-Galerkin weak form, reducing the differentiation order applied to the neural network, while boundary constraints are imposed through penalty terms. The variational residual is evaluated using fixed Gauss quadrature points and the strong-form residual on a fixed collocation set, which may fail to capture regions of rapid variation. To address this issue, we integrate hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Residual-based Adaptive Refinement. During training, the strong-form residual is computed on a dense candidate pool and points with the largest residuals are added adaptively to the collocation set. Since the weak formulation is defined in $H^{1}(Ω)$, it avoids the $H^{2}(Ω)$ regularity requirement that fails on cracked and non-convex domains. The proposed method is validated on four two-dimensional elliptic problems and consistently achieves substantial reductions in relative $L^{2}$, absolute $L^{\infty}$ and relative $H^{1}$ semi-norm errors through adaptive residual-driven point placement.

title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
abstract: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact Kähler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-Kähler nature of this notion. We also investigate different techniques for constructing examples of such manifolds. Finally, we examine the relationship between Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity and Kobayashi hyperbolicity in the examples considered, highlighting obstructions to the latter in the Calabi--Yau setting.

title: Spectral unions of four intervals tile the real line
abstract: We prove that every spectral union of four bounded intervals tiles the real line by translations. The argument combines periodicity of spectra, cofactor identities for the secular determinant, and a common tiling complement for the finite spectral fibers. We also establish a rigidity theorem for six complex numbers with prescribed vanishing power sums.

title: Federated Learning for Semantic Communications over Multiple Access Channels
abstract: This paper presents a federated learning (FL) framework for semantic communication (SemCom) over the multiple access channel (MAC), where multiple distributed transmitters simultaneously convey semantic information to a common receiver using end-to-end learned semantic representations. Semantic feature extraction, compression, wireless transmission, and semantic inference are jointly optimized through FL-based SemCom. Unlike conventional SemCom systems that train users independently, simultaneous semantic transmissions over the MAC enable concurrent training of multiple transmitters within the same transmission interval, thereby reducing training overhead and channel usage. Federated semantic aggregation is incorporated with shared and personalized encoder components, allowing transmitters with limited local training data to benefit from semantic representations learned from transmitters possessing larger datasets while preserving local adaptation. Evaluated using the CIFAR-10 dataset over fading channels, the proposed approach maintains high semantic inference accuracy under shared wireless access and significantly improves performance under severe data imbalance. In the meantime, simultaneous semantic transmissions can significantly reduce training overhead while preserving robust semantic performance across distributed transmitters with heterogeneous local datasets. These results highlight the potential of combining FL and SemCom to support scalable and communication-efficient edge intelligence in future wireless networks.

title: Symmetric List Objects
abstract: Cons-lists are fundamental to functional programming, and are well-understood as initial algebras, and as a concrete construction of free monoids. In category theory, such list objects can be axiomatised internal to any monoidal category, with nil and cons maps, and a recursion mechanism. When strengthened to support parametrised recursion, they can be shown to give the free monoid construction. We study a small variant on parametrised list objects called parametrised symmetric list objects, in a symmetric monoidal category, where the two frontmost elements are allowed to be permuted. We show that this gives a construction of free commutative monoids, and develop some related theory.

title: An $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling inequality in every dimension
abstract:
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\geq2$) be measurable with $0<|Ω|<\infty$, and let $u_Ω$ be its logarithmic potential ($N=2$) or Newtonian potential ($N\geq3$), normalized so that $Δu_Ω=χ_Ω$. We prove the sharp inequality \[
  \int_Ω|\nabla u_Ω|^2\,\mathrm{d} x
  \leq\frac{1}{2Nω_{N-1}}
  \iint_{Ω\timesΩ}\frac{\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y}{|x-y|^{N-2}}, \] where $ω_{N-1}=|\mathbb{S}^{N-1}|$, with equality if and only if $Ω$ is a ball up to a null set. In dimension two this settles the $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling conjecture of Fleeman and Khavinson. For $N\ge3$ it is equivalent to the scale-free bound that at most the fraction $(N-2)/(2N)$ of the total field energy lies inside $Ω$. We also obtain an explicit deficit identity, a sharp extension to bounded nonnegative densities, and consequences for torsional rigidity, Bergman analytic content, Brownian motion, and aggregation equations.

title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Structure of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
abstract:
We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups: for prime-power cyclic group equivariant, classes are represented by compatible vertex arrays or by edge arrays. In these coordinates we compute products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Then we assemble the results into arbitrary finite cyclic group equivariant case.
  Besides the computation, we also develop the Tate compression theory, which is used in the computation. The Tate compression diagram cut an equivariant spectra into several layer, which the homotopy group can be describe directly by each layers. From it we also give a filtration for $π_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}})$, compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

title: A complete classification of minimal value set polynomials
abstract: We give a complete classification of minimal value set polynomials (MVSPs), settling a problem introduced by Carlitz, Lewis, Mills and Straus in 1961. For MVSPs $F \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ with more than two values, earlier work showed that their value sets $\left\{F(a): a \in \mathbb{F}_q\right\}$ can be reduced to the form $\mathcal U^v=\{u^v:u\in \mathcal U\}$, where $\mathcal U$ is a vector space over a subfield of $\mathbb F_q$, and $v\geq 1$ is a suitable integer. This classification proceeds through two parallel constructions, according to whether $\mathcal U$ is itself a field or not, governed respectively by the cyclic multiplicative structure and by the additive linearized structure. In both cases, Hasse derivatives impose constraints on the root multiplicities of a distinguished factor of $F$, leading to a factorization that preserves the underlying structure in a polynomial of smaller degree and thus allows the argument to be iterated.

title: Wasserstein Bounds for Euler and Randomized Midpoint Langevin Sampling with Noisy Gradients
abstract: Stochastic-gradient Langevin methods are sampling algorithms that replace the gradient of the log probability density by a noisy, possibly biased evaluation. We study how such gradient-evaluation errors affect the Euler and randomized midpoint discretizations of Langevin dynamics by comparing each noisy chain with its exact-gradient counterpart. For continuously differentiable, strongly log-concave targets with globally Lipschitz gradients, we derive comparison bounds under a sub-Gaussian condition on the gradient noise. The resulting 2-Wasserstein bounds hold uniformly over iterations, and are linear in both the step size and the $L^2$ norm of the evaluation bias, with a square-root dependence on dimensionality. To the best of our knowledge, no comparable 2-Wasserstein bounds have previously been established for randomized midpoint with noisy gradients. For Euler, our results complement recent Wasserstein bounds by allowing biased evaluations, and by not requiring additional regularity assumptions on the evaluation errors.

title: Ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras
abstract: We construct ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras, generalizing the well-known binary case. These new structures are defined in terms of nonsymmetric operads. We construct these new operads using ternary operations defined in terms of ternary Rota-Baxter operators. The relations defining these operads lie in the quadratic subspace of the kernel of a rewriting morphism from a free operad to the operad generated by one associative ternary operation and one (or two commuting) unary operators satisfying the ternary Rota-Baxter relation(s). We use computational algebra to compute a basis for the quadratic component of the kernel and thereby obtain the quadratic relations which define these new operads. In the dendriform case, we obtain 3 operations satisfying 10 relations. In the quadri-algebra case, we obtain 9 operations satisfying 50 relations. The latter computations combine modular and rational arithmetic, but we are able to provide certificates of the results which can be verified in characteristic 0.

title: Finite algebras whose equational probability spectrum contains a big gap
abstract:
We classify the finite algebras $\mathbf{A}$ for which there is no value $p$ satisfying $\frac{1}{|A|}<p<1$ in the equational probability spectrum of $\mathbf{A}$. We will use the classification to determine which finite algebras have minimal equational probability spectrum.
  In our final section, we explore the relationship, for finite algebras, between the properties of (i)~having a finite equational probability spectrum and (ii)~being an abelian algebra.

title: Homotopy types and torsion in homology of generalized chessboard complexes
abstract: Multiple chessboard complexes are deleted joins of skeleta of a simplex. We classify their homotopy types for at most three rows and extend this classification to arbitrary column capacities, with the $2$-torus as the only exception to a wedge of spheres. We determine explicit homotopy decompositions for two families with four and five rows and use a common capacity redistribution map to construct infinite families with $2$- and $3$-torsion in integral homology. Together, these results give a negative answer to the Segre part of the problem posed by Reiner and Roberts on characteristic-free resolutions of Segre and Veronese modules and identify three as the largest number of rows for which all generalized chessboard complexes have torsion-free integral homology. Our $3$-torsion construction applies to every square ordinary chessboard complex with at least five rows. Combined with earlier results, it completes the proof of the Shareshian-Wachs conjecture on torsion in chessboard complexes.

title: Quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products
abstract: We provide obstructions to the existence of quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products of trees, hyperbolic spaces, and other right-angled Artin groups.

title: Exact Solution of the $(2+1)$-Dimensional Dunkl-Klein-Gordon Oscillator with a Uniform Magnetic Field in Non-Commutative Phase Space
abstract: We solve the Klein-Gordon oscillator in a non-commutative phase space, generalized using Dunkl derivatives, both with and without interaction with a uniform magnetic field. For each of these cases, we begin by introducing the Dunkl derivative into the standard commutative phase space to evaluate the reflection parity symmetries. Then, using the Seiberg-Witten map, we extend the generalized system to a non-commutative phase space. In both cases, we determine the eigenfunctions and the energy spectrum exactly (which correspond to generalized Landau levels when a magnetic field is present). Furthermore, we compute the non-relativistic limit of the system and graphically analyze the behavior of the energy spectra. Our results demonstrate that the combination of the Dunkl deformation parameters, the non-commutative phase space geometry, and the magnetic field produces a parity-dependent modification of the energy levels. Finally, we verify that when the external magnetic field or the non-commutative parameters vanish, our exact solutions correctly reduce to the commutative Dunkl models established in previous works.

title: Asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$
abstract: We study the asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ of stable pointed curves and the all-light Hassett spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0|n}$, for fixed genus $g\ge1$ as the number of markings tends to infinity. We prove central limit theorems for the full Betti distributions, whose variances grow linearly in $n$ with leading coefficients independent of the genus. For the normalized even Betti numbers, we establish refined local limit theorems with estimates uniform in degree. These local estimates yield asymptotic formulas for individual even Betti numbers and determine the sharp central ultra-log-concavity thresholds $\frac{3(e-2)}{2(3-e)}$ and $3$, respectively. For $g\ge2$, the off-diagonal Hodge components form proportions of exact orders $n^{-1/2}$ and $n^{-1}$ of the total cohomology of the two spaces, respectively. The conditional distributions of the Hodge difference $p-q$ given $p\ne q$ converge, for both spaces, to a single discrete law independent of the genus. We also prove that tautological classes account for all but a proportion of exact order $n^{-1}$ of the even cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$. The tautological degree distribution converges to the standard Gaussian under the centering and scaling of the ambient even Betti distribution. An explicit asymptotic formula for the ratio of the ordinary Euler characteristics of the light and heavy spaces answers a question of Kannan, Serpente and Yun. The proofs combine the heavy/light substitution with a stratification of the light spaces by stable cores, singularity analysis of Hodge generating functions, and refined Fourier estimates exploiting Poincaré duality.

title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
abstract: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting Kähler-Ricci solitons. It recovers the usual Miyaoka-Yau inequality in the Kähler-Einstein case. Our proof uses weighted equivariant Bogomolov-Gieseker and Langer inequalities for torsion-free sheaves, together with a weighted slope estimate for the canonical extension sheaf. We also construct toric examples showing that the existence of a soliton implies neither weighted semistability of the canonical extension sheaf nor nonnegativity of the equivariant Miyaoka-Yau number.

title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
abstract: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.

title: From gauge-covariant Noether invariants to electromagnetic velocity-dependent mechanics
abstract: For a charged particle, a spacetime symmetry need preserve the electromagnetic potential only up to a gauge transformation. Starting from the standard Noether--Bessel-Hagen construction, we make explicit the reduction from the relativistic gauge-invariant worldline charge to the generalized constants of nonrelativistic velocity-dependent mechanics, retaining the quasi-invariance boundary term throughout. With the convention $S_p=-mc\int ds+q\int A$, the canonical worldline one-form is $P=-m u^\flat+qA$, and a Killing vector satisfying $\mathcal L_XA=dχ_X$ generates $C_X=P(X)-qχ_X$. Its low-velocity limit is the Noether--Bessel-Hagen charge of the coordinate-time Lagrangian, from which generalized linear momentum, angular momentum and energy follow generator by generator. A uniform magnetic field gives an elementary gauge-dependent representative but gauge-invariant translational charge. The Darwin interaction then supplies the conservative $O(c^{-2})$ many-particle realization after field elimination, while a closed particle--field system is governed by the total stress-energy Killing charge. The result is an explicit reduction map linking three established descriptions without identifying their distinct conserved quantities.

title: A curve of genus $2$ over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and hexads of bitangents to a smooth quartic
abstract: In this paper we study the Abel-Jacobi map of a genus 2 curve over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ arising from a double cover of $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ branched along six lines. We utilize the so-called Mumford representations to conduct the calculations. As an application, we give an alternative proof of classical results on quartics and bitangents. Furthermore, we obtain a method to give explicit defining equations of quartic curves that have the six lines as bitangents and apply it to determine the number of connected components of the realization space.

title: On the Hodge Extension of Local Kähler Forms
abstract: Let $X$ be a Stein manifold, and let $K=\{h\le0\}$ be a compact sublevel set of a strictly plurisubharmonic function $h$ defined near $K$. It is known that $K$ is meromorphically convex in $X$ if and only if $dd^ch$ extends to a Hodge form on $X$. We show that if $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)$ is the direct sum of a free abelian group and a torsion group, for example if it is finitely generated, then any extension of $dd^ch$ to a Kähler form on $X$ can be modified, after replacing $h$ by a positive multiple, into a Hodge form. Thus meromorphic convexity of $K$ is equivalent to the extendability of $dd^ch$ as a Kähler form. We also show that the topological assumption cannot be dropped: we construct a Stein manifold $X$ of dimension $6$ with $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Q$, a sublevel set $K$ as above that is not meromorphically convex although $dd^ch$ extends to a Kähler form, and a totally real torus in $K$ that is isotropic for a Kähler form but is not meromorphically convex. This shows that the Hodge condition in Guedj's characterization of meromorphically convex totally real submanifolds cannot be weakened to a Kähler condition, and gives counterexamples to two criteria stated by Cieliebak and Eliashberg.

title: A Kohnen-Zagier Formula in Level 1
abstract: In 1985 Kohnen used the Shimura correspondence to prove a general formula relating the coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms of level $ 4N $ transforming with respect to the theta multiplier to central values of $ L $-functions for twists of newforms of level $ N $. This generalized previous work with Zagier. In this paper, we prove a Kohnen-Zagier type formula using Yang's Shimura correspondence for powers of the eta multiplier in level $ 1 $, relating the coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms to central values of $ L $-functions for twists of newforms of level $ 6 $. To do so we develop some of the theory of modular forms transforming with respect to powers of the eta multiplier and introduce Shintani lifts of level $ 6 $, with Fourier coefficients given in terms of cycle integrals.

title: Homogenization of degenerate parabolic equations with nonlinear Robin reactions in perforated domains
abstract: We study periodic homogenization of a parabolic equation with linear, degenerate bulk terms in a perforated domain, with a monotone nonlinear Robin reaction of order $\varepsilon$ on the pore walls. The storage coefficient may vanish on sets of positive measure, and the diagonal diffusion weights are not bounded below but satisfy an inverse-integrability condition. Under positivity of the mean storage, a quantitative cell-detection estimate yields strong compactness of the states and of the scaled traces. The effective equation has positive storage, a positive-definite diffusion matrix given by a weighted cell problem, and a nonlinear volume reaction obtained by averaging over the pore surface. We also prove a strong weighted-gradient corrector and uniform-in-time convergence of the dissipated and stored energies and of the states in the storage-weighted $L^2$ norm.

title: Tight Stationarity Transfer and Repeatability for Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods
abstract: Proximal-gradient methods are widely used for composite optimization, but inexact proximal updates introduce a residual in the proximal optimality condition, complicating the analysis of how stationarity changes across a step. We study this question for composite objectives consisting of a smooth convex term and a possibly nonsmooth weakly convex term, focusing on the relationship between the directional-stationarity measures at the input and output points of an inexact proximal-gradient step. We first establish separate input and output bounds, but their combination can yield a conservative estimate because their worst-case residual directions may differ. By exploiting the magnitude and orientation of this shared residual, we establish tight joint bounds and derive an exact one-step stationarity-transfer factor that strictly improves the estimate from separate bounds in the short-step regime. We also identify the precise residual-tolerance threshold for finite uniform stationarity transfer. A further distinction emerges over multiple steps: endpoint worst cases can repeat over arbitrarily many iterations, whereas interior worst cases cannot persist across two consecutive steps, yielding strict two-step submultiplicativity. These results also provide principled tolerance-selection rules, descent estimates, and stationarity-complexity guarantees for inexact proximal-gradient methods.

title: Exact Second-Order Asymptotics for the Gaussian Gray--Wyner Problem
abstract: We revisit the Gray-Wyner problem of lossy compression of bivariate Gaussian sources under the quadratic distortion measure and derive the exact second-order asymptotics. Specifically, we first identify the boundary rate tuples using the explicit first-order asymptotics by Yu (TIT 2023) and then characterize the tradeoff among three second-order coding rates subject to a constraint on the joint excess-distortion probability. Our main contribution is the achievability proof, where we derive a covariance shell covering lemma that is analogous to the type covering lemma for the discrete case. In particular, our covering lemma classifies the source sequences into power shell types via their empirical covariance matrix. For each such power shell type, we derive sufficient conditions on the compression rates so that covering within distortion levels are achievable. Finally, asymptotical analysis via the Berry-Esseen theorem yields the desired result.

title: A lattice order on the complex field
abstract: Birkhoff and Pierce asked in 1956 whether the field $\mathbb{C}$ of complex numbers admits a lattice order compatible with addition and multiplication. We answer the question affirmatively. Using a valuation with value group $\mathbb{Q}$, we construct a positive cone $P$ by a transfinite recursion of countable ordinal length. At each stage we extend a lattice order on a subspace while preserving its lattice operations in the whole field and maintaining multiplicative closure of the ambient positive cone. These subspaces eventually exhaust $\mathbb{C}$. The construction depends on choices of a valuation extension, compatible rational powers and vector-space bases. The cone $P$ contains $1$ and satisfies $\{x\in P\setminus\{0\}:x^{-1}\in P\}=\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$. The induced order is not total: $i$ is incomparable with $0$. For a chosen transcendental element $t$ and $i^2=-1$, one may prescribe $0\vee i=(t+i)/2$ and $0\vee(-i)=(t-i)/2$. Varying the first extension yields exactly $2^{\mathbf c}$ distinct lattice positive cones on $\mathbb{C}$, where $\mathbf c=|\mathbb{C}|$. The count concerns cones as subsets of $\mathbb{C}$.

title: Moments propagation in the Vlasov equation and application to the Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
abstract: In this paper, we study how the propagation of particle moments depends on the fluid velocity in the Vlasov equation. We present some new moment estimates involving the velocity in this equation. As an application, we establish Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin-type regularity criteria involving only the velocity field for weak solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes-Vlasov system.

title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract:
Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately
  $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.

title: Endpoint estimates for spherical maximal operators acting on radial functions in hyperbolic spaces
Curvature-Dimension Conditions Along Discrete Refinement Sequences
abstract: We introduce the sequence curvature--dimension condition $SCD(K,N)$ for complete refinement systems of finite metric probability spaces. The condition couples a transport action bound with entropy comparisons along a single probability section through the prescribed refinement layers. Within a bounded comparison range, we prove that midpoint comparisons on three consecutive layers characterize the condition on every fixed finite segment. If, in addition, the refinement sequence converges in the measured sense in its intrinsic bridge realization, then $SCD(K,N)$ is equivalent both to the vanishing of single-layer midpoint defects and to the entropic curvature--dimension condition $CD^{e}(K,N)$ of the limit. In the reverse direction, a $CD^{e}(K,N)$ bound on the limit yields quantitative recovery estimates that identify shrinking transport scales on which finite layers retain its second-order curvature comparison. These estimates are uniform over endpoint measures and include Dirac masses. Examples illustrate the effects of the refinement rule, the layer metrics and the reference measures.

title: On loop-soup clusters in three dimensions and higher
abstract:
We study clusters of the Brownian loop soup on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and of random walk and metric-graph loop soups on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ within a unified framework. For the continuum model, when the one-arm exponent $ξ(α)$ is positive, we prove that almost surely every cluster has Hausdorff dimension $3-ξ(α)$. A key step is to show that, conditioned on the one-arm event, a crossing cluster has capacity comparable to the crossing scale with uniformly positive probability. This gives one-arm estimates of order $αr^{-ξ(α)}$, uniformly down to zero intensity, and shows that $ξ(α)$ is strictly decreasing and left-continuous. Moreover, $1-ξ(α)\asympα$ as $α\downarrow0$. As another application of the one-arm estimates, we prove that several critical values coincide, resolving a conjecture of Jego and Lupu in arXiv:2601.04840.
  The proof combines a decoupling technique with a multiscale recursive argument to control the combined effects of large and small loops. These methods also extend to loop soups on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ for $d=3,4,5$, yielding capacity lower bounds of order $r$, $r^2/\log r$, and $r^2$ for the cluster of the origin, conditioned on the one-arm event, throughout the small-loop decay regime. In particular, these bounds imply strict polynomial comparisons between one-arm probabilities at different intensities in dimension three. We also show that the small-loop decay regime on $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ has upper endpoint $\frac{1}{2}$ by adapting the OSSS sharpness framework to the truncated loop soup.

title: Low-regularity global well-posedness for the defocusing cubic wave equation outside a ball with radial initial data
abstract: We study the three-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear wave equation with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition in the exterior of the unit ball, $Ω=\R^3\backslash\overline{B(0,1)}$, for radial initial data. For every $\frac12\leq s\leq\frac34$, we establish global well-posedness in $\dot H^s_{D,rad}(Ω)\times\dot H^{s-1}_{D,rad}(Ω)$, including the critical endpoint $s=\frac12$, without an additional $L^4$ assumption on the initial displacement. The proof uses the distorted Fourier transform associated with the Dirichlet Laplacian to establish radial Sobolev embeddings, including the quantitative estimate $\|f\|_{L^p(Ω)}\leq C\sqrt p\,\|f\|_{\dot H_D^{1/2}(Ω)}$ for $4\leq p<\infty$, with $C$ independent of $p$. We combine a nonlinear Fourier truncation argument with the critical Strichartz estimate to construct a global nonlinear component with high-frequency-truncated initial data. For the remainder, we construct a local energy solution in an affine energy space and derive a logarithmic energy inequality that prevents finite-time energy blow-up. Persistence of the original Sobolev regularity, uniqueness, and local Lipschitz dependence on each finite time interval complete the proof.

title: Beyond Reachability: When Edit Order Preserves Couplings in Graph Flow Matching
abstract: Shortest-path optimality does not guarantee that a memoryless graph generator preserves a prescribed source-target correspondence. We study whether reordering legal shortest edits can retain this correspondence without changing the pairing, mandatory edits, or sampling budget. Under a common Poisson clock, we establish an exact criterion for endpoint coupling recoverability: the source-blind Markov projection attains the unavoidable clock-error floor if and only if routes to distinct targets do not share graph states. Routes to the same target may merge without sacrificing endpoint fidelity. This characterization leads to an exact finite-state routing formulation and a legality-preserving scheduling procedure with recovery certificates. A marker-free construction demonstrates how shared edge structure can retain source distinctions, while a capacity-constrained family exhibits a sharp separation in paired error between edit orders with identical marginal error. Finally, a target-conditioned aliasing bound connects structural route design to the terminal fidelity of a learned graph-only generator. These results characterize when legal edit ordering can preserve a prescribed coupling under fixed operational costs.

title: Hilbert functions of filtered graphical zonotopal algebras
abstract:
The external zonotopal algebra of a graph is generated by nilpotent vertex elements $X_v$ and determines the graphical matroid after deleting loops. Replacing these generators by $f(X_v)$, for a power series $f(u)$, and filtering by word length gives a family of filtered algebras. We extend filtered graph reconstruction from simple graphs to loopless multigraphs without isolated vertices when the linear and quadratic coefficients of $f$ are nonzero. Nevertheless, even the family of Hilbert functions indexed by all polynomials does not determine the graph: two nonisomorphic ten-vertex trees have the same Hilbert function for every $f$, answering a question of Nenashev and the first author. For forests and series whose first nonconstant term has degree $k\ge 2$, we give a monomial presentation indexed by partial score vectors whose entries are divisible by $k$.
  For normalized nondegenerate functions, a boundary-state calculus gives a common finite parameter partition for all trees of a fixed maximum degree. In maximum degrees three and four, exact symbolic calculations identify these partitions by the vanishing of specified coefficients of $f^{-1}$. For functions with nonzero quadratic coefficient, the same calculus gives explicit recurrences for attached or connecting paths. Symmetry reductions, including commuting actions of $sl_2$ and the symmetric group on the leaves of a star, determine the generic Hilbert series of stars and two-vertex multigraphs and also apply to parallel edges and leaves in larger graphs. For cycles, we determine the highest-degree term and the first three nonconstant coefficients in the stable range. A weighted independent-set formula describes the trace sequence in the remaining conjecture.

title: Stable Dynamical Mass Transportation via port-Hamiltonian Structure
abstract: Dynamical optimal mass transportation over nonlinear systems is often hindered by the curse of dimensionality and open-loop implementation. We propose an alternative framework that sacrifices exact optimality in favor of stability, robustness, and scalability. We use a stochastic port-Hamiltonian system as a reference model. Under suitable structural assumptions, we show that its density converges asymptotically to a prescribed steady-state distribution. We then shape a deterministic nonlinear system into a compatible port-Hamiltonian form and add a local density-feedback term so that its closed-loop continuity equation matches the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation of the reference model. The resulting feedback drives a broad class of initial distributions to the target distribution. Because the density term is local at the particle level, the controller admits decentralized implementation and avoids solving a global finite-horizon transport problem online. Nonlinear examples and simulations illustrate the method. For linear systems with Gaussian targets, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for stabilizing density feedback and give explicit controller constructions.

title: Sheaves on quoric manifolds
abstract: Quoric manifolds are quaternionic analogues of quasitoric manifolds introduced by Hopkinson. Given a quoric manifold over a simple polytope, we study the stratification induced by the faces of the polytope. We then show that the equivariant derived category of constructible sheaves with respect to the face stratification is equivalent to the derived category of constructible DG-modules over a DG-algebra defined on the orbit space. Finally, we prove that the associated DG-algebra is formal.

title: Davenport constants with growing binary rank
abstract: We study the correction to the standard lower bound $D^*$ for Davenport constants of finite abelian groups with a growing elementary two-component. For every fixed nontrivial abelian $p$-group $H$ of odd order, we prove $D(H\oplus C_2^r)=D^*(H\oplus C_2^r)+(D(H)-1)\log_2 r+O_H(1)$, with a uniform version for varying $H$. For $C_3\oplus C_2^r$, we determine exact values on explicit infinite intervals of ranks. More generally, the correction is logarithmic or smaller precisely when the fixed group has at most one odd prime divisor. We show that the two-primary part affects the logarithmic coefficient: for $C_{24}\oplus C_2^r$, the ratio $(D-D^*)/\log_2 r$ has limsup at least $2.4933231\ldots>2$, whereas for $C_3\oplus C_2^r$ the limit is $2$. These upper limiting coefficients are unbounded even with the odd prime fixed. The proofs use binary codes and finite-field Fourier analysis.

title: Backward Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
abstract: In this paper, we establish a new estimate on the time-derivative of pointed Nash entropy and use it to give a new proof of backward pseudolocality for Ricci flow. The proof does not rely on Bamler's compactness theorem and structure theory concerning limits of Ricci flows. Our methods also work for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature.

title: Using delays for prescribed-time static output feedback stabilization of LTI controllable and observable systems
abstract: This paper addresses a stabilization problem: can every controllable and observable LTI system be stabilized by static output feedback? To the best of our knowledge, we provide, for the first time, a solution to this problem. Furthermore, the proposed design achieves prescribed-time convergence to the origin, with the convergence time arbitrarily assigned a priori and independently of the initial condition. Two static output-feedback methods are developed. The first employs multiple artificial output delays with smooth time-varying gains and provides an explicit gain construction for every controllable and observable LTI system, based on a generalized controllability--observability Gramian introduced in this paper. The second combines constant-gain feedback of the current output with time-varying-gain feedback of a single artificially delayed output and also applies to every controllable and observable LTI system. Its simpler structure requires auxiliary parameters whose existence is guaranteed but whose explicit construction is not provided for general MIMO systems; for SISO systems, the constant current-output gain can be readily selected. The multiple-delay design is further extended to known bounded and fast-varying (without any constraints on the delay derivative) measurement delays, yielding fixed-time stabilization under a corresponding rank condition, with an assignable settling-time bound greater than three times the delay bound. For unknown constant measurement delays, fixed-time stabilization is established for systems with nilpotent state matrices. A numerical implementation is also presented. Numerical examples involving nonminimum-phase, flexible-structure, and cart--pole systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

title: Is Dual Polarization Always Optimal? Unlocking New Spatial Degrees of Freedom
abstract: Current wireless communication systems are designed based on channel models obtained under the assumption of far-field operation, where electromagnetic waves can be approximated by a planar wave. In those circumstances, dualpolarized antennas seem to be the optimal solution for maximizing the spectral efficiency. However, the recent research on XLMIMO systems represents a paradigm shift, since communication may take place in the near-field and an additional degree of freedom can be achieved. This work presents a modular, lowcost tripolarized antenna at 2.4 GHz band, that is used to experimentally validate theoretical findings about tripolarized antennas, which are commonly based on orthogonal infinitesimal dipoles. The evaluation is carried out in two indoor scenarios and one outdoor scenario, with transmitter comprising multiple tripolarized antennas and a receiver equipped with a single tripolarized antenna. We show that this type of antenna can increase the number of spatial streams up to three or extend the region where terminals are able to achieve two spatial streams

title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.

title: A logarithmic error term for subset sums of zero-sum-free sets
abstract: For a positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the minimum number of distinct nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum-free $k$-element set, where the minimum is taken over all finite abelian groups. We prove $f(k)\ge \frac{k^2}{2}-13k\log(k+1)-116k$. Together with the classical upper bound, this gives $f(k)=k^2/2+O(k\log k)$, with the optimal leading coefficient. As a consequence, the Olson constant of every finite abelian group $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ol}(G)\le\sqrt{2|G|}+O(\log|G|)$. The argument combines a triangular lower bound for repeated supports, a count using blocks of two and three copies, and a greedy expansion argument. No restriction is imposed on the order of the group or on the stabilizer of the set of subset sums.

title: An analogue of $Γ$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
abstract: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $Γ$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.

title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
abstract: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.

title: Asymptotic Formula of the Lifespan of Classical Solutions to 1D Quasilinear Wave Equations
abstract:
We study the lifespan \(T^*(\varepsilon)\) of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem
  for the one-dimensional quasilinear wave equation
  $u_{tt}-(c(u)^2u_x)_x=0$,
  with initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$.
  We assume that $c'(θ)\sim a|θ|^{p-2}$ as $θ\to 0$,
  where \(a>0\) and \(p>3\) or $p=2$.
  We obtain explicit asymptotic formulas for
  $T^*(\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.
  We treat both the case $ψ\in L^1(\mathbb R)$
  and the case
  $ψ=ψ_1+\Braket{x}^{-α}$,
  where \(ψ_1\in L^1(\mathbb R)\) and \(0<α\le1\).
  Our results identify the dependence of the lifespan scale on the decay exponent,
  including the borderline case $α=1$.
  The proof combines Riccati equations along characteristics
  with a scaling argument inspired by Lindblad.

title: On the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue Problem
abstract: The classical Blaschke-Lebesgue problem seeks the convex body of minimal volume among all convex bodies of prescribed constant width. In this paper, we investigate the necessary conditions for volume minimizers of the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem via the inverse Gauss map and the inverse Weingarten transformation. We first introduce a generalized support function for hypersurfaces induced by the inverse Gauss map, characterize the Wigner caustic of constant width bodies, and accordingly construct convex bodies of constant width from prescribed functions. Building upon there results and applying the Brunn-Minkowski inequality, we establish a high-dimensional necessary condition: for almost every antipodal pair of a volume minimizer, one point is non-regular; at the other point, the minimum principal curvatures equals the reciprocal of the constant width. As an application, we provide a new proof for the two-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue theorem. Furthermore, we study the dimension-raising construction of Lachand-Robert and Oudet, and prove that every convex body produced by this construction satisfies our necessary condition. Finally, we put forward a conjecture stating that the sequence obtained by iterating this construction starting from a line segment yields minimizers for the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem for all dimensions.

title: Geometry of $m$-direct-sum morphisms
abstract: Let $V$ be a complex vector space of dimension $mk$ ($m\ge2$). A morphism from a positive-dimensional projective variety $f\colon X\to\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$ is $m$-direct-sum if $V=U_{x_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus U_{x_m}$ for every $m$ pairwise distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_m$ on $X$, where $U_x\subset V$ is the subspace represented by $f(x)$. We show that $X$ is necessarily a smooth rational curve. When the so-called drill $d(f)$ of $f$ is $1$ or when the rank $k$ is at most $2$, we give complete classifications of $f$ up to the automorphisms of $\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$. As applications, we classify all so-called skew scrolls in $\mathbb{P}^3$, which completely answers a question of Day. Then we show that if $X\subset \mathbb{P}(V)$ is a smooth, projective, nondegenerate subvariety whose higher-order Terracini locus is empty, then $X$ is the rational normal curve, which strengthens the critical Terracini rigidity discovered by Ballico and Chiantini. By using the same machinery, we also prove a dual version of Terracini rigidity. Finally, we show that $m$-unisolvent systems form an abelian category of finite length and that $7$ is the least diagonal exponent of a simple rank-three $2$-unisolvent system.

title: Equal diffusions and zero Dirichlet boundary conditions can induce blow-up
abstract: For a class of systems of two parabolic equations with equal diffusion and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, we show the existence of finite time blow-up solutions, although the corresponding system of ODE's has only global, exponentially decaying solutions. Such a phenomenon of blow-up induced by equal diffusions, which originates in the works of Bebernes-Lacey [SIAM J. Math. Anal. 21 (1990), 1415--1425, and J. Differential Equations 95 (1992), 105--129] and Weinberger [J. Differ. Equations 154 (1999), 225--237], was previously known, for instance, in the case of homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, but it had remained an open question whether it can happen in the homogeneous Dirichlet case. The latter, which corresponds to an absorption or cooling of the system at the boundary, that is a priori more stabilizing, requires nontrivial new ideas. As another new feature, we show that this can happen even if the nonlinearity acts only on a compact sub-region, and our proof actually covers the Neumann and Cauchy, as well as Dirichlet problems in a unified way.

title: New explicit examples of Mannheim pair in $\mathbb{L}^3$
abstract: In this paper, we construct explicit examples of Mannheim pairs, in the classical sense, in Minkowski 3-space $\mathbb{L}^3$, one for each of the five types of such pairs. In our main examples the Mannheim curve is neither a helix nor a slant helix. For each example we give the complete Frenet apparatus of both curves of the pair and their Cartesian coordinates in terms of elementary functions. The construction writes the tangent indicatrix in angular coordinates and uses a suitable auxiliary angle function, which reduces all the relevant integrals to elementary form; it is carried out both starting from the Mannheim curve and starting from its partner. In these coordinates, we also characterize the helices and the slant helices with timelike axis. We also prove, for the five types, that a Mannheim curve is a slant helix if and only if its partner is a helix, and we give an explicit example of such a pair.

title: High-dimensional two-sample testing: From optimal transport to optimal derangements
abstract: In recent years, optimal transport has emerged as a useful framework for constructing distribution-free multivariate two-sample tests by transporting observations to a reference distribution under a suitable transportation cost. However, existing optimal transport-based tests can perform poorly in high dimension, low sample size (HDLSS) settings, and their performance depends critically on the choice of the reference distribution and transportation cost. We investigate this phenomenon and show that suitable choices can substantially improve their performance. Motivated by this analysis, we introduce a class of two-sample tests based on optimal derangements that do not require an external reference distribution. The minimum distance pairing test of Rosenbaum arises as a special case when the optimization is restricted to a subclass of derangements, thereby revealing a connection between this method and optimal transport. We propose the optimal derangement (ODER) test and its distribution-free variant, the ODER-SHC test, obtained by restricting the minimization to derangements consisting of a single Hamiltonian cycle. We establish their consistency under both HDLSS and classical large-sample asymptotic regimes. We also develop corresponding procedures based on the $L1$ distance and establish their high-dimensional consistency under conditions involving coordinate-wise energy distances. These $L1$ distance based tests can also discriminate between two high-dimensional distributions with identical first two moments but different marginal distributions. Analyses of benchmark datasets and extensive simulation studies demonstrate the performance of the proposed methods across a variety of alternatives and data settings.

title: On the Supersingular reduction of Cubic fourfolds with Complex Multiplication
abstract: If $X$ is a K3 surface with complex multiplication by a CM field $E$, Kazuhiro Ito proved that the height of the reduction of $X$ in characteristic $p>0$, and its Artin invariant if it is supersingular, can be computed from the decomposition of $p$ in $E$. We present analogous results for cubic fourfolds by using the main theorem of complex multiplication for cubic fourfold, proved by Rikuto Ito.

title: On the motivic approach to the Abhyankar rectifiability problem and concrete rectifications
abstract: We study closed embeddings of the complex affine line into affine three-space. We prove that, for every such embedding, the complete-intersection normal map identifies the $\mathbb{A}^1$-fundamental sheaf of its complement with $\mathbf{K}_2^{\mathrm{MW}}$. The proof compares torsors under arbitrary strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves. A nodal projection expresses a torsor by a normal parameter and finitely many node parameters. Extension across the node axes gives equations for the latter. Their correction terms increase a nilpotent filtration generated by the Milnor-Witt symbols of the branch-height differences. We deduce the vanishing of the first Alexander sheaf of every complex embedded line. We also construct polynomial rectifications using finite inverses and affine modifications, including rectifications of the Shastri trefoil and a harmonic figure-eight over $\mathbb{Z}[a]/(a^2-a+1)$, with arbitrary base change. The companion repository (https://github.com/qft98romanov-hash/abhyankar-moh-trefoil) contains explicit rectifiers, their inverses, proofs, and symbolic checks. We prove that a normal map with a polynomial section and geometric generic affine-line fiber is a coordinate projection. We formulate the remaining rectifiability and descent questions; the general complex rectifiability problem is not settled here. An appendix treats other fields, normal orientations, and arithmetic descent.

title: Tensor products of 2-representations
abstract: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.

title: A $π/ 4$ lower bound for random access in symmetric linear ensembles under optimal decoding
abstract: We study the expected number of random linear observations required to recover a prescribed information symbol. For ensembles with uniformly random supports, independently sampled nonzero coefficients, and uniformly bounded column weights, we prove that the asymptotic normalized expected recovery time is at least $π/4$ under optimal decoding. The result holds over finite or infinite fields and extends the lower bound previously established for binary fully symmetric codes under peeling decoding. For singleton - pair observations, we determine the exact limiting expectation and show that optimal and peeling decoding have the same limit, independently of the field and coefficient distribution. The minimum within this family is approximately $0.793933445$, which explicit constructions attain asymptotically over every fixed finite field.

title: Optimal approximation error approach in Bayesian inverse problems
abstract: In many inverse problems, evaluating the forward operator is computationally expensive, making it common practice to accelerate inference with a less costly approximate model. However, such approximations introduce unwanted bias and must be carefully accounted for to ensure the reliability of the solution. This phenomenon is particularly pronounced in Bayesian inference, where accurate posterior characterisation typically requires a large number of forward model evaluations. In this paper, we focus on the approximation error model (AEM), which compensates for the modelling error by adjusting the likelihood density. More precisely, AEM incorporates the model error into the additive Gaussian noise distribution. A central challenge in this approach is how to choose the modified noise mean and covariance in a principled way. To address this, we propose a new framework, optimal approximation error (OAE) which determines the noise model by minimising the expected information loss, measured via the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the true and approximate posterior distributions. We show that the standard enhanced error approach (EEA) is recovered as the minimiser of the expected divergence between likelihoods rather than posteriors and develop OAE as a direct alternative targeting posterior accuracy. We establish bi-convexity of the OAE objective, introduce a regularised, provably convergent proximal alternating minimisation scheme, and derive closed-form expressions in the Gaussian linear setting. We further show that OAE estimates computed from empirical training data are statistically consistent. Numerical experiments on a linear CT problem and a nonlinear Darcy-flow problem show that OAE improves posterior accuracy relative to both the uncorrected and EEA-corrected likelihoods.

title: Polynomial-Time Constructions of Asymptotically Good Random Access Codes from Linear Codes
abstract: Random access codes (RACs) encode a $q$-ary input string into fewer $q$-ary symbols while allowing any requested input symbol to be recovered with probability above the random-guessing value $1/q$. However, it remains unclear what asymptotic guarantees on compression and recovery probability should be required of RACs. We address this question by introducing the notion of asymptotically good RACs and give two polynomial-time constructions. First, an $[n,k,d]_q$ linear code with $d\ge2$, together with an encoder based on its orthogonal-array property, yields an $(n,n-k)_q$-RAC with worst-case decoding success probability \[ p_{\rm wc}=\frac{1}{q}+\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)\frac{d-2}{n}. \] These OA-RACs are asymptotically good whenever the underlying linear codes are, and Garcia--Stichtenoth algebraic-geometry codes give a concrete polynomial-time realization. Second, a direct-sum strategy using OA-RACs derived from $q$-ary Hamming codes and the trivial $(1,1)_q$-RAC yields asymptotically good RAC families at every prescribed RAC rate $R_{\rm RAC}=(n-k)/n\in(0,1)$. Numerical results demonstrate favorable finite-length performance of both constructions.

title: Nice Partitions of Signed-Graphic Arrangements Are Inductive Factorizations
abstract: Nice partitions of hyperplane arrangements give tensor factorizations of Orlik-Solomon algebras as graded vector spaces. In general, a hyperplane arrangement admitting a nice partition need not be free. In this paper, we consider signed-graphic arrangements, the subarrangements of type-$B$ Weyl arrangements, over fields of characteristic different from $2$. We prove that every nice partition of a signed-graphic arrangement is an inductive factorization and hence that the arrangement is free, with nonzero exponents given by the part sizes. In particular, Terao's conjecture holds for the intersection lattices of signed-graphic arrangements admitting a nice partition.

title: Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of Perelman's pseudolocality theorem for Ricci flow, which does not rely on Perelman's Harnack-type inequality. The key step is an estimate relating initial local $μ$-entropy to pointed Nash entropy at later spacetime points. The argument also works for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian flow, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature lower bound. As a consequence, we can also prove the quantitative rigidity results concerning pointed Nash entropy due to Hein-Naber and Bamler for such geometric flows. In the appendix, we also show that the other results in Bamler's work (arXiv:2008.07093), when suitably modified, remain valid for Laplacian flow with bounded torsion. These include log-Sobolev/Poincaré inequality for conjugate heat kernel measure, heat kernel estimates, and dependence of the pointed Nash entropy on its basepoint.

title: Uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of nodal states for a mixed-power scalar field equation
abstract:
We consider the scalar field equation $$\begin{cases} -Δu+u+λ|u|^{q-1}u =μ|u|^{p-1}u, & x\in\mathbb R^n,\\[2mm] u(x)\to 0, & |x|\to\infty, \end{cases}$$
  where $n\geq3$, $1<q<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, and $λ,μ>0$. We study uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of its sign-changing radial bound states. The proof combines a comparison argument for the shooting variation across nodal intervals with uniform compactness estimates for families of bounded nodal number and continuation in a normalized parameter. We show that, for every integer $k\geq1$, fixing the centre and requiring $u(0)>0$ leaves exactly one radial bound state with $k$ nodes. Its radial linearized operator has trivial kernel in the radial space. For each fixed $k$, the corresponding normalized solutions form a global $C^1$ branch.

title: Determination of weight enumerators of binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60
abstract: We construct three binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ with weight enumerators for which no binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ were previously known to exist. This completes the determination of the weight enumerators that occur for binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$.

title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds of type K
abstract: A Calabi-Yau threefold of type K is a free quotient $X=(S\times E)/G$ of the product of a K3 surface and an elliptic curve. We construct a family of geometric Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$ by using Liu's product construction on $S\times E$ and then inducing along the Galois covering. The family has dimension $2h^{1,1}(X)$, and is disjoint from the $\widetilde{\GL}_2^+(\R)$-orbit of Li's stability conditions. These threefolds carry a K3 fibration, and the pushforward of an object from a smooth K3 fiber is (semi)stable if and only if it is (semi)stable on the K3 surface.

title: Hybrid CutFEM-IFEM model for embedded and immersed interfaces with triply-cut cells for the 2D Poisson problem
abstract: We present a hybrid CutFEM--IFEM method for 2D Poisson problems with an immersed fluid--fluid interface and an embedded fluid--solid interface on a single unfitted mesh. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both unfitted finite element methods and immersed interface techniques to handle complex interface geometries and strong discontinuities efficiently. A composite equivalent polynomial representation of the Heaviside and Dirac delta functions is used to integrate on triply-cut cells. Moreover, the IFEM basis functions are enriched with the lift functions exactly representing solution and flux jumps. Numerical examples show optimal convergence for linear and quadratic elements, with accuracy comparable to that of a mesh fitted to both interfaces.

title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
abstract: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity. The main analytic difficulty is to obtain estimates uniform over lattices of unbounded determinant. We address this by combining a reduction based on primitive sublattices of codimension one and least determinant with explicit bounds for theta norms and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.

title: Equivalence of freeness and higher order freeness of hyperplane arrangements
abstract: Using vector bundle theory, we prove that an essential hyperplane arrangement in an $\ell$-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero is free if and only if its module of logarithmic derivations of order $p$ is free for some $1\le p\le\ell-1$. The same statement holds for multiarrangements.

title: Minimizing the spectral radius of unicyclic graphs with fixed order and dissociation number
abstract: A dissociation set of a graph G is a vertex subset S contained in V(G) such that the induced subgraph G[S] has maximum degree at most 1, and the dissociation number of G is the cardinality of a maximum dissociation set denoted by Φ(G). In this paper, we first derive a sharp lower bound on the dissociation number for all unicyclic graphs. Furthermore, we also study the graphs with minimum spectral radius among all unicyclic graphs with given order and dissociation number and explicitly identify all extremal graphs for \(n-4 \le Φ(G) \le n-1\).

title: Reduced and Mixed-Precision Block Householder QR Factorization
abstract: Recent advances in hardware architecture have highlighted the importance of reduced-precision arithmetic for improving performance and reducing energy consumption in large-scale scientific applications. However, uniformly low-precision methods can suffer from numerical instability, especially in fundamental linear algebra routines. Mixed-precision strategies therefore play an important role in balancing efficiency, stability, and accuracy. In this paper, we focus on the block Householder QR decomposition using the WY representation and study its behavior in reduced- and mixed-precision settings. Starting from a uniform half-precision variant, we show that performing norm computations with fp32 accumulation is necessary to avoid overflow and underflow on large matrices. Based on this observation, we introduce mpWYQR, a mixed-precision algorithm that increases the precision of only selected computations and avoids most of the precision conversions required by the existing mixed-precision blocked QR algorithm (mpBQR3) introduced in [L. M. Yang, A. Fox, and G. Sanders, SIAM J. Sci. Comp., 43.3 (2021), pp. A1723--A1753]. Our analysis shows that mpWYQR accuracy is governed by low-precision unit roundoff, and that its error bound exceeds that of mpBQR3 by only a constant factor, with identical heuristic bounds. In experiments across a range of matrix sizes and condition numbers, we show that mpWYQR retains mpBQR3 accuracy while running up to $18\times$ faster and using less memory. We also discuss the performance cost of computing inner products in higher precision, and the library support needed for an efficient GPU implementation.

title: The asymptotics of off-diagonal book Ramsey numbers
abstract:
Let $B_n$ be the book graph consisting of $n$ triangles sharing a common edge. We prove upper bounds for $r(B_{\lceilαn\rceil},B_n)$ that asymptotically match the known lower bounds in the remaining range $1/6<α<1/4$. Combined with the known results for the other ranges of $α$, this completely determines the asymptotics of the Ramsey number $r(B_{\lceilαn\rceil},B_n)$ for every fixed $0<α\le1$: \[
  r(B_{\lceilαn\rceil},B_n)=(c(α)+o(1))n,
  \qquad
  c(α)=
  \begin{cases}
  2, & 0<α\le1/6,\\[1mm]
  \displaystyle\frac{3}{1+2p_α^2},
  & 1/6<α\leα_0,\\[3mm]
  (1+\sqrtα)^2, & α_0<α\le1,
  \end{cases} \] where \(α_0:=\frac{52-16\sqrt3}{121}, \;\;
  p_α:=\frac{1-\sqrt{α(3-2α)}}{1-2α}
  \;\; (1/6<α\leα_0).\) Consequently, the random lower bound is asymptotically tight if and only if $α\geα_0$, thereby determining exactly the range of $α$ for which the conjecture of Conlon, Fox and Wigderson holds. The proof develops a defect-compensation framework around a $K_4$-free auxiliary graph.

title: Electromagnetic Potentials via the Extended Maxwell System
abstract: We construct electromagnetic potentials on arbitrary open 3-dimensional sets for anisotropic, non-homogeneous materials, thus rendering any topological assumption like simple connectedness or the absence of holes superfluous in this context. The main idea is to invoke the extended Maxwell system the easy solution theory of which then yields existence of both scalar- and vector potentials.

title: A fully nonlinear parabolic segregation problem
abstract: We study a two-phase parabolic free boundary problem arising as the segregation limit of a competition-diffusion system with strong interactions and fully nonlinear diffusion. The positive and negative phases are governed by different equations and are coupled through global viscosity inequalities. We construct viscosity solutions that are Lipschitz in space and $1/2$-Hölder in time, and establish differentiability in space across the free boundary, including at singular points. At regular points, we prove that the solution has a parabolic $C^{1,α}$ asymptotic expansion, and deduce that the free boundary is locally a $C^{1,α}$ hypersurface. The proof relies on a parabolic Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman monotonicity formula to classify blow-up limits, followed by an improvement of flatness argument.

title: Class groups of polynomial Krull domains
abstract: A polynomial Krull domain is a Krull domain contained between $\mathbb Z[X]$ and $\mathbb Q[X]$. The domains of this class are precisely the Noetherian integrally closed domains between these polynomial rings by a result of Heinzer, and they have been recently classified by Chang and the second author of this paper as rings of polynomials which are integer-valued over a finite set of ultrametric balls in $\mathbb C_p$, as $p$ ranges through the set of primes in $\mathbb Z$. We show here that every ideal class of a polynomial Krull domain contains a prime ideal. Furthermore, given such a Krull domain $R$, we prove that there exists a polynomial Krull domain $R'$ that is Dedekind, contains $R$ and has the same class group as $R$.

title: Turán number of three disjoint cliques of arbitrary sizes
abstract: The Turán number $\rm ex(n,H)$ of a given graph $H$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph. In this paper, for all $p\ge q\ge r\ge 2$ and $n\geq p+q+r$, we determine the exact value of $\rm ex(n,K_p\cup K_q\cup K_r)$ and describe all extremal graphs.

title: Inverse Scattering of Periodic Surfaces with Multilayer Superlenses: Perturbation Analysis and Resolution Enhancement
abstract: This paper presents a rigorous mathematical analysis of inverse scattering for periodic surfaces through a multilayer superlens. Using the transformed field expansion, we derive a highly explicit reconstruction formula. We theoretically prove that under perfect matching, the reconstruction factor is independent of the number of layers and depends solely on the total material thicknesses, achieving uniform boundedness when the slab thickness dominates. By establishing first-order perturbation formulas and high-frequency asymptotics, we quantify how small material losses induce exponential amplification of high-frequency errors. Crucially, we show that increasing the number of layers substantially reduces this amplification coefficient. Consequently, for fixed total thicknesses, multilayer structures offer significantly improved stability and extended resolution limits for subwavelength reconstruction.

title: Stability of a Fréchet-type functional equation
abstract: We establish the generalized Hyers-Ulam stability of the Fréchet-type functional equation \begin{align*} \sum_{\emptyset \neq I \subset \{ 1, 2, \ldots, n+1 \}} (-1)^{|I|-n+1} f \Bigg( \sum_{i \in I} x_i \Bigg) = 0 \end{align*} in the sense of Găvruţa.

title: The residue field as an infinite syzygy
abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m},k)$ be a commutative Noetherian ring which is either local or positively graded over the field $k$. We provide a method based on liftings for constructing free coresolutions of $k$ over $R$. We apply this method to twisted trivial extensions of the node $k[u,v]/(uv)$ to build a family of positively graded $k$-algebras of dimension $1$ over which $k$ is an infinite graded syzygy, resolving an open question of Iyengar in the negative. We also prove a formula for alternating sums of lengths of Ext modules when $R$ is positively graded, and use it to show that a graded free coresolution of $k$ cannot dualize to a resolution unless $R$ is Artinian Gorenstein.

title: Phase-Space Realization of Stochastic Multivalued Dynamics with Gyroscopic Subdifferential Coupling
abstract: We introduce a new framework for stochastic variational inequalities with oblique reflections generated by non-symmetric matrix coefficients. The loss of symmetry fundamentally changes the structure of the reflected dynamics: besides the dissipative component, it produces a genuinely gyroscopic component describing rotational effects that are invisible to the associated energy forms. To capture this hidden component, we consider planar obstacle problems and we lift the dynamics to an extended phase-space system, where the dissipative and gyroscopic mechanisms are naturally separated. This leads to a new notion of solution, for which we establish existence and uniqueness. The resulting framework allows for genuinely rotated reflections, which can lead to angle-controlled rotations.

title: The Minimax Complexity of Federated Optimization under Interpolation: The Role of Oracle Models
Damped stochastic mirror descent for non-smooth ill-posed problems in Banach space
abstract: We introduce a damped variant of the stochastic mirror descent method for systems of non-smooth nonlinear ill-posed operator equations in Banach spaces. At each iteration, the method samples a random subset of the equations, performs a mirror-descent step in the dual space with an adaptive step size derived from the discrepancy principle, and applies a damping term that prevents the iterates from drifting away from the initial guess. The scheme accommodates non-smooth forward operators through a family of bounded linear surrogates, admits general $p$-convex penalty functionals which also includes trained convex penalty, allows the noise level to differ from equation to equation, and dispenses with two classical requirements, namely reflexivity of the image space and Gâteaux differentiability of the forward operator. We study its regularization properties under an \textit{a posteriori} stopping rule by proving first that the iteration terminates after finitely many steps almost surely, and then that the mean-square error of the iterates tends to zero as the noise level vanishes. Numerical experiments on a system of non-smooth semilinear inverse source problems and the identification of a diffusion coefficient confirm the theoretical analysis and shows improved convergence results.

title: Langevin Dynamics of Non-reciprocally Coupled Spherical Spin Glasses
abstract: We analyze the limiting dynamics of two copies of a disordered mean-field spherical $p$-spin system coupled non-reciprocally to one another and initialized independently of the disorder. We prove that, on every finite time interval, as the system size tends to infinity, the empirical correlation and integrated response functions converge almost surely and in $L^q$ for $q \geq 1$, uniformly in time, to the unique non-random solution of a system of coupled integro-differential equations. For even $p$-spin models, we establish stationarity and exponential decay of the correlation and response functions in the high-temperature regime. In the special case of the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, we derive explicit representations of the limiting correlation and integrated response functions.
