These representations allow us to characterize the long-time dynamics throughout the full range of temperatures. In particular, we prove the occurrence of aging in the low-temperature regime and fluctuation-dissipation behavior in the high-temperature regime, and provide a separate characterization of the dynamics at the critical temperature.

title: Introduction to Separable Simplicial Algebras
abstract: We study separable simplicial algebras and Azumaya simplicial algebras.

title: Two-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions
abstract: It is trivial that $1$-dimensional $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates. Coupier, Henry, Jahnel and Köppl proved the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in dimension 2; and then for sufficiently large dimensions, Bäumler, Jahnel, Köppl, Lodewijks, Reeves and Tóbiás showed this is still true. In this paper, we verify that the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions $d\ge 3.$

title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
abstract: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
abstract: In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla's special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of \cite[Remark 2.4]{BLMM17}, pointed out by Bruinier--Zuffetti \cite{BZ26}. Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily--Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work.

title: Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Semilinear Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
abstract: We develop a rigorous mathematical framework for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations. The invariant Gaussian measure of the associated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, which need not be time-reversible, serves as the reference measure. We define thermodynamic quantities in terms of probability densities and derive the entropy balance equation. We obtain explicit expressions for the entropy production rate and prove that its vanishing in the stationary state is equivalent to time reversibility. Sample-path entropy production is identified with the logarithm of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the forward path measure with respect to the time-reversed path measure and is shown to satisfy fluctuation theorems. For nonstationary systems, sample-path entropy production decomposes into housekeeping heat and free-energy dissipation, each satisfying an integral fluctuation theorem. Both have nonnegative expectations, and the mean free-energy dissipation equals the decrease in relative entropy with respect to the stationary distribution. The theory is applied to semilinear stochastic heat equations with spatially correlated noise, a random polymer model, a nonlinear model with a divergence-free drift, and two coupled stochastic heat equations in contact with heat baths at different temperatures.

title: A note on a problem of Ma and Chen
abstract: Let $S=(s_1,s_2,\cdots)$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. For any real number $α>0$, let $S_α=(\lfloorαs_1\rfloor,\lfloorαs_2\rfloor,\cdots)$. We prove that if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for every positive integer $n$, then there exists $0<α<1$ such that $S_α$ is strongly complete. In addition, this gives a negative answer to a problem of Ma and Chen in [Acta Arith. 203 (2022), 307--318]. We also prove that the same result is true if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

title: On $q$-middle convolution and generalized $q$-hypergeometric equation
abstract: We investigate higher-order $q$-difference equations obtained by successive applications of a $q$-analogue of addition and the $q$-middle convolution. We construct an $n$-dimensional system of linear $q$-difference equations and derive a single $q$-difference equation whose coefficients are polynomials of degree at most $1$ in the independent variable. Under certain conditions on the parameters, the resulting equation is a generalized $q$-hypergeometric equation of order $n$. We also obtain a multiple Jackson integral representation of solutions and give sufficient conditions for its convergence. By suitably choosing the functions appearing in the integrand and specializing the parameters, we obtain $q$-hypergeometric series solutions of type ${}_n φ_{n-1}$.

title: A time-map description of the one-dimensional (p,q)-Laplacian Fučik spectrum
abstract:
We study a one-dimensional Fučik-type boundary value problem (BVP) driven by the nonhomogeneous, one-dimensional $(p,q)$-Laplacian, \[
  -\left(|u'|^{p-2}u' + |u'|^{q-2}u'\right)'
  =
  λ(u^+)^{p-1}
  -
  μ(u^-)^{q-1},
  \qquad
  u(0)=u(L)=0,
  \qquad L>0, \] where $1<q<p$ and $λ,μ\in\mathbb{R}$. The problem is asymmetric: the positive component is paired with the $p$-power and the negative component with the $q$-power. This asymmetry prevents the standard homogeneous $p$-Laplacian scaling argument from producing explicit Fučik curves.
  We first prove a quadrant reduction theorem. Any positive nodal interval for a solution forces $λ>0$, and any negative nodal interval forces $μ>0$. Hence, all sign-changing solutions occur for values of $(λ,μ)$ in the positive quadrant. Outside the positive quadrant, only one-sign solutions can occur.
  We also formulate the equation as an autonomous planar system and establish existence and uniqueness for its initial value problem in the positive quadrant. We then impose the second Dirichlet condition through a shooting formulation and show that every zero of a nontrivial Dirichlet solution is simple and isolated. This provides the dynamical foundation for the subsequent construction and gluing of nodal humps of solutions.
  Inside the positive quadrant, we use a classical one-dimensional time-map method to obtain a projected-geometry description of the spectrum, or the set of values of $(λ, μ)$ for which there exist nontrivial solutions. Every nodal solution has a common energy $E>0$ shared by all positive and negative humps.

title: A finiteness result for split exceptional dual pairs
abstract: We prove that big theta lifts have finite length for thirteen split exceptional dual pairs arising from the minimal representations of the split real groups of types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$.

title: Bound-preserving and mass-conserving projection BCFD methods for incompressible miscible displacement in porous media
abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze two novel structure-preserving projection schemes for the incompressible miscible displacement problem in porous media. These schemes are specifically designed to preserve two essential physical properties--concentration bounds and the mass balance identity, and are accompanied by a rigorous error analysis for the projection approach. Both schemes are second-order accurate in space but differ in temporal accuracy: one is first-order and the other is second-order. Methodologically, both schemes comprise a prediction step for the concentration variable, based on a second-order modified upwind discretization together with an implicit-explicit finite difference approximation, followed by a projection (or correction) step that enforces the desired physical constraints, namely bounds and mass conservation. For the first-order temporal scheme, the velocity and pressure are solved at the first step on staggered spatial grids with explicit treatment of concentration. In contrast, for the second-order scheme, to ensure well-posedness and to suppress non-physical oscillations in the simulation, the velocity and pressure are solved at the final step with the concentration treated implicitly. A rigorous numerical theoretical framework is established for the first-order scheme, encompassing optimal-order error estimates, stability, and proofs of the existence and uniqueness of the numerical solutions. The numerical analysis framework is further extended to the more involved second-order scheme, and the corresponding theoretical results are briefly outlined. Finally, numerical examples, including some 'real' simulations, are presented to verify the theoretical findings and demonstrate the strong performance of the proposed schemes. In particular, the occurrence of viscous fingering is successfully captured and confirmed by the numerical results.

title: Strong approximations for dependent random fields
abstract: We establish strong Gaussian approximations for centered stationary random fields on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, represented as measurable functions of i.i.d.\ innovations. Under finite $p$th moments, $p>2$, and sufficiently fast decay of spatial dependence, we construct a single coupling of the field with an i.i.d.\ Gaussian field. Its partial sums, scaled by the long-run standard deviation, approximate those of the original field almost surely, uniformly over all rectangular prefixes and all observation scales. Over a cube of side length $n$, the approximation error is $O_{\mathrm{a.s.}}(n^{\max\{d/p,(d-1)/2\}})$ up to logarithmic factors. While $d/p$ is the familiar moment term, the surface term $(d-1)/2$, absent for independent planar arrays, emerges as a cost of dependence, and cannot be removed even for finite-range Gaussian fields. The assumptions accommodate nonlinear and noncausal fields without imposing mixing. The proof combines a permanent dyadic blocking, a local Gaussian coupling in tensor Haar coordinates driven by a Doob martingale with vanishing conditional third moments, and a comparison of the resulting dependent Gaussian blocks with white noise.

title: Soliton resolution conjecture and soliton gases for the Benjamin-Ono equation with infinite-order multisolitons in the sharp well-posedness space
abstract:
We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for infinite-order multisoliton solutions in the sharp well-posedness space $H^s(\mathbb R)$, $s>-\frac12$, and construct soliton gases in $H^{s}(\mathbb R)$ with arbitrary $s\in\mathbb R$, for the Benjamin--Ono equation. In particular, our work addresses two important open problems about inverse spectral for Lax operator, including the problem of spectral characterization of infinite-order multisolitons and that of determining the range of their asymptotic parameters.
  A central ingredient of our work is a spectral decomposition adapted to rough initial data. This extends the global soliton--radiation description to weakly weighted $H^s$ data while allowing infinite negative eigenvalues. Another important ingredient is a continuous norming action that extends finite inverse spectral shifts to gas limits while retaining a full continuous norming weight. Our framework provides a basis for studying infinite-order soliton resolution and the construction and asymptotics of soliton gases for nonlocal equations.

title: Maximal regular subsemigroups containing the group of units of transformation semigroups that preserve a uniform equivalence relation with two classes
abstract: Let $X$ be a nonempty set and $E$ an equivalence relation on $X$. The semigroup $T_E(X)$ consists of all transformations on $X$ that preserve $E$. Although the collection of all regular elements of $T_E(X)$ is not, in general, a subsemigroup, we investigate maximal regular subsemigroups of $T_E(X)$ containing the group of units $G_E(X)$. We construct two such maximal regular subsemigroups, denoted by $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$, and show that their maximality holds in full generality for an arbitrary set $X$ and an arbitrary equivalence relation $E$ that is neither the identity relation nor the universal relation on $X$ (whether finite or infinite, uniform or non-uniform). Furthermore, when $X$ is finite and $E$ is a uniform equivalence relation with exactly two classes of cardinality at least $2$, we provide a complete classification by proving that they are the only maximal regular subsemigroups containing $G_E(X)$.

title: Sharp Bounds on Torsional Rigidity of Metric Graphs with Signed Delta-Vertex Strengths
abstract: We study torsional rigidity on finite compact connected metric graphs with real \(δ\)-vertex strengths in the regime of strictly positive torsion. For a fixed total length \(L>0\), let \(I_+\) be the sum of the positive strengths and \(I_-\) the sum of the magnitudes of the negative strengths, with \(I_+>I_-\). We determine the sharp infimum and the exact threshold for a finite universal supremum. The supremum is finite precisely when \(I_-<I_+/(1+LI_+)\). In this regime, an interval with strengths \(I_+\) and \(-I_-\) at opposite endpoints attains the sharp Saint--Venant bound. At and beyond the threshold, torsional rigidity is unbounded even among three-vertex paths with the same data and strictly positive torsion. The sharp infimum is \(L^2/(I_+-I_-)\) throughout the range \(I_+>I_-\ge0\). It is not attained by any finite graph and is approached by graphs with two vertices joined by increasingly many parallel edges of equal length, preserving both strength totals separately. A vertex-matrix formulation and explicit path examples clarify the relation between strength placement, spectral positivity, and solvability.

title: A conditional no-splash criterion for two-fluid Euler--MHD interface
abstract: We study a two-dimensional incompressible two-fluid system: an inviscid, irrotational Euler phase and a viscous, conducting MHD phase, separated by a free interface. We prove a conditional quantitative no-splash criterion for smooth solutions in a specified admissible class. In addition to a bound on the trace of the Euler velocity, an initial bound on the magnetic trace and bounds on the bulk vorticity, this class imposes bounds on the interface Biot--Savart potential and its tangential derivative, fixed exponential vertical localization, and the normal derivative of the bulk vorticity at the interface together with one tangential derivative of it. It also requires a Biot--Savart representation of the Euler velocity up to a bounded-gradient harmonic part and a positive initial chord-arc bound. Under these assumptions the chord-arc functional has a uniform positive lower bound on $[0,T]$, depending only on the interval length, the decay width and the a priori bound, after an enlargement that absorbs the surface tension and the densities. The proof combines a maximum-principle analysis of the interface-vorticity equation, in which the magnetic field enters through the Lorentz term and the pressure jump, with a geometric reduction in the style of Fefferman--Ionescu--Lie.

title: Nonlinear coercivity and orbital stability of smooth solitary waves for the modified Camassa--Holm equation
abstract: In this paper, we establish orbital stability of smooth zero-background solitary waves for the modified Camassa--Holm equation in $H^1(\R)\cap W^{1,4}(\R)$ for the full range $γ<c<2γ$. The main difficulty is that spectral coercivity of the Hessian does not by itself yield nonlinear coercivity in this topology, because normalized perturbations may develop derivative concentration. In order to overcome this obstruction, we apply a penalized Lyapunov functional and introduce a derivative factorization. The key ingredient is a concentration-coercivity principle for the normalized Lyapunov energy, which yields local nonlinear Lyapunov coercivity. Our result extends the $H^1(\mathbb R)\cap W^{1,4}(\mathbb R)$ orbital-stability results of Li and Liu [Ann. PDE, 2021] and Zhang and Zhu [JDE, 2025] to the entire parameter range $γ<c<2γ$.

title: Carnot geodesics with Hölder controls
abstract: We construct an explicit length-minimizing curve in a polynomial rank-two sub-Riemannian structure on $\R^4$. Its arclength parametrization is $C^{1,1/2}$ and is not $C^{1,α}$ near an interior point for any $α>1/2$. Minimality is proved by an approximate calibration chosen separately for each competitor. The example admits a minimizing lift to a rank-two Carnot group of step five. Generalizations are announced.

title: Finite-volume and thermodynamic-limit lower bounds for the coherently driven Bose--Hubbard model via the Lieb--Yamazaki method
abstract: We derive rigorous lower bounds on the ground-state energy of the coherently driven Bose--Hubbard model using a Lieb--Yamazaki positive-operator decomposition. The resulting quadratic bounding Hamiltonian is diagonalized by displacement and Bogoliubov transformations, yielding explicit stability conditions and finite-volume bounds in arbitrary dimension. We establish the thermodynamic-limit energy density and characterize the excitation spectrum of the bounding Hamiltonian. We also derive its Gaussian-state observables, including filling, number fluctuations, and second-order correlations, and identify regimes of antibunching and sub-Poissonian statistics. Numerical calculations assess the tightness of the bounds across representative parameter regimes.

title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver Empowered Hybrid Non-orthogonal Multiple Access
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel uplink Hybrid Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) architecture assisted by Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers (RAQRs) to improve energy efficiency by addressing the physical constraints of atomic sensing. We formulate a joint optimization problem encompassing phase measurements and multi-user power allocation to minimize the total transmit power. This problem is particularly challenging due to the non-linear amplitude-only observations of atomic vapor cells. To decomposes the resulting non-convexity, we develop a hierarchical three-layer decomposition optimization framework that systematically decouples the global problem. The inner layer employs a customized Expectation Maximization-Gerchberg-Saxton (EM-GS) algorithm to resolve phase ambiguity and estimate equivalent channel gains. The middle layer derives closed-form optimal power allocation solutions via Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. The outer layer utilizes linear Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) detection for high-reliability signal recovery. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over conventional RF-based Hybrid NOMA. Notably, the atomic architecture achieves approximately a 93% reduction in total power consumption compared to Orthogonal Multiple Access (OMA) baselines while maintaining strict backward compatibility, thereby laying a solid foundation for practical deployment in next-generation green communication networks.

title: MacKay-Neal Codes for DNA Channels under Block-MAP Decoding
abstract: We prove achievability below the symmetric information rate (SIR) under block maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoding for a fixed-degree MacKay-Neal (MN) socket ensemble on the quaternary insertion-deletion-substitution channel used to model DNA reads. For every integer $\ell\ge4$, the $(\ell,3,3)$ socket ensemble, with one transmitted bit fixed and an independent uniform known offset, has limiting rate $r_\star=6/\ell$ bits per stored nucleotide. If the joint SIR $J_t$ of a fixed number $t$ of reads under independent, uniformly distributed input nucleotides exceeds $r_\star$, the ensemble-average full extended-word block error is $O(1/n)$, and deterministic graph-offset sequences attain the same limiting rate and message-average error bound. This result concerns the discrete rate family $6/\ell$, not arbitrary rates approaching a given SIR. The channel permits arbitrarily many insertions and unbounded drift, with no alignment supplied to the receiver. The proof combines established MN parity and distance estimates with a strict arbitrary-candidate-list bound and a list construction that accounts for hidden output boundaries.

title: Nevanlinna Theory on Berkovich Curves
abstract: We develop a value distribution theory for finite analytic morphisms between proper connected quasi-smooth Berkovich curves over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. The central tool is a multi-tail Dirichlet Green function on finite truncations of a generalized skeleton, which makes non-Archimedean potential theory on skeleta compatible with global Nevanlinna asymptotics. Using it, we prove the first main theorem as an exact identity relating the characteristic, counting, and proximity functions. For logarithmic targets we establish a second main theorem in both ramified and level-one truncated forms. The defect relation is also given. The theory provides a Berkovich-analytic framework for non-Archimedean value distribution, bridging classical Nevanlinna theory and its $p$-adic counterpart.

title: On the Witt liftability of quasi-F-split Calabi--Yau varieties
abstract: We prove that a quasi-$F$-split strict Calabi--Yau variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of odd characteristic $p$ admits a smooth projective lifting over $W(k)$ if $p\geq d-1$, or if $p=d-2$ and $H^0(X,T_X)=0$. We also prove $W_3(k)$-liftability in odd characteristic.

title: Logarithmic fractional Hardy inequalities
abstract:
We establish sharp fractional Hardy inequalities in the critical regimes $sp=d$ and $sp=1$, with explicit logarithmic weight functions. In the whole-space setting, for $p>d\ge 1$, $sp=d$, we prove that \begin{equation*}
  \int_{\mathbb R^d} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{2d}}\,dx\,dy \geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}\right)^p \int_{B_R}|u(x)|^p W_{p,d,R}(x)\,dx, \end{equation*} for $u\in C_c(B_R)$, where $W_{p,d,R}$ is a logarithmic-type weight and the constant is sharp. We also show that the corresponding inequality with the simpler weight $|x|^{-d}(\log(R/|x|))^{-p}$ cannot hold with any positive constant. Furthermore, we derive two-sided estimates and asymptotic formulae for $W_{p,d,R}$, including its limiting connection with the classical Hardy inequality. In the half-space $\mathbb{R}^{d}_{+}$, we establish an analogous sharp fractional Hardy inequality in the critical case $sp=1$, with an explicit logarithmic weight depending on the distance to the boundary. We also investigate the asymptotic behaviour of this weight, obtaining estimates that describe its behaviour near the boundary. These results elucidate the role of logarithmic weights in critical fractional Hardy inequalities in both whole-space and half-space settings.

title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $γ_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_jγ_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14{,}639{,}440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.

title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito (J. Math. Biol. 2008) showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop (two one-sided benefits and one one-sided harm) together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs.

title: The 120-Cell Dissected by the Hyperplanes of Its Final Stellation: the golden ring Z[phi] as foundation, from Kramer's seven cells to 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits
abstract: The diagonals of a regular pentagon dissect it into eleven pieces and draw a pentagram; the dodecahedron dissected by the twelve face planes of its inner core gives Kramer's seven "elementary cells" of 1982. We define the stellation dissection of a golden regular polytope in any dimension as the dissection of the convex hull of its final regular stellation by the facet hyperplanes of the core, show that the core has phi^(-d) of the inradius of the hull for d = 2, 3, 4, and carry the dissection out for the first time on the 120-cell. The foundation is the arithmetic of the golden ring Z[phi], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt 5): vertices and hyperplanes live in Z[phi]^d, every orientation test is the exact sign of an element of Z[phi], decided with integers, and the pieces are named by sign vectors. We develop this foundation from scratch (conjugation, norm, units, the primes sqrt 5, 2, 3, the exact sign test, the lattice x -> (x, conj x), the vertex modules of the dodecahedron and the 120-cell, the icosian ring) and let it carry the geometry. The definition bifurcates in dimension four: the star cut at depth phi^(-4), a unit, has 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits of H4; the hereditary cut at depth 1 - phi^(-4) = sqrt 5 / phi^2, a unit times the ramified prime, induces the three-dimensional dissection on every facet and has 8,161 cells in 8 orbits. New here: all vertices of the dodecahedral and of the hereditary dissection lie in the vertex module of the polytope being cut, whereas the star cut needs the denominators 2, 3 and 5; the seven kinds of pieces of the dodecahedron are exactly the I_h-orbits of sign vectors, with stellation layer equal to the number of plus signs. We catalogue the four-dimensional pieces and treat the circumscribed disc, ball and 4-ball. Every number quoted is recomputed exactly by a script whose output is reproduced in an appendix.

title: Crescent configurations in three dimensions
abstract: A crescent configuration of $n$ points in $\mathbb R^d$ is a set in general position whose distinct pairwise distances have multiplicities $1,\ldots,n-1$. We construct such a configuration in $\mathbb R^3$ for every $n\geq3$, giving a uniform bound of three for the minimum dimension. The proof uses equally spaced parameters on a short circular helix and Rolle's theorem. We also give explicit integer-coordinate configurations with $O(n\log n)$ bits per coordinate, and prove that every finite initial segment of the sequence $(\cos j,\sin j,2j)_{j\geq0}$ of length at least three is a crescent configuration.

title: Optimality Conditions and Solution Set Characterisations of Convex Minimal Time Optimisation Problems
abstract: The paper studies convex minimisation problems involving a composition of a coordinatewise nondecreasing convex function with a finite family of nonnegative, locally Lipschitz continuous and convex functions. We establish complete dual optimality conditions and characterise the entire solution set using multipliers and subgradients associated with a given solution. The results are applied to norm optimisation problems involving minimal time functions with different convex dynamics sets and convex target sets. The sum, maximum and p-norms yield minimal time versions of the Fermat--Torricelli, Chebyshev centre and p-Fermat--Torricelli problems, respectively. Examples in finite and infinite dimensional spaces are provided to illustrate the solution set characterisations.

title: Directed isoperimetry and infinitely fast robbers
abstract: We study the fast version of the cops and robber game on finite digraphs with unit-speed cops and an unbounded-speed robber. We prove a lower bound for the cop number of every strongly connected digraph in terms of its order, maximum out-degree, and out-vertex expansion, extending Mehrabian's isoperimetric lower bound to digraphs, where connected components are replaced by forward reachable sets. For strongly connected abelian Cayley digraphs of fixed out-degree, we show that the ratio of the cop number to the number of vertices is comparable to each of out-vertex expansion, vertex expansion of the underlying undirected graph, minimum nontrivial character displacement, the square root of the unnormalized Laplacian spectral gap of the underlying undirected graph, and the reciprocal of its diameter. The comparison constants depend polynomially on the out-degree. In the undirected case, we also compare pathwidth with these parameters, complementing the bounded-degree treewidth comparison of Alon and Mehrabian. Combining the directed lower bound with recent cyclic sweep techniques for abelian Cayley graphs, we determine the order of the cop number of positively oriented tori and directed Heisenberg graphs.

title: Dimension-free exponential entropy quotients over $\mathbb{F}_2$
abstract: Let $X$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^m$, and let $X'$ be an independent copy. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a subspace $G$ with $\dim G\le 2^{320(1+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}H(X)$ such that $H(q_GX)\le(1+\varepsilon)(H(q_GX+q_GX')-H(q_GX))$. In particular, the quotient entropy is at most $(1+\varepsilon)(H(X+X')-H(X))$. The coefficient is independent of the ambient dimension, and its exponential order in $1/\varepsilon$ is necessary. The structural result is a logarithmic rigidity estimate for finite weighted families of laws with averaged subspace entropy sparsity. A common variational quotient controls both a family and its convolution family without decreasing the original family's normalized mean entropy defect. Posterior families preserve averaged sparsity, and a fresh-index argument combines a local-to-global estimate with the entropic Marton theorem to increase the defect ratio at a fixed multiplicative sparsity cost. We also obtain two-input almost-additivity and concentration of moderate-doubling sets on subspace cosets at the same exponential scale. The constants are not optimized.

title: Lyubeznik numbers of the face rings of simplicial posets
abstract: For a simplicial poset $P$, Stanley assigned the face ring $A_P$, which is the quotient of the polynomial ring $S:=K[t_x \mid x \in P \setminus \{\widehat{0} \}]$ by the ideal $I_P$. This is a generalization of Stanley-Reisner rings, but the grading of $S$ is more involved. Building on our previous paper, we further develop and complete the study of the local cohomology modules $H_{I_P}^i(S)$. In our categorical framework, $\mathrm{Ext}_S(A_P, S)$ ``encodes" all the information of $H_{I_P}^i(S)$. We treat $H_{I_P}^i(S)$ in a reasonably explicit way. In particular, Lyubeznik numbers $λ_{i,j}(A_P)$ can be simply expressed in terms of $[\mathrm{Ext}_S^*(\mathrm{Ext}_S^*(A_P,S), S)]_\bf{0}$, and depend only on the homeomorphism class of the underlying space of the CW complex associated with $P$ and $\mathrm{char}(K)$.

title: EKR Results for Cuspidal Representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$
abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_χ$ be a cuspidal representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$. A subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_2(q)$ is \emph{$t$-intersecting} if $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\{v \in \mathcal{S}_χ: g_1v = g_2v\} \geqslant t$ for any $g_1, g_2 \in S$. In this paper, we determine $\max{|S|}$ where $S$ is $t$-intersecting.

title: Arithmetic classification of the Dirichlet eigenvalues for a one-dimensional nonlocal $p$-Laplacian problem
abstract: We classify the arithmetic nature of the Dirichlet eigenvalues of a homogeneous nonlocal one-dimensional $p$-Laplacian problem with power-type nonlinearity $|u|^{q-2}u$. For rational $p,q>1$, either all eigenvalues are algebraic or all are transcendental. Algebraicity holds exactly when the interval length is an algebraic multiple of a distinguished scale determined by a beta value. This scale is transcendental. When $p=q$, the criterion reduces to algebraicity of the interval length divided by $π$,independently of the rational exponent.

title: On isomorphisms of tetravalent Cayley graphs over generalized quaternion groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $S$ be a subset of $G$ with $1\not\in S$. $S$ is called a $CI$-subset of $G$ if for any $T\subset G$, whenever $Cay (G,S)\cong Cay (G,T)$, there is an element $σ\in Aut(G)$ such that $S^σ=T$. For a positive integer $m$, $G$ is called an $m$-$CI$-group if all subsets $S$ of $G \setminus \{1\}$ with $|S|\leq m$ and $S^{-1}=S$ are $CI$-subsets. In this paper, we show that the generalized quaternion group of order $4n$ is a $4$-$CI$-group if and only if $n$ is odd.

title: Notes on Orlicz Spaces and Interpolation
abstract: Orlicz spaces are a natural generalization of classical Lebesgue spaces. They are built upon convex growth functions and provide a flexible framework for studying integrability conditions beyond power-type behavior. In this survey paper, we present the basic definitions, main properties, and fundamental results concerning Orlicz spaces, and also discuss the Marcinkiewicz interpolation result for Orlicz spaces.

title: The Characteristics of Finite Projections of Certain Stochastic Processes and Queues
abstract: This thesis studies finite projections of transient regenerative processes, constructed by conditioning regeneration cycles to be finite. It develops comparisons between the original and projected laws, including finite-time bounds and best-approximation properties for specified metrics and comparison classes. Applications concern birth-and-death processes, Markov chains and semi-Markov processes, with explicit queueing examples. Structural results describe projections associated with different regeneration states, invariant measures and connections with Martin boundary kernels. The thesis also studies reconstruction of birth-and-death rates from passage-time laws and continued-fraction representations of Laplace-Stieltjes transforms for skip-free semi-Markov processes, together with truncation-error bounds. This is a corrected English edition of a Romanian doctoral thesis completed in 1998 and defended in 1999. The preface distinguishes the historical work from corrections and later additions made for this edition.

title: Sizes of cross-intersecting families
abstract:
The size of cross-intersecting families ${\cal F}_1, \dots, {\cal F}_d$ is usually measured by the sum or the product of the sizes $|{\cal F}_i|$. These two natural size functions have different extremal structures, and different techniques have been developed for them.
  We introduce the cross-degree of a size function and show that the potential extremal structures of maximum cross-intersecting families are the same for all size functions of finite cross-degree, including the sum and the product. Our main tool is a strengthened form of the generating family method of Ahlswede--Khachatrian, based on standard generating families and on local modifications of cross-intersecting families, which we call mutations. It treats two completely different types of extremal structures in a unified way and, unlike the original method, needs shifting in only one step.

title: A Characterization of Functions on the Integer Lattice That Are L-Extendable through Local Convex Extensions
abstract:
L-extendable functions on the integer lattice are functions that admit a $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation; that is, values can be assigned to the additional half-integral points, while keeping the original values at integer points, so that the resulting function is $\frac12$UJ-convex. Various examples of L-extendable functions and their applications are known. A general characterization of L-extendability for functions on the integer lattice, however, remains open.
  In this paper, we study the L-extendability of functions on the integer lattice. We first obtain a necessary condition: L-extendable functions are integrally convex. We then consider a special subclass of L-extendable functions, namely, those whose local convex extensions give L-convex relaxations. This subclass has a useful optimization property: the optimal value of the original function coincides with that of the $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation given by its local convex extension, a property not guaranteed for general $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxations. We characterize this subclass by showing that a function is L-extendable through its local convex extension if and only if it is integrally convex and its restriction to every unit hypercube is D-convex, where D-convexity is a discrete convexity associated with reflected Freudenthal simplicial divisions. This subclass strictly contains the class of D-convex functions. We also give a combinatorial characterization of D-convex subsets of the vertices of a unit hypercube: a set $X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ is D-convex if and only if it is majority-closed and contains a relative opposite pair.

title: Classification of threshold dynamics for the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous NLS
abstract: We study the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation $i\partial_{t}u+Δu+|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{4-2b}{d}}u=0$ in dimensions $d\ge3$. For $\frac12<b<\min\{2,d/2\}$, we prove that every forward-global $H^1$ solution with mass equal to that of the ground state $Q$ either scatters forward or coincides with $e^{it}Q$, up to phase rotation and scaling. As a consequence, every solution with nonradial $H^1$ initial data at the ground-state mass must be global and scatter in both time directions. For $0<b\le\frac12$, analogous rigidity and scattering results hold under an additional finite-variance assumption. The key new ingredients in our proof are a nonradial incoming/outgoing decomposition and exterior frequency-decay estimates, which yield the kinetic-energy localization needed for a localized virial argument.

title: Data-driven stochastic asymptotic regularization for ill-posed inverse problems with a posteriori and heuristic stopping
abstract: A novel Data-driven STochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{D-STAR}) method is proposed for solving linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, which incorporates a data-driven drift and a stochastic diffusion mechanism. Both known and unknown noise level cases are accommodated by the method, thereby making the framework applicable to a broader range of practical inverse problems. For known noise level, a modified discrepancy principle is employed, whereas for unknown noise level, a heuristic stopping rule based solely on noisy data is developed. For each stopping rule, an appropriate diffusion term is defined and the well-posedness of the associated stochastic differential equation is demonstrated. The finite termination of \texttt{D-STAR} method under both stopping rules is established and its convergence to the exact solution in the noise-free setting is proved. For the noisy data, stability and the regularization property in the mean-square sense are further established. In addition, the uncertainty quantification of the proposed method and its comparison with the Stochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{SAR}) method under both rules are provided. Furthermore, it is shown that local minima arising in the Data-Driven Iteratively Regularized Landweber (\texttt{DDIRLI}) method may be escaped. Finally, detailed numerical experiments, including comparisons with existing \texttt{DDIRLI} and \texttt{SAR} methods, are presented on X-ray computed tomography and nonlinear schlieren tomography for both stopping rules, thereby demonstrating the performance of \texttt{D-STAR}.

title: Meromorphic solutions of a nonlinear differential-difference equation with two exponential terms
abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$ be integers. We study finite order meromorphic solutions of the nonlinear differential-difference equation \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+P_{d}(z,f)=p_{1}(z){\rm e}^{α_{1}z^{k}}+p_{2}(z){\rm e}^{α_{2}z^{k}}, \end{equation*} where $P_{d}(z,f)\not\equiv 0$ is a difference polynomial in $f$ of degree $d\leq n-1$ whose coefficients are small meromorphic functions with respect to $f$, $p_{1},~p_{2}$ are nonzero meromorphic functions with $T(r,p_{j})=o(r^{k})$, $j=1,2$, and $α_{1}\neqα_{2}$ are nonzero constants. We prove that every such solution has order exactly $k$, and obtain sufficient conditions on $n,~d,~k$ for the equation to admit no finite order meromorphic solution with $N(r,\frac{1}{f})=S(r,f)$. Our results extend the known ones from linear exponents $z$ to polynomial exponents $z^{k}$, and replace the linear difference polynomials with the degree restriction $d\leq n-2$ assumed in the literature by general ones of degree $d\leq n-1$. Examples show that the restrictions on $n$ and $d$ are sharp.

title: Inflection sets of permutations
abstract: In 2020, Brualdi and Dahl introduced the discrete derivative $σ'(i)=σ(i+1)-σ(i)$ of a permutation $σ\in\Sym_n$. In this paper, we focus on the second derivative of a permutation, $σ''(i)=σ(i+1)+σ(i-1)-2σ(i)$, and the inflections it determines. We show that for even $n$, the only distinct permutations with the same second derivative are the identity and its reverse, while for odd $n$, the second derivative is not injective even after excluding them. We then study which sets of pairs of integers $(i,j)$ are the inflection set of some permutation and whether a given set is witnessed in $\Sym_n$ for infinitely many $n$. We show that exactly $14$ permutations of $[n]$ have no inflections when $n\ge5$. For a single inflection $\{(k,m)\}$, we determine all $n$ for which it is witnessed in $\Sym_n$: we prove it is always witnessed, and it is witnessed for only finitely many $n$ if and only if $m\ge 2k+1$. In that case, all such $n$ satisfy $2m-2k+1\le n\le 2m-k+2$ (apart from $k=2$, $n=m+1$), and, perhaps surprisingly, this range has gaps once $k\ge 10$, the smallest occurring at $(k,m,n)=(10,21,30)$. Finally, we characterize maximally inflected permutations, whose second derivative alternates in sign, and show that their number $|\mathcal M_n|$ satisfies $2E_n\le|\mathcal M_n|\le(2/3)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1}\,n!$, where $E_n$ is the Euler zigzag number.

title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features
abstract: Kernel methods face two recurrent bottlenecks: the cubic cost of inverting an $n\times n$ kernel matrix, as in kernel ridge regression, and the evaluation of kernel integrals, as required in kernel quadrature. Existing low-rank kernel and Gaussian process approximations primarily address the former bottleneck, but do not control the downstream quadrature error when both the kernel matrix and kernel mean are approximated, particularly when the integrand lies outside the kernel reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We address both challenges through an operator-adapted finite-feature approximation. Specifically, we construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting finite-feature estimators in kernel quadrature, with extension to other related kernel methods. Our results show that, with $m \lesssim n$ basis functions, the truncated estimator attains the corresponding benchmark statistical rates. The theory covers fixed/random designs, noisy/noiseless observations, oversmoothing/undersmoothing regimes, and Matérn/Gaussian-type weights. We provide explicit error bounds that quantify the roles of the spectral cutoff, regularization parameter, lengthscale, sampling geometry, and operator boundary condition. We verify the convergence results in numerical experiments.

title: In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization
abstract: Multi-fidelity learning uses low-fidelity information (coarse-scale PDE models) together with limited high-fidelity data (fine-scale solutions) to obtain high-accuracy PDE solutions. It is a data-driven approach to downscale reduced-order models to solve PDEs efficiently and accurately. Standard multi-fidelity learning focuses on one operator or PDE; given a new PDE, retraining using additional coarse-fine solution pairs may be required, which is costly. In this work, we propose an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework for learning multiple multi-fidelity operators with one shared model. The model is trained using paired low- and high-fidelity examples as demonstrations from multiple operators, together with a new coarse-scale solution query, to predict the corresponding fine-scale solution. Once trained, given a new PDE operator, a few (fewer than five) coarse-fine demonstration pairs, and a low-cost coarse query, the model predicts the corresponding fine-scale solution without fine-tuning. When the target operator appears in the training dataset but has a different prediction goal, such as predicting beyond the training time interval, no additional demonstrations are needed. Instead, the model uses training coarse-fine pairs from that PDE and information from other training operators. Testing then only requires generating a low-cost coarse-scale solution query, without fine-tuning. Notably, our smallest model contains only 255,364 trainable parameters, corresponding to approximately 456 parameters per training operator for 560 operators.

authors: with Appendix joint with Daniel Apsley
title: Test ideals can be computed by boundaries
abstract: Let $R$ be a normal $F$-finite ring of characteristic $p>0$. We show that one effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $Δ$, with $K_R+Δ$ $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$, computes the big test ideal. This answers a question of Schwede and Smith. More generally, we prove their conjecture that test module of a Cartier algebra acting on an ideal is the test module of a single map $ψ$ in the algebra and even the image of $ψ$. We prove a global version for schemes quasi-projective over an $F$-finite local ring as well. In particular, every such normal, locally strongly $F$-regular scheme admits an effective boundary $Δ$ for which $(X,Δ)$ is locally strongly $F$-regular and $K_X+Δ$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$.

title: A $p$-Laplacian Problem with Slightly Subcritical Regularly Varying Nonlinearity
abstract: We study a quasilinear elliptic problem involving the $p$-laplacian operator and a slightly subcritical nonlinearity with a sign-changing weight. We assume that the slightly subcritical nonlinearity is a regularly varying function at zero and at infinity, which are not necessarily asymptotic to a power at infinity. We state sufficient conditions which guarantee a Palais-Smale condition. We also provide a bifurcation theorem for these nonlinearities, which allow us to state the existence of a bifurcated branch of positive solutions, containing a turning point, and multiplicity of solutions.

title: Prescribed mean curvature surfaces of Riemann minimal type
abstract: We construct analogues of Riemann minimal examples among surfaces in the Euclidean 3-space whose mean curvature is given by a prescribed function on the unit sphere in terms of their Gauss map. Specifically, we obtain a 2-parameter family of complete, properly embedded surfaces foliated by circles and straight lines and invariant under a nontrivial translation.

title: The geometry of Floquet states
abstract:
This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians.
  The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.

title: Solution of Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem
abstract: In 1991, Laczkovich asked whether every measurable set of positive measure in $\mathbb R^d$ can be mapped onto a cube with a Lipschitz map. We show that the answer is positive for every $d$. Our results also give a positive answer for Kolmogorov's problem on contractions onto polygons with small measure loss in the case of Jordan measurable sets.

title: Order invariance of the generalized Rosenblatt transform on standard Borel spaces
abstract: The Rosenblatt transform maps a random vector to independent uniform variables through successive conditional distribution functions; for laws on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with atomless conditional distributions and a fixed order of the coordinates, it is the almost surely unique monotone triangular map with this property. For a fixed reference law, transform-based tests remain valid under every fixed admissible order, but that choice can still affect their statistical power. We extend the generalized Rosenblatt transform to laws on countable products of standard Borel spaces, which requires, in addition to an order on the index set, a total order on each component space. For fixed orders, we establish identification and uniqueness results for this extended generalized Rosenblatt transform (EGRT) that parallel those for the classical transform. We then characterize order dependence in two senses: first demonstrating conditions under which the EGRT is invariant under linear extensions of prescribed partial orders, and second showing that under every admissible order the output of the EGRT retains all the statistical information from the input observations over reference-dominated families. We close with a brief discussion of what these results mean for the relationship between order choice and goodness-of-fit testing.

title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
abstract: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper étale correspondence $Ω:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(Ω)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.

title: Sharp global stability for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation near equilibrium
abstract: We study the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation near a global Maxwellian and have found the bifurcation between the stability and instability in $H_{x}^{s}$ Sobolev space. We prove a strong-weak type instability result in the $s<1$ regularity regime, and establish the global stability under the regularity $s>1$ via the interplay between the dissipation and dispersive effects. In this intricate competition of dispersion, dissipation, large-velocity growth, and the asymmetric nature of the gain and loss terms, we prove that the instability is jointly generated by the dispersive effect and the loss term structure. To reach the sharp regularity for the global stability, we incorporate the dispersive effect into the dissipative energy framework for the analysis near equilibrium. This hence concludes sharp threshold and provides a complete characterization of global well-posedness near equilibrium.

title: Examples of rigid Twistor D-modules
abstract: The well-established theory of D-modules gives a framework to study linear differential equations from the perspective of algebraic geometry. A significant advancement in this theory has been the introduction of Twistor D-modules by Claude Sabbah and Takuro Mochizuki: These objects expose inherent, but hidden information of the underlying differential equations in an elegant way. We explain the foundational concepts of Twistor D-modules and give concrete examples of these objects. We introduce a notion of rigidity for Twistor D-modules, which these examples fulfill. We conclude with a certain algebraicity conjecture about rigid Twistor D-modules, which we prove in a special case.

title: Existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for weighted complete intersections
abstract: We prove that every smooth well formed Fano or Calabi-Yau weighted complete intersection admits a nef-partition. As an application, we establish the existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for all such Fano weighted complete intersections.

title: A Primer on Instanton Physics - A Short Course
abstract: These six lectures, delivered at the University of New Brunswick 6-21 October 2026, are an introduction to instantons in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory for senior undergraduate and beginning graduate students. The first four lectures deal solely with particle mechanics, building the necessary background for the last two that cover applications in semi-classical field theory.

title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
abstract: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ there exists a finite generating set $A$ such that $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;A)$ is contractible for all $t\ge 1$. We prove this as a special case of a more general result about certain groups. Let $G$ be a group and $H$ a subgroup. A subgroup $F\le G$ is a supplement of $H$ in $G$ if $G=HF$. We prove that for $H\le G$ with $F$ a supplement of $H$ in $G$, for generating sets $A_H$ and $A_G$ of $H$ and $G$ satisfying certain conditions involving $F$, the Vietoris-Rips complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;A_G)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A_H)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$. In particular this applies to affine Coxeter groups, since free abelian groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. Beyond these general results, we also investigate affine Coxeter groups $W_a$ specifically using the standard generating set $S$, and prove contractibility of $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ for large enough $t$.

title: Projected Brion's theorem
abstract: We present an analogue of Brion's theorem for the projected integer-point transform. Brion's theorem writes the integer-point transform of a rational polyhedron $P$ as the sum of the rational functions associated to its vertex cones. The pushforward $π_*$ along a lattice projection $π$ turns the transform of $P$ into the generating function of the numbers of lattice points in the fibres of $π$. We group the vertices of $P$ into contracted classes, generated by the edges whose direction $π$ kills, and show that the sum of the rational functions associated to the vertex cones in a contracted class can be pushed forward along $π$, yielding a rational function decomposition of the projected integer-point transform. For a lattice polytope, the classes correspond to the connected components of the fixed locus of the associated toric variety under the action of a subtorus, and our formula resembles the localization formula for this subtorus. We use this decomposition to provide an explicit formula for the projected integer-point transform of a linear family of polytopes. We illustrate this result with families of Gelfand--Zetlin and string polytopes.

title: Simple Cuts, Simple Landscapes: Global Synchronization and Rank-Width-One Matrices
abstract: We study how the structure of the coupling matrix $\boldsymbol A$ shapes the energy landscape $E_{\boldsymbol A}(\boldsymbolθ)=-\frac12\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\cos(θ_i-θ_j)$ of the Kuramoto model. We prove that, for an entrywise nonnegative coupling matrix $\boldsymbol A$ with connected support, if $\boldsymbol A$ has rank-width one over $\mathbb R$, then the landscape is "simple", i.e., every local minimum is synchronized. The rank-width bound is sharp, and the result has many interesting implications for global synchronization. The key contribution of this work is to uncover a structural synchronization mechanism beyond the rank-one regime, which has served as a starting point for earlier analyses of global synchronization.

title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and give examples of smooth connected spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.

title: Regular closedness off the real axis for root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
abstract: For each integer $h\ge1$, let $Z_h$ be the closure in the complex plane of the roots of nonzero integer polynomials whose coefficients have absolute value at most $h$, with no degree restriction. We prove that $Z_h$ is regular closed off the real axis: every non-real point of $Z_h$ is a limit of interior points. The root-closure identification of Espigulé and Juher, for which we include a self-contained proof, shows that the same closure arises from monic polynomials and that outside the closed unit disc it is the connectedness locus of $h+1$ equally spaced collinear similarities. The main step proves that this locus is regular closed off the real axis; this was known for $h=1$ by Calegari, Koch and Walker, for $h\ge19$, and inside an explicit lens. The symmetry $z\mapsto1/z$ then gives the full-plane statement. The proof adapts the method of traps of Calegari, Koch and Walker, using a neighboring-piece criterion, short chains through consecutive digits, and Rouché's theorem. We also classify the convex attractors.

title: Compactification of parabolic Hermitian--Einstein moduli spaces on complex surfaces
abstract: Let $\overline{X}$ be a compact complex surface with a Gauduchon metric, and let $D\subset\overline{X}$ be a smooth connected divisor. We construct an Uhlenbeck compactification of the moduli space of rank-two parabolic Hermitian--Einstein connections with prescribed holomorphic determinant.

title: Proof of the conjecture about inequality of $1/H$-variations of fractional Brownian motion along the equidistant and the Lebesgue partitions
abstract: We give an analytic proof of the comparison conjectured by Das, Łochowski, Matsuda and Perkowski for the fractional Brownian level-crossing constant: for standard fractional Brownian motion, $c_H>\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $0<H<1/2$ and $c_H<\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $1/2<H<1$, where $Z\sim N(0,1)$. At $H=1/2$, both constants equal one. The main tool is Gaussian comparison under ordering of increment variances. It applies because truncated variation is translation invariant and lattice-submodular, as follows from its minimum-total-variation characterization. A tangent variogram produces Brownian motion with an independent Gaussian drift on the upper side, and a periodic Brownian bridge on the lower side. The former has an explicit stationary reflection rate. For the latter we calculate an integrated cyclic crossing count by first-passage Laplace transforms. Elementary hyperbolic, theta-series, and Gamma inequalities then give strict comparisons on both full parameter ranges. No numerical integration, simulation, interval certificate, or quantitative local expansion at $H=1/2$ is used.

title: A Retrospective-Approximation Interior-Point Method
abstract: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for solving nonlinearly constrained continuous optimization problem instances wherein the objective function is defined by an expectation over a random variable argument and the constraints include inequalities (and perhaps equalities) involving functions that may be nonconvex. The algorithm combines a retrospective-approximation strategy for handling the objective and an interior-point approach for handling the constraints. In each iteration of an outer loop, the objective is approximated by an empirical average over a set of realizations of the random variable argument and the resulting sampled problem is solved with an interior-point method that allows inexact search-direction computations for computational flexibility. Termination conditions for the interior-point method are tailored for those needed for convergence guarantees by the outer loop. Over the outer loop, the sample set is updated adaptively in such a manner that convergence guarantees for solving the original optimization problem can be assured. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the proposed algorithm can outperform competing methods that have comparable theoretical guarantees.

title: Amitsur groups of Imprimitive Fano Threefolds
abstract: We classify possible Amitsur groups of smooth imprimitive Fano threefolds defined over $\cc$ that admit a faithful action of a finite group.

title: A First-Order Phase Transition in Spin-Imbalanced BCS Theory of Superconductivity
abstract: We study a translation-invariant BCS functional of superconductivity for a system of spin-$1/2$ fermions with spin-dependent chemical potentials, $μ_+\neqμ_-$. Numerical work of Caldas and Mota and analytical work of Freiji, Hainzl, and Seiringer has suggested an unusual first-order phase transition in spin-imbalanced BCS models, in which the normal state becomes globally unstable while remaining locally stable. Here, we prove that a first-order phase transition occurs in such spin-imbalanced BCS functionals. For each sufficiently small fixed spin imbalance and sufficiently low temperature, there is a coexistence coupling $λ_{\mathrm{fo}}$ strictly below the linear-stability threshold $λ_{\mathrm{lin}}$ of the normal state at which the Cooper pair density exhibits a nonzero jump and the minimized energy has a kink. The methodological insight is a coercivity estimate obtained by decomposing the BCS energy minimization into two parts, where the ``inner'' problem minimizes over the one-particle density matrices at fixed pairing and can be exactly solved by a Legendre--Fenchel transform.

title: Anchored isoperimetry in percolation
abstract: We show that, for any infinite transitive graph $G$, the infinite cluster after supercritical percolation almost surely inherits the anchored isoperimetry of $G$. Moreover, the probability of violating the corresponding isoperimetric inequality decays exponentially in the isoperimetric profile of the host graph. This was previously known only for nonamenable transitive graphs, $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and very recently for transitive graphs of polynomial growth. Our proof combines the thinning-and-sprinkling technique with a novel counting algorithm.

title: Controllability of Nonlocal Partial Differential Equations
abstract: This chapter provides a short survey of recent developments in the controllability of nonlocal partial differential equations. We first review controllability results for evolution equations involving nonlocal spatial operators. Particular attention is devoted to unique continuation properties, observability inequalities, and Carleman estimates in establishing controllability properties. We then discuss controllability issues for partial differential equations with memory terms, highlighting how memory effects influence reachable states, null controllability, and exact controllability. We review and compare various analytical techniques developed to overcome the difficulties arising from the nonlocal structure. We also provide a critical assessment of some of these methods. Throughout the chapter, we emphasize the interplay between controllability and observability, the adaptation of classical control methods to nonlocal settings, and the distinctive phenomena that arise in comparison with local equations. We then discuss geometric inequalities and their role in the controllability of diffusion models. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current challenges and several open problems, aiming to provide directions for future research.

title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
abstract: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

title: A Gaschütz Lemma for linear algebraic groups with applications to the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
abstract: The classical Gaschütz Lemma states that for a surjective morphism $G\to H$ of finite groups, generators $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ of $H$ can be lifted to generators $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ of $G$, provided that $G$ can be generated by $d$ elements. We prove an analog of this statement for linear algebraic groups. This has applications to the algebraic-geometric theory of linear differential equations: We show that every regular singular differential embedding problem over the rational function field has a regular singular solution. We also establish a purely algebraic variant of the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence on the punctured projective line that works over any countable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.

title: Anisotropic error estimates for the $L^{2}$-projection onto discontinuous finite element spaces
abstract: Anisotropic error estimates are determined for the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto discontinuous finite element spaces in two and three dimensions. These estimates are determined in $W^{m,p}$-seminorms, in which $p \in [1,\infty]$ and $0 \le m \le k+1$, where $k \ge 0$ is the polynomial degree. The analysis relies on a geometric condition that is equivalent to the maximum angle condition. As an application, an apriori error analysis is presented for a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin discretization of the Poisson problem on two and three dimensional anisotropic meshes.

title: Homogeneous polynomial approximation on symmetric convex bodies: A proof of Kroó's conjecture
abstract: We resolve Kroó's 2004 conjecture on homogeneous polynomial approximation in every dimension, without smoothness or curvature assumptions. For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, every continuous real function on $\partial K$ is uniformly approximated by sums of homogeneous polynomials of degrees $n$ and $n+1$ as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, approximation of the constant function by homogeneous polynomials of degree $2n$ is uniform over all such bodies in each fixed dimension. Via homogenization, we also resolve Kroó's 2019 weighted approximation conjecture for every convex admissible weight on Euclidean space. The key construction produces homogeneous polynomials with a common Gaussian boundary profile and localization errors controlled by arbitrary polynomial weights. Its analytic core is a weighted Gaussian approximation theorem: for \(d\ge2\), sufficiently broad Gaussians on $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ can be approximated by $e^{-f}F$, where $f$ is nonnegative, convex and Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, and $F$ is a Schwartz function with Fourier support in an arbitrarily small ball about the origin. Small Fourier support allows Taylor truncation to a lower degree, while the remainder enforces decay through homogenization. We then use positive spherical quadrature and degree raising to yield the full approximation theorem.

title: On strongly FP-injective accessibility and weakly FP-projective periodicity
abstract: Accessibility results are established for (Cartan-Eilenberg) strongly FP-injective complexes, by first proving the accessibility of Strongly FP-injective modules and then utilizing the pseudopullback theorem. We also prove that every acyclic complex of weakly FP-projective modules has weakly FP-projective cycles over left $<\aleph_m$-coherent rings for a non-negative integer $m$. This is achieved by introducing the cotorsion pairs $\bigl(\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj,\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}inj\bigr)$, cogenerated by all $\aleph_m$-presentable weakly FP-projective modules, and proving that acyclic complexes of modules from the class $\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj$ have weakly FP-projective cycles for every non-negative integer $m$.

title: Characterization of sets in metric spaces where the big Lipschitz derivative is infinite
abstract: Let $X$ be a metric space without isolated points. In this paper we prove that $E$ is a $G_δ$-set in $X$ if and only if there exists a continuous function $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ whose big Lipschitz derivative is infinite precisely on $E$. To this end, we introduce a new generalization of the classical Takagi function to the setting of metric spaces.

title: Central limit theorems for high-dimensional ridge regression under uniform subsampling
abstract: We study ridge regression based on uniformly subsampled observations in high-dimensional linear models, where the number of predictors and the sample size grow proportionally. Subsampling is implemented through independent Bernoulli indicators with a common selection probability. We establish central limit theorems for linear contrasts of the ridge estimator, allowing for non-Gaussian predictors and general population covariance matrices. Under a vanishing-signal assumption, we obtain an explicit bias correction in the isotropic case and develop consistent estimators of the asymptotic variances. These results enable asymptotically valid tests for linear contrasts of the regression parameter in the isotropic setting. Our proofs exploit the resolvent representation of the ridge estimator and combine leave-one-out arguments with deterministic equivalents from random matrix theory.

title: The Birthday Problem and the Birthday Person Problem: Intuition, Probability and Cryptographic Applications
abstract: The present work discusses the birthday problem and the birthday person problem, two classical problems in probability theory widely used to illustrate situations in which human intuition diverges from mathematical results. Taking the work of [1] as its main reference, the study analyzes the probability of birthday coincidences within groups of people, considering a year with 365 days and assuming that all birth dates are equally likely. The birthday problem seeks to determine the probability that at least two people in a group share the same birthday, showing that, even in relatively small groups, the probability of a coincidence increases rapidly due to the large number of possible pairwise comparisons among individuals. In contrast, the birthday person problem investigates the probability that a previously selected person shares the same birthday as another member of the group. This probability increases more slowly, since the number of relevant comparisons is restricted to the pairs formed by the selected person and the remaining members of the group. Despite the interpretative differences, both problems share a similar mathematical foundation based on combinatorial analysis and probability theory. In addition to the theoretical development, numerical results and graphical representations are presented to illustrate the behavior of the probabilities involved and to visualize how the likelihood of coincidences increases as the number of people grows. Finally, applications related to computing and cryptography are discussed, particularly the study of collisions in hash functions and the so-called birthday attack. The discussion highlights the importance of probabilistic reasoning in understanding apparently unlikely phenomena, while also emphasizing how the growth in the number of possible combinations directly influences the results obtained.

title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
abstract: We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang's descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, Kähler--Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture.

title: The convolution product is generally not an open map
abstract: We show that the convolution product $\ell^1(G)\times \ell^1(G)\to \ell^1(G)$ is not an open map if $G$ is either non-abelian or contains an element of infinite order. The case $G=\mathbb Z$ solves a problem posed by Kania and Maślany.

title: Models of n-dimensional categories as $n\to\infty$
abstract: We verify that saturated complicial sets model the right limit of the $\infty$-categories of $(\infty,n)$-categories, whereas the canonical comparison with the left limit is not an equivalence. By contrast the category of strict $ω$-categories is equivalent to both the right and left limits of the categories of strict $n$-categories.

title: On a family of domains associated with $μ$-synthesis in $M_2(\mathbb C)$
abstract: In this paper, we show that the domain $\mathbb H$ serves as a unifying domain for $\mathbb G_2, \mathbb E$ and $\mathbb P$ by proving that each of these domains is an analytic retract of $\mathbb H$. Further, we prove that the bidisc $\mathbb D^2$ and the Euclidean unit ball $\mathbb B_2$ are also analytic retracts of $\mathbb H$. Then the rational $\overline{\mathbb H}$-inner functions, i.e., the rational maps from $\mathbb D$ into $\overline{\mathbb H}$ whose boundary values lie in the distinguished boundary of $\mathbb H$, are characterized. Two different versions of Schwarz type lemma for $\mathbb H$ are established of which one provides a necessary and sufficient condition. Finally, capitalizing on the theory of $\mathbb H$, we present alternative proofs to a few known results on $\mathbb P$ from the literature.

title: Larger Crossing Families
abstract: We give the first explicit constant for crossing families of linear size by showing that every set of $n$ points in general position in the plane contains a crossing family of size approximately $\frac{n}{79}$. We further identify some conditions where there are even larger crossing families. The first such condition forbids the existence of a large different pattern, namely non-convex 4-clusters: We show that every point set contains either a large non-convex 4-cluster or a large crossing family. The second condition is the existence of many crossings: We give a bound for the size of a crossing family in terms of the number of crossings of the complete geometric graph drawn on the point set.

title: Approximating the poles of a Painlevé V transcendent for the Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel
abstract: The Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel has an expression as an integral containing a Painlevé transcendent $r$ satisfying Painlevé V, in the same way that the Fredholm determinant of the Airy kernel has an expression involving the Hastings-McLeod solution of Painlevé II. In this paper we use Padé approximation to approximate the poles of this Painlevé transcendent $r$ in the complex plane. We use Padé approximation near $0$, Hermite-Padé approximation near $0$ and two-point Padé approximation near $0$ and infinity.
