title: A Feasible-Direction-Type Method for Nonconvex Optimization with Infeasible Starts
abstract: We develop an infeasible-start extension of the Topkis--Veinott feasible-direction method for nonconvex composite optimization. At each main iteration, a strongly convex local model is used to obtain objective descent while limiting increases in constraint violation. A separate feasibility-reduction step is invoked when feasibility improvement is needed. Under a feasibility-reduction condition, we establish the standard first-order rate for reducing the Fritz John residual and constraint violation. We then verify that both proximal-gradient and regularized Gauss--Newton methods applied to minimizing the squared constraint-violation function satisfy the required feasibility-reduction property under a Polyak--Łojasiewicz condition. Numerical experiments compare the reduction methods, including an experimental prox-linear variant, and compare the scalar-regularized and curvature-enhanced subproblem formulations.

title: Intrinsic Non-Reductive Geometric Invariant Theory and Moduli Spaces of Principal Bundles with Non-Reductive Structure Groups
abstract: We prove the existence of moduli spaces for algebraic stacks with a weak action of $Θ= [\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m]$ (including stacks of filtered objects and unstable $Θ$-strata) for which the center admits a good moduli space and the retraction to the center has flat, finitely presented relative inertia, providing a stack-intrinsic generalization of the existence of non-reductive Geometric Invariant Theory quotients. As an application, we construct quasi-projective coarse moduli spaces of principal bundles over a smooth projective curve with non-reductive structure groups, including moduli spaces of Ramanathan unstable principal bundles of fixed Harder--Narasimhan type.

title: Representations and $n$-universality of hermitian lattices over local and number fields
abstract: Let $E/F$ be a quadratic field extension. For any positive integer $n$ an integral hermitian form over $E/F$ is called $n$-universal if it represents all integral hermitian forms of rank $n$ over $E/F$. We study $n$-universal hermitian forms when $F$ is a local field of characteristic $\neq 2$ or a number field. In the local case, we characterize $n$-universal integral hermitian forms and provide finite criterion sets for $n$-universality. In the number field case, we show that an indefinite integral hermitian form is $n$-universal if and only if it is $n$-universal everywhere locally.

title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
abstract:
We develop a framework for pure and mixed graphon colourings and use it to study the limiting behaviour of graph partition parameters under cut convergence. Pure colourings correspond to measurable partitions, while mixed colourings assign a probability distribution on the colour set to each point. We develop the representation, equivalence and convergence theory, and show that every mixed graphon colouring has an equivalent pure representative, possibly on a different probability space. For each fixed finite colour set, we establish compactness and describe the topology of coloured graph limits using the cut norm on graphons and the weak-$*$ topology on colourings. The usual coloured cut distance characterises convergence for pure colourings, but not for general mixed colourings.
  As applications, we prove that the Cheeger constant and modularity converge to their mixed graphon counterparts along cut-convergent graph sequences whose orders tend to infinity, assuming uniformly linear minimum degree and positive limiting edge density, respectively. Both mixed functionals are invariant under graphon equivalence. We also establish their continuity in cut distance on the corresponding classes of graphons, with a stability bound for the Cheeger constant. For modularity, we further characterise coloured graphons attaining extremal modularity values and prove attainment of the mixed optimum for each fixed number of colours. We also exhibit a graphon whose modularity supremum is not attained by any finite colouring.

title: Composition factors and finite representation type
abstract: We prove that an Artin algebra has finite representation type if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture on composition factors and finite representation type recorded by Auslander, Reiten and Smalo.

title: Dimensions of Fano schemes of lines on hypersurfaces
abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbb{C}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$. We prove that an $m$-dimensional integral projective family of lines sweeping a variety of dimension $y$ satisfies $m\le\max\{2y-d-1,n-3\}$. This proves the de Jong-Debarre conjecture for $d\le n$ and the Beheshti-Starr bound for lines on smooth hypersurfaces for $d\ge n+1$.

title: Small-time Wasserstein action for KPZ and $Φ^4_3$
abstract: We determine the leading small-time Wasserstein action of the full spatial laws of centered KPZ and dynamical $Φ^4_3$, both started from zero. The leading term is Gaussian, with an explicit heat-trace constant. A common comparison also determines the ratio of length to displacement. For KPZ, a first-chaos cancellation yields a quadratic coupling error. For $Φ^4_3$, two weighted entropies and an adjoint estimate give comparison bounds uniform in the spectral cutoff. Integrating a Gaussian rotation gives a differentiable realization of the full law; the comparison holds at every positive time.

title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
abstract: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.

title: Solitons on Statistical Manifolds and Their Submanifolds
abstract:
Statistical manifolds, introduced by Amari in information geometry, carry a pair of dual torsion-free connections $(
abla,
abla^{*})$ together with a Riemannian metric. In this chapter we survey the theory of \emph{statistical solitons}, that is, vector fields and constants that solve the Ricci-soliton equation simultaneously for $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$, together with the statistical analogue of almost quasi-Yamabe solitons. We discuss two principal settings: (i) statistical warped products $\R	imes_f N_2$ and $N_1	imes_f\R$ for (pseudo) Riemannian manifolds $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$, where the soliton equation constrains the warping function; and (ii) statistical submanifolds of Kenmotsu statistical manifolds, where the position of the Reeb field $ξ$ relative to the submanifold and the presence of concircular or concurrent vector fields determine the Einstein, $η$-Einstein or quasi-Einstein character of the submanifold. We further review the results of Blaga and Chen on gradient solitons and statistical structures, in particular the connections $
abla^θ$ defined by a $1$-form, volume formulas and bounds for the Ricci tensor. We also describe Chen-type inequalities for statistical warped product submanifolds, which give the extrinsic context in which such solitons live. Key steps of the proofs, remarks on the sharpness of hypotheses, worked examples, and open problems are included.

title: The equal norm Grassmannian: topology and applications to frame fields
abstract: Given an orientable rank-$d$ vector bundle over a $d$-manifold, the Euler class is the unique obstruction to finding a nowhere-zero section. An equal norm Parseval frame is a certain collection of sections, one of whose properties is that the lengths of each vector at each point are equal. This makes the Euler class an obvious obstruction to finding such a frame. In this work we show that this is the only obstruction so long as the number of sections is at least $2d+2$. We also identify precise obstructions when the number of sections is $2d$ and produce examples showing that for smaller numbers of sections it is sometimes impossible to find Parseval frame fields.

title: Regularity of Symbolic Powers of Polymatroidal Ideals and Supermodular Prime Intersections
abstract: Let $S=\mathbb{K}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $\mathbb{K}$. For a polymatroidal ideal $I\subseteq S$ generated in degree $d$, we prove $$ω(I^{(s)})=\operatorname{reg} I^{(s)}=\operatorname{reg} I^s=sd\qquad(s\ge1),$$ where symbolic powers use all associated primes and $ω$ denotes the largest degree of a minimal generator. Thus every symbolic power has a degree resolution. The argument uses a regularity bound for supermodular prime intersections, obtained from Takayama's formula and a homological estimate for noncover complexes. For every nonzero proper squarefree monomial ideal $L$, we also show $\operatorname{reg} L^{(s)}\le s\min\{m,λ(L)-\operatorname{ht}L+1\}$, where $m$ counts the minimal primes and $λ(L)$ is the support size, and obtain equality for skeleton and pure skeleton ideals. Finally, for every $d\ge3$, we construct a simple graphic matroid whose basis ideal is generated in degree $d$ and has a second symbolic power that is not componentwise linear.

title: Well-Posedness and Regularity for a Modified Liquid Crystal Model with Transport Noise
abstract: We prove well-posedness for a stochastic Lin-Liu model of modified liquid crystals, coupling an incompressible fluid to a director field under transport and multiplicative noise. On smooth bounded domains in two dimensions, we prove global well-posedness for energy-class initial data, provided the leading coefficient of the polynomial director potential is positive. On the torus, we establish local well-posedness in time-weighted $L^p$-$L^q$ frameworks with Besov initial data, including regimes of low and negative regularity.

title: Finite-State Time-Inhomogeneous Markov Chains Conditioned to Survive
abstract: We study conditioning on long survival for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains on finite state spaces. We assume that a sequence of substochastic transition kernels converges to an irreducible substochastic kernel and that the transition probabilities admit asymptotic expansions up to order $n^{-2}$. Under these assumptions, we construct a positive space-time harmonic function and prove that the limiting path distributions under conditioning on long survival are given by the corresponding Doob h-transform. We also investigate the long-time behavior of the resulting conditioned process. Finally, we apply our general theory to an elephant random walk, a generalized Pólya urn model, time-inhomogeneous Wright--Fisher and Moran models, and noncolliding random walks.

title: The exact digirth and out-degree bounds for $C(k,k)$-subdivision and out-forest in digraphs
abstract:
For each integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud ({\small European J. Combin., 2024}) asked for the smallest integer $g_k$ such that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two and digirth at least $g_k$ contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$. We completely resolve this problem by proving that $g_k=k+1$. Our proof relies on a refinement of Thomassen's theorem ({\small Discrete Math., 1985}) on two directed cycles intersecting in exactly one vertex: we prove that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two contains two directed cycles intersecting in exactly one arc.
  We also establish an embedding theorem for out-forests with prescribed images of their roots, under minimum out-degree and digirth conditions determined by the number of leaves and the heights of vertices in antichains. As an application, for integers $k,\ell\ge2$, we show that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least \(k\) and digirth at least \(k(\ell-1)+1\) contains \(k\) directed paths of length \(\ell\) sharing only their initial vertex, which can be prescribed arbitrarily. This improves the previous digirth bound \((k^\ell-1)/(k-1)+1\) of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud to a sharp bound.

title: PBW theorem for affine super Yangian
abstract: We prove a Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the distinguished affine super Yangian $Y=Y_{1/2,1/2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n))$, where $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. With respect to the current filtration, there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{gr}_F Y\cong U\!\left(\operatorname{uce}\!\left( \mathfrak{sl}(m|n)\otimes\mathbb C[z^{\pm1},u] \right)\right), \] where $\operatorname{uce}$ denotes the universal central extension. For any totally ordered classical basis homogeneous in parity and current degree, ordered supermonomials in arbitrary fixed filtered lifts form a vector-space basis of $Y$, with odd exponents restricted to zero or one. The proof identifies the classical presentation through Steinberg Lie superalgebras and establishes injectivity using evaluation homomorphisms, iterated coproducts in degreewise completions, and coefficientwise tensor separation.

title: Regularity theory for non-local almost minimal surfaces via Euler-Lagrange inequalities at small scales
abstract:
We extend the notion of non-local almost minimal sets introduced in [Dipierro, Valdinoci, and Villa, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2026)] by admitting lower-order powers for the remainder term.
  We combine classical techniques and a new, weaker version of the Euler-Lagrange inequalities (at a microscopic scale) to obtain $\mathcal{C}^{1,α}$-regularity for non-local almost minimal sets, up to Hausdorff dimension $n-3$.
  In turn, this formulation is well-suited for the non-local counterpart of the so-called Massari's problem for sets with prescribed mean curvature. In particular, such a generalization allows us to consider sets with $L^p$ non-local mean curvature (with $p\geq n/s$), which do not satisfy any curvature equation (neither in the classical nor in the viscosity sense).
  The results presented here lie beyond the reach of previously established methodologies. Indeed, the approach developed herein is based on a conceptual shift relative to the existing literature, which relied on a strong form of the Euler-Lagrange equation that is not available for general non-local almost minimal sets.

title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks
abstract: Lane-changing (LC) maneuvers are highly challenging vehicle interactions, with substantial implications for traffic safety and efficiency. Developing effective LC strategies for connected and automated vehicles in mixed traffic is complicated by the uncertainty associated with surrounding-vehicle behavior and the computational burden of embedding realistic prediction models within optimization schemes. To capture these complex interactions while retaining tractability, this study proposes a data-driven optimization framework that embeds neural network (NN) surrogates for safety and lateral comfort within a Bézier-curve-based trajectory planner. Specifically, the safety cost during the LC process is quantified via a surrogate composed of an input convex recurrent neural network (ICRNN) encoding the planned trajectory, a fully input convex neural network (FICNN) embedding the LC duration, and a partially input convex neural network (PICNN) decoder fusing them with historical traffic states; separately, another FICNN surrogate approximates the optimal lateral comfort cost as a function of the LC duration. Both surrogates are embedded via linear programming (LP) formulations, avoiding the binary variables required by conventional mixed-integer programming (MIP) approaches for NN-embedded optimization. We further theoretically establish their exactness at optimality and extend the framework to problems with additional analytical objective terms and multiple surrogates. Experiments on a hybrid dataset combining real-world and simulated trajectories demonstrate that the proposed method achieves surrogate accuracy competitive with unconstrained baselines while substantially improving optimization efficiency over conventional MIPs. Closed-loop simulations further show that the proposed planners markedly reduce the weighted planning cost and consistently outperform baseline methods.

title: Mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
abstract: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. We prove existence of viscosity solutions when the initial set is horizontally mean-convex and either non-characteristic, or axisymmetric and with horizontal mean curvature extending continuously across the characteristic set. A key ingredient is an approximation scheme by sets with prescribed Riemannian mean curvature, which preserves the mean-curvature bounds up to an arbitrarily small error. We further show that, when the evolving level sets form a generalized \(C^2\)-foliation, the horizontal mean curvature blows up around characteristic points. This provides an obstruction to self-similar evolution in the axisymmetric class considered above and, in particular, shows that the Pansu sphere cannot evolve self-similarly.

title: Analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient Toda systems: W-invariants and Weyl orbits
abstract: We classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient Toda systems for all simple Lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. We encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the Cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_μ$ and the mass element $q_σ$. We show that $p_μ-q_σ=wp_μ$ for some Weyl group element $w\in W$. The proof uses the Drinfeld-Sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $W$-invariants for Toda systems. Asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading Laurent coefficients of the $W$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. This agreement enables us to conclude the above Weyl-orbit result. In particular, the quadratic constraint is the local Pohozaev identity. Only with the full set of $W$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact Weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. Together with the author's explicit families in [Nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.

title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
abstract: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

title: Universality in randomly connected neural networks: old and new on a conjecture of Geman and Hwang
abstract: Randomly connected networks are ubiquitous in computer science, physics or biology. A central question is whether, and how, their collective dynamics depend on the choice of the distribution of the random couplings. Forty years ago, Geman and Hwang formulated a precise version of this \emph{universality} question for randomly connected neural networks. We come back to these conjectures, review what was proven since, provide a few new extensions and propose new conjectures in this paper. For $n$ neuron networks with couplings with a mean scaling as $1/n$ and light enough tails, two classes of limits are expected. For \emph{weakly heterogeneous} couplings, with variance $o(1/n)$, the network is predicted to converge to a McKean--Vlasov equation, and a broad literature has established this under general assumptions. For \emph{strongly heterogeneous} couplings, with variance of order $1/n$, the limit is a non-Markovian equation driven by a self-consistent Gaussian process. After landmark results for Gaussian couplings, universality was only recently established for linear interactions, while the continuous-time nonlinear case relevant to neuroscience remained open. Here, in the weakly heterogeneous regime, we prove quenched convergence on every time interval under a fourth-moment assumption only, and convergence in probability under an assumption slightly stronger than a second moment. In the strongly heterogeneous regime, we prove convergence for nonlinear interactions in continuous time, averaged over sub-Gaussian couplings and on every time interval, by a relative-entropy comparison with Gaussian couplings. We then extend the conjecture to heavy-tailed couplings, and propose a limit driven by a self-consistent $α$-stable process, for which we prove existence for every $α\in(0,2)$ and uniqueness for $α\in[1,2)$, and provide extensive numerical evidence in all three cases.

title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
abstract:
We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[θ_1,\ldots,θ_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$.
  We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.

title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
abstract: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type. We test the method on a stochastic pitchfork model and a spatial stochastic Swift-Hohenberg equation. In both models, classification improves with longer observation horizons, closer proximity to the bifurcation, stronger noise, and larger nonlinear effects. However, these conditions are also linked to a higher risk of noise-induced tipping in the subcritical case. The useful early-warning window is therefore determined by a balance between obtaining enough information to identify the bifurcation type and doing so before noise-induced tipping becomes too likely. In spatially extended systems, we find that observing the full spatial field allows classification over shorter observation horizons, and performance improves when a broader range of spatial modes contributes to the observed dynamics. Altogether, we identify the conditions under which the method can reliably distinguish between supercritical and subcritical bifurcations.

title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
abstract:
Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases. For example, a theorem of Buekenhout and Van Maldeghem from 1994 proves Kantor's conjecture under the stronger assumption that $G$ acts distance-transitively on the set of points of $\mathcal{Q}$.
  In this paper, we study Kantor's conjecture in the setting where $G$ acts primitively on both the points and lines of $\mathcal{Q}$. Here a theorem of Bamberg et al. implies that $G$ is almost simple with socle $X$ a finite simple group of Lie type, and several special cases where the Lie rank of $X$ is at most $2$ have recently been settled in a sequence of papers. Our main theorem resolves the problem for all almost simple groups of Lie type, thereby completing the proof of Kantor's conjecture for generalized quadrangles with a flag-transitive automorphism group acting primitively on points and lines.

title: Inhomogeneous Geometric Last Passage Percolation and the $q$-deformed Jacobi Unitary Ensemble
abstract: We study directed last passage percolation with geometric weights in a spatially inhomogeneous environment. We derive an explicit limit shape and establish fluctuation limits for the passage time, showing that, depending on the strength of the inhomogeneity, the limiting fluctuations are governed by Fredholm determinants associated with either the Airy or Bessel kernel. Our approach is based on an exact relation between the passage time and the smallest particle of the $q$-deformed Jacobi unitary ensemble ($q$-JUE). As part of our analysis, we derive the macroscopic limiting density of the $q$-JUE, which provides a natural $q$-deformation of the classical Wachter distribution, as well as of the limiting distribution of the Meixner ensemble. We further establish Airy and Bessel scaling limits for the smallest particle, which are of independent interest.

title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
abstract: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper. As in earlier work, the proof proceeds by showing that all rank 3 Coxeter arrangements are clean arrangements, meaning that every biclosed set is weakly separated from its complement by a hyperplane. As a consequence, we also deduce Dyer's Conjecture A for all rank 3 Coxeter groups, which asserts that cover relations in extended weak order are given by toggling a single root.

title: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory
abstract: We establish a direct connection between the entanglement bootstrap and the Doplicher--Haag--Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, we prove Haag duality and establish a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, we further construct an affine bijection from density matrices on the entanglement-bootstrap fusion space to normalized positive intertwiners in the corresponding operator-algebraic fusion channel. These results connect the entropic and operator-algebraic descriptions of anyons directly, without passing through exactly solvable lattice models.

title: Localization of generators of Markov processes via the Dynkin operator
abstract: In this article, we consider a Feller process whose resolvent has the strong Feller property. Using the Dynkin operator of this process, we define local realizations of the generator on an open subset $U$ of its state space. In particular, this allows us to describe the generator of the process killed upon leaving a regular, open subset $U$ as a realization of a maximal operator subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. Besides the definition via the Dynkin operator, we also consider other possible definitions of such a local realization: a definition in terms of the unkilled semigroup, a definition based on approximation with elements of the generator and a probabilistic definition using martingales. Under mild additional assumptions, we prove that all these definitions are equivalent.

title: Modified Scattering for Infinite-Rank Hartree--Fock Equations
abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the Hartree--Fock equation with Coulomb interaction in dimensions $d\geq2$ for small initial density matrices of possibly infinite rank. We prove global well-posedness and modified scattering governed by a resonant Hartree-Fock equation. Our approach is based on the half-density formulation and a final-state construction for the resonant dynamics. We also characterize the stationary states of the resonant Hartree--Fock equation and prove that ordinary linear scattering fails when the initial density matrix has rank at least two. These results extend long-range modified scattering to genuinely operator-valued infinite-rank Hartree-Fock evolution. Despite cancellation between the direct and exchange terms, the long-range effect persists, with resonant dynamics evolving on the same logarithmic time scale as in the Hartree equation.

title: Transfer kernels and the Schur multiplier
abstract: In this article we prove that if $H$ is a normal subgroup of a finite group $G$ with $G/H$ cyclic, then the kernel of the transfer map $G/G' \longrightarrow H/H'$ equals $(G:H)$ times the order of the cokernel of the natural map $M(H) \longrightarrow M(G)$.

title: Matrix orthogonal polynomials related to diffference operators for $L$-orthogonal polynomials
abstract: The difference operator $J$ arising from the higher order occurrence for the $L$-orthogonal polynomials is studied using various families of matrix orthogonal polynomials. The matrix orthogonal polynomials determine the polar decomposition of $J$ and its adjoint $J^\ast$ considered as operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$. The special case of symmetric $J$ leads to the case where the matrix polynomials reduce to diagonal matrix polynomials. The example of the symmetric case with constant coefficients for $L=2$ is discussed in detail.

title: Unique Positive Extremals and Sharp Stability Constants for Singular Moser-Trudinger Inequalities
abstract:
We combine spectral perturbation with orthogonal transformations in $H_0^1(Ω)$ to study singular Moser-Trudinger inequalities under the energy constraint $\int_Ω|\nabla u|^2\,dx\le1$, where $Ω$ is a smooth bounded planar domain containing the origin. For the weight $|x|^{-2β}$, $0\leβ<1$, the positive maximizer is unique for small $α>0$, and the sharp global stability constant satisfies \[
  C_α=\fracα{2}
  \left(\frac1{μ_1}-\frac1{μ_2}\right)+O(α^2),
  \qquad α\downarrow0, \] where $μ_1<μ_2$ are the first two weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues. We compute the second asymptotic coefficient by a weighted quartic maximization on the second eigenspace, even when the second eigenvalue is multiple. An exact reduction to the sphere orthogonal to the maximizer identifies the attaining functions and yields a limiting global-to-local ratio of $1/2$. On the disk, the energy derivative with respect to the central value characterizes radial constrained degeneracy and yields finitely many exceptional normalized parameters. Combined with known critical uniqueness and nondegeneracy, this gives uniform quadratic stability near criticality, while compactness and analytic reduction yield finite-power stability throughout the admissible range.

title: The Polynomially Self-repelling Motion
abstract: [Kosygina et al. 2023] showed that the rescaled polynomially self-repelling walk does not converge to any Brownian motion perturbed at extrema (BMPE). Motivated by this result, we introduce an explicit candidate for the scaling limit, the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM), and study its properties. The construction relies on a new family of continuous stochastic flows, called polynomially self-repelling flows, introduced in [Yu 2026]. A key ingredient in relating the limiting process of the rescaled walk to the PSRM is a joint Ray-Knight theorem for rescaled local time processes, extending the classical Ray-Knight theorems of [Tóth 1996].

title: Lifting mod $p$ Galois representations over local fields
abstract: Let $K$ be a local field with absolute Galois group $G_{K}$ and let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$. We prove that every continuous representation $G_K\to \operatorname{GL}_{n}(k)$ lifts to a continuous representation $G_K\to\operatorname{GL}_{n}(W(k))$ where $W(k)$ is the ring of infinite Witt vectors over $k$.

title: Large tight components and Dirac thresholds for tight Hamilton cycles
abstract: For every odd integer $r\ge1$, let $q_r=1-2^{-r}\binom r{(r-1)/2}$. We show that, for every odd $r\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph with at least $q_r\binom nr$ edges contains a tight component with at least $(1/2-o(1))\binom nr$ edges. This confirms a conjecture posed by Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2024. As an application, for every odd $r\ge1$ and every integer $k\ge\lceil r(3-2q_r)\rceil$, we prove that the asymptotic minimum $(k-r)$-degree threshold for a tight Hamilton cycle in a $k$-uniform hypergraph is $q_r$, which settles, in this range, another conjecture of Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2022 stating that the lower-bound construction due to Han and Zhao is asymptotically optimal. Our proof combines an isoperimetric inequality for Johnson graphs with a Kruskal-Katona-type theorem, which is of independent interest.

title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
abstract: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.

title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $φ$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $ρ$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_ρ$, $\overlineΔ_ρ$, $IC_ρ$, and $δ_ρ$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}π$, $i_{b\sharp}π$, $i_{b\sharp!}π$, and $i_{b!*}π$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $π$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $φ$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.

title: Invariant means, coset correct means and the Hahn-Banach Theorem
abstract: We show that, in ZF set theory, the existence of "coset correct means" on all groups is equivalent to the Hahn-Banach Theorem, as well as to the existence of invariant means on abelian groups.

title: Variable Metric Three Operator Splitting
abstract:
To minimize the sum $f + g + h$ of three convex functions when $f$ is differentiable with a Lipschitz-continuous gradient,
  we present a proximal algorithm, variable-metric three operator splitting (VMTOS), a generalization of the three operator splitting (TOS) scheme of Davis and Yin.
  We establish convergence guarantees by controlling changes in the metric.
  The smallest saddle-point residual among the first $k$ primal-dual iterates is $\tilde{O}(k^{-1/2})$.
  When $f$ and the convex conjugate $h^*$ are strongly convex and the accepted metrics and their inverses are uniformly bounded, the rate improves to $\tilde{O}(β^k)$ for some $β\in (0,1)$.
  We develop a practical Barzilai--Borwein update for diagonal metrics that satisfies our bound on metric changes.
  Under the same strong convexity assumptions, this update guarantees the required uniform metric bounds, yielding R-linear convergence.
  Numerical experiments on benchmark optimization problems show that VMTOS is competitive with other proximal algorithms.

title: Uncertainty principles as forcing mechanisms
abstract:
In this note we first consider the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. We show that it acts as a {\bf forcing mechanism} in the following sense. Real functions that approach its limit are close to Gaussian distributions, with proximity both in the sense of total variation distance and Wasserstein-1 distance.
  We next consider the uncertainty principle for functions defined on finite Abelian groups, and show that it acts as a forcing mechanism in the following sense. Functions that approach its limit are close (after translation and modulation by a complex exponential) to indicator functions of some subgroup, with proximity measured in ${\mathbb {L}}^1$-norm.

title: Exh subspaces of bounded variation spaces generated by submeasures
abstract: In the present paper we are building one more bridge between the theory of ideals on the set of natural numbers and the theory of spaces of functions of bounded variation. It is already known that $F_σ$ ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Fin}(φ)$, where $φ$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a nice generalization of different concepts from the theory of functions of bounded variation (Waterman variation and Chanturya classes). In this paper we show that analytic P-ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Exh}(φ)$, where $φ$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a generalization of spaces of functions continuous in $Λ$-variation. The properties of this generalization are investigated.

title: The vanishing viscosity limit for the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations around a small obstacle
abstract: We investigate the interaction between a vanishing obstacle and the vanishing viscosity limit in the setting of the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. We work in the space exterior to a small obstacle in three dimensions. We prove quantitative convergence rates, assuming that the obstacle is sufficiently small, namely smaller than a constant times the viscosity. The convergence holds as long as the solution to the limit problem is known to exist and stays sufficiently smooth. This extends the results of Iftimie, Lopes Filho and Nussenzveig Lopes to the inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations. Moreover, we can show improved convergence rates and convergence of the gradient in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

title: An asymptotic Jensen-Polya criterion for GRH
abstract: The Jensen--Pólya criterion expresses the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for Dedekind zeta-functions as a real-rootedness condition on their Jensen polynomials. Previous asymptotic results require large shifts, while computations establish real-rootedness in the Riemann case through a finite range of degrees. Here we study the unshifted family as the degree tends to infinity. For every number field $K$, we prove unconditionally that $J_{K,d}(X)$ is nonzero and has at least $d-C_K\sqrt{d\log d}$ distinct negative real zeros for all sufficiently large $d$, where $C_K>0$ depends only on $K$. Therefore, the proportion of real zeros tends to one with error $O_K(\sqrt{\log d/d})$. The main theorems have been autoformalized in Lean~4 by AxiomProver.

title: Improved LCL Equivalences and Curve Decoding Alphabet Sizes
abstract:
Local Coordinate-wise Linear (LCL) properties, introduced by Levi, Mosheiff, and Shagrithaya (2025), capture coding-theoretic properties such as list decoding and list recovery. They showed that every LCL property has the same rate threshold for random linear codes (RLC) and random Reed--Solomon codes (RRS). Brakensiek, Chen, Dhar, and Zhang (2025) extended this to random additive codes. Thus any property of all subspace design codes holds for RLCs and RRS at the same rate.
  In this work, we improve the probabilistic guarantees in the RRS local equivalence theorem and extend the equivalence to all known subspace design constructions individually. Each such construction, including folded Reed--Solomon codes, has the same LCL threshold as RLC and RRS codes. We apply these results to alphabet-size bounds for curve decoding.
  Curve decoding, introduced by Goyal and Guruswami (2025) and Carmon et al. (2026), is a row-span-constrained LCL property implying proximity gaps (PG), correlated agreement (CA), and mutual correlated agreement (MCA), relevant to IOPs and SNARKs. Informally, a rate-$R$ code $C \subset \mathbb{F}^n$ is $(\ell,δ,a,b)$-curve decodable if any degree-$\ell$ curve $u:\mathbb{F}\to\mathbb{F}^n$ that is $δ$-close to $C$ on at least $a$ points has at least $b\leq a$ nearby codewords lying on a degree-$\ell$ curve in $C$.
  Goyal and Guruswami (2025) and Goyal, Guruswami, Sun, and Wootters (2026) established curve decodability for RLC and RRS codes at radius $δ$ approaching $1-R$, but with large alphabets in $\ell$ and $η:=1-R-δ$. Using our improved LCL equivalence and rank-sensitive counting inspired by Goyal and Guruswami (2026), we exponentially improve alphabet requirements while matching the best known values of $(a,b)$. For $\ell=O(1)$, our alphabet-size bounds match the best known for list decoding, and improves results for PG, CA, and MCA.

title: Dice enterprises and polynomial approximation: uniform query tails
abstract: A binary-output dice enterprise uses independent rolls of a die with unknown face probabilities $\mathbf p$ (along with fair coin flips) to simulate a coin with bias $f(\mathbf p)$. We determine which power-law tails, uniform over the closed probability simplex, are attainable for the number $N$ of rolls. For continuous $f$ with values in $(0,1)$ and $q>0$, some enterprise for $f$ satisfies $\sup_{\mathbf p}\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf p}(N>n)=O(n^{-q})$ if and only if $f$ can be approximated uniformly by polynomials of degree $k$ with error $O(k^{-2q})$. When this holds, the same tail bound is attained by an oblivious enterprise, which chooses its number of rolls before rolling. The characterization extends to multiple dice, with total degree on a product of simplices; it then suffices to roll the dice in a fixed cyclic order. For $q>1$, these enterprises have a uniformly bounded expected number of rolls.

title: The Oriented Freudenthal Suspension Theorem
abstract: The Freudenthal Suspension Theorem states that the connectivity of the unit map $X\rightarrowΩΣX$ of the suspension-loop adjunction for a pointed space $X$ is twice the connectivity of $X$ itself. We extend this theorem to $X$ being a pointed $(\infty,\infty)$-category, i.e. an oriented space in the sense of Gepner--Heine.

title: Stationary Limits of the Point Spectrum
abstract: We give an example of a directed set whose Tukey spectrum is not closed under stationary limits. This is a counterexample to a theorem due to Isbell from the 60's. We isolate a combinatorial principle arising from our example, between stationary reflection and weak compactness.

title: Finite-size ignition laws near a vanishing branching deficit on near-regular simple graphs
abstract: We study heterogeneous bootstrap percolation on uniform simple graphs with prescribed degrees of mean $d\to\infty$ and deviations at most $C\sqrt d$. Thresholds are independently one with probability $(1-c/d)/d$ and two otherwise; seeds form an independent uniform set of prescribed size $a$. Let $T_a$ be the terminal number of active vertices and $b$ be one minus the mean number of threshold-one descendants of a reached vertex. Let $K\sim d^2$ be the quadratic response coefficient. If $b>0$ and $nb^3/K\to\infty$, we prove, uniformly over seed counts $a$, $ \mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)=Φ(\frac{a-nα_{\mathrm{det}}}{w})+o(1)$ with $w=\sqrt{nb/K}$, where $α_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the exact empirical response-barrier center and $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. Put $a_0=(n/K)^{1/3}$. If $d^4/n\to0$, $a/a_0\to x>0$ and $λ=ba_0\to\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)\to p(x,\ell)$, the one-sided Brownian parabolic survival probability. A sequential absolute-error law joins these regimes. A graphical counterexample shows that replacing the exact center by its leading term can cause limiting probability error $1/2$. The proof balances adaptive early-exploration transfer against late concentration at a tunable physical horizon, despite exponentially rare simplicity. We also prove quantitative and mesoscopic-seed refinements in explicitly narrower regimes. The only external graph-enumeration input is a stated reduction of McKay--Wormald's estimate; the probabilistic estimates for the cascade argument are proved in the text and appendices.

title: A Note on the Smoluchowski Coagulation-Fragmentation Equation with Fractional Laplacian
abstract: In this work, we assess the well-posedness of the Smoluchowski coagulation-fragmentation equation with fractional Laplacian. In particular, we consider a truncated set of discrete Smoluchowski-type equations modeling the formation of clusters, with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, where the diffusive term describes a non-standard behavior in the movement of particles ('anomalous' diffusion).

title: Serre's conjectures for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$
abstract: The present article proves (assuming GRH and a minor technical result) the veracity of Serre's conjectures for the field $\Q(\sqrt{13})$. In doing so, we prove a ``reduction to level 1'' result that holds for any real quadratic field with narrow class number one. However we can only establish the needed base cases for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$.

title: Continuous Envy-Free Allocation via Reciprocal Preference Matrices: An Alternative to Sperner-Based Discretization
abstract: Fair allocation problems on a continuous simplex are often approached through Sperner-type discretizations: agents label mesh vertices according to their preferences and a fully labelled elementary triangle gives a discrete localization of a fair outcome. We develop a continuous alternative for three agents and three alternatives by representing preferences with multiplicatively consistent reciprocal pairwise-comparison matrices. Two independent ratios per agent induce exact linear indifference boundaries and turn envy-free allocation into a finite-dimensional feasibility problem. For the six possible assignments, we introduce an assignment score $Φ$ built from the agents' consistent priority vectors and prove that an incentive solution component is nonempty if and only if its assignment is the unique minimizer of $Φ$, whereas a disincentive solution component is nonempty if and only if its assignment is the unique maximizer. Consequently, the strict solution region is either empty or a unique convex preference region whose closure lies in the interior of the simplex. The weak solution set is never empty and degenerates exactly when $Φ$ has ties. We also compare the exact continuous formulation with Sperner-based discretization, including the boundary convention required in the disincentive model. Under exact consistency, the model uses six independent pairwise thresholds, whereas a regular triangular mesh with resolution $m$ contains $(m+1)(m+2)/2$ vertices. The method therefore exchanges a stronger parametric preference assumption for an exact continuous solution set and a resolution-independent elicitation stage.

title: Selection spectra and sharp perturbations of normal sequences
abstract:
For a bounded sequence $y=(y_n)\subset E^*$ and $0<p<\infty$, let $$ G_p(y)=\{x\in E:(y_n(x))\in\ell_p\}, $$ and call $y$ $p$-strongly normal when $G_p(y)$ is dense in $E$. We study the spectra obtained by passing to subsequences and, for Schauder basic sequences, to normalized successive blocks. Their possible values are exactly $$ \varnothing,\quad (0,\infty),\quad (1,\infty),\quad [r,\infty),\quad (r,\infty)\qquad (r>1), $$ and the possible pairs are precisely the nested pairs. Every admissible pair has a normalized weakly null $1$-unconditional basic realization, even in the fixed dual $\ell_\infty(\mathfrak c)=\ell_1(\mathfrak c)^*$, and may be realized with empty spectrum for the original sequence.
  We also determine sharp universal perturbation classes: $\ell_p$ for $p$-strong normality at a fixed exponent, $c_0$ for the whole subsequence spectrum, and $\ell_1$ for the block spectrum. More generally, for every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal $A\subsetneq c_0$, membership of the error sequence in $A$ is exactly the universal condition preserving density of the $A$-summability domain.
  Finally, we extend the author's 2012 selection example from exponent one to every $p>0$ and to every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal. The good subsequences are exactly those whose index sets have uniformly bounded runs of consecutive integers; in the good case the detected quotient is isomorphic to $c_0$ and the whole selected sequence is weak-star Schauder basic.

title: The smallest singular value of products of random combinatorial and deterministic matrices
abstract: Let $p\in(0,1/2]$ be fixed, and let $d,n$ be positive integers satisfying $d=pn$. Let $Q_n$ be an $n\times n$ random combinatorial matrix whose rows are independent and uniformly distributed over the vectors in $\{0,1\}^n$ having exactly $d$ ones. For an arbitrary deterministic invertible $n\times n$ matrix $M$, we establish two-sided bounds for the smallest singular value of $Q_nM$. More precisely, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left( \varepsilon\le s_n(Q_nM)\cdot \|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \le \varepsilon^{-2} \right) \ge 1-C\left( \varepsilon+d^{-1/2}+e^{-c\,\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})} \right)-2e^{-cn}, \] where positive constants $C, c$ depend only on $p$ and $\operatorname{sr}$ denotes the stable rank. Consequently, for any sequence of deterministic invertible matrices $M$ satisfying $\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})\to\infty$, $s_n(Q_nM)$ is typically of order $\|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{-1}$. In particular, taking $M=\mathbf I_n$ recovers the known $n^{-1/2}$ scale for $s_n(Q_n)$.

title: Local Hardy and bmo Spaces on Filtered Lie Groups
abstract: We develop a theory of local Hardy and $bmo$ spaces on a connected Lie group with polynomial growth whose Lie algebra is endowed with a filtration. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that the local Hardy spaces enjoy an appropriate atomic decomposition, are compatible with Calderón--Zygmund operators, and can be identified with certain Triebel--Lizorkin spaces, as it happens in the classical settings.

title: Gradient Estimates for Hessian Equations with Measure Data
abstract: In this article, we establish the interior gradient estimates for $k$-Hessian equations with measure data. We use the ideas from the potential theories for the $p$-Laplacian type equations and pointwise estimates of $k$-subharmonic functions by Labutin. The interior gradient regularity is optimal for $k\geqslant3$, while for $k=2$, we prove the interior $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ and $C^{1,α}$ estimates for $2$-subharmonic solutions.

title: Number of ends of conjugacy diagrams
abstract: For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a finitely generated group $W_n$ with a conjugacy class such that the conjugacy diagram of this class has exactly $n$ ends. For this class, we compute the quotient spaces of the space of derivations of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[W_n]$ modulo quasi-inner and inner derivations, as well as the corresponding component of the first Hochschild cohomology.

title: Random Non-Commutative Error-Correcting Codes
abstract: Chapman, Dinur, and Lubotzky recently introduced the theory of non-commutative error-correcting codes, generalizing classical coding theory to arbitrary groups via $δ$-robust subsets used to detect proper subgroups. Building on this foundation, this paper systematically studies an analogue of random codes for arbitrary groups, exploring the extent to which the classical Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound holds in this non-commutative setting. While random universal codes of linear size in free groups are shown to be asymptotically bad, we establish a complete characterization for general families of finite groups. Specifically, a family of finite groups admits good random codes (forming a GV family) if and only if it exhibits uniform polynomial maximal-subgroup growth. Furthermore, we provide explicit quantitative bounds on the rate and optimal distance range based on intrinsic parameters, proving that families of finite solvable groups always form GV families and determining the exact probabilistic rate for direct powers of a fixed finite simple group.

title: Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for Nonlinear Optimization
abstract: We introduce the Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for hybridizing nonlinear optimization methods with pre-trained neural operators (NOs). SNAP targets parametric optimization problems arising from variational formulations of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), where many parameter instances require repeated solves. Inspired by multilevel line-search methods, SNAP operates in cycles, combining classical optimization steps with a search direction generated by a pre-trained NO. Since NO-generated search directions carry no a priori descent guarantee, SNAP employs an a posteriori safeguard by accepting only corrections that satisfy prescribed descent and acceptance conditions. We prove global convergence of the SNAP algorithm and show that it preserves the convergence rate of the underlying optimization method independently of the employed NO architecture. Moreover, we also show that when the NO corrections are sufficiently accurate, SNAP converges faster, with the improvement directly related to the NO training error. To demonstrate SNAP's efficiency in practice, we run numerical experiments on a diverse set of nonlinear parametric optimization problems, including parametric minimal surface, Allen--Cahn, and nonlinear Helmholtz problems. The efficiency of SNAP is demonstrated by comparing two NO architectures, Fourier neural operator (FNO) and Transolver, and by using SNAP as a standalone solver and as a nonlinear preconditioner. Our numerical results show a substantial reduction in the number of required iterations, while demonstrating robustness and generalization across a wide range of problem parameters and mesh resolutions.

title: Eternal Total Positivity and Matrix-Dependent Hadamard Thresholds
abstract: We study entrywise powers of totally positive matrices. Our first question is which matrices remain totally positive under every positive Hadamard power. We call them eternally totally positive. Our second question concerns a fixed totally positive matrix: what is the smallest exponent after which all of its entrywise powers are totally positive? We call this number the Hadamard threshold of the matrix. Unlike the usual critical exponent, this threshold depends on the individual matrix. We give a complete characterization in order three, obtain explicit bounds for the transition exponent, and construct symmetric matrices that realize every threshold in $[0,1)$. We also prove the basic transformation rules and continuity of the threshold on the normalized $3\times3$ totally positive cone. For higher orders, we introduce the logarithmic core and use it to expand each minor near the zero exponent. This reduces the $4\times4$ problem to the full determinant and the $3\times3$ submatrices. For symmetric $4\times4$ matrices, we show that a positive-definite logarithmic core makes the full determinant positive for every positive exponent. A two-parameter Hankel family then realizes every threshold in $(1,2)$. Hence the exact range of thresholds in the symmetric order-four case is $[0,1)\cup(1,2)$; neither $1$ nor $2$ is attained. We also give a recursive symmetric ETP criterion in every order and an explicit classification for symmetric Toeplitz matrices of order four. In order five, a certified example exhibits an intermediate-power obstruction in a nonprincipal minor. An explicit order-three condition and a finite critical-point test give a complete order-five test.

title: The Mean First-Reaction Time on a Thin Filament in a 3-D Domain
abstract: We study the mean first-reaction time (MFRT) of a Brownian particle in a bounded three-dimensional domain $Ω$ with a reflecting boundary $\partialΩ$, that contains a thin reactive filament. The filament is a tube of cross-sectional diameter $\varepsilon\ll 1$ around a smooth closed curve $Γ$, and its surface is partially reactive with reactivity $b$. As $\varepsilon\to 0$ the filament reduces to a line source in the outer problem. Its cross-section enters only through a logarithmic reactive capacitance $d_c(b)$, so that the MFRT is $\mathcal{O}(-\log[\varepsilon d_c])$. This contrasts with the $\mathcal{O}(\eps^{-1})$ scaling for spatially localized traps of radius $\eps$. Using matched asymptotic expansions, we derive a Fredholm integral equation on $Γ$ for the line density of the reactive flux. It sums all powers of $ν\equiv -1/\log[\varepsilon d_c]$ and involves two geometric quantities: the regular part $R$ of the Neumann Green's function, which encodes the interaction of $Γ$ with $\partialΩ$, and an intrinsic self-energy of $Γ$ that depends only on its shape. The framework extends to multiple filaments, splitting probabilities, a spatially heterogeneous diffusivity, and the principal eigenvalue of the Laplacian. For the unit sphere we solve the integral equation with a simple trapezoidal Nyström scheme, and we validate the predictions for rings, linked rings and torus knots against full 3-D finite-element solutions.

title: Sparse domination for $q$-variation associated with functional calculus
abstract: We establish sparse domination for the $q$-variation of functional calculus families $\{\varphi(tL)\}_{t>0}$ on spaces of homogeneous type. Under generalized Gaussian estimates, we consider holomorphic multipliers of injective accretive operators, and Sobolev-type spectral multipliers of non-negative self-adjoint operators. For the Sobolev-type multipliers, we show that our regularity assumption is sharp in general except the endpoint. As corollaries, we obtain weighted $q$-variational estimates for Bochner-Riesz means and regularized Schrödinger groups. Finally, we give several examples of operators to which our results apply.

title: cuPDQPx: A GPU-Accelerated Restarted Halpern PDHG for Large-Scale Convex Quadratic Programming
abstract: We present cuPDQPx, a GPU-accelerated, factorization-free first-order solver for large-scale convex quadratic programming (QP). Building on the restarted reflected Halpern primal-dual framework of cuPDLPx, we introduce an auxiliary-variable splitting that yields explicit updates without linearizing the quadratic objective or solving inner quadratic subproblems. A preconditioned proximal point interpretation yields both sublinear and linear fixed-point residual convergence guarantees. For practical efficiency, cuPDQPx integrates diagonal preconditioning, step-size selection, adaptive restart, and adaptive primal and quadratic weight updates. cuPDQPx is implemented in C and CUDA with optimized sparse matrix-vector products, kernel fusion, and CUDA Graphs. Numerical experiments on the Maros-Mészáros collection, a convex subset of QPLIB, and synthetic large-scale QPs demonstrate that cuPDQPx has strong numerical performance at both $10^{-4}$ and $10^{-8}$ tolerances.

title: Equivariant Morita equivalence for finite cyclic group actions on noncommutative tori
abstract: Li proved that the noncommutative tori $A_θ$ and $A_{gθ}$ are strongly Morita equivalent whenever $g\in\mathrm{SO}(n,n|\mathbb{Z})$ and $gθ$ is defined. We study equivariant extensions of these equivalences for canonical finite cyclic group actions. Let $W\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfy $W^tθW=θ$, $W^k=I_n$ and $1\notin\operatorname{spec}(W)$, and write $ρ(R)=\operatorname{diag}(R,(R^t)^{-1})$. If $gρ(W^t)g^{-1}=ρ(P)$ for some $P\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$, we equip Li's $A_{gθ}$--$A_θ$ Heisenberg equivalence bimodule with a compatible $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action. Consequently, the crossed products $A_{gθ}\rtimes_{α_{P^t}}\mathbb{Z}_k$ and $A_θ\rtimes_{α_W}\mathbb{Z}_k$ are strongly Morita equivalent. For the canonical flip action by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that Morita equivalence of crossed products implies Morita equivalence of the underlying tori in every dimension, and prove the converse in dimensions two through four. For each fixed dimension $2\leq n\leq 4$, the complete invariants are the central rank and canonical $K_0$-trace range of the underlying torus, with the latter taken up to positive scaling. For the standard cyclic group actions of orders $2$, $3$, $4$ and $6$ on rotation algebras, we prove that the crossed products are Morita equivalent exactly when the action orders agree and the parameters lie in the same fractional-linear $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-orbit, generalizing the result of Bönicke et al.\ from irrational to arbitrary real parameters. We also construct infinite families of distinct parameters giving Morita-equivalent crossed products for each fixed $W$ satisfying the stated hypotheses.

title: Multiplicity of normalized solutions for the $L^2$-supercritical Kirchhoff equation with partial confinement
abstract: We study the existence of positive normalized solutions for the nonlocal Kirchhoff equation with partial harmonic confinement \[-\left(a+b\int_{\mathbb{R}^{3}}|\nabla u|^{2}\,dx\right)Δu +(x_1^2+x_2^2)u+λu=|u|^{p-2}u,\] subject to the mass constraint $\int_{\mathbb{R}^{3}}|u|^2\,dx=μ$, where $a,b>0$ are constants, $\frac{14}{3}<p<6$, $μ>0$ is a prescribed mass, and $λ\in\mathbb{R}$ is a Lagrange multiplier associated with the mass constraint. For every sufficiently small $μ>0$, we prove the existence of two positive normalized solutions. One of these solutions is a local minimizer, while the other is obtained at a mountain-pass level. The construction of the local minimizer relies on a combination of profile decomposition and a new nonlocal merging technique, yielding compactness up to translations in the unconfined $x_3$-direction. The mountain-pass solution is obtained by considering positive solutions defined on expanding balls. A uniform bound on the Morse index allows us to obtain a spectral estimate for the limiting Lagrange multiplier. Together with an energy comparison, this spectral estimate yields strong convergence in the energy space and recovers both the prescribed mass and the Kirchhoff coefficient.

title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given.

title: Fast rigid rotational alignment of voxelized 3-D density maps in sliced Wasserstein distance
abstract: We develop a fast method for the rigid alignment of voxelized three-dimensional density functions over $\mathsf{SO}(3)$ using sliced optimal transport. Our approach efficiently transforms each density map into a tensor of one-dimensional quantile functions, taken from central slices over the unit sphere, such that the Euclidean distance of the transformed volumes approximates the sliced 2-Wasserstein distance. Our formulation is therefore compatible with existing, fast, voxel-based Euclidean alignment algorithms. We provide theoretical analysis and numerical experiments demonstrating that the sliced 2-Wasserstein distance is a robust metric for comparing three-dimensional shapes and for computing their rigid alignment.

title: Unstable radial equilibria as sharp concentration thresholds for the Jäger--Luckhaus model on the unit disk
abstract: We identify unstable radial equilibria as sharp concentration thresholds for the Jäger--Luckhaus chemotaxis system on the unit disk with no-flux boundary conditions. Concentration is compared through cumulative mass. At fixed total mass, every radial initial profile more concentrated than an unstable equilibrium produces finite-time blow-up, whereas every nonstationary profile less concentrated than that equilibrium generates a global, uniformly bounded solution converging to the least concentrated radial equilibrium. We also classify the radial equilibria and determine their nonlinear stability. Let $Λ= j_{1,1}^{2}$, where $j_{1,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_1$. For $M\ne Λπ$, the least concentrated equilibrium is the unique locally asymptotically stable equilibrium under mass-preserving radial perturbations. It is spatially homogeneous for $M<Λπ$ and strictly increasing for $M>Λπ$. Every other radial equilibrium, including the homogeneous state at $M=Λπ$, is nonlinearly unstable. These results clarify how total population and initial spatial aggregation jointly determine collapse or bounded redistribution, and how stable peripheral enrichment can occur within the radial model.

title: On the median of the beta distribution in relation to the median of the gamma distribution
abstract: The median of the beta distribution has no closed form, but it is closely tied to the median of the gamma distribution. Kerman's approximation has the ratio form $g(α)/(g(α)+g(β))$ with $g(x) = x - 1/3$, a lower bound on the gamma median, and it is a lower bound on the beta median for $1/3 < α< β$. The ratio form built from the true gamma median is a tighter lower bound, asymptotically exact as $β\to \infty$. The ratio form built from the Wilson-Hilferty approximation to the gamma median, implicit in a classical approximation to the $F$ distribution but little known as an approximation to the beta median, is an upper bound on the edge $α= 1$ and for large shape parameters. The ratio form that is exact on the lines $α= 1$ and $β= 1$ yields a new approximation to the gamma median, which is an upper bound on it for shape parameter below 1 and a lower bound above 1; no ratio form gives the beta median exactly. For large shape parameters, the logit of the median has an explicit second-order expansion. For small shape parameters, bounds in elementary functions are asymptotically tight, and odds-corrected forms of the low-$α$ asymptote, with an elementary factor that is exact on the edges $α= 1$ and $β= 1$, are, numerically, one-sided bounds within 0.44% of the median that are exact on the lines $α= 1$, $β= 1$, and $α= β$. Steering their exponents with four fitted constants, and interpolating between two ratio forms where both shape parameters exceed 1, gives an approximation in elementary functions that is exact on those lines and numerically within 0.065% of the median over the whole domain. Most of the proofs are machine-verified in Lean 4.

title: NS-Leibniz bialgebras, the Yang--Baxter equation and relative Rota--Baxter operators
abstract: We introduce NS-Leibniz bialgebras and establish their equivalence with matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-Leibniz algebras. In the coboundary case, skew-symmetric solutions of the NS-Leibniz Yang--Baxter equation yield NS-Leibniz bialgebras and correspond to $\mathcal{O}$-operators for the dual regular representation. We study quasi-triangular and factorizable structures, and relate factorizable tensors to quadratic Rota--Baxter NS-Leibniz algebras of any fixed nonzero weight. We also construct compatible bialgebra structures from skew-adjoint Nijenhuis operators commuting with the Rota--Baxter operator.

title: Locally unital $C^*$-algebras and limitations of seminorm criteria for compact operators
abstract: We study the problem of geometric characterization of Banach-compact and $\mathcal A$-compact operators on Hilbert $C^*$-modules in terms of uniform structures generated by seminorms. Previously, such a criterion for $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators was obtained by Troitsky for countably generated range modules with a suitable system of seminorms. Using locally unital $C^*$-algebras as modules over themselves, we establish fundamental limitations of such characterizations. Namely, we show that for nonunital locally unital $C^*$-algebras not only does Troitsky's criterion fail to extend, but, more generally, no system of seminorms can characterize $\mathcal A$-precompactness by total boundedness, nor Banach-compactness of bounded operators or $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators by total boundedness of the images of the unit ball. Moreover, the same statement holds for Hilbert $C^*$-modules $\mathcal N$ whenever the algebra $\mathbf K(\mathcal N)$ of $\mathcal A$-compact operators is locally unital and nonunital. We also study Troitsky-type systems of seminorms and their relation to $\mathcal A$-precompactness. We prove that every $\mathcal A$-precompact subset is totally bounded with respect to the strongest of such structures. Consequently, for Hilbert $C^*$-modules admitting a standard frame, all the corresponding notions of total boundedness coincide.

title: Convergence rates of mixed primal-dual dynamical systems with implicit Hessian damping and Tikhonov regularization
abstract: We propose a mixed-order primal--dual dynamical system with implicit Hessian damping and Tikhonov regularization for linearly constrained convex optimization, and derive a corresponding fast primal--dual algorithm. The proposed dynamical system couples a second-order primal equation with a first-order dual equation without requiring twice differentiability of the objective function. An energy analysis establishes $\mathcal{O}(t^{-2})$ convergence rates for the augmented Lagrangian gap, feasibility violation, and objective residual along an extrapolated primal trajectory. For the proposed algorithm, we construct discrete energy estimates and establish the corresponding $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2})$ rates at the extrapolated primal iterates. In particular, in the critical regularization regimes $ε(t)=a/t^2$ and $ε_k=a/k^2$, these accelerated rates hold simultaneously with strong convergence of the primal trajectory and primal iterates to the minimum-norm solution, respectively, under suitable parameter and trajectory conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence behavior of the proposed dynamical system and the corresponding algorithm.

title: A Paley-Wiener-Type Theorem with Applications to Inverse Medium Scattering for the Schrödinger Equation
abstract:
This paper develops a new uniqueness framework for inverse scattering problems for the time-harmonic Schrödinger equation using multi-frequency data. Our approach is based on a Paley-Wiener-type theorem that characterizes the support of the potential through the asymptotic growth of a generalized Fourier integral along imaginary frequencies, allowing for nontrivial amplitude functions.
  Within this framework, we obtain two major results on identifying the shape of the support of the potential in three dimensions, for both the plane-wave incidence and point source incidence, respectively. For plane-wave incidence, we prove that the location and shape of the convex compact support of an essentially bounded potential are uniquely determined by fixed-angle far-field data from two opposite incident directions or by backscattering far field data, provided that the potential is real-valued and sign-definite near the boundary of its support. For point-source incidence, we show that near-field backscattering data, namely the scattered field evaluated at the source point as the source ranges over a sufficiently large sphere, uniquely determine the location and shape of the convex support under the same assumptions on the potential. The proofs rely on meromorphic extension and the Paley-Wiener-type theorem.

title: Tikhonov-Regularized Dynamics and Inexact Algorithms for Nonlinear Saddle-Point Problems
abstract: In this paper, we study a Tikhonov-regularized second-order primal--dual dynamical system for smooth nonlinear convex--concave saddle-point problems in real Hilbert spaces. The dynamical system incorporates a vanishing damping coefficient $α/t$, a Hessian-driven term, and a critical Tikhonov regularization coefficient $c/t^2$. By constructing suitable Lyapunov functions, we establish strong convergence to the minimum-norm saddle point and fast convergence rates under the same parameter conditions, without imposing any eventual inside/outside-ball condition. Specifically, the primal--dual trajectory converges strongly to the minimum-norm saddle point, while the primal--dual gap and the velocity norm decay at rates $o(t^{-2})$ and $o(t^{-1})$, respectively. Furthermore, we propose an inexact primal--dual algorithm with a computable relative residual criterion and prove strong convergence of the generated sequence to the same minimum-norm saddle point, together with an $o(k^{-2})$ convergence rate for the primal--dual gap. Finally, numerical experiments on nonlinear and bilinear problems of different dimensions illustrate the minimum-norm selection property and compare the performance of the proposed dynamical system and algorithm with related methods.

title: Convergence of Levenberg--Marquardt method in Banach spaces
abstract: We study the Levenberg--Marquardt method for nonlinear inverse problems in Banach spaces under a Hölder stability estimate. Under suitable assumptions on the geometry of the Banach space and the Fréchet derivative of the measurement operator, we establish the well-definedness of the method, local convergence and convergence rates for exact data, and the monotonic decrease of the Bregman distance up to the stopping index for noisy data. These results extend the corresponding Hilbert space theory to the Banach space setting.

title: CA2 numbers and the Riemann hypothesis: a numerical investigation of Ramanujan's inequalities
abstract: Robin's criterion reduces the Riemann hypothesis to an inequality for colossally abundant (CA) numbers, and Wu's theorem reduces the test further to the subclass CA2. We study this reduction numerically and consider smaller subsets on which the same criterion remains sufficient. We also show that the logarithmic decay law suggested by Briggs's computations follows from Ramanujan's conditional bounds. To investigate the next term, we compare the normalized Robin difference with Ramanujan's oscillatory expression involving the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. The resulting difference has a slowly varying component on both CA and CA2. Its scaled values continue to vary over the computed range, leading to questions about convergence, upper bounds, and higher-order terms. We describe the sampling used in the figures and estimate the error from truncating the sum over zeros.

title: Borsuk number in four dimensions is at most seven
abstract: We prove that every bounded set of diameter one in four-dimensional Euclidean space can be covered by seven balls of diameter strictly smaller than $0.9999$. In particular, the Borsuk number satisfies $b_4\le7$. The proof combines geometric arguments based on contact points of the circumball with an exact finite computation. For small and large circumradius, the covering centres are constructed analytically. In the remaining range, a suitable triangle of contact points reduces the problem to a four-parameter family of ball polytopes. The parameter cube is subdivided into 23494 boxes. For each parameter box, candidate centres are found by nonlinear optimization, and the resulting covering is verified using exact rational interval arithmetic and paraboloid lifting.

title: Reciprocity formulas for generalized Dedekind character sums
abstract: In this paper, we apply the Fourier series technique to establish a new formula for the product of the generalized Bernoulli function and the Bernoulli function. As applications, we derive some reciprocity formulas for generalized Dedekind character sums. In particular, we show that the reciprocity formulas of Berndt, Can, and others follow as special cases.

title: Nodal radial solutions for a zero-mass $(p,q)$-Laplacian equation with Hardy-Hénon type weight
abstract: We establish the existence of radial nodal solutions for a class of zero-mass $(p,q)$-Laplacian equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with a Hardy-Hénon type weight $|x|^α$. The absence of lower-order potential terms motivates the use of a homogeneous radial variational framework adapted to the mixed $p$- and $q$-growth structure. A key ingredient is a weighted Sobolev embedding theorem that establishes continuity and compactness in the appropriate range of exponents and identifies the sharp interval for continuous embedding. Building on these results, we construct sign-changing radial solutions through a variational method based on radial partitions and critical levels.
