For $m=5$ this profile is negative at one point, yielding infinitely many counterexamples. The counterexamples are not diagonal, and the diagonal case $k=m$, which is the case relevant in practice, remains open. These results do not imply a failure of the Fasi--Higham algorithm. Rather, they delimit the range in which the auxiliary positivity conjecture can be used as a theorem.

title: The Discrete Monotonicity Property in Rank Two
abstract: The Betke--Henk--Wills conjecture predicts a bound for lattice-point counts in terms of successive minima. Malikiosis introduced the discrete monotonicity property for normalized residue counts as a sufficient condition for this bound and its extension to nonsymmetric convex bodies. We prove that every compact convex set satisfies this property for lattice subgroups of rank at most two, in arbitrary ambient dimension.

title: A Hierarchical Online-Compression Approach to Proportional Subsets of Bounded Orthonormal Systems
abstract:
Let $(φ_i)_{i=1}^n$ be an orthonormal system on a probability space with $\|φ_i\|_\infty\leq L$. We prove that, for every $2\leq k<n$, there is a set $I$ of at least $n-k$ indices such that $$ \|f\|_2\leq CM_k\sqrt{\log(e+M_k)}\|f\|_1 $$ for every $f$ in the span of $(φ_i)_{i\in I}$, where $M_k=L\sqrt{\frac{n}{k}\log(2k)}$. This replaces the logarithmic exponent $\frac{5}{2}$ in the corresponding theorem of Guédon, Mendelson, Pajor, and Tomczak-Jaegermann by $\frac{1}{2}$. We also obtain a partition into two sets of cardinality $\frac{n}{2}+O(\sqrt n)$ for which both spans satisfy the resulting norm comparison, and for uniformly bounded systems the proportional estimate is $C\sqrt{\log n\log\log n}$ for sufficiently large $n$.
  This is the third paper in a series systematically using gradient descent as a proof mechanism in harmonic analysis, following the $Λ(p)$ and Bernoulli restricted isometry papers of Burstein, Iosevich, and Krause, and the descent here is entropic mirror descent. We represent each function in an $L_1$ ball by a probability measure of controlled relative entropy, and this entropy pays for the corrections to the predictions of its coefficients. Processing the thresholds from large to small, we obtain a single weighted bound for all the corrections, which we turn into a finite description of approximate coefficient squares and then into a conditional Rademacher estimate, and symmetrization completes the argument directly on the $L_1$ ball. We also record consequences for concentration and for recovery from coefficient measurements.

title: Generative Rate-Distortion-Perception Theory on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: Generative communication uses transmitted information to control stochastic generation at the receiver. A fundamental question is how much source-specific information must be communicated so that outputs generated at the receiver satisfy prescribed fidelity and reliability requirements while preserving the conditional source distribution. We address this question for sources on compact Riemannian manifolds by developing a generative rate-distortion-perception (GRDP) framework without common randomness. We formulate an asymptotic operational GRDP function under a geodesic distortion radius and a failure-probability constraint, and establish its single-letter characterization through an equivalent informational formulation. Furthermore, for the informational formulation with the high-reliability limit, we derive a geometric lower bound determined by the largest source probability mass of a region with bounded geodesic diameter, together with an upper bound based on probabilistic coverings of the source manifold. Small-radius analysis of the lower bound reveals the roles of intrinsic dimension and scalar curvature in the required communication rate. For uniformly distributed sources on compact homogeneous Riemannian manifolds, we prove that the bounds coincide, yielding an exact characterization of the limiting GRDP function. We further specialize this result to unit spheres, obtaining an explicit expression that relates the minimum communication rate to the geodesic distortion radius and intrinsic dimension, revealing that for the $d$-dimensional unit sphere with $d\ge2$, increasing the communication rate by $d$ bits per source symbol can reduce the distortion radius by more than half.

title: An involution for recurrences of Tricomi and other special functions
abstract: Recently two new integrated recurrences were given for the Kummer function which together with the six recurrences already given in standard literature gave a total of eight recurrences, each one linking the baseline function to one of it's eight contiguous functions. Two new recurrences for the Tricomi function are given here which complete the set of eight recurrences for the Tricomi function linking it to it's contiguous functions. The involution presented previously is examined in detail for the recurrences of Cylinder, Associated Legendre and Kummer/Tricomi functions. This involution converts any given recurrence to a recurrence with the parameter shifts reversed, which creates conjugate pairs. One pair for Cylinder functions, two pairs for Associated Legendre functions and 4 pairs each for Kummer and Tricomi functions. Uniqueness is proven using Wronskians for the integrated recurrence relations, such that contiguous functions are single occupancy slots with only one integrated recurrence possible for each slot and for each independent solution of the ODE. For Cylinder and Associated Legendre functions this is simple, as the recurrences are identical for each independent solution. However, for Kummer and Tricomi functions the recurrences are different. This difficulty is bypassed using Gamma functions to scale the Tricomi recurrences to match the Kummer recurrences for each conjugate pair. It is not possible to match globally. This allows uniqueness to be proven using Wronskians on a pair by pair basis. Hence the involution system behaves like a Pauli Exclusion principle for contiguous functions, with only one recurrence possible for each solution of the ODE.

title: The cross quadratic bisectional curvature of Kähler $C$-spaces of classical type
abstract: In this paper, we show that any Kähler $C$-space of classical type has nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature. As a consequence, such manifolds are Fano. This confirms a substantial part of a conjecture of Ni-Zheng (Conjecture 1.5 in \cite{NZ}).

title: A Spectral Boundary for Independence Learnability
abstract: Learning independence is fundamental to statistical inference and machine learning, yet learning independence between entire time series by a test remains challenging when only a single observation record is available. Existing guarantees often rely on structural or mixing assumptions, while stationarity and ergodicity alone do not permit consistent testing. In this work, we identify a class-level boundary governed by shared nontrivial Koopman eigenvalues, which represent common persistent oscillatory frequencies of the two processes. When no such eigenvalues are shared, we extend shift-based rank calibration with finite-window dependence witnesses and a data-adaptive threshold to construct a deterministic, weakly consistent test with finite-sample false-positive control, without quantitative mixing assumptions. Conversely, we show that no possibly randomized test can achieve vanishing false-positive probabilities under every independent jointly totally ergodic law while consistently detecting every dependent jointly totally ergodic law with a shared nontrivial eigenvalue. This impossibility already holds for binary observations and persists within any prescribed nonempty open eigenvalue window, identifying a spectral obstruction to universal learning of full-process independence.

title: An Alternative Settlement Rule for State-of-Charge-Limited Resources in Electricity Markets
abstract: Standard two settlement markets compute the total profits of their participants as a sum of day-ahead (DA) profits and incremental real-time (RT) profits. This procedure was originally designed for conventional generators, which can always deliver their day-ahead (DA) awarded schedule in real time because their capacity is invariant across market clearings. Energy storage resources, by contrast, are state-of-charge (SOC) limited. Therefore, their ability to honor a DA award in real time depends on the SOC available at the moment of dispatch, a quantity that can differ materially from what was assumed at the DA stage. According to the current rules in CAISO, whenever the storage state of charge (SOC) is not sufficient to support the day-ahead award the RT market may impose an instruction to "buy back" or "sell back" that may lead to a monetary loss that is covered by the system operator via uplifts in the bid cost recovery (BCR) scheme. These circumstances have resulted in storage resources capturing a disproportionate share of uplift payments---totaling approximately $75.2 million in CAISO between 2022 and 2025. This paper formalizes the asymmetry between SOC-unlimited (generator) and SOC-limited (storage) resources and proposes an alternative settlement rule in which the total storage profit is computed as the maximum between real-time only compensation and the existing day ahead plus incremental real-time compensation. Through our analysis and a case study based on a realistic version of the California system, we demonstrate that while the proposed rule does not guarantee non-negative profits in all cases, it can reduce - and in favorable conditions eliminate - the negative profit outcomes that trigger make-whole BCR payments.

title: Sharp potential and Brenier map $W_2$-stability for log-concave sources
abstract: We study stability of Brenier potentials and maps under changes of the target measure. Let $κ>0$, for a full support $κ$-strongly log-concave source $ρ$, possibly with a non-smooth potential, the normalized transport potentials satisfy \[ \|u_μ-u_ν\|_{L^2(ρ)}\leqslant\sqrt{2/κ}\,W_2(μ,ν) \] for arbitrary targets with finite second moments. The proof controls normalized Laguerre cell barycentres by their mass derivatives and centers the potential velocity to remove unbounded source cell locations. Bounded variation interpolation then yields the sharp map exponent $1/3$ for targets in a common compact set, \[ \left\Vert T_μ-T_ν\right\Vert _{L^{2}(ρ)}\leqslant \operatorname{Const} \cdot W_{2}\left( μ,ν\right) ^{1/3}. \] Sharpness of the exponents for both the potential and Brenier map stability are established.

title: Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
abstract:
We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders give the same total error, but they divide it differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time.
  For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, with a power series that converges for all time in exponentially weighted trajectory norms. The linearized semigroup has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, exponential stability, Kato smoothing, Crandall-Pazy regularity and analyticity of the solution maps hold uniformly in the mesh size.
  These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. In exponentially weighted time-integrated norms the semidiscrete solutions converge uniformly on balls, at the rate $h^{1/6}$ in $L^4(0,\infty;L^2)$ for data in $L^2$ and at the rate $h^{2/3}$ in $L^2(0,\infty;H^1)$ for data in $H_0^1$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$. For the unweighted scheme, a grid wave packet of zero group velocity destroys mesh-uniform Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity.

title: On Proximity Gaps for One-Point Algebraic Geometric Codes
abstract:
Proximity gaps and correlated agreement underpin the soundness of interactive oracle proofs. We establish these properties for general one-point algebraic geometry (AG) codes, extending corresponding results for Reed-Solomon codes. For codes of length $n$ over $\mathbb F_q$ with designed distance $n-m$, write $ρ=m/n$ and fix $ρ\in(0,1)$. For polynomial curves of degree at most $\ell$ and any $0<\varepsilon<1$, we prove correlated agreement with multiplicative slack $\varepsilon$ and soundness $O(\ell(\ell+1)/(\varepsilon q))$ whenever $e\le(1-\varepsilon)(n-m)/2$, with no additional genus penalty. This gives asymptotically good AG code families from Garcia--Stichtenoth tower of unbounded length over a fixed field with soundness bounds independent of $n$, beyond the RS restriction $n\le q$. We also establish mutual correlated agreement up to radius $(1-\sqrtρ-η)n$, with soundness $O(\ell n/(η^3q))$ for $0<η<1-\sqrtρ$. Our half designed distance proof combines auxiliary divisors, simultaneous Berlekamp-Welch interpolation, and error-incidence counting to obtain a common polynomial representation without a Polishchuk-Spielman divisibility lemma.
  Finally, two counterexamples on the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower show limitations beyond half the minimum distance, at radii below the Johnson bound and with positive slack. The first requires a positive constant soundness lower bound independent of $q$ and $n$, precluding a uniform $O(1/q)$ guarantee throughout the Johnson regime. The second fixes the field and lets the relative gap above half distance tend to zero while ruling out correlated agreement for every soundness parameter $σ<1$, with positive limiting rate and relative error radius.

title: Exponential Ergodicity and Invariant Distribution of a Degenerate Reflected SDE with Stable Noise
abstract: We study a two-dimensional degenerate stochastic differential equation with oblique reflection and spectrally positive strictly stable noise of index in $(1,2)$, motivated by join-the-shortest-queue systems with heavy-tailed interarrival times. A polynomial-exponential Lyapunov function and fixed-time minorization establish positive Harris recurrence and exponential ergodicity in weighted total variation. We construct the invariant law from a stable path and prove its absolute continuity. Regulator identities describe stationary dependence and recover the joint Laplace transform from the queue marginal. Idleness inherits the classical stable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck tail; the queue has a sharp exponential tail with a polynomial prefactor whose power is half the stable index and a positive constant represented through regeneration. Conditional on small idleness, idleness divided by the conditioning threshold and the queue converge to independent beta and size-biased limits. Under large-queue conditioning, normalized idleness and queue excess converge to independent Mittag-Leffler and exponential limits.

title: A short proof of the Segal conjecture for $C_p$
abstract: We give a new proof of the generalized Segal conjecture for the cyclic group of prime order p, i.e. the fact that the Tate diagonal of any bounded below spectrum is a p-completion. The idea, inspired by Hahn and Wilson's argument, is to use descent along the equivariant map from the p-fold tensor power of the field with p elements to its topological Hochschild homology. The only computational input that we use is the calculation of the homotopy rings of this topological Hochschild homology and its Tate construction, together with the map induced by the cyclotomic Frobenius.

title: Generalized Frobenius Structures on Hurwitz Spaces, Their Open Extensions and Associated Principal Hierarchies
abstract: We construct generalized Frobenius structures on Hurwitz spaces of arbitrary genus using extended primary differentials. Through contour integrals involving the Cauchy kernel, we derive explicit dispersionless Lax representations for the principal hierarchies of these structures and their almost-dual counterparts. We also construct solutions to the open WDVV equations for both the original and almost-dual structures, and derive explicit principal hierarchies for the resulting rank-one extensions. Finally, we show that these constructions admit Shramchenko deformations.

title: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves
abstract: We study the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes from genus-two curves over finite fields. Let $C_\mathcal{ L}(D,G)$ be such a code over $\mathbb F_q$, with length $n$ and dimension $k$. Assume that $3\leq k\leq n-3$. We prove that $n<(2q+10\sqrt q+16)/3$. This bound holds for every prime power $q$ and for both parities of $k$. It gives a uniform upper bound of $2q/3+O(\sqrt q)$ for the maximal length. The explicit bound is strictly smaller than $q+1$ when $q\geq125$.

title: Symmetric Policy Optimization for Zero-Sum Markov Games
abstract: We propose a simple and symmetric method for policy optimization in discounted zero-sum Markov games. The method, termed symmetric policy iteration, operates by evaluating the joint policy and solving the corresponding regularized matrix game at each iteration. By employing a diminishing sequence of regularization strengths, we establish the global linear convergence of the proposed method to the optimal value function and the saddle point. In particular, the method does not require solving any standalone Markov decision process throughout policy optimization, and is symmetric in the sense that it stays invariant regardless of whether we are solving the min-max or the max-min version of the game. To the best of our knowledge, this appears to be the first simple and symmetric policy-based method attaining global convergence for discounted zero-sum Markov games.

title: Pre-modular fusion categories of global dimension $2p$
abstract:
Let $p>5$ be a prime. In this paper, we show that a pre-modular fusion category of
  global dimension $2p$ is either pointed or tensor equivalent to $\text{Rep}(D_{2p})$.

title: Centres of mass, Steiner's theorem, and equations of Erdős-Moser type
abstract: We study the Erdős--Moser equation $1^k+2^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$ and its analogue in arithmetic progressions, $\sum_{i<m,\ i\equiv b \pmod q} i^k=m^k$, by means of centres of mass, through what we call the half-mass principle. For the progression equation we show that a solution with exponent $k$ has at most $\lfloor k/\log 2+3/2\rfloor$ terms for all $k<10^{55}$, which is best possible for real solutions and replaces an exponential bound; that for $k=3$ solutions with exactly $n$ terms exist if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5\}$, and then infinitely many; and that there are no solutions at all for $k=4$, more generally for every $k=2^s\ge 4$, and for every even $k$ with $4\le k\le 24$. These results rest on a uniform estimate for the Erdős--Moser equation: the real exponent $κ_m$ for which $1^κ+\dots+(m-1)^κ=m^κ$ satisfies $κ_m=\log 2\,(m-3/2-γ_m/m)$ with $0<γ_m<1/(8\log 2)$ for every $m\ge 3$. The method also explains the constants: $3/2$ is a Steiner quotient $(ρ^2+d^2)/2d$, and $25/12-3\log 2=1/12-f''(\log 2)/2$ with $f(λ)=λ/(e^λ-1)$, which explains why this number is so small.

title: Efficient variance reduction for randomized Kaczmarz methods via residual-tracking control variates
abstract: The randomized Kaczmarz (RK) method is a widely used and effective class of iterative algorithms for solving large-scale linear systems. For inconsistent systems, however, the persistent variance caused by randomization prevents the method from converging exactly to the least-squares solution. In this paper, we introduce a residual-tracking control variate framework for reducing this variance while retaining the row-action structure and low per-iteration cost of RK. The resulting variance-reduced RK method uses constant step sizes, accesses only sampled rows of the coefficient matrix, and requires \(O(m+n)\) auxiliary storage. We prove that the proposed method converges linearly in expectation to the unique least-norm solution for general linear systems, including inconsistent and rank-deficient cases, with a convergence factor of the same order as that of the RK method. Furthermore, we incorporate the momentum acceleration into our framework and provide theoretical guarantees for its improved convergence rate. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods, particularly for ill-conditioned systems and high-accuracy computations.

title: The trace distribution of $r$-primitive $k$-normal elements of finite fields
abstract: Let \(q=p^e\) be a prime power and \(n\geq1\). Let \(L=\F_{q^n}\) and \(K=\F_q\). We study the trace distribution of \(r\)-primitive \(k\)-normal elements of \(L\) over \(K\). We first derive exact formulas for the number of \(k\)-normal elements of \(L\) with a prescribed trace in \(K\). For \(r\mid q^n-1\), \(0\leq k\le n-1\), and \(a\in K\), let \(\mathcal{N}_{r,k}(a)\) denote the number of \(r\)-primitive \(k\)-normal elements of \(L\) with trace \(a\). We establish a sufficient condition for \(\mathcal{N}_{r,k}\) to be constant on \(K^\times\). We also identify a subgroup \(H_r\) of \(K^\times\) and prove that \(\mathcal{N}_{r,k}\) is constant on each coset of \(H_r\). Finally, we obtain a necessary and sufficient character-sum condition for \(\mathcal{N}_{r,k}\) to be constant on \(K^\times\).

title: Boundedness in a chemotaxis system with nonlinear diffusion and singular sensitivity
abstract:
This paper studies the following chemotaxis system with nonlinear diffusion and singular sensitivity \[ \begin{cases}
  u_t = \nabla \cdot \left( (u+a)^{m-1} \nabla u \right)
  - χ\nabla \cdot \left( u \dfrac{\nabla v}{v^k} \right), \\[4pt]
  v_t = Δv - v + u, \end{cases} \] in a smoothly bounded domain \(Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n\), \(n \geq 2\), subject to no-flux boundary conditions, where \(χ,k,a,m>0\). For suitably regular initial data, we prove global existence and uniform-in-time boundedness of classical solutions if one of the following conditions holds: \[ \begin{aligned} & n=2,\quad k\in(0,\infty),\quad m>1;\\ & n\ge 3,\quad k\in\left(0,\tfrac12\right),\quad
  m>1+\frac{(1-k)(n-2)}{n};\\ & n\ge 3,\quad k\in\left[\tfrac12,1\right),\quad
  m>\frac{3n-2}{2n};\\ & n\ge 3,\quad k\in[1,\infty),\quad
  m>\max\left\{1,\frac{3n-2}{2n+2}\right\}. \end{aligned} \] The main contribution is the physically relevant three-dimensional case. In particular, for every \(χ>0\), \(a>0\), \(m>1\) and \(k\ge 1\), the system admits a global bounded classical solution. Thus, in dimension three, nonlinear diffusion of porous-medium type removes the smallness restriction on the chemotactic sensitivity $χ$ that earlier results require in the case \(m=1\) and \(k\geq 1\).

title: On certain mapping properties of a weighted totally geodesic $k$-plane transform on the real hyperbolic space
abstract: In this article, we study a weighted analogue of the totally geodesic $k$-plane transform on the real hyperbolic space. Throughout the article, we are concerned with the mapping properties of this transform. Particularly, we first consider the existence of the operator on weighted Lebesgue spaces, where the weights under consideration are natural to the geometry of the hyperbolic space. Then, we proceed to see the $L^p$-improving mapping properties of the said transform on radial functions. Further, we also prove end-point boundedness results on Lorentz spaces of radial functions. Lastly, we look into the problem of weighted $L^p$-$L^p$ boundedness, and obtain partial results in this direction. In the way of obtaining these results, we also give a spherical integral representation of the weighted totally geodesic $k$-plane transform.

title: The Support-Distribution Conditions for MSRD Codes Reduce to a Single Inequality
abstract: Byrne, Gluesing-Luerssen, and Ravagnani determined the number of codewords with a prescribed nonzero support in a linear maximum sum-rank distance code whose blocks have a common number of columns. Their formula depends only on the code parameters and the support dimensions. Evaluating it for arbitrary parameters gives a family of necessary nonnegativity conditions for existence. We prove their conjecture that this family is equivalent to the condition at the vector of total dimension $d+1$ obtained by filling the longest blocks first, where $d$ is the distance parameter. The resulting explicit criterion applies over every finite field $\mathbb F_q$, for all row numbers $n_i\leqslant m$ and $1\leqslant d<N$, where $m$ is the common number of columns and $N$ is the total number of rows. It also covers the boundary cases in which this vector fills each of its nonzero blocks completely, not explicitly included in the conjecture's displayed parameter range. The proof uses a generating function and an exchange identity to reduce the problem to vectors obtained by filling the longest blocks first. We then estimate alternating sums of elementary symmetric polynomials, with a separate argument for $q=2$. The dual conditions admit the same reduction. For codes that exist, the joint condition follows from sphere-packing bounds for the code and its dual. An infinite family of parameters satisfies the joint condition but admits no such linear code.

title: Quasi-crystalline phase separation in one dimension
abstract: We investigate a Modica-Mortola energy in heterogeneous materials with a quasi-crystalline microstructure, described by a suitable notion of almost periodicity. In the regime where phase separation occurs at a finer scale than homogenization, we establish compactness and $Γ$-convergence results in one dimension for vector-valued phases. The main novelty lies in the explicit characterization of the effective surface energy, which reveals the interplay between phase separation and homogenization. In particular, we prove that heterogeneities can promote the splitting of a phase separation into several energetically favorable microscopic transitions.

title: Coefficient Recombination and Error Estimates for the L2 Method for Subdiffusion on Nonuniform Meshes
abstract: The L2 discretization of the Caputo derivative is attractive for its high-order accuracy, but its analysis on nonuniform temporal meshes is complicated due to the lack of a monotone structure in the discrete coefficients. This difficulty is particularly significant for deriving sharp $L^2$ error estimates in the presence of the typical weak singularity of subdiffusion solutions near the initial time. In this work, we develop a coefficient-recombination framework for the L2 method on nonuniform meshes. Under the adjacent step-ratio condition $0.86\le ρ_k\le 1.16$, $k\ge2$, we prove that the recombined L2 coefficients are positive and monotone. A key ingredient is a cross-row recombination technique: with the recombination parameter associated with a fixed time level, all coefficient rows retain positivity and monotonicity, which allows us to close an induction for the $L^2$ error analysis. For solutions exhibiting the standard initial weak singularity, we derive an $L^2$ error estimate on nonuniform meshes satisfying the step-ratio condition. On a modified graded mesh with grading parameter $r>1$, the estimate yields the convergence rate $\mathcal{O}\!\left(N^{-\min\{rα,\,3-α\}}\right)$, and hence recovers the optimal order $\mathcal{O}(N^{-(3-α)})$ whenever $r\ge(3-α)/α$. Numerical experiments on random nonmonotone meshes and modified graded meshes confirm the theoretical estimates.

title: A Positivity-Preserving Numerical Method for the Free Cox-Ingersoll-Ross Equation
abstract: We introduce a positivity-preserving drift-implicit square-root Euler method for the free Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) equation driven by free Brownian motion. The method is obtained by discretizing the square-root equation implicitly in the drift and preserves strict positivity of the numerical solution without any step-size restriction. Under the Feller condition, we establish the uniqueness of the global strictly positive solution and derive an upper bound for its operator norm. A key ingredient for the error analysis is a free stochastic differential representation of the inverse square-root process. Another key ingredient is an a priori grid-point error estimate for sufficiently small step sizes that yields uniform upper and strictly positive lower spectral bounds for the numerical solution on any fixed finite time interval. These results support the strong convergence of order $1$ and improve the classical results. Moreover, both the exact and numerical solutions are exponentially stable with respect to perturbations of the initial value. The numerical stability holds for arbitrary step sizes, and the associated discrete decay rate converges to its continuous counterpart as the step size tends to zero. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

title: Riccati Equations and the Third Problem of Halmos
abstract:
Rencently, Fang, Hou, Jiang, and Zhang reduced Halmos's third problem to invertible operators with conjugate bi-geometric form. An operator has such a form if, with respect to an orthogonal decomposition, it admits a representation
  $$ T = \begin{pmatrix} A & C \\ 0 & B \end{pmatrix}, \quad A^*, B \in B_1(O_δ),$$
  where $O_δ=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<δ\}$ for some $δ>0$, and $B_1(O_δ)$ denotes the rank-one Cowen--Douglas class.
  We restrict our attention to the case $B=A^*$ with strictly positive coupling $C$, and settle Halmos's third problem for this class of operators. More precisely,we prove that every such operator $T$ is invertible and that $T^{-1}$ has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace. This result contributes to the study of Halmos's third problem within the conjugate bi-geometric framework.The proof combines monotone solutions of operator Riccati equations with strong operator convergence to construct invariant subspaces for associated Hamiltonian operator matrices.

title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
abstract: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.

title: Approximation of the relaxed Euler system at the level of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
abstract: We study the global well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$, for the relaxed compressible Euler system with a Maxwell-type constitutive law for the stress tensor. We show that the corresponding compressible Navier-Stokes solutions serve as both relaxation limits and large-time asymptotic profiles of the global relaxed Euler solutions constructed here. Given a Navier-Stokes background satisfying suitable boundedness and decay assumptions, we construct global smooth relaxed Euler solutions for each fixed $α\in(0,1]$ and sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. Here, the background need not be small. After subtracting the stress initial layer, the approximation error is $O(\varepsilon^α)$ uniformly in time. Under suitable additional conditions on the initial perturbations, this error decays in $L^2$ faster than the decay of standard Navier-Stokes background, uniformly in $\varepsilon$, identifying the background solution as a large-time asymptotic profile. As an application, we obtain the corresponding small-data results using classical Navier-Stokes theory to verify the background assumptions.

title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
abstract: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors. The resulting graph is called a triadic closure of $H$. We study the effect of this operation on local convergence. More precisely, we prove that if a sequence of potentially random finite undirected graphs of $\left( H_n \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges locally in probability to a rooted graph $H^*$, then the corresponding sequence of triadic closures converges locally in probability to the same triadic closure of $H^*$. As a consequence, we obtain a general limit theorem for the clustering coefficients of triadic closures. In particular, we show that the triadic closures can have a strictly positive limiting clustering coefficients even when the limiting clustering coefficients of the parent graph sequence is zero. Finally, we apply our results to several classical sparse random graph models including Erdős-Rényi, configuration, preferential attachment models and compute the limiting clustering coefficients of their triadic closures.

title: Poincaré series of degree-two Chow varieties
abstract: Let $C_{p, 2}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the Chow variety parametrizing effective algebraic $p$-cycles of degree two on $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. We show that its rational cohomology is pure Tate and concentrated in even degrees. An anti-invariant Chern class identity yields a presentation of the cohomology ring as a fiber product, which in turn determines the cohomology over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$. We identify the ordinary Poincaré polynomial with the known virtual formula, determine the optimal ranges over which the coefficients stabilize, and compute the nonrational Poincaré series of the stable space $D(2)$. For the Lawson--Michelsohn map $D(2)\longrightarrow D(\infty)$, the first nonzero rational homotopy kernel occurs in degree eight and is one-dimensional, while the integral kernel has rank one. Finally, we compute the relative homology of the pair $(D(2),BU)$ over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$ and show that additional cohomology generators and nonzero rational homotopy kernels arise in unbounded degrees.

title: Weighted Harris--oscillation contraction and invariant expectations for nonlinear Markov semigroups
abstract:
We establish a weighted contraction principle for sublinear Markov semigroups on noncompact state spaces. Its abstract inputs are a Lyapunov drift condition and a strict local contraction of oscillations on a Lyapunov sublevel set. For locally uniformly parabolic diffusion semigroups, the latter is obtained by applying the parabolic Harnack inequality to both the upper evolution and its conjugate lower evolution: if $u=T_t\varphi$, then $u-m$ and $M-u$ solve the upper and lower Bellman equations, respectively. Combining the resulting local oscillation contraction with the Lyapunov drift yields a strict contraction in a weighted oscillation seminorm, a unique invariant sublinear expectation in the finite-Lyapunov-moment class, and weighted exponential convergence for Borel observables controlled by the Lyapunov function.
  To treat bounded Borel data for $G$-SDEs, we use a canonical covariance-law representation, progressively measurable state maps compatible with conditioning and pasting, and a stopped dynamic programming principle. A probabilistic Krylov--Safonov argument then gives positive-time Hölder regularisation before viscosity identification, thereby avoiding a measurable-data envelope argument. The abstract result is verified for ordinary locally uniformly elliptic SDEs, multiplicative $G$-SDEs, and the full equation with quadratic-variation drift \[
  dX_t=b(X_t)\,dt
  +\sum_{i,j=1}^m h_{ij}(X_t)\,d\langle B^i,B^j\rangle_t
  +\sum_{j=1}^mσ_j(X_t)\,dB_t^j. \] For the full equation the hypotheses are expressed through the effective drift and covariance and are required uniformly over all covariance scenarios. Finally, the contraction and stochastic continuity of the associated stationary process yield ergodicity in the sense of Feng and Zhao.

title: A Sharp Bound of Crossing Limit Cycle for Planar piecewise linear Systems with a Straight Switching Line
abstract: Determining the maximum number of crossing limit cycles in planar discontinuous piecewise linear systems separated by a straight line is a central problem in nonsmooth dynamical systems and a natural piecewise-linear counterpart of Hilbert's sixteenth problem, yet its sharp uniform upper bound has long remained an open problem. In this paper, we prove that any such system admits at most three crossing limit cycles. Combined with known examples realizing three crossing limit cycles, this result establishes that three is the sharp uniform upper bound.

title: On the Turán Number of the Cartesian Product of Two Stars
abstract: We study the Turán number of the Cartesian product of two stars, a family whose order of magnitude is known. For most pairs of star sizes, we determine the leading coefficient exactly. In the remaining congruence class, we give explicit lower and upper bounds for the coefficient at the leading scale. Our lower bounds use blowups of polarity graphs, and our upper bounds use structural estimates on neighbourhoods.

title: $e$-Positive caterpillars have maximum degree at most three
abstract: Dahlberg, She, and van Willigenburg conjectured that every $e$-positive tree has maximum degree at most three. We prove this conjecture for caterpillars. Our proof introduces a specialization--cone method: we evaluate chromatic symmetric functions under finite-support specializations that are nonnegative on the elementary symmetric functions, express the evaluations through transfer matrices, and certify negativity using finitely generated cones. Two specializations and three cones handle all caterpillars remaining after a connected-partition reduction, with no bound on the number or spacing of their trivalent vertices. The required cone inclusions and strict sign inequalities are certified by exact rational arithmetic. We also exhibit two infinite families of non-spider caterpillars of maximum degree four that admit connected partitions of every type, showing that Wolfgang's criterion alone leaves cases requiring further obstructions. Our result also reduces Li's criterion on $e$-positivity for caterpillars of maximum degree three to an explicit condition on the positions of trivalent vertices.

title: Subindices of two-element subsets of finite groups
abstract:
Let $A$ be a nonempty subset of a group $G$. A right subfactor relative to $A$ is a subset $B$ maximal under inclusion among those for which every element of $AB$ has a unique representation as $ab$, with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$. Left subfactors are defined analogously using $BA$. The infima and suprema of the cardinalities of right and left subfactors define four \emph{subindices}. A subset is called \emph{index-stable} if its four subindices coincide.
  For any infinite group $G$, every nonempty finite subset of $G$ is index-stable.
  For finite groups, the situation is more complicated. We prove that for a two-element subset of a finite group, the left and right subindices coincide pairwise. Let $A=\{x,y\}$ with $x\ne y$, and let $X$ be the cyclic subgroup generated by $x^{-1}y$. Then the lower subindex of $A$ is $|G:X|\cdot\lceil |X|/3\rceil$, and the upper subindex is $|G:X|\cdot\lfloor |X|/2\rfloor$. These formulas imply that $A$ is index-stable if and only if $|X|$ is one of $2,3,4,5,7$.
  For any two-element subset of a finite group $G$, the lower subindex is at least $\lceil |G|/3\rceil$, and the upper subindex is at most $\lfloor |G|/2\rfloor$. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in each of these bounds.
  All two-element subsets of a finite group are index-stable if and only if every element of the group has order $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$, $5$, or $7$. We give a complete structural classification of such groups.

title: The maximum number of triangles in regular graphs
abstract: We determine the maximum number of triangles in $n$-vertex $k$-regular graphs and characterize all extremal graphs for all admissible orders when $k$ is odd and for an explicit range of orders when $k$ is even. For even $k$, we also give explicit lower and upper bounds for the remaining orders. As a consequence, we obtain a lower bound on the number of independent sets of size three in $k$-regular graphs and characterize all equality cases. Our exact results confirm the conjecture of Petingi and Rodríguez and the triangle case of a conjecture of Cambie, de Joannis de Verclos and Kang for all odd $k$ and the specified orders when $k$ is even. Moreover, for every even $k\ge18$, we construct counterexamples to both conjectures and obtain a recursive characterization of all extremal graphs of order at least $Ck$, where $C$ is an absolute constant.

title: A polynomial method over formal power series
abstract: We give new upper bounds on families of integer vectors with prescribed coordinate multiplicities and a forbidden scalar product. Our method uses coefficient functions over formal power series and recovers the Frankl--Wilson bound for binary vectors. For vectors in $\{-1,0,1\}^n$, we obtain an exponential improvement over the ordinary polynomial count in a wide range; in certain regimes, we determine the lower limit of the exponential base. We use the new bounds to make progress on several questions in combinatorial geometry. In particular, we improve the base of the exponent in Borsuk's partition problem: we construct finite subsets of $\mathbb R^N$ requiring at least $(1.37+o(1))^{\sqrt N}$ parts of smaller diameter for all sufficiently large $N$, and obtain a base of $1.3839$ along a subsequence of dimensions.

title: Turán numbers for suspensions of bipartite 2-regular graphs
abstract: For a graph $R$, let $\widehat R:=K_1+R$ denote its suspension, obtained by adding a new vertex adjacent to every vertex of $R$. For every fixed nonempty bipartite $2$-regular graph $R$, we determine $\operatorname{ex}(n,\widehat{R})$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and characterize all extremal graphs. Three distinct cases arise, according as $R$ is $2C_6$, a disjoint union of copies of $C_4$, or neither of these. This extends the known exact Turá results on odd wheels to suspensions of arbitrary bipartite 2-regular graphs.

title: The entropy spectra of chaotic maps of an interval
abstract: For a continuous self-map f of a real interval L, let ent(f) denote the supremum of the topological entropies of the restrictions of f to its compact invariant sets; for a compact interval this is the usual topological entropy. For a class P of maps, the entropy spectrum of P is the set of values ent(f) taken by the maps f in P. We determine the entropy spectra of the three standard classes of chaotic maps of the compact interval [0,1]. Devaney chaotic maps have spectrum [(1/2) log 2, infinity], maps of positive entropy have spectrum (0, infinity], and Li-Yorke chaotic maps have spectrum [0, infinity]; thus every entropy compatible with the known lower bounds actually occurs, and the three spectra are strictly nested. Mixing maps have spectrum ((1/2) log 2, infinity], and Devaney chaotic maps with at least two fixed points have spectrum [log 2, infinity]. As a consequence, a Devaney chaotic map of the interval attains the minimal entropy (1/2) log 2 only if it has a unique fixed point and is not mixing. For an arbitrary interval, compact or not, maps with a point of least period n have spectrum [log sigma_n, infinity], where sigma_n are the Stefan constants, and Li-Yorke chaotic maps have spectrum [0, infinity]. The proofs combine a truncation theorem for maps of non-compact intervals, showing that clipping a map to a compact subinterval never creates entropy; a horseshoe argument showing that two fixed points force entropy log 2 on transitive maps; and explicit constructions, including an exact piecewise linear family, a mixing map of infinite entropy, and a square-root construction that halves the entropy of a transitive map.

title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
abstract:
Let $X=V_5$ be the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Along the negative zero-tilt-slope paths for rational-curve ideal classes, degree five is the first degree admitting a positive point correction. We determine the resulting degree-five outer good moduli space: it is reduced with exactly two irreducible components, a normal ten-dimensional principal branch and a smooth corrected branch $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Their scheme-theoretic intersection is a normal determinantal ninefold. Along its singular locus, the principal branch has transverse rank-one $2\times 4$ determinantal singularities, while the intersection has the corresponding $2\times 3$ singularities.
  We construct an explicit small resolution of the principal branch as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petković--Rota Kuznetsov-component sixfold along its point locus. Uniform wall exclusion and point-correction bounds for degrees two through five establish the first correction threshold; the corrected degree-five factors are precisely the ideals of elliptic linear sections parametrized by $\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$.

title: A priori error analysis for the Shliomis ferrofluid model without magnetic regularization
abstract: We develop and analyze a family of conforming, energy-stable spatial semidiscretizations of the Shliomis ferrofluid model in two and three space dimensions. Unlike many existing numerical analyses, we treat the system without introducing magnetic diffusion. The limited spatial control supplied by the energy law complicates the treatment of magnetic nonlinearities in the error analysis. Our formulation retains the rotational coupling and nonlinear magnetic relaxation and incorporates the magnetic normal-flux condition naturally, overcoming the dimensional restriction and boundary-enforcement difficulties of the two-potential approach of Benavides, Nochetto and Shakipov (2026). The error analysis combines consistent stabilization of the Maxwell constraint with a cancellation arising from exact incompressibility and the pointwise symmetry of the Hessian of the magnetic potential. We prove global solvability of the semidiscrete scheme and establish a priori error estimates for sufficiently regular exact solutions under explicit approximation and projection-stability assumptions. We also construct an averaged $\mathrm{H}^2$-conforming projector, following Girault and Scott (2002), that is defined on $\mathrm{L}^1(Ω)$, and establish its Sobolev approximation and stability properties. These properties are needed for the error analysis and are of independent interest.

title: A sharp lower bound for torsional rigidity of convex domains
abstract: For every bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, we establish the following sharp inequality for torsional rigidity $$T(Ω)\ge\frac{2(d+1)}{d}\int\limits_Ω\operatorname{dist}(x,\partialΩ)^2\dd x,$$ where $T(Ω)=4\int\limits_Ωu\dd x$ and $-Δu=1$ in $Ω$, $u\in H^1_0(Ω)$. Equality holds for balls.

title: Designing battery swapping and charging networks for electric freight transport under demand uncertainty
abstract: Long-haul truck electrification requires rapid energy replenishment near freight demand, although dispersed hubs may lack sufficient grid capacity. We study a "Swap-Locally, Charge-Centrally" architecture embedded in a relay freight network: swapping remains close to freight flows, charging can be shifted to grid-suitable hubs, and co-location is retained where economical. A multi-period, two-stage stochastic location-inventory-fleet model coordinates station deployment, replenishment assignments and grid-bounded charging capacity with scenario-dependent battery stocks, batch sizes and incremental fleet requirements. Corridor electrification competes with temporary diesel operation. Building on submodularity-based constraint generation for location-inventory systems, we give an alternative scalar partial-minimization proof that the battery value function is submodular, show that the fleet recourse is affine in the binary swap-station decisions, and develop a Lovász-cut Benders decomposition with hub-period block cuts and a convex battery oracle with analytic gradients and memoization. On a seven-state southeastern U.S. freight network, the method reaches gaps below 0.01% on all five instances, the largest in about four minutes, whereas a strengthened extensive formulation reaches this tolerance only on the two smallest instances within three hours. Stochastic planning avoids the capacity shortfalls of a mean-value plan, and joint planning avoids the battery and fleet costs that sequential siting shifts downstream. The optimized network uses remote charging selectively, keeps most replenishment local, and expands geographic coverage before intensifying capacity within its committed deployment plan.

title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework
abstract: For a time-homogeneous Markov process, the fixed-lag solution operator \( (T_τf)(x)=\mathbb E[f(X_{t+τ})\mid X_t=x] \) of the Kolmogorov backward equation evolves observables linearly and deterministically, even when the dynamics are stochastic. We approximate this operator using a two-stage method where we first approximate this operator directly from data, without knowledge of the governing equation (e.g., Fourier Neural Operator), and then compress the Galerkin projection onto a finite-dimensional observable space that is fixed in advance or selected variationally. The error analysis traces the learning error of the estimator, the sampling error of the Galerkin inner products, and the invariance and reconstruction properties of the observable space to the computed spectra and forecasts. The sampling error enters only through a multiplicative factor. Near an isolated spectral cluster, the invariance defect of a subspace controls its distance from the target invariant subspace. The forecast error is controlled by the one-step error of the reduced model and the projection error of the observable; when the measure is invariant and the reduced model preserves constants and is stable on mean-zero observables, the bound is uniform in the horizon. For deterministic dynamics, a learning rate for Fourier neural operators (FNOs) gives one explicit bound for the learning error. Numerical experiments illustrate spectral approximation and forecasting, including long-rollout stability and a comparison with extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) when fewer transition pairs than basis functions are observed.

title: Exponential singularity and rank bounds for random symmetric matrices
abstract:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ real symmetric random matrix whose entries above the diagonal are independent, each with largest atom at most $β\in (0,1)$. The diagonal entries have an arbitrary joint distribution and are independent of the entries above the diagonal. We prove that \[
  \mathbb{P}[\mathrm{rank}(A)\le n-k]\le 2e^{-c_βnk},\qquad 1\le k\le n, \] where $c_β>0$ depends only on $β$. This extends Han's corank bound to the full range $1\le k\le n$. No moment assumptions are needed, and the entries need not be centered or identically distributed. In particular, the case $k=1$ gives an exponential singularity bound under the uniform atom assumption. Our argument also gives a new proof of the exponential singularity bound for symmetric Rademacher matrices obtained by Campos, Jenssen, Michelen, and Sahasrabudhe. For every fixed $p\in (0,1)$, it yields the exponential singularity bound conjectured by Costello and Vu for the adjacency matrix of the Erdős--Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$, where the case $p=1/2$ was previously proved by Han.

title: On edge-ordered Ramsey numbers of hypergraphs
abstract: For an integer $h\geq2$, an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $H^<$ is an $h$-uniform hypergraph with a linear ordering of its hyperedges. For an integer $q \geq 1$, the edge-ordered Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(H^<;q)$ of $H^<$ is the smallest positive integer $N$ such that there exists an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $G^<$ on $N$ vertices such that, for every $q$-coloring of the hyperedges of $G^<$, there is a monochromatic copy of $H^<$ in $G^<$ preserving the hyperedge order. In this note, we show that, for every edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $F^<$ on $n$ vertices with $m\geq1$ hyperedges, $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(F^<;q) \leq R_h(F;q)^{Cm^2}$ where $F$ is the underlying unordered hypergraph, $R_h(F;q)$ is its standard $q$-color Ramsey number, and $C=C(h,q)>0$ is a constant. For fixed $h\geq3$ and $q\geq2$, this shows that prescribing the hyperedge order does not require an increase in the tower height of the classical upper bound. It also settles a problem posed by Fox and Li (2020), and for $h=2$ gives the bound $2^{O(n^4\log n)}$, improving their bounds for every fixed $q \geq 3$.

title: Splitting Compositions of Monotone Operators
abstract:
Coupled convex optimisation equilibria, bilinear saddle and potential systems, and nonlinear electronic device laws lead naturally to inclusions of the form $0\in Hx+A(Bx)-b$, where $A$ and $B$ are maximal monotone but their composition need not be monotone. We introduce a new class of splitting algorithms that solve such inclusions. Introducing the intermediate graph variable $y\in Bx$ exposes a directed two-row system. A one-parameter family of kernels produces a lower-triangular warped-resolvent iteration evaluated with one application of $H$ and the ordinary resolvents $J_{αA}$ and $J_{βB}$. Appropriate specializations of the problem data and algorithmic parameters recover forward--backward, inertial, primal--dual, and Douglas--Rachford constructions, while setting $H=b=0$ generates three novel algorithms for the pure composition $0\in A(Bx)$.
  Convergence of the coupled method is certified by an explicit nonnegative two-block gain matrix. Its Schur condition yields contraction in particular weighted norms, global linear convergence, and residual error estimates. For the general problem class, our convergence condition is shown to be sharp for an explicitly constructed linear family. When the problem is specialized to a pure composition, we prove convergence under the weaker assumption that only one operator is strongly monotone. This weaker regime is illustrated on a nonlinear circuit problem. We further illustrate our methods by solving inference problems for cascaded equilibrium neural networks.

title: Balancing tautological intersection numbers
abstract: We prove the three balancing inequalities conjectured by the authors about 20 years ago: moving one unit from a larger index to a smaller one cannot decrease a mixed tautological intersection number, whether the two distinguished insertions are psi classes, kappa classes, or Hodge Chern classes.

title: Meromorphic order from Taylor coefficients, least singular values of Hankel matrices and rational approximants
abstract: We introduce a natural notion of generalized order for entire and meromorphic functions and express it in terms of their Taylor coefficients. More precisely, one formula uses the least singular values of Hankel matrices of the coefficients, and the other uses their determinants. These formulas generalize the classical coefficient formula for the order of entire functions and its extensions by Edrei and Sheremeta. The proof combines a theorem of Pommerenke with a bound for the Nevanlinna characteristic that results from a convergence theorem for rational approximants introduced by Prokhorov. We also characterize the largest class of growth scales for which the associated generalized order is well-behaved.

title: Singularity removal in nonlocal operator inequalities on domains and applications
abstract: We prove that certain classes of nonlocal integral estimates on domains, involving operators, may be reduced to the local analogues without the singular weight on cubes. The theory applies to two-sided inverse doubling and quasi-monotone kernels with some moment conditions, and with a left-hand-side operator with average domain-bi-Lipschitz properties. Direct applications to fractional semi-norm inequalities in Peridynamics, such as fractional Korn's inequalities and Geometric Rigidity Estimates are presented.

title: Diameter-two graphs whose mutual-visibility chromatic number equals their chromatic number
abstract: A set $S$ of vertices of a graph $G$ is a mutual-visibility set if every pair of vertices of $S$ is joined by a shortest path whose internal vertices avoid $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $χ_μ(G)$ is the least number of mutual-visibility sets into which $V(G)$ can be partitioned. Klavžar, Kuziak, Valenzuela Tripodoro and Yero (2025) proved that $χ_μ(G)\leχ(G)$ whenever $G$ has diameter two, observed that equality holds for complete bipartite graphs, and asked whether there are any other diameter-two graphs attaining equality. We answer this question in the affirmative. We construct a graph $G_{11}$ of order 11 and diameter two with $χ_μ(G_{11})=χ(G_{11})=3$, and an infinite family of such graphs obtained from $G_{11}$ by replacing one vertex with pairwise non-adjacent copies of it.

title: Complete regular dessins and non-metacyclic bicyclic 2-groups with cyclic commutator subgroup
abstract:
We study complete regular dessins with underlying graph ${\mathcal K}_{2^e,2^f}$, where $e\geq f\geq 2$, whose automorphism groups are non-metacyclic. Together with the cases of coprime orders and odd-prime-power orders, this is one of the basic classes needed for Jones's open classification problem for regular dessins of complete bipartite graphs. Within the 2-power case, the present paper treats the subcase in which the commutator subgroup is cyclic; it is the first of three papers devoted to the non-metacyclic case.
  Our approach is group-theoretic. The automorphism group $G$ of a regular dessin of ${\mathcal K}_{2^e,2^f}$ admits an exact bicyclic factorization $G=\langle b\rangle\langle w\rangle$ of type $(2^e,2^f)$ with $\langle b\rangle\cap\langle w\rangle=1$. For a fixed group $G$, two exact generating pairs give isomorphic dessins exactly when they lie in the same orbit under ${\rm A}ut(G)$. Thus the classification reduces to three group-theoretic tasks: determining the isomorphism classes of the possible groups $G$, characterizing their exact bicyclic generating pairs, and computing $|{\rm A}ut(G)|$. Berkovich and Janko divided the relevant non-metacyclic groups, through parameterized presentations, according to whether the commutator subgroup is cyclic, contains a cyclic subgroup of index $2$, or contains a cyclic subgroup of index $2^r$ with $r>1$. However, their classification does not identify which parameter values in these presentations define isomorphic groups; this problem was raised by Janko in {J}. We carry out these steps for the cyclic-commutator case. This settles Janko's isomorphism-classification problem in this case and yields a complete classification and enumeration of the corresponding regular dessins.

title: A short survey on the convexity of level sets for divergence-form elliptic equations
abstract:
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded, smooth and (uniformly) convex domain, and let $u$ be a positive solution to an elliptic boundary value problem with zero Dirichlet data. A classical problem in the analysis of partial differential equations is to determine whether the convexity of $Ω$ is inherited by the superlevel (or sublevel) sets of $u$.
  This survey considers divergence-form equations in bounded convex domains. For torsion functions, first eigenfunctions, and semilinear equations with sublinear nonlinearities, concavity of suitable transforms of $u$ gives positive results. Two further methods, i.e. envelope constructions and constant-rank theorems for level-set curvature, often provide alternative routes to convexity and related properties. These results are complemented by counterexamples, showing that in general convexity of the domain and ellipticity of the operator do not guarantee quasiconvexity for every solution. We present these counterexamples through a shared underlying idea, and describe the distinct ways in which different equations implement this idea.

title: Higher genus polylogarithms associated with the D'Hoker-Hidding-Schlotterer connection
abstract: We study higher genus polylogarithms associated with the D'Hoker-Hidding-Schlotterer (DHS) connection defined on families of Riemann surfaces of any genus with marked points. Under separating degenerations of Riemann surfaces, we show that the DHS connection can be constructed by gluing the Brown-Levin (BL) connections on elliptic curves and the Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov (KZ) connections on pointed Riemann spheres. Therefore, the associated higher genus polylogarithms can be described explicitly as power series in deformation parameters and their logarithms for the families of Riemann surfaces whose coefficients are expressed by multiple zeta values and elliptic multiple zeta values.

title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
abstract:
We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two. Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle.
  More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic Néron--Severi lattice. The key new result is the congruence property of the subgroup generated by reflective involutions in $O(U\oplus N)$ for anisotropic even lattices $N$ of signature $(1,1)$. Combined with the local generation theorem and Chow-theoretic criterion of Li--Yu--Zhang, this gives the required reflective decompositions and their consequences for zero-cycles.

title: Large Ree groups acting point and line-primitively on finite generalised quadrangles
abstract: Suppose we have a finite thick generalised quadrangle whose automorphism group $G$ acts primitively on both the set of points and the set of lines. Then $G$ must be almost simple. Furthermore, $\textrm{soc}(G)$ cannot be isomorphic to ${}^2 B_2(2^{2m+1})$ or ${}^2 G_2(3^{2m+1})$, where $m$ is a positive integer. In this paper, we show that $\textrm{soc}(G)$ cannot be isomorphic to ${}^2 F_4(2^{2m+1})$.

title: The fundamental solution of a family of anisotropic fourth-order parabolic equations: small-time asymptotics and related Gaussian estimates
abstract: We study the fundamental solutions of a class of uniformly elliptic fourth-order parabolic equations in two dimensions, whose principal symbols are not necessarily strongly convex. For constant-coefficient operators, we derive precise small-time asymptotic formulas along certain special directions. These formulas are obtained by the method of steepest descent and reveal the dependence of the asymptotic behavior on the coefficients of the symbol. We subsequently consider operators with bounded measurable coefficients, subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions, and establish Gaussian bounds for their fundamental solutions by means of Davies' exponential perturbation method. The exponential constant in these bounds is shown to be sharp, as a consequence of the constant-coefficient asymptotics.

title: Syzygy-Quiver Formulas and Finitistic Dimensions of Special Biserial Algebras
abstract:
Let $Λ$ be a finite dimensional algebra over a field $\mathbf{k}$. We introduce the reachable syzygy quiver of $Λ$, a directed multigraph whose vertices are the isomorphism classes of indecomposable nonprojective direct summands of iterated syzygies of simple modules, and whose arrows record nonprojective summands of first syzygies. The projective dimension of a vertex is one plus its directed path height, allowing the global and finitistic dimensions of $Λ$ to be read off from this height function. This formula holds for every finite dimensional algebra, but its states are arbitrary modules.
  We show that when the first syzygy of an indecomposable module admits a closed combinatorial description from the bound quiver, this state space reduces to a smaller combinatorial quiver, making the global and finitistic dimensions exact computable invariants. We carry this out in three stages. Over a special biserial algebra, the Liu--Morin closure theorem identifies the reachable syzygy quiver with a string-syzygy quiver whose vertices are string modules. Over a string algebra, this compresses to the relation-chain quiver of Xin and Zhang, recovering their global dimension formula along with a parallel formula for the finitistic dimension. Over an arbitrary biserial algebra, the universal formula holds, but uniform compression to paths or strings is impossible, with the Skowroński--Waschbüsch algebra providing a witness. Finally, we show two string algebras may share the same Gabriel quiver but have distinct global dimensions, proving the ideal of relations is indispensable for these invariants, and we prove that a pointwise homological reduction to a string algebra on the same quiver preserving the monomials of the relations is impossible.

title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.

title: Symbolic depth functions of edge ideals via local graph structure
abstract: We study the depth of symbolic powers of edge ideals, focusing on local properties of graphs. First, we give several sufficient conditions for the symbolic depth function to be non-increasing, using local properties of graphs and local cohomology. Next, we give a counterexample to a conjecture of Minh, T.N. Trung, and Vu concerning the stable value of the symbolic depth function, where the difference between the conjectured value and the actual value can be arbitrary large. Finally, we study a conjecture of Muta stating the depth of a symbolic power of an edge ideal is at least that of the corresponding ordinary power. We prove it for graphs whose connected components are unicyclic or bipartite.

title: A New Perspective on Optimal Power Flow: From Control Theory to Numerical Optimization
abstract: The optimal power flow (OPF) problem is a classical non-convex optimization problem with nonlinear constraints and multiple potential solutions. Existing methods often fail to find the global optimal solution, motivating the development of a method to identify multiple local solutions. This paper applies the optimal control principle to solve the OPF problem, aiming to systematically explore all feasible solutions within a single run. We first handle the constraints in the OPF problem using the penalty method and the Lagrange multiplier, and then reformulate it as an optimal control problem. The connection between the two problems is established by the maximum principle. Moreover, a numerical algorithm is proposed to solve this optimal control problem. The state trajectory of the system can rapidly and stably converge to the solution of the OPF problem. By designing the initial control sequence, the proposed method can successfully find multiple solutions and escape local solutions. Finally, simulations were conducted on several representative test systems to validate the potential of the proposed method in identifying multiple solutions for non-convex problems.

title: Spectral Characterization, Local Rigidity and Morse Index of Bubble Solutions to the CR Fractional Yamabe Problem
abstract: We study bubble solutions to the critical CR fractional Yamabe equation on the Heisenberg group for the full range \(0<γ<\frac{Q}{2}\), including the admissible integer-order cases. The CR fractional operator is genuinely nonlocal and is described by Gamma-function spectral multipliers. Its structure differs from that of the Euclidean fractional Laplacian, so the linearized analysis cannot be obtained by a direct extension of integer-order arguments. We develop a direct spectral approach based on the Cayley intertwining relation and the complex spherical-harmonic decomposition, which characterizes the kernel of the linearized operator in terms of infinitesimal translation and dilation modes without reducing the equation to an integral equation or requiring a separate decay analysis. As a byproduct, we obtain the exact normalization constant of the standard bubble throughout the admissible range. We then prove three main results: $(i)$ the non-degeneracy of the bubble manifold; $(ii)$ the local rigidity of the bubble manifold, via a uniform invertibility estimate on the orthogonal complement of the tangent space, with an explicit optimal constant; $(iii)$ the Morse index of every positive bubble is exactly one. The results provide a unified spectral and variational framework for the CR Yamabe problem on the Heisenberg group, covering both integer and noninteger orders.

title: Sharp Tilting Inequalities
abstract: For positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$ and $1/2\leα\le1$, we establish $\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[A\,D\log(A^α+B^α)(B^α)\right] \le s^s(1-s)^{1-s}\operatorname{Tr}[A^αB^{1-α}]$, where $s=(1-α)/α$, with the optimal coefficient. The proof uses a superoperator representation of the directional derivative of the logarithm and an Araki-type estimate for the derivative of a fractional power. Both this inequality and its symmetric-quotient counterpart extend to positive trace-class $A$ and positive, possibly unbounded, self-adjoint $B$ on a separable Hilbert space.

title: Topological Insights and Combinatorial Frameworks for Twist Knot Complements
abstract: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends. In this article, we present explicit topological and combinatorial descriptions of all twist knot complements via the construction of suitable cell structures. Our method produces a closed $3$-dimensional pseudomanifold with a single vertex, arising from prescribed face pairings of a faceted $3$-ball. Removing the vertex yields the complement of the corresponding twist knot. The construction naturally induces ideal triangulations of these knot complements, several of which are shown to be facet-minimal. Beyond providing concrete models, our approach offers new perspectives on the topology of knot complements and leads to some open research problems.

title: On equivariant affineness in elliptic cohomology
abstract:
We investigate equivariant affineness in spectral algebraic geometry: the phenomenon where $\infty$-categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of a spectral stack are equivalent to $\infty$-categories of modules over an equivariant ring spectrum. In the nonequivariant case, this is known as 0-affineness, and has been studied by Gaitsgory, Mathew--Meier, amongst others. Allowing for equivariant phenomena opens up a much wider class of spectral stacks to be studied through the lens of spectra.
  The spectral stacks at the heart of our analysis are oriented elliptic curves, their associated Hilbert schemes, and related constructions. When working over the universal base, so the moduli stack of oriented elliptic curves, we show that these spectral stacks are $U(1)$-, $U(n)$-, and $SU(n)$-equivariantly affine, with associated $G$-ring spectrum Gepner--Meier's equivariant topological modular forms $\mathrm{TMF}_G$. Our results also encompass the groups $Sp(n)$ as well as all finite products of such groups. Our most general result is a relative statement over an arbitrary base stack. These results can be viewed as an integral and global refinement of Greenlees' algebraic model for modules over rational $U(1)$-equivariant elliptic cohomology.

title: Characterizations of $\varphi$-inner uniform domains and $\varphi$-uniform domains in metric spaces
abstract: In this paper, we study $\varphi$-uniform/-inner uniform domains in metric spaces. In our first main result, we establish quantitative characterizations of three different definitions of $\varphi$-uniformity/-inner uniformity in length spaces. In our second main result, we obtain a geometric sufficient condition of $\varphi$-uniform/-inner uniform domains in doubling length spaces, which extends the corresponding result of Guo-Huang-Wang [arXiv 2025] and Gao-Guo-Huang-Wang [arXiv 2025] for linear case.

title: Conic-Lifting for Learning-rate-free Convex Optimization
abstract: A central topic in online and stochastic optimization is to design algorithms that do not require tuning of hyperparameters. Successful strategies in online learning include AdaGrad-style learning rates, Conic Blackwell algorithms, and parameter-free algorithms. However, these classes require different, often difficult, analyses. We develop a unifying family of Online Convex Optimization (OCO) algorithms that require no user-tuned learning rate on convex domains that may be unbounded. The construction lifts the domain to a cone by adding one scalar coordinate, an idea going back to Blackwell (1954). The lifted subgradients are orthogonal to the corresponding lifted decisions, leaving the comparator scale free to optimize in the regret analysis. Applying Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) and Online Mirror Descent (OMD) on the cone recovers Conic Blackwell Algorithm (CBA) and Conic Blackwell Algorithm Plus (CBA$^+$) on bounded domains in Hilbert spaces and extends them to finite-dimensional normed spaces with a strongly convex squared norm. For arbitrary nonempty closed convex domains in these spaces, a known gradient bound yields parameter-free regret guarantees. Surprisingly, on an unconstrained Hilbert space, the construction recovers the Krichevsky--Trofimov (KT) coin-betting algorithm exactly. We also give a parameter-free algorithm for unconstrained domains that requires no gradient bound.

title: Propagation of Sobolev Regularity for Integral-Invariant Weak Solutions of the Linear Transport Equation
abstract: Previous work strengthened the time integrability of integral-invariant weak solutions from L^1 to L^\infty within a spatial L^2 framework.This paper studies the propagation of Sobolev regularity for integral-invariant weak solutions of the conservative linear scalar transport equation.We first derive a representation formula along the flow and a distributional equation from integral identities against adjoint-transported test functions on domains moving with the same characteristic flow,and relate the weak formulation in time, including an endpoint term for the initial data, to representatives satisfying the pointwise-in-time integral definition.We then give a unified proof for k=1,2:under u_0\in H^k(Ω_0)and Assumption \mathsf A_{k+1},the pullback of the solution belongs to C^1([0,T];H^k(Ω_0)),the material derivative has spatial $H^k$ regularity,and the Eulerian time derivative has spatial H^{k-1} regularity.The corresponding time continuity is understood after pullback to the fixed domain by the flow.In both cases, U\in H^1(Q);when k=2, we further obtain \nabla_xU\in H^1(Q;\R^d).The pullback differentiability and the spatial estimates for the material derivativeprovide information beyond first-order space-time Sobolev regularity alone.The proof combines estimates for the characteristic flow with Sobolev product and composition rules.Under the additional assumption that the zero extension of the initial data belongs to H^2(\R^d),we also establish $H^1(0,T;H^1(\R^d))$ regularity in the fixed ambient space.Counterexamples show that these results concern regularity propagation under additional assumptions: general L^2 initial data do not automatically yield spatial smoothing,and spatial regularity of the material derivative cannot replace the corresponding regularity of the Eulerian time derivative.

title: Length Bounds for MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Arbitrary Positive Genus
abstract: We study the length of maximum distance separable algebraic geometry codes from curves of arbitrary positive genus. For fixed genus, we prove that the asymptotic ratio of the length to the field size is at most $1/2$ when both the dimension and the codimension grow faster than the logarithm of the field size. We also give explicit bounds under logarithmic dimension conditions. The bounds hold in every characteristic and are uniform in the curve and the evaluation set. The proof combines character sums on the Jacobian with an estimate for sums of distinct points.

title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan 2-lift towers via Hilbert modular forms
abstract:
Expander graphs have been central objects of study for over fifty years. Ramanujan graphs attain the asymptotically optimal nontrivial adjacency-eigenvalue threshold for infinite fixed-degree families. The original arithmetic constructions by Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak (1988) and Margulis (1988), and the iterative $2$-lift method of Bilu-Linial (2006) provide different approaches to Ramanujan graph constructions. Motivated by work on Mealy automata, we combine both approaches to give the following new arithmetic construction.
  For every prime $p\equiv 1\pmod {17}$, we construct a infinite tower of $(p+1)$-regular non-bipartite Ramanujan graphs on $2^n$ vertices, with label-preserving $2$-lifts between consecutive levels. These construction is strongly explicit: for fixed $p$, a neighbor or lift sign is computable in $O_p(n^3)$ bit operations.
