The construction uses fixed algebraic $2$-adic transformations, specified by finite data computable in preprocessing depending only on $p$.
  The main number-theoretic tool is Blasius's Ramanujan-Petersson theorem for Hilbert modular forms, applied through the Jacquet-Langlands correspondence to obtain the sharp bound $|λ|\leq2\sqrt p$ for every nontrivial adjacency eigenvalue of our $(p+1)$-regular graphs. The transformations preserve $2$-adic distance, which gives the binary covers and an explicit formula for their signings.

title: A-T-menability and metric amenability for HLS groupoids
abstract: We characterise coarse embeddability of box spaces into Hilbert space in terms of a-T-menability of the associated Higson-Lafforgue-Skandalis (HLS) groupoids. Moreover, we prove that a-T-menability and metric amenability are independent for HLS groupoids: all four possible combinations occur among HLS groupoids associated with approximating sequences of the free group $\mathbb F_2$. The two separating examples are constructed using relative expansion and twisted spectral-gap techniques, respectively.

title: Sharp observation time for wave equations with an inverse-square boundary potential
abstract:
We determine the sharp observation-time threshold for the autonomous, pure-potential wave equation with an inverse-square boundary singularity on the unit ball. For every fixed $κ<0$, full-boundary observability holds on $(-T,T)$ whenever $T>1$ and fails when $T<1$. This resolves, for this model, the optimal-time question raised by Enciso, Shao, and Vergara [J. Eur. Math. Soc. 23 (2021), 3459--3495] and extends their parameter range $-\frac12<κ<0$ to all $κ<0$, including the limit-point regime $κ\leq-\frac12$.
  Our approach is based on the Ingham--Beurling theory of nonharmonic Fourier series. Spherical harmonic decomposition reduces the problem to one-dimensional singular operators, for which we establish frequency separation, local counting estimates, and lower bounds for the boundary norming constants, uniformly in the angular parameter. A quantitative Ingham--Beurling inequality then yields the sharp-time observability estimate.
  As a by-product, this spectral approach provides an independent proof of boundary observability and an explicit functional characterization of its maximal $L^2$ observation domain. The latter is described by a weighted $\ell^2$ condition on the spectral coefficients and consists precisely of energy solutions whose distributional Neumann trace belongs to $L^2$. It contains the boundary-admissible energy solutions considered in Enciso--Shao--Vergara's original work.

title: Guaranteed indirect delivery in directed networks: The joint extremal function and explicit attaining constructions
abstract: A messenger and a pursuer move alternately on a finite loopless directed graph, with complete information and waiting permitted. The messenger moves first and wins upon reaching a designated recipient, before interception there. We determine the maximum number $M(n,m)$ of ordered nonadjacent source--recipient pairs for which delivery is guaranteed against every initial pursuer position, among graphs with $n$ vertices and $m$ arcs. We give the exact value and an explicit attaining graph for every admissible pair $(n,m)$. For $n\ge12$, a piecewise formula describes sparse growth, the interval $2n\le m\le n(n-3)$ in which every missing pair can be guaranteed, a dense staircase, and the zero range above $n(n-2)$. Complete finite tables cover smaller orders. The proofs combine degree and support bounds, local strategy composition, protected routing, and constructions in the missing-arc graph. Finite exceptional cases use explicit strategy certificates and complete computational exclusions. Reproducible programs and certificates accompany the paper; a Lean development verifies the complete formula for $n\ge12$ and $m\ge24$, the claimed scores of prescribed constructions at every admissible pair, and further finite upper bounds. Its remaining obligations are stated separately.

title: Optimal fiber comparisons for random tensors
abstract: We extend Seginer's matrix norm comparison to tensors with optimal dependence on the tensor order. For a real tensor $T$ of order $k\ge2$ with centered, integrable, independent and identically distributed entries, we prove $\mathbb{E} f(T)\le\mathbb{E}\lVert T\rVert_{\mathrm{inj}} \le C\sqrt{k\log k}\,\mathbb{E} f(T)$, where $f(T)$ is the largest Euclidean norm of a one-dimensional fiber and $C$ is universal. The comparison holds for every finite rectangular format, and the entry law may depend on both the dimensions and the tensor order. We show that the factor $\sqrt{k\log k}$ is optimal by considering Rademacher tensors on $[2]^k$.

title: Contour-Based Fast Fractional Integration in a Jacobi Fractional Polynomial Basis
abstract: We develop a contour-based method for applying Riemann--Liouville fractional integrals in a Jacobi fractional polynomial basis with an endpoint weight. A Gamma-ratio representation reduces the action to contour quadrature and banded ultraspherical solves. For a fixed number of contour nodes, the cost and storage are linear in the polynomial dimension. For fractional equations, we construct selected diagonals of a short rational approximation directly and use their banded factorizations as reusable right preconditioners for Krylov iterations. Numerical experiments show accurate integral actions and substantially reduced solution costs across Abel, multi-order, BBO, deferred-correction, eigenvalue, and boundary-value problems.

title: Optimality and Exact Moment-SDP Formulations for Robust Two-Stage Convex Polynomial Multiobjective Optimization
abstract: In this paper, we study Geoffrion properly efficient solutions of affinely adjustable robust two-stage convex polynomial multiobjective optimization problems with spectrahedral uncertainty. For convex polynomial data, we establish sufficient optimality conditions and necessary conditions under a Slater condition. Under SOS-convexity, we obtain an exact SOS characterization of proper efficiency. Using strictly positive weighted-sum scalarization, we develop a finite-dimensional moment-SDP formulation and establish its optimal-value exactness under the strict feasibility condition. We further establish the recovery results connecting Geoffrion properly efficient solutions with moment-SDP optimal solutions.

title: Optimal quantitative stability for the anisotropic Alexandrov soap bubble theorem and Heintze-Karcher inequality
abstract:
The present paper provides linear quantitative stability estimates for the anisotropic Alexandrov soap bubble theorem. The estimates are sharp and, to the authors' knowledge, provide the first sharp quantitative version of Alexandrov's theorem in the anisotropic setting.
  Our estimates establish quantitative closeness to the Wulff shape, also providing sharp control of the closeness of the Gauss maps. As shown by the authors for the classical case, such a control can play a crucial role in achieving optimal profiles for arbitrary deviations and stronger measures of closeness. We also obtain sharp control of the so-called (anisotropic) excess.
  The paper also provides the first sharp quantitative version of the anisotropic Heintze-Karcher inequality. For the Heintze-Karcher inequality, the stability estimates providing closeness of the Gauss maps and control of the excess are new even in the classical (isotropic) setting.

title: Stopping Rules and the Poisson Boundary of Random Walks on Countable Groups
abstract: In this paper, we study the terminal laws and Poisson boundaries obtained by stopping random walks on countable groups. For a transient walk, we give a direct Green-potential characterization of randomized stopping distributions and show that the terminal law determines the mean stopping time. On free groups, this yields finitely supported randomized stopping distributions at a positive total variation distance from every ordinary stopping distribution. We construct symmetric, fully supported recurrent measures of finite entropy on countable locally finite groups and obtain ordinary strict boundary enlargements when the group is not Choquet-Deny. For generating source and terminal measures of finite entropy, positive asymptotic entropy of the source forces the stopping time to have finite mean. A direct proof of the finite-mean entropy formula and boundary preservation then shows that a finite-entropy stopping chain has at most one strict enlargement. An exact stopped-word entropy identity shows that infinite-mean ordinary stopping with a finite-entropy terminal law has infinite conditional history entropy.

title: Linear hereditary quasirandomness
abstract: Conlon, Fox and Sudakov (\emph{Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.} \textbf{164} (2018), 385--399) conjectured that hereditary subgraph counts force quasirandomness with linear dependence on the counting error. We prove this for every graph containing an edge. Let \(H\) have \(r\) vertices and \(m\ge1\) edges, and fix \(p\in(0,1)\). If every subset \(S\) of an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) contains \(p^m|S|^r\pmδn^r\) labelled injective copies of \(H\), then \(\lvert e_G(A,B)-p|A||B|\rvert\le C_{H,p}δn^2\) for all \(A,B\subseteq V(G)\), where \(e_G(A,B)\) counts ordered adjacent pairs. The proof extracts averaged rooted counts and represents each nonlinear term by a linear map in one selected edge factor. Composing two such maps gives an edge substitution with a superlinear cut-norm bound. A separate star expansion gives stronger local estimates for triangle-free graphs. The linear order is best possible even when \(2e(G)/n^2=p+O(n^{-2})\).

title: Unified transform method for nonautonomous linear evolution equations: rigorous analysis and qualitative theory
abstract: Established herein is the rigorous extension of the celebrated Fokas unified transform method for linear evolution PDE with time-dependent coefficients. As illustrative examples, considered below and rigorously analysed in detail are non-homogeneous initial-boundary-value problems, formulated on the half-line, for the heat equation and the modified heat (also widely known as Barenblatt's pseudo-parabolic) equation with reaction terms and temporally varying coefficients. Solution formulae are derived formally via suitable implementation of the UTM, and rigorously verified a posteriori, in the classical sense. The latter task relies on complex-analytic tools and careful interpretation of the obtained integral representations. The explicit solutions established here are then used for investigating qualitative properties. These include regularity, boundary behavior near the axes of the domain as well as long-range and eventual periodicity asymptotics. Notably, smoothness of the solution up to the boundaries depends on compatibility conditions between initial, boundary and forcing data, into which interjected now are initial values of the coefficients. Further results pertaining to solution uniqueness, analyticity and controllability of the addressed problems are thence deduced in light of the preceding qualitative theory.

title: Random semigroups á la Gromov
abstract: We introduce a model of random semigroups analogous to Gromov's density model for random groups. For a fixed number $n\ge 2$ of generators and a density parameter $δ\in (0,1)$, we impose a uniformly chosen set of $\lfloor n^{2δl}\rfloor$ relations of the form $u=v$, where $u,v$ are distinct words of length at most $l$, and study the resulting semigroup as $l\to\infty$. We prove that, with overwhelming probability, above density $1/2$ the semigroup is trivial, while below density $1/2$ it contains a free subsemigroup of rank two, has a Golod-Shafarevich semigroup algebra over every field, and has a homomorphic image which generates a non-elementary hyperbolic group. We also show that the small cancellation condition $C(m)$ holds with overwhelming probability whenever $δ<1/2m$. Finally, for $n\ge 3$, at critical density $1/2$ we obtain a subsequential limiting distribution on finite semigroups, with positive mass at the trivial semigroup and unbounded support in size. This contrasts with random groups, which have order at most two with overwhelming probability at critical density.

title: Carbon-Aware Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Decision-Focused Learning
abstract: Electric vehicles produce no tailpipe emissions, but charging them produces emissions that depend on the time-varying generation mix of the electricity consumed. We study an Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with a carbon-aware objective that accounts for charging-related emissions alongside conventional routing costs. The problem determines routing, charging, and waiting decisions, allowing charging demand to be shifted toward periods with lower grid carbon intensity. Because these decisions depend on forecasts of future carbon intensity, we propose a decision-focused learning approach so that the training of the model employed for predicting the carbon intensity of the grid over time is solver-aware. In particular, we train a linear predictor using approximate SPO+ directions and employ a time-limited Large Neighborhood Search followed by exact postprocessing as the underlying solver. Experiments on realistic Germany-based instances show that explicitly considering charging-related emissions reduces realized emissions by 28.76% on average relative to carbon-blind optimization, although at the expense of higher non-carbon operating cost. Moreover, decision-focused training reduces realized total cost by 2.30% on average relative to conventional prediction-focused learning and performs better on 75.5% of the test instances, despite substantially lower pointwise predictive accuracy. Finally, we show that its average advantage remains positive across varied solver configurations and carbon-cost weights.

title: Automorphism groups of smooth quartic threefolds
abstract: We classify finite groups of automorphisms of smooth quartic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$. Every such group embeds into one of $17$ maximal groups, which we realize by explicit equations and matrix generators. Among finite subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}(5,\mathbb{C})$ preserving a smooth quartic threefold, there are exactly $24$ maximal ones up to conjugacy, and we use them to determine the $194$ groups that occur as full automorphism groups. As an application, we classify the finite groups of projective automorphisms of smooth quartic surfaces and show that there are exactly $12$ maximal ones up to conjugacy in $\mathrm{PGL}(4,\mathbb{C})$.

title: Improving Energy Efficiency of Uplink RSMA via Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver
abstract: This paper investigates an uplink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) network empowered by a Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR) to maximize energy efficiency (EE). To overcome the amplitude-only measurement limitation of the considered direct readout RAQR, we devise a phase alignment mechanism that linearizes the received signal while retaining full channel energy, thereby enabling tractable optimization. The resulting non-convex fractional EE problem is transformed via Dinkelbach's method. For IoT scenarios with symmetric rate requirements, we derive exact closed-form power allocation from the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, which yields a globally optimal bisection search with negligible computational latency. For asymmetric rate requirements, we develop a generalized block coordinate descent-based power allocation (BCD-PA) framework that eliminates reliance on expensive interior-point solvers. We further propose a low-complexity paired allocation (LC-Paired) that exploits user pairing and closed-form bandwidth solutions via the Lambert-W function. Simulation results confirm that the KKT-based scheme attains the highest EE, while the BCD-PA offers a flexible complexity-performance trade-off. The LC-Paired scheme drastically reduces computational cost with only moderate EE degradation.

title: Existence and spectral instability of steady rolls in the Nikolaevskiy equation: a computer-assisted study
abstract: The Nikolaevskiy equation is a model of short-wave pattern formation coupled to a neutral long-wave mode, and it is believed that all of its spatially periodic steady states are unstable. Existing results are formal, numerical, or restricted to a small neighbourhood of onset. We give computer-assisted proofs of three results. First, for every wavenumber q in [0.9, 1.1] and every control parameter r between the onset value (1-q^2)^2 and 4, the equation has a nontrivial, real-analytic, odd steady roll; these rolls form a single continuous two-parameter family that bifurcates from the trivial state at onset, with an explicit amplitude bound proportional to the square root of the distance to onset. Second, every roll of this family with r in [0.25, 4] is spectrally unstable on the real line: its linearisation has a Bloch eigenvalue with real part at least 6.7e-4, and at least 0.13 for r >= 0.575. Third, at nine sample points we enclose, at a small Bloch number, the eigenvalue numerically identified with the long-wave (Matthews-Cox) branch; its real part is positive at seven points and negative at two, while strongly unstable eigenvalues exist at all nine. The proofs combine a parametrised Newton-Kantorovich theorem, a desingularisation near onset, Taylor-model bounds on parameter boxes, and a Weyl-sequence argument for the Bloch spectrum; all estimates are evaluated in rigorous interval arithmetic.

title: Non-linear contexts and dependent operads
abstract: We study the category $\mathbf{Dep_{aff}}$ of finite posets and opfibrations between them, and prove that it is a perfect operator category in the sense of Barwick. Based on its additional properties, we propose a definition for a dependent operator category, and formulate a notion of dependent affine operad in a fibered way. In the particular case of $\mathbf{Dep_{aff}}$, we investigate the basic theory of such operads, establishing that the category of algebras for an operad is monadic over a canonical presheaf topos of "dependent sets". We finally extend this theory to a setting where we allow variable duplication, which we refer to as general dependent operads.

title: The number of $C_4$-free graphs
abstract: Erdős, Frankl and Rödl showed that the number of graphs on $n$ vertices with no copy of a non-bipartite graph $H$ is $2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,H)}$, whereas Morris and Saxton showed that this fails for $C_6$. Answering a question of Erdős, we prove that the number of $C_4$-free graphs on $n$ vertices is $2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,C_4)}$. The proof combines a modified hypergraph container method that treats pairs of vertices with large codegree separately, with a new bound on the number of matchings in a graph.

title: Inverse scattering problem for the fifth-order Schr${\rm\bf\ddot{o}}$dinger operator on the whole axis
abstract: A method of solution for the inverse scattering problem for the linear fifth order Schr${\rm\ddot{o}}$dinger operator is found. Two closed systems of linear singular integral equations are obtained. From solutions to these equations, potential on the left and right half-axes is restored unambiguously.

title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
abstract: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.

title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers for 3-uniform tight hypergraph cycles
abstract: Let $C^{(3)}_n$ be the $3$-uniform tight cycle on $n$ vertices, that is, the $3$-uniform hypergraph on a cyclically ordered set of $n$ vertices whose edges are precisely the triples of consecutive vertices in the given cyclic order. We asymptotically determine the off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-uniform tight cycles. This is an off-diagonal analogue of a result of Haxell, Łuczak, Peng, Rödl, Ruciński and Skokan [Combin.\ Probab.\ Comput.\ 18 (2009), no.\ 1-2, 165--203] on the diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-uniform tight cycles.

title: The Mézard-Parisi formula
abstract: This paper proves the Mézard-Parisi formula for the free energy of random $K$-sat and diluted $p$-spin models with even $p$, completing an approach developed in earlier work of the author and collaborators. The upper bound was established by Franz and Leone. Here the matching lower bound is proved for a general class of diluted models under symmetry and integrability assumptions. The main new contribution is a proof of an approximate form of the Mézard-Parisi reproducibility hypothesis without assuming that the overlap distribution has finite support.

title: Stability of the $L^p$ Poisson-Neumann problem under small perturbations of the coefficients and the domain
abstract:
In this article, we obtain three stability results for the Poisson-Neumann problem: (1) the stability of the $L^p$ Poisson-Neumann problem under small Carleson perturbations of the coefficients, (2) the preservation of the $L^p$ Poisson-Neumann problem when transitioning from the Laplacian to operators in a special form with oscillations satisfying a small Carleson condition (''small special DKP operators''), and (3) the stability of the $L^p$ Poisson-Neumann problem under small bi-Lipschitz transformations of domains.
  In contrast to the Neumann problem, the Poisson-Neumann problem is notably more self-contained, as results pertaining to it do not require assumptions regarding the $L^{p'}$ Dirichlet problem, making it a more suitable object for a perturbation theory.
  As intermediate steps, we establish estimates on the square functional for solutions to the Poisson problem and their gradients on chord arc domains, which are of independent interest for specialists.

title: Lipschitz volume rigidity for non-collapsed $\rm RCD$ spaces with boundary
abstract: We study Lipschitz-volume rigidity for non-collapsed ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, possibly with boundary. We prove that a measure-preserving $1$-Lipschitz map between such spaces restricts to an isometry from the interior of the domain onto its image, where the latter is equipped with the intrinsic length distance. We then characterize when this interior rigidity extends to an isometric bijection between the whole spaces, in terms of the behavior of the map on the boundaries. Along the way, we establish a rigidity result of independent interest in a more general class of rectifiable metric spaces.

title: A new sharp Sobolev inequality between the $Q$-curvature and the scalar curvature on Euclidean space
abstract: We establish a sharp Sobolev-type inequality on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 5$, that interpolates between the second-order energy and a weighted first-order term. Specifically, we determine the sharp constant $S_{4,2}$ in the inequality \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^n} (Δu)^2\,dx \ge S_{4,2} \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\nabla u|^{2}|u|^{\frac{4}{n-4}}\,dx\right)^{\frac{n-4}{n-2}}, \end{equation*} for any $u\in\dot H^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and we classify the cases of equality. This solves the problem of minimizing the total $Q$-curvature of among metrics on the sphere, conformal to the standard metric, with fixed total scalar curvature.

title: Epimorphism testing with dihedral targets
abstract: We consider the problem of deciding whether or not there is an epimorphism from the class of finitely presented groups to a fixed finite group. We show this problem is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete when the target is a non-nilpotent dihedral group. This complements work of Kuperberg and Samperton (2018, Geom. Topol.) who showed the same result when the target is a fixed finite non-abelian simple group. We also include a survey of complexity and reduction results when the source and target are classes of finitely presented groups.

title: Higher order unknotting numbers for knots and links
abstract: Ohyama, Taniyama and Yamada showed that finite type knot invariants are insensitive to the unknotting number: for any integer n and any knot K, there is an unknotting number 1 knot which cannot be distinguished from K by any finite type invariant of order $\le n$. We generalize this result in three directions. First, we prove an analogous result for all higher order unknotting number given by $C_n$-moves. Second, we give several extensions to the link case. Third, we show that a similar result holds for ribbon 2-knots.

title: Affinizations and braided module categories
abstract: We relate affinizations of braided monoidal categories to braided module categories, allowing a twist by a braided monoidal automorphism. Our main theorem establishes a bijection between twisted braided structures on a right module category and extensions of its action to the corresponding twisted affinization. We also show that the twisted affinization is the free twisted braided module category on one object. We give explicit presentations of twisted affinizations, both as monoidal categories and as module categories, using invertible dots and reflection relations. We also describe the relation to cylinder twists and tensor-pair cylinder twists, including the naturality condition needed to obtain a braided module structure. As applications, we obtain module-category presentations of the affine Kauffman and affine oriented skein categories and an orientation-reversing twisted version of the latter. We realize the disoriented skein category as a quotient of this twisted affinization by a single additional relation.

title: Arithmetic localization for quasiperiodic long-range operators with monotone potentials
abstract: We study one-dimensional quasiperiodic operators with $α$-Hölder monotone potentials and long-range hopping satisfying $|T(x,y)|\leq \varepsilon e^{-ρ|x-y|}$. Under an explicit smallness condition on $\varepsilon$, we establish uniform Anderson localization for such operators in the regime $ρ>αβ$, where $β$ is the exponential strength of frequency resonances. Our proof extends the arithmetic localization strategy for monotone quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators by Jitomirskaya and Kachkovskiy to the long-range setting, without relying on the Lyapunov exponent.

title: The functional analytic approach establishes the Corona theorem in the theory of SCV
abstract: We give an affirmative solution of the original Corona problem (1962) for certain bounded pseudoconvex domains or polydomains in $\mathbb{C}^n$, including the balls and polydiscs, by using the Gleason solvability property of such domains for $H^\infty(G)$. In fact, we establish an equivalency of the Corona problem and Gleason's problem (1964) in the theory of several complex variables. Indeed, we extend our recent works on both problems based on the functional analytic approaches, and extend recent work of Clos, as well as apply the usual Banach algebra method. As an application, we establish the I. J. Schark's theorem for these $G$'s. We also obtain a welcome extension of a result of Krantz and Li (1995) for a bounded, strictly pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with $C^3$ boundary.

title: Effective interface laws for Darcy--Boussinesq convection across a vanishing low-permeability layer
abstract: We study Darcy--Boussinesq convection in a layered porous medium containing a thin layer whose thickness $h_0$ and permeability $K_0$ vanish simultaneously. The competition between these two small parameters is measured by the effective hydraulic conductance $α= \lim \frac{K_0}{h_0} \in [0,\infty]$. We show that the collapsing layer is replaced by an effective interface whose transmission law depends qualitatively on this ratio. When $α= 0$, the limiting interface is impermeable; when $ 0 <α<\infty$, the normal Darcy flux is proportional to the pressure jump, yielding a finite-resistance transmission law; and when $α=\infty$, the pressure is continuous and the interface becomes hydraulically transparent. We establish estimates uniform in the layer thickness and permeability, quantitative convergence of solutions on every finite time interval, and upper semicontinuity of the associated global attractors. The analysis has to accommodate both a degenerating geometry and a loss of coercivity in the pressure equation. In particular, we use a generalized Poincaré inequality for piecewise $H^1$ pressures, a pressure extension across the collapsing layer, and uniform thin-strip estimates. The results provide a rigorous finite- and long-time validation of effective interface models for convection through thin low-permeability interphases.

title: Graded Automorphism of Multiparameter Quantum Matrix Algebra
abstract: We determine the graded automorphism group of the multiparameter quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_{λ,\mathbf p}(M_n(\Bbbk))$ over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ for all $n\ge2$ and $λ\ne1$. No other restrictions are assumed on $\mathbf p$ or $λ$. Every graded automorphism is a torus automorphism, possibly followed by transposition or by simultaneous reversal of the row and column indices. We give the precise parameter conditions for these two involutions. As an application, we also determine the full automorphism group when the multiplicative group generated by the parameters is torsion-free.

title: A Sharp Fisher-Information Inequality for Boolean Pairs: Proof of the Amari--Kobayashi Conjecture
abstract: Consider two terminals that observe correlated uniform binary vectors and separately compress their observations to one bit. We prove that, for every blocklength and every correlation parameter in $(-1,1)$, the Fisher information retained by the resulting pair of bits is maximized by matching parity functions of an appropriate degree, thereby resolving a conjecture of Amari and Kobayashi. The proof combines a Fourier-based bound on the derivative of the normalized covariance with a scalar inequality for signed polynomials subject to a global range constraint.

title: Tensor products of Leibniz bimodules and Grothendieck rings -- an addendum
abstract: We continue our investigation of certain associativity properties (namely, alternativity, power-associativity, or being a Jordan ring) of the non-associative multiplication defined on the Grothendieck group of the category of finite-dimensional Leibniz bimodules which we started in \cite{FW}. Namely, we prove that for every finite-dimensional non-zero Leibniz algebra over an arbitrary field this Grothendieck ring is not power-associative. As a consequence, the Grothendieck ring is also neither alternative nor a Jordan ring. This corrects and generalizes some of our results in the last section of \cite{FW}.

title: Differential Properties of Objective and Value Functions for Discounted Markov Decision Processes with Finite State and Action Sets
abstract: This paper studies differential properties of objective functions for discrete-time discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs) with finite state and action sets, when differentiation is considered with respect to the discount factor. Given a fixed discount factor for an MDP, we estimate the norms and seminorms of the objective functions, their derivatives, and the value function at a different discount factor. We then use these estimates to prove that objective functions, their derivatives, and value functions are Lipschitz continuous in discount factors. As a result, if an MDP is solved with a fixed discount factor, then we can estimate the value function at a different discount factor without solving it again.\\ %Following these estimations, we also reveal the relations between the seminorms of objective functions, their behavior when the discount factor approaches $1,$ and the discount factors at which the set of optimal policies changes.

title: Symmetry and uniqueness of degree $-1$ minimizers of a chiral magnetic energy
abstract: We consider the two-dimensional energy of a chiral magnet, consisting of the exchange energy, a bulk Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction with constant $κ\ne0$, and the Zeeman energy in an applied field $h>0$. We prove that the minimizers of this energy among maps of degree $-1$ are exactly the translates of one axially symmetric Bloch skyrmion, whose helicity is determined by the sign of $κ$. This holds for $h \geq c κ^2$, where $c \in(π^2 / 16,1)$ is determined by the slope of the radial profile at the origin; in particular, it holds in the whole range $h\geκ^2$, which answers a question raised by Melcher and by Döring and Melcher. The proof is a calibration argument. Using the profile of the skyrmion, we write the energy density of an arbitrary map as a weighted topological density, plus a divergence, plus a nonnegative remainder, and we show that this identity can be integrated for every map of finite energy. The method also gives the uniqueness of the monotone solution of the profile equation for $h\geκ^2/2$.

title: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations
abstract: We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey "Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond". Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset $B_1+\dots+B_k$ of $k$ infinite sets, for every $k$; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host-Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. We also answer, positively or negatively, questions on monochromatic sets $B+mB$, on sumsets in sets of logarithmic density, on polynomial sumset configurations, on sums of the form $B_{i_1}+\dots+B_{i_m}$ with $B_i$ drawn from a density family, on random sets, on ordered sumsets in shifted primes, on sums and products in $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$, and on sumsets in abelian groups. Several of these answers concern the questions as literally stated, and two follow directly from known examples; in each case we say so and discuss the natural corrected question. Finally, answering a question of Kousek and Radić, we show that the supremum of the lower Banach densities of sets $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B+t\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and every $t\ge0$ (respectively $B+B\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B$) is $1/2$ (respectively $3/4$). The main theorem and most of the other results are formalized in Lean 4, with some published theorems entering as explicit hypotheses.

title: Ghirlanda-Guerra identities and cavity equations for diluted spin glass models
abstract: This note supplies the details of the cavity lower bound used in "The Mézard-Parisi formula" [8]. Specifically, we show that small perturbations that do not change the limiting free energy can be chosen so that the asymptotic Gibbs measures arising in the Aizenman-Sims-Starr lower bound satisfy both the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities and the cavity equations. These calculations are standard and require only minor modifications of arguments already available in the literature. We record them here for completeness, avoiding a lengthy repetition of these arguments in [8].

title: A Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation of the EndoWake model for optimal wind farm layouts
abstract: Wind Farm Layout Optimization places turbines to maximize the expected energy under a wind rose, each turbine lowering the wind downwind. In the EndoWake model the wind field is a variable, propagated by linear inequalities, and layouts are certified by branch-and-check. On a ladder of grids it certifies the $10\times10$ grid and leaves the larger grids open after one hour. We tighten the relaxation by a convexification computed rather than derived: every pattern of turbines inside a small tile of the grid is enumerated once with its power and enters the master as a column. The device is valid because the wind field is antitone, and exact, for the cubic power curve, with a Benders cut at integer layouts. Reduced-cost fixing and propagation between overlapping tiles shrink the master before the tree search, and the tree repeats the fixing at every improving incumbent. The incumbent comes from a tile heuristic or an LP dive. On the same computer as the branch-and-check, the $12\times12$ and $14\times14$ grids close in 48 and 395 seconds. The $16\times16$ grid is certified on five seeds from random starts, one job per seed, the heuristic on a GPU, in 1413 seconds under the uniform rose and 6484 seconds under a non-uniform one. Times are medians. A pre-specified test set of 36 unseen instances with forbidden cells confirms the advantage in the axial setting. Certified means closed at the solver's gap of $10^{-4}$: the optimum lies within it plus a residual of at most 0.00042%.

title: The complete existence spectrum of periodic complementary ternary pairs of weight nine
abstract: For two sequences with entries $0,\pm1$, periodic complementarity means that their periodic autocorrelation functions sum to zero at every nonzero shift. We give necessary and sufficient conditions on the length for the existence of such pairs of total weight nine, where weight counts nonzero entries. The conditions decide existence at any prescribed length by divisibility tests. The main new result bounds the length of primitive pairs with two nonzero components. A pair is primitive if it cannot be shortened by removing uniformly inserted zeros after independent cyclic permutations. We prove primitive-length bounds of $64,48,64$ for weight distributions $(5,4),(6,3),(7,2)$. These bounds make the classification finite and prove that the earlier searches contain every required case. Exhaustive enumeration gives $91$ primitive sequence-equivalence classes. Including the five known circulant classes gives $96$ representatives from which every pair can be generated. The same catalogue gives class counts at every length. For constructing one pair, $33$ displayed seeds suffice. The results settle earlier conjectures on the weight distributions and decide exactly which orders admit the associated two-circulant weighing-matrix construction.

title: $\mathrm{BMO}$ Domains and Quasicircles Associated with Zygmund Functions
abstract:
We investigate graph domains and graph curves from the viewpoints of $\mathrm{BMOA}$, Zygmund regularity, and asymptotic geometry. First, we prove that every graph domain is a $\mathrm{BMO}$ domain, which provides a proof of a statement of Astala and Zinsmeister. We then use a Weierstrass-type function to construct a Bishop-Jones quasicircle that is asymptotically conformal but not asymptotically smooth. This example yields the strict inclusions \[
  \mathrm{VMOA}(\mathbb H)
  \subsetneq \mathrm{BMOA}(\mathbb H)\cap B_0(\mathbb H),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{SS}(\mathbb R)
  \subsetneq \mathrm{SQS}(\mathbb R)\cap\mathrm{S}(\mathbb R). \] Finally, by a localized lacunary construction, we produce a compactly supported locally absolutely continuous function $f$ with $f'\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R)\setminus\mathrm{VMO}(\mathbb R)$ whose graph is an asymptotically conformal chord-arc curve that is not asymptotically smooth.

title: Data-driven Regularization for Inverse Problems
abstract:
In many applications, we are interested in studying an object of interest $x$. However, its properties are often not directly measurable. Instead, we only observe $y = F(x)$, where the (known) function $F$ is referred to as the forward mapping. To infer about $x$ from the observation $y$, we seek an (approximate) inverse mapping $x \approx F^{-1}(y)$. This process is known as solving the inverse problem.
  In practice, the inverse mapping $F^{-1}$ may be ill-defined or discontinuous, which forces us to choose a certain solution from many possible ones based on prior assumptions on $x$. Such assumptions about $x$ are typically incorporated into the inversion process through regularization. Therefore, the first part of this course focuses on the classical regularization theory of inverse problems.
  In the second part, we transition to algorithmic approaches for solving inverse problems. The foundation for this lies in the variational formulation of inverse problems, where reconstructions are obtained by minimizing specific functionals. Here, we will explore key optimization principles, discuss their practical implementation, and examine how they contribute to robust reconstructions.
  Today, classical methods are often modified to incorporate data-driven machine learning techniques, which improve the empirical performance. However, this often comes at the cost of explainability or convergence guarantees. Such properties are critical, for example, in medical applications, where one wants to be confident that reconstructed abnormalities are of physical nature and not phantoms resulting from the method.
  For these reasons, we discuss a number of machine learning methods for inverse problems, such as unrolling techniques, learned regularizers and plug-and-play methods, and explore their performance guarantees.

title: Formality transmission
abstract: Across mathematics, formality results are usually established through general criteria rather than by constructing explicit equivalences. These criteria include domination, puncturing, highly-connected formality, intrinsic formality, formality descent, formality in families, purity, etc. In this article, we prove that all these criteria are instances of a single theorem, formality transmission. This unifying framework allows us to extend these criteria in several directions, beyond characteristic zero and to differential graded algebras over operads or properads, leading to diverse new formality results.

title: Minimum-degree thresholds beyond bounded colourability
abstract: We survey recent developments on minimum-degree thresholds in extremal graph theory, with an emphasis on structural refinements of the chromatic-threshold problem. The chromatic threshold asks when a linear minimum-degree condition forces bounded chromatic number in an \(H\)-free graph; its complete classification shows a striking finite trichotomy. We discuss several stronger and related threshold notions in which bounded colourability is replaced by bounded \(H\)-free homomorphic images, bounded neighbourhood complexity via VC-dimension, exact blowup structure for maximal \(H\)-free graphs, and improved quantitative bounds in graph removal lemmas. In contrast with the rigidity of the chromatic threshold, these newer parameters exhibit richer behaviour, including separations from \(δ_χ(H)\), new exact values, accumulation points in fixed-chromatic spectra, positivity phenomena for 3-chromatic graphs, asymmetric variants, and failures of monotonicity.

title: Fast rates for the classification of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths
abstract: In binary classification problems, plug-in classifiers can sometimes achieve faster excess risk rates than the underlying estimation rate. In this work, we study a supervised classification problem based on repeated independent observations of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths, with both time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous drifts. We show that, under a suitable separation condition on the class-dependent drifts, a plug-in classifier attains an excess risk of quadratic order in the corresponding parametric or nonparametric estimation error. The theoretical approach utilizes the Wiener chaos representation and spectral theory to characterize the log-likelihood ratio as a quadratic form of Gaussian random variables, enabling a precise analysis of margin behaviour and deviation results. This extends the fast-rate results from classification problems with linear discriminant models and Gaussian white noise models to dynamical diffusion systems with Gaussian structure.

title: Optimality of the BCC lattice among 3D lattice quantizers
abstract: We study the problem of the best approximation (w.r.t. the optimal transport metric $W_p$, $p \in [1,\infty)$) of the three-dimensional Lebesgue measure on a domain of volume 1 by a discrete probability measure supported on a Bravais lattice. This problem is known as the quantization problem and it arises in numerical integration, electrical engineering, discrete geometry and materials science. As the lattice size tends to zero and the cardinality of the support of the discrete measure tends to infinity, this reduces to the following geometric optimization problem: Amongst three-dimensional Bravais lattices with determinant $1$, which lattice minimises the $p$-th moment of the lattice Voronoi cell? Barnes and Sloane (1983) proved that the BCC lattice is optimal for the case $p=2$, which is known as the vector quantization problem in the signal compression literature. Bambah (1954) proved that the BCC lattice is optimal for the limiting case $p=\infty$, which is the sphere covering problem. Based on these results, Graf and Luschgy (2000) conjectured that the BCC lattice is optimal for all $p \in [1,\infty)$. Three dimensions is the critical dimension in the sense that in two dimensions the optimal lattice is independent of $p$, whereas in four dimensions it varies with $p$. In this paper we give support in favour of Graf and Luschgy's conjecture by proving that the BCC lattice is a local minimiser for all $p \in [1,\infty)$ and a global minimiser for $p$ near 2. While the conjecture asserts that the global minimiser is independent of $p$, we prove a bifurcation theorem which shows that the set of critical points depends on $p$ and that $p=2$ is a distinguished case. Our proofs combine results from discrete geometry by Barnes and Sloane (1983) and Conway and Sloane (1992) with optimal transport theory, the calculus of variations, bifurcation theory, and some delicate positivity estimates.

title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
abstract: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

title: Hilbertian Fields and Profinite Iterated Monodromy Groups Over Transcendental Elements with Specializations of Infinite Index
abstract: Given a field $L$ and polynomial $f(x)/L$, one can consider the indices of the profinite iterated monodromy groups formed over the ground field within the profinite iterated monodromy groups over elements transcendental over $L$. For any countable Hilbertian field $k$, we show random Galois fixed field extensions almost surely make the indices infinite over all ground field elements, with certain conditions on $f(x)$. This is a generalization of a result in arXiv:2012.03076 by Dittmann and Kadets.

title: Rigidity of Kähler-Finsler Metrics with Constant Radial Curvature
abstract:
In this paper, we prove that a smooth strongly pseudoconvex Kähler--Finsler metric $F$ satisfying the constant radial curvature condition \[ Ω(χ,\barχ)χ=cF^2χ,
  c\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}, \] is induced by a Hermitian Kähler metric of holomorphic sectional curvature $2c$. Under the Abate--Patrizio curvature symmetry \[ \langleΩ(\cdot,\barχ)χ,χ\rangle =\langleΩ(χ,\barχ)\cdot,χ\rangle, \] this result gives Hermitian rigidity for nonzero constant holomorphic sectional curvature and the classification of complete simply connected metrics of negative curvature. As an application, we show that the Kobayashi metric of a bounded strongly convex domain with smooth boundary is Kähler--Finsler if and only if the domain is biholomorphic to the unit ball. We also prove that the universal cover of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain $D $ with smooth boundary is biholomorphic to the unit ball if and only if its Kobayashi metric is a smooth strongly pseudoconvex Kähler--Finsler metric. Furthermore, we give two explicit examples to illustrate the distinction between the weakly Kähler--Finsler and Kähler--Finsler conditions.

title: On the maximum interval index of a graph
abstract: For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value. We also prove that, for every n >= 31, the maximum interval index among graphs without pendant vertices equals (n^3 - n)/6 - 2(n - 4) and it is attained by a dumbbell graph, obtained by joining two 4-cycles by a path.

title: Dense Minors from the Crux
abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_α(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $αd$ for any fixed $0<α<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $Ω(\sqrt{d\,C_α(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.

title: On the variational characterization of a laminated core model in ferromagnetic materials
abstract: Accurate prediction of iron losses in transformers, electric motors, and generators at elevated frequencies requires accounting for eddy currents in laminated magnetic cores during field simulation. We study local material models for these lamination losses that resolve the inhomogeneous magnetic-field distribution across the thickness of the respective steel sheets via one-dimensional diffusion equations. This allows to incorporate skin-effect and eddy-current losses in the laminations at each material point of a two- or three-dimensional magnetic-field simulation. The macroscopic material response is described implicitly through a minimization problem involving a set of internal variables which encode the load history and current state of the material. The variational structure of these problems allows us to prove well-posedness, to include anisotropy and hysteresis, and to develop efficient globally convergent solvers for the evaluation of the macroscopic material response. The proposed framework thus allows to efficiently and reliably predict magnetic behaviour of laminated core material over a wide frequency range and is well-suited for integration into nonlinear magnetic field solvers.

title: Iterative Methods for Solving New Generalized Absolute Value Equations
abstract: In this paper, we propose two iterative methods, the modified Picard method (MPM) and the generalized Traub method (GTM), to solve a new generalized absolute value equation (NGAVE). We establish their convergence under appropriate assumptions. Additionally, numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the developed algorithms.

title: Efficient Low-Rank Approximation of Quaternion Matrices via Adaptive Cross Approximation
abstract: The adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm is a powerful tool for constructing low-rank matrix approximations using only a small subset of matrix entries. While extensively studied for real and complex matrices, its extension to quaternion algebras, remains largely unexplored. This paper presents the first comprehensive framework for adaptive cross approximation operating natively in the quaternion algebra H. Unlike approaches that rely on real embeddings or complexifications, our method preserves the algebraic structure of quaternions throughout the computation, avoiding information loss and maintaining the natural correlations between quaternion components. We develop a fully quaternionic ACA algorithm with rigorous theoretical foundations, including convergence analysis, error bounds, and complexity estimates. The algorithm achieves O(r(m+n)) complexity per iteration and demonstrates quasioptimal approximation properties comparable to the quaternion singular value decomposition (QSVD), but with significantly reduced computational cost. We provide a detailed MATLAB with numerical experiments on color image compression. Our results show that native quaternion ACA outperforms significantly the basic SVD algorithm in terms of computational efficiency, with very close approximation accuracy.

title: Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales
abstract: For one-dimensional strict local martingales of the form $\mathrm{d} X_t=σ(X_t) \mathrm{d} W_t$ starting from $X_{0}=x_{0}>0$, we prove the strong rate $\mathbb{E}\left[|X^h_N-X_T|\right] \lesssim h^{\min\{θα,\frac{1}{2}\}}$ for a discrete scheme~$X^h$ truncated at a level $h^{-α}$, with time step~$h$, as $h\downarrow 0$, where~$θ$ depends on the truncation property. For the CEV model $σ(x)\equiv x^{1+γ}$ in particular, the rate is~$\frac{1}{2}$ for any $γ\in (0,1)$ (up to a logarithmic pre-factor at $γ=\frac{1}{2}$).

title: Instability theory of stationary solutions for nonlinear Schrödinger equations
abstract: We study the orbital instability of algebraically decaying stationary solutions of nonlinear Schrödinger equations in dimensions $d\ge2$, taking competing double-power nonlinearities as a canonical model. At zero frequency, the essential spectrum of the linearized operator touches zero, and the usual $H^1$ coercivity is lost. We construct the zero-frequency limit $η_0$ of the frequency derivatives $\partial_ωφ_ω$ of standing-wave profiles and determine its sharp asymptotic behavior. For a stationary ground state $φ_0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, we prove instability if $\langle x\rangle\,φ_0\notin L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ or, when $\langle x\rangle\,φ_0\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, if the duality pairing $\langleη_0,φ_0\rangle$ is negative. This criterion is a zero-frequency counterpart of the negative slope condition in the Grillakis--Shatah--Strauss theory. The proof combines variation of parameters for the linearized ODE with a shooting analysis that determines the global behavior of the homogeneous solution regular at the origin. We then localize $η_0$ to construct an unstable direction and establish instability through a Lyapunov functional argument based on the variational characterization of ground states. The results extend with essentially the same proofs to a class of multiple-power nonlinearities.

title: On convex envelopes of bilinear terms over polygonal domains
abstract: We develop an algorithm for computing the convex envelope of the bilinear function $f(x,y)=xy$ over possibly nonconvex polygonal domains. Building on existing methods for convex polytopes, our approach uses the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions and an analysis of the contact points between affine underestimators and the graph of $f$. Nonconvex domains admit additional contact configurations that prevent several simplifications available in the convex case. We resolve these configurations explicitly and show that the envelope admits a finite polyhedral subdivision with affine, quadratic, or rational expressions on its cells. For orthogonal polygons, whose edges are horizontal or vertical, we establish substantial reductions in the generator sets needed to compute the envelope. We also present methods for constructing such domains as relaxations of two-dimensional projections of nonlinear optimization problems. An illustrative example quantifies the loss in relaxation strength caused by convexifying the domain before computing the envelope. Computational experiments on MINLPLib instances show that cuts derived from orthogonal polygons strengthen root relaxations and reduce branch-and-bound nodes in aggregate.

title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules
abstract: Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules. In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules. In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schröer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules. In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.

title: Solid Arithmetic D-modules
abstract: We introduce a solid ring of arithmetic differential operators analogue to Berthelot's D-dagger, and its derived infinity-category of solid quasi-coherent modules. We show that there is a fully faithful functor from Berthelot's derived category of bounded complexes of D-dagger-modules with coherent cohomology into our new category.

title: Arbitrary Dirichlet Eigenvalue Multiplicities on Smooth Star-Shaped Euclidean Domains
abstract: In every fixed dimension \(N\ge3\), for any finite list of positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\), we construct smooth strictly star-shaped Euclidean domains whose first \(\ell+1\) distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues can have multiplicities \(1,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\) respectively. The condition "star-shaped" is almost optimal in the sense that this statement can not hold for bounded convex domains. In fact, we show that the second Dirichlet eigenvalue of any bounded convex domain has multiplicity at most $N$, and this bound is sharp.

title: Rational points of exact period three for the quadratic family
abstract: For the quadratic family $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$ over $\Q$, we isolate a general $S$-unit and ABC template for rational periodic cycles: under the ABC conjecture, any rational quantity built from the consecutive-point sums of a rational period-$n$ cycle whose value and shift-by-$1$ are both $S$-units (with $S$ the support of the denominator of $c$) has logarithmic height at most $(1+\eps)\sum_{p \in S} \log p + O_\eps(1)$. Specializing to period $3$ in the change of coordinates $u = x_0 + x_1$ and $v = x_0 + x_2$, the period-$3$ condition reduces to $v = -1/(1+u)$, forcing the parameter $t = u$ to satisfy $t, t+1 \in \Z[S^{-1}]^\times$; the template then yields, under ABC, $\max\{|a|,|b|,|a+b|\} \le C_\eps \rad(d)^{1+\eps}$ for $t = a/b$ in lowest terms. We also characterize the period-$3$ locus on the $(u,v)$-plane intrinsically, isolating the ghost curve. Extending the height bound to higher periods remains an open structural question.

title: $L^p$ integrability of functions with Fourier support on High codimension manifolds
abstract: Let $n,k\ge 2$ and $N_{n,k} = \binom{n+k}{k}-1$. We prove that if $f \in L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{N_{n,k}})$ and $\hat{f}$ is supported on the $n$-dimensional Parsell-Vinogradov manifold, then $f \equiv 0$ whenever $1\le p < p_{c}(n,k) = n+ \binom{n+k}{n+1}$. This improves the bound by Agranovsky and Narayanan, and generalizes the moment-curve result of Guo-Iosevich-Zhang-Zorin-Kranich. The exponent $p_{c}(n,k)$ is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$, since it matches the convergence exponent $p_{n,k}^{\mathrm{Tar}}$ of Tarry's problem. Our result also yields a general lower bound $p_{n,k}^{\mathrm{Tar}} \ge p_{c}(n,k)$, improving Ikromov's bound by $n-1$. The proof combines the rotation symmetry of Parsell-Vinogradov manifold with the essential orthogonality of rotated covering boxes.

title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
abstract: We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.

title: Invariant probability measures on holomorphic functions on the unit disk
abstract: We study probability measures on the space of holomorphic functions on the unit disk that are invariant under pre-composition by conformal automorphisms and give no mass to constant functions. We determine the slowest possible growth of functions supported by such measures. Let $M_f(R)$ denote the maximum modulus of $f$ on the hyperbolic ball of radius $R$ centered at the origin. We show that given a non-decreasing function $G:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$, there exists an $\textrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$-invariant probability measure $μ$ on $\textrm{Hol}(\mathbb{D}, \mathbb{C}) \setminus \{\textrm{constant functions} \}$ such that $\log^+ M_f(R)=O_f(G(R))$ for $μ$ almost every $f$ if and only if $\int_1^\infty (R/G(R)) \, dR <\infty$. For the lower bound, we use a mass transport argument to show that almost every trajectory of the gradient flow of $\log |f|$ has finite energy. To establish sharpness, we construct holomorphic functions of slow growth on infinite Riemann surfaces.

title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
abstract: Bérczi, Gehér, Imolay, Lovász, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,α}$, $0<α<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.

title: Complexity of finding color-avoiding connected components
abstract:
Two vertices of a (not necessarily properly) arc-colored digraph are called arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected if, after the removal of the arcs of any at most $\ell$ colors, they remain strongly $k$-arc-connected. The arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components are maximal sets of vertices such that any two of those vertices belonging to the set are arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected in the graph.
  We investigate the problems of finding the arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components and the maximal arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected subgraphs of an arc-colored digraph. We also consider possible generalizations to $k$-vertex-connectivity and to vertex-colored digraphs. We show that despite the seemingly minor differences in definitions, the complexity of these problems varies significantly: some can be solved in polynomial time, while others are NP-hard. It also turns out that in some cases the problem is NP-hard when multiple colors can be assigned to each vertex, but the problem becomes polynomial-time solvable when each vertex is single-colored.

title: The Hénon equation beyond the critical Sobolev exponent
abstract: We consider the Dirichlet problem $-Δu=|x|^αu^p$, $u>0$ in $Ω$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, where $Ω\subset R^N$, $N\ge 3$, is a bounded domain containing the origin and $α>0$. We prove that a solution exists for every exponent $1<p<p_α=\frac{N+2+2α}{N-2}$, in particular in the whole Sobolev-supercritical range $\frac{N+2}{N-2}\le p<p_α$, provided $Ω$ is invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and satisfies an angular monotonicity condition. This class contains the balls, the oblate ellipsoids of revolution, lens-shaped domains, and non-convex, non-smooth and non star-shaped domains. The solution is obtained by minimizing the Rayleigh quotient on a suitable closed convex cone.

title: Mean-Square Convergence Analysis of a Three-Level MGRIT Method for Linear Stochastic Evolution Equations with Additive Noise
abstract:
We investigate the mean-square convergence of a three-level multigrid reduction-in-time (MGRIT) method based on F-relaxation for linear stochastic evolution equations driven by additive Gaussian noise. The method combines exponential Euler time stepping on the finest grid with implicit Euler discretizations on the two coarser grids. The inexact solution of the intermediate-level full approximation scheme problem gives rise to coupled error recursions involving two interlevel propagator discrepancies. Under a common spectral decomposition of the drift and noise covariance operators, we establish a geometric contraction estimate in a modal mean-square norm, with a contraction factor uniform in the temporal grids and both coarsening factors. We further derive fixed-iteration temporal error bounds that are uniform in the first coarsening factor and explicitly quantify the dependence on the second.
  For a fixed iteration count $k$ and a fixed second coarsening factor, we prove an $O(ΔT_1^r)$ error bound relative to the finest-grid reference solution for $0<r\le k+1$ provided that $\mathcal R_{r,B}<\infty$. 
  We also prove that the error-propagation operator is nilpotent on each fixed temporal grid, ensuring finite termination of the iteration. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence behavior and compare temporal critical-path work under a unit-cost model.

title: Vanishing near the virtual cohomological dimension of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$
abstract:
We prove the Church--Farb--Putman conjecture that \[
  H^{N_n-i}(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z);\mathbb Q)=0,
  \qquad N_n=\binom n2,\quad n\ge2,\quad 0\le i<n-1. \] The proof relies on Franke's filtration of the weighted automorphic cochain complex, developed in his proof of Borel's conjecture. We treat trivial and nontrivial cuspidal support separately. For nontrivial support, we combine a degree calculation with the Chenevier--Lannes lower bound of $11$ for the motivic weight of level-one regular algebraic cuspidal representations of rank at least two. This reduces the contributing inducing data to a trivial factor and a Speh factor attached to such a representation. We construct primitives for closed lifts of cohomology classes in the filtration quotients by combining an Eisenstein residue identity with a cochain homotopy and finite distributions in the spectral parameters. A finite-filtration lifting argument then yields vanishing for nontrivial cuspidal support. The trivial-support case is treated using Franke's topological model.

title: Least common multiples of polynomial values: averaging, ray classes, and Galois statistics
abstract: We study analogues over number fields and the probabilistic congruence input that enters averaged versions of this problem. We prove an asymptotic formula for the least common multiple of ideals in a fixed ray class, record local equidistribution estimates for random $S_n$-polynomials, and give a conditional reduction of the averaged higher degree problem to explicit dispersion and large prime collision estimates. We also formulate an individual quadratic number field analogue and reduce it to a prime ideal quadratic root equidistribution statement together with a geometric pair counting estimate. The Galois group counting input is updated using Bhargava's theorem over $\mathbb Q$ and the determinant method estimates of https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35030 .

title: Split Quaternion Toolbox: A MATLAB Implementation
abstract: This paper presents a MATLAB toolbox for working with split quaternions and split quaternion matrices. Split quaternions, also known as coquaternions, form a four-dimensional associative non-commutative algebra over the real numbers with a signature (+,+,-,-). The toolbox provides two main classes: SplitQuaternion for scalar-valued split quaternions and SplitQuaternionMatrix for matrix-valued split quaternions. The implementation includes arithmetic operations, algebraic functions, matrix operations, linear algebra utilities, and various conversion methods. The toolbox is designed to be intuitive for users familiar with MATLAB's standard matrix operations while providing the full power of split quaternion algebra. This paper details the implementation, provides numerous examples, and demonstrates the toolbox's capabilities through practical demonstrations. The MATLAB toolbox is accessible at https://github.com/SalmanAhmadi-Asl/Split_Quaternion.git.

title: Randomized Symplectic Model Reduction: One-Pass Basis Construction and Sketched Hamiltonian Assembly
abstract: Symplectic model order reduction of Hamiltonian systems yields reduced dynamics that conserve the reduced Hamiltonian along exact trajectories, avoiding the artificial energy drift that can arise from conventional projection methods. For large-scale spatial discretizations, however, basis construction and reduced-operator assembly can involve substantial offline costs. Randomized numerical linear algebra can reduce these costs through low-dimensional sketches while supporting streaming and parallel implementations. We develop randomized techniques for two parts of the offline stage while preserving the Hamiltonian structure of the reduced dynamics. First, we introduce the one-pass sketched randomized cSVD (Ops-rcSVD), a one-pass randomized variant of the complex-SVD algorithm. Combining randomized range finding with an independent left sketch, Ops-rcSVD constructs an ortho-symplectic reduced basis from a single pass over the snapshot ensemble. Second, for quadratic Hamiltonian systems, we introduce a randomized reduced-Hamiltonian assembly based on sketching the reduced basis and operator actions, yielding a reduced Hamiltonian system by construction. We derive bounds for the snapshot projection error, uniform-in-parameter perturbation bounds for the sketched reduced Hamiltonian, and an energy-norm estimate for the difference between reduced and sketched reduced trajectories. Experiments on large-scale systems show that Ops-rcSVD attains projection accuracy comparable to deterministic and two-pass randomized constructions while reducing basis-construction time. They further demonstrate accurate sketched reduced-Hamiltonian assembly when storing the complete snapshot ensemble is no longer feasible.

title: Planarity estimates and codimension reduction for ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
abstract: We derive an interior planarity estimate for space-time proper mean curvature flows of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$, $n\geq5$, that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. The estimate is parabolically scale-invariant and it requires neither curvature nor entropy bounds. The proof combines Naff's gradient estimates with a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, Naff's estimates alone do not give the gradient terms a sign. We bound these terms from below with an argument we developed in a previous work. As a consequence, for $n\geq5$, and by known results for $2\leq n\leq4$, every space-time proper ancient solution that is uniformly $\frac{4}{3n}$-pinched is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace. This replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu by space-time properness, and improves their pinching constant in dimensions two, five and six. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.

title: Moments of characteristic polynomials at random matrix Gram points
abstract: We evaluate the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix at the points on the unit circle where the polynomial takes real values. In analogy to the Riemann zeta function we call these the ``random matrix Gram points''. On the random matrix side we answer in the affirmative a question of Richard Hall, who expected that zeta on the Gram points should be larger than typical. We prove that for any fixed positive $k$, the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the random matrix Gram points is larger than the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the whole unit circle. For large $N$ the leading-order asymptotic term is the same size, but all lower-order terms are larger. In an appendix we show how to adapt the heuristic recipe of Conrey--Farmer--Keating--Rubinstein--Snaith to conjecture moments of zeta at Gram points, and show by example that the second and fourth moments calculated by following the recipe agree with previously proven results.

title: A note on the ideal lattice of a weighted Leavitt path algebra
abstract: Let $K$ be a field and $L_K(E,w)$ the Leavitt path algebra of a row-finite weighted graph $(E,w)$. Suppose that $L_K(E,w)$ is not isomorphic to an ordinary Leavitt path algebra. We prove that the ideal lattice of every countably generated unital $K$-algebra embeds as a closed interval into the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$. The embedding preserves multiplication of ideals modulo the lower endpoint of the interval. It follows that the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$ is not distributive and that ideal multiplication in $L_K(E,w)$ is not commutative. Moreover, we show that if $(E,w)$ is countable, then $L_K(E,w)$ has exactly $|K|^{\aleph_0}$ ideals, prime ideals, left primitive ideals, and right primitive ideals.

title: The Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in dimensions three and four
abstract: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, confirming the Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Blind Passive Beamforming in RIS-Assisted MIMO Systems
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) are a promising solution for improving millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications by controlling signal propagation. Yet, selecting the optimal RIS configuration remains challenging due to the high-dimensional search space and signaling overhead. We propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework for blind passive beamforming, where a Deep Q-Learning (DQL) agent learns an adaptive policy to select near-optimal RIS configurations while sounding only few codewords, without channel state information. Results show that our approach outperforms Q-Learning (QL) and conventional baselines in convergence, performance, and overhead reduction.

title: On short averages of the Fibonacci partition function
abstract: We show that short averages of the Fibonacci partition function over $(H, H + H^α]$ can be significantly smaller than long averages over $(0,H]$, for any constant $α\in (0,1)$. This provides a negative answer to a question that we asked in our previous work on this topic (Journal of Number Theory, 2024).

title: A complete theory of local minimizers for periodic variational problems
abstract: We study the periodic problem in the Calculus of Variations and give a complete characterization of the positive definiteness of the second variation, extending the Reid Roundabout Theorem to periodic boundary conditions. Two formulations are established: one in terms of conjugate and semi-coupled points, and one in terms of the existence of a symmetric solution of the associated Riccati equation satisfying a boundary inequality. We show by an explicit example that the latter condition, while sufficient, is not necessary except in dimension one. As applications, we obtain sufficient conditions for weak and strong local minimizers of periodic solutions of the Euler-Lagrange equation.

title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. Numerical experiments for a semiconductor inverse problem confirm that the proposed Bayesian all-at-once approach yields a speedup of approximately a factor of two, while having a comparable reconstruction quality as the conventional reduced-based setting.

title: EPPA for Reducts of the Random Graph
abstract: We prove that finite two-graphs have coherent EPPA and that neither graphs modulo global complementation nor two-graphs modulo global complementation have EPPA. This completes the classification of EPPA and coherent EPPA for the reducts of the random graph, answering a question and confirming a conjecture of Evans, Hubička, Konečný and Nešetřil.

title: A Transfer Principle for Elliptic Carleman Estimates: Application to Discrete Calderón Stability
abstract: We develop a transfer principle that lifts continuous elliptic Carleman estimates to mesh-uniform estimates for conforming Galerkin discretizations. The main difficulties are twofold: discrete states generally lack the \(H^2\)-regularity required by the continuous estimate, and the Carleman parameter \(s\) must be controlled relative to the mesh size \(h\).
