Once the stack is exhausted, the walk is in a non-excited regime and moves uniformly among the neighbouring vertices. The model is closely connected to foraging ecology, where repeated visits to a location can deplete local resources and thereby influence the attractiveness of that location for future visits. We prove that the process exhibits a sharp phase transition between recurrence and transience. The critical threshold is determined by the branching-ruin number of the tree, which is equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the tree's boundary under a suitable metric. Our result substantially extends Zerner's recurrence-transience criterion for multi-excited random walks on $\mathbb Z$ [Probab. Theory Related Fields 133 (2005)] to general trees.

title: Singular value decompositions over $\ast$-algebras with applications to tensor decompositions
abstract: The singular value decomposition (SVD) provides optimal low-rank approximations of real and complex matrices by the Eckart--Young theorem, and SVD-based tensor decomposition algorithms such as the higher-order singular value decomposition (HOSVD) and the tensor train singular value decomposition (TT-SVD) inherit quasi-optimality guarantees from it. We extend the SVD to matrices over a finite-dimensional $\ast$-algebra $K$. Our main contribution is a characterization of the algebras $K$ for which every matrix admits an SVD, and of the inner products on $K$ for which the Eckart-Young theorem holds. We introduce a notion of ordered SVD, show that ordered SVDs reveal the rank of a matrix over $K$ and yield optimal truncations, and give an explicit algorithm that computes an ordered SVD from the structure of the algebra. We then extend the Tucker, tensor train, and tree tensor network (TTN) decompositions and their SVD-based decomposition algorithms to tensors over $K$, and show that TT-SVD retains a quasi-optimality guarantee over every such $K$, whereas HOSVD, ST-HOSVD, and TTN-SVD do so when $K$ is commutative. Viewed in real or complex coordinates, these constructions give novel decomposition formats of ordinary tensors. We illustrate our new methods by compressing data from a variety of scientific applications, and show that they can achieve lower approximation error than their classical counterparts at equal storage.

title: Shifted convolutions of divisor functions
abstract: We establish the leading asymptotic for the shifted correlations of divisor functions.

title: Complete Kähler Manifolds with pinched Ricci curvature
abstract: In this paper, we prove that a connected complete Kähler manifold of complex dimension at least two satisfying $\Ric\geq\varepsilon Rg\geq0$ for a fixed $\varepsilon>0$ is compact or Ricci-flat.

title: Division and noetherianity in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes
abstract:
We show that the local rings of quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes need not be Noetherian. More precisely, we construct quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes $C^M$ whose local rings $C^M(\mathbb{R}^d,0)$ are not Noetherian for any $d\geq 2$. Conversely, we exhibit quasianalytic classes whose local rings in dimension two are regular and Noetherian.
  Our approach is based on the problem of exact division: if $f=\varphi g$, where $f\in C^M$, $\varphi$ is real-analytic, and $g\in C^\infty$, under which conditions does it follow that $g\in C^M$? We introduce a quantitative scale-growth condition on the defining weight sequence $M$ and prove that exact division holds in two variables whenever this condition is sufficiently strong relative to the rate at which the nonreal branches of the complex zero set of $\varphi$ approach the real plane. We also construct quasianalytic weight sequences with prescribed growth thresholds and establish corresponding counterexamples to exact division. These yield nonclosed principal ideals and, consequently, non-Noetherian local rings.

title: The fractional Faber--Krahn inequality in sharp quantitative form
abstract: We prove that the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the fractional Laplacian satisfies the sharp quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality. This was conjectured by Brasco, Cinti and Vita, who proved the inequality with a sub-optimal exponent. The proof adapts to the non-local setting the level-set argument recently introduced by Guerra, Machado and Ramos for the Laplacian. It is carried out on the horizontal level sets of the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of the torsion function, where the asymmetry appears only as a boundary value at the corner of the extension variables.

title: Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits for the total edge-length of random directional nearest-neighbour graphs
abstract: We study planar random spatial graphs defined by inserting an edge between every point of a homogeneous Poisson process on the unit square and a nearest-neighbour within a fixed cone of directions (if there is such a point). We prove large-sample distributional limit theorems for the total Euclidean edge length of the graph, where the limit distribution is either Gaussian (due to contributions from the bulk) or, when one or both of the boundaries of the cone of directions align with the edges of the square, a convolution of Gaussian with a non-Gaussian law arising from boundary effects due to long edges near a boundary. This work extends previously known cases, including the ordinary nearest-neighbour graph (full cone of directions), where the Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Bickel & Breiman and Avram & Bertsimas, and Bhatt & Roy's minimal directed spanning forest (with 'south-west' directions), where the non-Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Penrose & Wade.

title: The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$
abstract: We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two. We also prove numerical dimension zero and construct the unique projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal minimal model. Its Picard number is one and its canonical divisor has order two. The perfect cone compactification is a Mori dream space, and the birational automorphism group of $\mathcal{A}_6$ is trivial. The proof combines normal vanishing on the Prym locus, polar intersections on abelian boundary fibers, and an exact theta calculation. A discrepancy estimate recovers the modular open subset from the minimal model.

title: Full immersions in Eulerian group-labeled graphs
abstract: An immersion of a graph H in a graph G is full if the immersion uses every edge of G. We give a structure theorem for group-labeled Eulerian graphs excluding a fixed group-labeled graph as a full immersion.

title: Graphical Models Induced by Irreversible Event Accumulation on Trees
abstract:
Decomposable graphical models are usually adopted for their computational convenience rather than derived from a data-generating mechanism. We show that a special class of them arises naturally from the irreversible accumulation of events along a branching history. Each event is attached to an edge of a latent rooted tree and is inherited by everything below that edge; an observation records which events have occurred at a randomly chosen node, not necessarily a leaf. When the tree is a path, this is the cumulative coding of an ordinal variable, whose indicators form a Markov chain; in the general tree case the Markov chain is replaced by a junction tree.
  The conditional independence graph of the event indicators is always decomposable and, in fact, is the line graph of the tree (maximal cliques correspond to nodes where two or more edges meet and separators are the single events on the edges joining two such nodes). The graph determines the tree up to the choice of root. A connected graph arises in this way if, and only if, it is chordal, any two of its maximal cliques share at most one vertex, no vertex is in three maximal cliques, and the graph is such that any two maximal cliques share at most one vertex. This provides a simple graphical test for compatibility with the mechanism (necessary but not sufficient, as irreversibility also constrains the distribution's support).
  The structure breaks down if we look at just the leaves, and measurement error destroys the exact screening and leads to a denser graph rather than simply a weaker dependence. We discuss inference, provide diagnostics for departures such as recurrent events, illustrate them on some simulated data and discuss their application in the context of mutation accumulation and lineage tracing where both ancestral and descendant types are sampled together.

title: Marginal Composite Likelihood Estimation of Bergomi Models from High-Frequency Option Prices
abstract: We develop a theory for estimating the kernel parameters of Bergomi-type stochastic volatility models from option-price time series. The framework allows positive kernels that may be singular at the origin, including the pure power-law kernel of the rough Bergomi model. Using the option-price representation of cumulative forward variance, we formulate the statistical experiment as exact observations of this quantity on increasingly fine time-maturity grids over a fixed horizon. The model has an infinite-dimensional state driven by a single Brownian motion, resulting in a rank-one leading covariance across maturities. Our construction takes maturity differences and then logarithmic time increments. Approximating the resulting diffusion coefficients by maturity-averaged kernels removes the unobserved forward variance curve from the leading term. Positivity of the kernel allows the leading covariance to be recovered from the marginal variances, motivating a weighted marginal composite likelihood contrast. We prove consistency without relative rate restrictions between the time and maturity meshes, allowing the true parameter to lie on the boundary. Under additional regularity and nondegeneracy assumptions and explicit mesh rate conditions, we establish $\mathscr F_1$-stable asymptotic normality, where $\mathscr F_1$ is the terminal model $σ$-field. The Gaussian limit has deterministic sandwich covariance and is independent of $\mathscr F_1$, so the limit is preserved under equivalent changes of probability measure. We also provide sufficient mesh rate conditions for the pure power-law kernel.

title: Quantitative propagation of chaos on arbitrary finite time intervals for the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation
abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck (VRFP) equations on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unregularized interaction potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$. On every finite time interval on which the limiting classical solution satisfies the stated regularity assumptions, the particle marginals with a product initial law converge at an algebraic rate in the particle number, with constants growing at most exponentially in the marginal order. For the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a weighted $C^m$ initial probability density, $m\ge3$, with Gaussian velocity decay and polynomial spatial decay of order $M>3$ gives convergence to the global classical solution on every finite time interval. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law with weighted BBGKY estimates. A decomposition of the potential and a bounded modification of the far-field force yield weighted bounds growing geometrically in the marginal order on the prescribed interval. A centered second-moment estimate permits summation of the error hierarchy, and a synchronous coupling transfers the estimate to the original dynamics.

title: On the Converse of Shimoda's Theorem
abstract: We study Shimoda's theorem on the holomorphicity of a function $f(z,w)$ defined in a bidisc $U\times V=\left\{ \left| z \right|<1 \right\}\times \left\{ \left| w \right|<1 \right\},$ which is holomorphic with respect to $w\in V$ for each fixed $z\in U$ and is holomorphic with respect to $z\in U$ for each fixed $w\in E$, where $E\subset V$ is a countable set with at least one limit point in $V$. Shimoda proved that in this case $f(z,w)$ is holomorphic in $U\times V$ except for a nowhere dense closed subset of $U\times V$. We prove a converse: for any relatively closed nowhere dense set $S\subset U$ such that $\partial U\bigcup S$ is connected, there exists a function satisfying the conditions of Shimoda's theorem that is holomorphic in $(U\setminus S)\times V$ and doesn't extend holomorphically to any point of $S\times V$.

title: Terminal Localization of Empirical Reverse Diffusions under Singular Score Errors
abstract: For a finite empirical target, the exact reverse diffusion is driven toward training points by an attraction whose strength diverges as the forward noising time decreases to zero. We study whether this terminal localization persists under progressively measurable score errors that may themselves be singular. For reverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, from an arbitrary initial law and under a deterministic error envelope \(E\) imposed along the perturbed trajectory satisfying \(t\int_t^T E(σ)/σ\,dσ\to0\), we prove almost-sure convergence to a training point, together with explicit uniform bounds on a terminal window with probability arbitrarily close to one. Every training point has positive terminal probability, although the terminal selection probabilities need not match the empirical weights. The results cover power-law errors \(E(t)=O(t^{-γ})\), \(0<γ<1\), including infinite squared-error energy. For suitable errors in this range, the exact and perturbed full path laws can be mutually singular while their terminal laws share the same finite support. For suitable switched perturbations at the critical scale \(t^{-1}\), arbitrarily small positive amplitudes can produce a nonzero terminal displacement with arbitrarily high probability. These results quantify stochastic robustness of empirical terminal attraction without requiring absolute continuity of the full path laws.

title: Limiting ESD for a weighted sample covariance matrix
abstract: We study the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of the random matrix $M_N=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N f(|πY_i|^2)\,Y_iY_i^\top$, where $π$ is a rank $k$ orthogonal projector on $\R^p$, $Y_1,\dots,Y_N$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian vectors, and $k\to \infty$, $p/N\to γ$. We here assume that $f(x)=g(x/k)$ for some function $g$ discontinuous at $x=1$. We show that the asymptotic ESD is characterized by a Marchenko--Pastur equation, independently of $k$. We also show that the result extends to sub Gaussian random vectors $Y_i$ and to the case where the projector is replaced with a more general weight $φ(Y_i)$. Last, in the Gaussian case, we study the emergence of outliers due to the weighting.

title: Analytic Kasparov product for non-separable C$^*$-algebras
abstract: We develop an analytic framework for the explicit construction of Kasparov products on uncountably generated Hilbert modules over non-separable C$^*$-algebras by extending the classical Kasparov bimodule picture. In particular, this yields a well-defined functor from the category of general C$^*$-algebras whose restriction to separable C$^*$-algebras coincides with classical KK-theory and which satisfies several properties expected of non-separable KK-theory. A key idea of the extension is to replace a single Fredholm operator on a Kasparov bimodule with a net and to encode the directed system of separable C$^*$-subalgebras. We also introduce the notion of freely complementable Hilbert modules and develop cropping techniques to extend Kasparov's technical theorem beyond the countably generated setting. It naturally gives rise to a sufficiently broad class of C$^*$-algebras that provides a non-commutative analogue of paracompactness and includes all $σ$-unital algebras.

title: Galois module structure of Deligne--Lusztig varieties for $\mathrm{GL}_3$
abstract: Let $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)\to\overline{\mathbf{X}}(w)$ be the ramified Galois cover of compactified Deligne--Lusztig varieties. Our objects of study are the Lefschetz numbers for the action of the finite covering group $T^{wF}$ on the coherent cohomology of the structure sheaf of $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$. The Lefschetz numbers for all elements of $T^{wF}$ determine the virtual $T^{wF}$-representation given by the alternating sum of these cohomology groups. In the two cases of Deligne--Lusztig surfaces of type $A_2$ and ${}^{2}A_2$, we give explicit formulas for the Lefschetz numbers for a generator of the stabilizer of an irreducible component. It follows that the equivariant Euler characteristic of the compactification $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$ is not virtually free as a virtual module over the covering group.

title: Computer-Assisted Results for \(n\)-Sided Non-Transitive Dice Taking Face Values in \([n]\)
abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage. For \(n=6\), we identify the two unique non-transitive cycles of length \(6\). We present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is the largest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage.

title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $λ$-convex bodies
abstract: For a given $λ> 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $λ$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/λ$. We show that among all $λ$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $λ$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/λ$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $λ> 0$.

title: On separators in $K_t$-minor-free graphs
abstract: This manuscript presents a proof of the Alon--Seymour--Thomas conjecture developed under the author's guidance using ChatGPT 6pro. The author has checked every formula and theorem by hand and used Codex to assist with writing. GPT 6.1 Sol (Max) was also used to check the proof repeatedly and to generate numerous examples for verification. More precisely, for every integer $h\geq3$, every $n$-vertex $K_h$-minor-free graph has a vertex set of size at most $\min{n,21h\sqrt n}$ whose deletion leaves every component with at most $2n/3$ vertices.

title: Extreme values of Artin $L$-functions at $s=1$
abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a Galois extension of number fields with Galois group $G$. Let $χ$ be any character on $G$ and $κ(χ)$ be the leading coefficient of the Laurent series of the Artin $L$-function $L(s,χ)$ at $s=1$. Cho, Lemke Oliver, and Zaman (2026) recently established a conditional bound for $κ(χ)$ assuming GRH for the Dedekind zeta function of $K$. Up to implied constants, we show that the extremal values of these bounds are attained for an infinite family of extensions $K/\mathbb{Q}$ and all irreducible faithful characters $χ$, provided $G$ is a regular Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. All characters $χ$ are permitted without restriction when $G$ is abelian, $A_n, S_n$, or any sporadic group. Our method removes the assumptions of GRH and Artin's holomorphy conjecture from an argument of Duke (2003) by following the strategy of Lemke Oliver, Thorner, and Zaman (2024) on the existence of extremal class numbers for number fields of arbitrary degree. Key ingredients include progress by Débes (2017) towards Malle's conjecture, and an Artin $L$-function large sieve by Lemke Oliver and Smith (2024).

title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
abstract: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Schütz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. We conjecture that the number of copies of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ equals the number of copies of $\mathbb{RP}^{2}\wedge\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in the even spectrum.

title: Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons II
abstract: We extend the formalism of Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons to include Wilson Loops.

title: Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons I
abstract: We define mathematically the Point-Splitting Perturbative Chern-Simons Theory. The framing anomaly arise directly from the dependence of the configuration space of points on the frame.

title: An Adaptive Transferable Neural Network for Partial Differential Equations with Anisotropic or Sharp Solutions
abstract: Transferable neural network (TransNet) has demonstrated great potential for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with high accuracy and efficiency. However, it struggles significantly when dealing with PDEs featuring anisotropy or sharp solutions. In this work, we propose an adaptive transferable neural network (A-TransNet), a novel machine learning framework that adaptively expands neurons in regions with large solution gradients to effectively capture complex solution behaviors. Instead of relying on training or random sampling, the location parameters of newly added neurons are determined by integrating the active subspaces method and local gradient analysis based on posterior gradient information. This adaptive strategy enables neurons to be allocated where they are most needed, thereby improving the resolution of anisotropic and sharp features without additional computational costs. Moreover, the shape parameters of new neurons are automatically determined from the neuron density induced by their locations, further enhancing the network representation capability. An iterative neuron expansion strategy is developed, together with rigorous analysis of stability, a posteriori error estimation, and convergence of the proposed A-TransNet method. Extensive numerical experiments on challenging PDE problems with anisotropic and sharp solutions demonstrate that A-TransNet achieves superior accuracy, efficiency, and robustness compared with existing methods.

title: Multivariate Lebesgue bounds for R-Leja lower grids
abstract: We establish an algebraic upper bound for the Lebesgue constant of multivariate polynomial interpolation on $\mathfrak R$-Leja lower grids. For each fixed dimension $d\geq2$ and every nonempty finite lower set $A\subset\mathbb N_0^d$, let $P_A$ denote the corresponding grid with $N=|A|$ nodes. We prove $Λ(P_A)\leq C_dN^{β_d}$, where $q_d=d/(d-1)$ and $β_d=1+q_d^{-1}\log_2(1+2^{q_d})$. The exponent satisfies $β_2=2.160964\ldots$ and increases to $\log_2 6=2.584962\ldots$ as $d\to\infty$, improving both the cubic estimate and the exponent $3-1/d$ obtained from quadratic prefix bounds. Our proof exploits the binary structure of known univariate estimates to control sums of powers of Lebesgue constants over interpolation prefixes. A weighted Hölder inequality and a disjoint-box packing argument then transfer these prefix-moment bounds to arbitrary lower sets. The resulting estimate is uniform over all lower-set shapes and choices of disk Leja maximizers, with constants depending only on $d$.

title: Model-assisted estimation of the finite population mean via local linear regression with associated kernels
abstract: In this paper, we propose a general regression-assisted estimator of the population mean based on local regression with associated kernels, a broad class that encompasses both classical (symmetric) kernels, such as the Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels, and asymmetric kernels, such as the gamma kernel. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator, including explicit expressions for the bias, mean squared error, and asymptotic normality, under a unified framework that applies to any kernel in this class. Through simulation studies on nonnegative data and one real-data application, we compare the finite-sample performance of the estimator based on the gamma kernel with those relying on the Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels. When the data are supported on the positive real line, symmetric kernels suffer from boundary bias near zero due to mass assignment outside the support, whereas the gamma kernel, naturally adapted to $[0,\infty)$, alleviates this effect. The results confirm that the choice of kernel within the associated matters in practice, and that asymmetric kernels provide a reliable and efficient alternative when the underlying regression function is supported on the positive real line or exhibits marked asymmetry.

title: Compact and Hilbert-Schmidt composition operators on weighted Hardy spaces
abstract: Lefèvre, Li, Queffélec, and Rodríguez-Piazza [12] recently characterized the sequences $β$ for which the weighted Hardy space $H^2(β)$ has the same bounded composition operators as the Hardy space $H^2$. We investigate the analogous questions for the compactness and the $p$-Schatten classes: for which sequences $β$ does the space $H^2(β)$ have the same compact or $p$-Schatten class composition operators as $H^2$?

title: Entropic Fluctuations in Quantum Statistical Mechanics: A Review
abstract: The celebrated Evans--Searles, respectively Gallavotti--Cohen, fluctuation theorem concerns certain universal statistical features of the entropy production rate of a classical system in a transient, respectively steady, state. In this paper, we review and compare several possible extensions of these fluctuation theorems to quantum systems. We present, in an introductory way, the approach proposed in a recent series of works [Lett. Math. Phys. 114, 32 (2024): doi:10.1007/s11005-024-01777-0], [Rev. Math. Phys 38, 2461006 (2026): doi:10.1142/S0129055X24610063], [Commun. Math. Phys. 406, 201 (2025): 10.1007/s00220-025-05360-z] and [J. Math. Phys. 67, 022101 (2026): doi:10.1063/5.0311182] including a previously missing extension of the Gallavotti--Cohen (steady state) version of the FT to two-time measurement entropy production in the algebraic setting of quantum dynamical systems. We focus on the open quantum systems, where a small system interacts with several (infinitely extended) reservoirs, and discuss the following approaches: naive, two-time measurement, phase space contraction and ancilla state tomography. We review the connection with modular theory. The latter provides a way to extend the classical notions to the quantum domain. We discuss the quantum version of the principle of regular entropic fluctuations, introduced in the classical context in [Nonlinearity 24, 699 (2011): doi:10.1088/0951-7715/24/3/003]. Finally, we relate the statistical properties of these various notions of entropy production to spectral resonances of quantum transfer operators and apply this approach to a paradigmatic model of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: the spin-fermion model. The results presented here shed a new light on the nature of entropic fluctuations in quantum statistical mechanics.

title: Thin ends and topological spanning trees
abstract:
Halin conjectured in 1964 that every connected graph has an end-faithful spanning tree. He proved this for countable graphs, but in the early 1990s Seymour and Thomas and, independently, Thomassen found uncountable counterexamples. Both are infinitely connected and hence one-ended, and their unique end has uncountable degree (i.e.\ contains uncountably many pairwise disjoint rays).
  Several authors have since asked how much of the conjecture survives. Diestel asked in 1992 whether a graph has an end-faithful spanning tree as soon as all its one-ended connected subgraphs have one; by a theorem of Polat, this would give end-faithful spanning trees in all connected graphs whose ends have countable degree. Diestel and Kühn introduced topological spanning trees, a topological variant of end-faithful spanning trees that exists in every one-ended connected graph, and asked in 2004 whether every connected graph has one. And Carmesin asked in 2019 whether every graph has a spanning tree that is end-faithful at least for its thin ends, the ends of finite degree.
  We answer all three questions in the negative. We show that the uncountably chromatic graph from an earlier note of ours on a problem of Erdős and Hajnal has only ends of countable degree, each dominated by only countably many vertices, yet it has neither an end-faithful nor a topological spanning tree. A refinement of this graph moreover has no spanning tree that contains a ray from every end of degree~1.

title: Ergodicity as an obstruction to classification by higher-rank invariants
abstract:
Given a collection of mathematical objects and a natural notion of equivalence (such as isomorphism), we want to find a complete classification. This paper presents methods for proving anti-classification results, that is, when a complete classification is not possible using certain classifying invariants.
  The problem of using real numbers as classifying invariants is well understood. In this case, the obstruction to classifiability is ergodicity. We consider classifiability by higher rank objects, such as countable sets of real numbers, and present a simple ergodicity-like obstruction for classifiability. This method is particularly useful when applied in various models of ZF where even weak fragments of the axiom of choice fail.

title: Twinor Theory: Field Equations from $(A)dS_4^{\mathbb C}$ Spin-Tractors: A Twin to Twistor Theory Modelled on $(A)dS_4^{\mathbb C}$
abstract: Twinor theory is formulated as a spacetime-based counterpart to twistor theory using holomorphic reductive Cartan geometry modelled on complexified $(A)dS_4$. The fundamental spin-tractor bundle defines Dirac twinors, its symmetric powers define ladder twinors, and their extremal Lorentz components define chiral twinors. The general \textit{twinor field equation} is $D\mathbf Y=\mathbf J$. Its adjacent contractions and mixed divergence are constrained by source relations; no additional equation is imposed on its completely symmetric projection. On a flat torsion-free Lorentzian background, the adjacent equations with the mass-normalization source and vanishing additional contracted sources, together with vanishing mixed divergence, reproduce the massive \textit{Dirac--Fierz--Pauli system}; the massless chiral realization gives the zero-rest-mass equations. Within the fixed mass normalization, the reality condition yielding a positive real mass squared is the \textit{anti-de Sitter reality condition} on the particle scale, independently of the cosmological scale and background curvature. The mass-coupling phase is therefore present in the classical connection before quantization. Nonlinear gravity is formulated through the full adjoint curvature, with energy--momentum and spin currents specifying Einstein--Cartan dynamics without requiring an action. The adjoint Bianchi identity constrains source compatibility, while a BGG-type sequence organizes torsion-free infinitesimal deformations. Matter interactions enter through the coupled connection and contracted source relations, with curvature compatibility recorded by $D\mathbf J=\mathcal F_D\mathbf Y$. Both chiralities are retained, and the additional consistency requirements for interacting higher-spin fields are distinguished from the underlying bundle construction.

title: Geometric Proofs of Riemann-Type Theta Relations
abstract: We present a geometric method for deriving theta function identities from automorphisms of positive definite quadratic forms. Given an automorphism of a quadratic form with matrix $A$, we construct a rational isometry of $I_n\otimes A$ that fixes the diagonal subspace pointwise. Elementary lattice decompositions and finite character sums then yield explicit transformation formulas for the associated theta functions. As applications, we give a geometric proof of Schultz's generalization of the Borweins' cubic theta identity and recover two related quadratic theta identities.

title: Non-Archimedean Rigidity and the Uniform Dynamical Manin--Mumford for $\left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$
abstract: We prove a uniform form of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for split endomorphisms $Φ= \left(f_1,\ldots,f_n\right): \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n \to \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where each $f_i$ has degree $d \geq 2$ and at most one $f_i$ is exceptional. Specifically, we bound the number of irreducible components of $\overline{\operatorname{Prep}\left(Φ\right)\cap V\left(\mathbb{C}\right)}^{\operatorname{Zar}}$ uniformly, depending only on $\left(n,d,\operatorname{deg} V\right)$. We also obtain uniform statements for the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture. Our approach combines a degeneration argument via ultrafilters with a new non-archimedean rigidity theorem, along with the quantitative dynamical Zhang's inequality by Mavraki and the second author.

title: Failure of the $H^1\times H^1\longrightarrow L^{1/2,\infty}$ estimate for the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal function and applications
abstract:
In contrast to Christ's theorem that the lacunary spherical maximal operator is bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ ($d\geq2$), we show that the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal operator $$
  \mathcal B_{\mathrm{lac}}(f,g)(x)
  =\sup_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}
  \Bigl|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-2^\ell y)\,g(x-2^\ell z)\,dσ(y,z)\Bigr| $$ is not bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)\times H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ for any $d\geq1$. In particular, it is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, we construct two finite linear combinations of smooth, compactly supported, mean-zero $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$-atoms for which the ratio of the weak $L^{1/2}$ quasinorm to the product of the two Hardy norms is at least $c_d\log(N+1)$. This lower bound holds already for the supremum over a suitable set of $N$ dyadic radii. For $d=1$ this answers the case $p=q=1$ of a question in Borges's survey. For every $k\ge3$ and $d\ge1$, a modification of the construction proves that the lacunary $k$-linear spherical maximal operator does not map $(H^1(\mathbb R^d))^k$ into $L^{1/k,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. We also indicate extensions to certain hypersurfaces and to horizontal spherical averages on the Heisenberg group.

title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on Kähler manifolds
abstract: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected Kähler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.

title: Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity
abstract: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic invariant measure is subsequently established by constructing a generalized coupling through a controlled auxiliary equation. Finally, the results are extended to other types of viscosities as well as to different stochastic hydrodynamical models.

title: Moduli space of irregular singular $λ$-connections and the relative symplectic form
abstract: We study the moduli space of $λ$-connections with ramified singularities on a smooth projective curve $X$. We construct a quasi-projective relative moduli scheme $M^α_{\mathrm{Hod}} \to Λ$ of $α$-stable $λ$-connections over a base parameter space $Λ$. This moduli space connects the irregular de Rham moduli space ($λ=1$) and the irregular Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs bundles equipped with non-zero irregular local exponents ($λ=0$). Furthermore, we show that $M^α_{\mathrm{Hod}}$ is smooth over $Λ$ and carries a canonical relative symplectic form $ω_{M^α_{\mathrm{Hod}}/Λ}$, yielding a natural Poisson structure on the total space.

title: A p-adic Valuation Calculus for Permutations with Restricted Cycle Lengths
abstract: Let a_A(n) be the number of permutations of {1,...,n} all of whose cycle lengths lie in a set A. We develop a valuation calculus for these numbers. Mobius inversion writes the exponential generating function as an Euler product, and at a prime p the factors with non-p-integral exponents, the blocks, determine a finite knapsack problem. Its optimal value gives a lower bound for v_p(a_A(n)), and the bound is attained exactly when one residue modulo p, the sum of the terms of the optimal choices, does not vanish. For a fixed set A and prime p the bounds and residues for all n <= N cost O(N^2) operations. When one block is strictly the most efficient, the valuation inside each residue class is that of a locally analytic p-adic function. We use the calculus to determine the 2-adic and 3-adic valuations for cycle lengths at most 3, 4 and 5, to prove the divisibility conjectures recorded in A378495, A079128, A193437 and A193438 and the 3-adic statements recorded in A057693 and A070945, and to treat 99 OEIS sequences in all. We also prove sharp divisibility and gcd theorems, show that at n = 111 the gcd of the counts over all sets of excluded cycle lengths containing {1,2,3} is one third of the gcd over the sets {1,2,3,k}, and determine eventual divisibility and tail gcds modulo composite integers. Part of the paper is formalized in Lean 4.

title: Optimal Neural Estimation for High-Dimensional Nonparametric Regression under Multisource Covariate Shift
abstract: We study high-dimensional nonparametric regression under multisource covariate shift, where $\mathrm J$ sources of training data share a common regression function but differ in their covariate distributions, sample sizes, and noise variances. Our goal is to combine these sources to estimate the regression function accurately under a target covariate distribution. We propose an oracle weighted neural estimator and establish its minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors through matching upper and lower bounds. The resulting rate is $\mathsf n_{\rm eff}^{-2p/(2p+K)}$, where $p$ and $K$ denote the effective smoothness and dimension of the regression function, and the effective sample size is \begin{align} \mathsf n_{\rm eff} =\sum_{j=1}^{\mathrm J} \frac{n_j}{(1+σ_{ρ,j})σ_{ε,j}^{2}}. \nonumber \end{align} Here, $n_j$ is the sample size of source $j$, $σ_{ε,j}^{2}$ is its noise variance, and $σ_{ρ,j}$ controls the deviation between the covariate distribution of source $j$ and the target covariate distribution. We also develop an adaptive procedure that requires no knowledge of source noise variances or covariate-shift parameters. Under suitable conditions, this procedure attains the oracle minimax rate up to logarithmic factors.

title: Tangential center problem for planar Hamiltonian differential equations
abstract: Consider a planar Hamiltonian differential equation with a nondegenerate center at the origin. The Tangential Center Problem asks for a characterization of polynomial perturbations for which the center persists at first order. This problem plays a fundamental role in the study of the center-focus problem. We propose an effective algorithmic approach to the Tangential Center Problem for planar polynomial Hamiltonian differential equations. Using this approach, we obtain a complete solution of the quadratic Tangential Center Problem. We further apply it to a non-generic family of cubic Hamiltonian differential equations containing the planar Hamiltonian Lotka--Volterra equation. For a general cubic polynomial perturbation, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the vanishing of the corresponding first Poincaré--Pontryagin--Melnikov function and characterize all tangential centers.

title: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
abstract:
We prove that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system and that a quasi-local spectral flow transports the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. Let $Φ_h$ be a free fermionic interaction, possibly including pairing terms, whose infinite-volume Majorana coefficient operator $h$ has no spectrum in $(-g,g)$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an even self-adjoint many-body interaction. For sufficiently small $|λ|$, we construct pure ground states $ω_λ$ of the interacting bulk system $Φ_λ=Φ_h+λ\mathcal V$ and quasi-local automorphisms $β_{0,λ}$ such that $ω_λ=ω_0\circβ_{0,λ}$, where $ω_0$ is the free ground state of $Φ_h$. Each $ω_λ$ has a GNS Hamiltonian with gap at least $g-C_*|λ| \|\mathcal V\|_*$, where $\|\cdot\|_*$ is the relevant interaction norm.
  Our result allows polynomial decay of both the free coefficients and the many-body interaction. For two-site interactions on a uniformly discrete point set $Γ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, a sufficient condition is decay as $(1+|x-y|)^{-\varpi}$ with $\varpi>2d$, for both the hopping and pairing coefficients and the interaction terms. The spectral-flow generator preserves the spatial exponent of the polynomial interaction norm, and its automorphisms satisfy locality bounds at that exponent. If $h$ and $\mathcal V$ have stretched-exponential decay, so does the spectral-flow generator.
  The proof constructs the spectral flow and establishes the gap through an excitation-number comparison, using polynomial propagation bounds for evolved interactions proved in a companion paper.

title: Levi-Civita's type theorem for projectively equivalent sub-Riemannian metrics on step 2 distributions
abstract: This paper extends the classical results of Eisenhart (1923) and Levi-Civita (1896) on the classification of pairs of germs of Riemannian metrics with the same geodesics, either as parametrized curves (affine equivalence) or as unparametrized curves (projective equivalence), to sub-Riemannian metrics on arbitrary step 2 distributions: at every stable point in the projective case and at every point in the affine case. This extends the results of Zelenko (2004) for contact and even-contact distributions and the affine result of Lin and Zelenko (2024) for step 2 distributions with ad-surjective Tanaka symbols; our projective result covers the ad-surjective case as well. In the affine case, we prove that if a sub-Riemannian metric admits an affinely equivalent metric that is not constantly proportional to it, then locally it is a product of two sub-Riemannian metrics. In the projective case, we prove the 2019 conjecture of Jean, Maslovskaya, and Zelenko on generalized Levi-Civita pairs; in particular, the distribution admits a product structure, the squares of its components are involutive, and the restrictions of the two metrics to each leaf of the corresponding foliation are conformal to each other under the appropriate pullback. The proof is based on a new graph-theoretic formalism, in which compatible moving frames are represented by the vertices and edges of certain graphs. As a byproduct, we introduce a new discrete invariant of step 2 nilpotent graded Lie algebras, the characteristic tuple. The compatible graphs are used on the open dense set where this tuple is locally constant; the resulting bracket relations are identities between smooth tensors, so they extend by continuity across the points where the tuple jumps. Consequently, our classification holds without any assumption of local constancy of the characteristic tuple.

title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
abstract: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric. We prove that when $\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact connected embedded submanifold without boundary, with positive reach, and $\mathrm{A}\subset\mathcal{M}$ is a subset that is sufficiently dense in $\mathcal{M}$ with respect to the reach, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is bounded below by $1/2$ of the Hausdorff distance between them. We extend this result in two ways. First, we show that the factor $1/2$ can be improved using Jung's theorem. Second, we prove bounds on the Gromov-Hausdorff distance for pairs of subsets of $\mathcal{M}$. When $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ is equipped with the two-dimensional Euclidean metric, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ and any sufficiently dense subset of $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ can be expressed explicitly as a function of the Hausdorff distance between the two. We use interleavings between geometric simplicial complexes, nerve lemmas, properties of reach and the nearest-point projection map, and the fundamental class to produce the inequalities for general $\mathcal{M}$. We use the Borsuk-Ulam theorem for $\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{S}^1\subset \mathbb{R}^2$.

title: An Arithmetic Property of Intertwining Operators for Real Reductive Groups
abstract: Let $G$ be the group of complex points of a connected split reductive group defined over ${\mathbb Q}$. We study the standard intertwining operator between representations parabolically induced from essentially tempered cohomological representations of Levi subgroups of maximal parabolic subgroups. Under certain algebraicity, purity, and criticality hypotheses, the operator is holomorphic and invertible at a particular point of evaluation. The relative Lie algebra cohomology of these induced representations is one-dimensional in the lowest nonzero degree. Under prescribed rational generators of these one-dimensional spaces, we show that the intertwining operator is a nonzero rational multiple of a certain product of ratios of local $L$-factors. This is a cohomological version of Langlands's calculation of the Gindikin-Karplevic formula. The main theorem provides a local input for the arithmetic study of special values of Langlands--Shahidi $L$-functions.

title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problems for Sturm--Liouville Operators with Potentials in $L^p(0,1)$
abstract:
We study an optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for a one-dimensional Sturm--Liouville operator on a finite interval. The problem is to find a potential $V \in L^p(0,1)$ that realizes a prescribed finite set $λ_1^* < λ_2^* < \dots < λ_m^*$ and has the smallest $L^p(0,1)$-distance from an a priori given potential $V_0 \in L^p(0,1)$.
  We formulate and prove results on the regularity of the isospectral manifold, the existence of an OISP solution, and an explicit analytic representation of the optimal potential by means of a power map applied to a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions.
  Using a unified differential-algebraic approach to squared eigenfunctions, we show that whenever these squares are linearly dependent, the corresponding potential can be expressed in terms of them and is an analytic function.
  For $p=2$, we prove that nondegenerate stationary points are isolated and that the number of global minima is finite provided that each of them is nondegenerate. For every $1<p<\infty$, we establish uniqueness for the first eigenvalue when $λ_1^*\geλ_1(V_0)$ and generic global uniqueness in the sense of Baire category in $L^p(0,1)$.
  A separate section provides examples with at least two global minima for $m=1,2$ in the presence of a sufficiently high finite symmetric barrier. We describe an iteration with frozen eigenfunctions and a local Newton--KKT method with continuation in the spectral data, and state explicitly the limits of their guarantees.
  The final part discusses applications of OISP theory to nonlinear boundary value problems and to applied problems of diagnostics and optimal spectral design of acoustic and electromagnetic resonators.

title: The Segal conjecture for large objects and semiadditive lifts
abstract:
We prove a projection formula for homotopy fixed points of trivial actions of finite $p$-groups. More precisely, for every bounded-below, $p$-complete spectrum $X$ whose mod-$p$ homology is $I$-complete, the canonical map \[ (\mathbb S_p)^{BG}\otimes X \overset{\simeq}{\rightarrow} X^{BG} \] is an equivalence for every finite $p$-group $G$, where $I$ is the augmentation ideal of the Steenrod algebra.
  Building on earlier joint work with Burklund, our proof combines the Adams--Gunawardena--Miller calculation with an adaptation of Carlsson's induction. As an application, using the work of Yuan, we construct height-one semiadditive lifts of such spectra and show that their cohomology of $p$-finite spaces depends only on the $1$-type.

title: Matrix Nearness Problems Revisited
abstract: Given a nonempty set of matrices $\mathcal{E} \subseteq \mathbb{C}^{m \times n}$ and a matrix $A \not\in\mathcal{E}$, a matrix nearness problem (or matrix distance problem) consists in finding a matrix in $\mathcal{E}$ that is closest to $A$, in some norm, as well as the corresponding distance. This article is a survey of matrix nearness problems and of numerical algorithms for their solution. We pay special attention to modern related topics, such as Riemannian optimization and pseudospectra, that were not discussed in depth in previous reviews about this topic. Besides collecting known facts, we also prove some foundational results that, at least in the present form, we could not locate in the literature.

title: On generic subsystems of a Smale space
abstract: We study properties of generic compact invariant subsystems of a fixed Smale space in the Hausdorff topology. For a transitive Smale space, we show that the hyperspace of all subsystems contains an open and dense family of NMC subsystems, a dynamically degenerate class with finite orbit structure. A substantially different picture emerges in the closure of the infinite transitive locus: minimality, unique ergodicity, and zero topological entropy are generic, while subsystems conjugate to regular Toeplitz shifts are dense. Despite generic zero entropy, typical subsystems exhibit large oscillations in complexity: we prove that they have infinite slow entropy at the polynomial scale, and their slow entropy at the stretched-exponential scale is equal to one. For mixing Smale spaces, we further study the closure of the infinite totally transitive subsystems. In this hyperspace, minimality, unique ergodicity, and zero entropy remain generic; the conjugacy class of any Sturmian subshift is dense; and uniquely ergodic subsystems whose invariant measure is weakly mixing form a residual set. In particular, topological weak mixing is generic in this space.

title: The maximum degree of Nosal graphs
abstract: A graph $G$ with $m$ edges is a Nosal graph if its spectral radius $λ(G)$ exceeds $\sqrt m$. At the threshold $λ(G)=\sqrt m$, the star $K_{1,m}$ shows that one vertex can be incident with all $m$ edges. In contrast, Li, Liu and Zhang [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 179 (2026)] proved that every Nosal graph $G$ with sufficiently many edges satisfies $Δ(G)\le\frac12m+m^{0.99}$, where the constant $\frac12$ is best possible. In this paper, we prove that every Nosal graph $G$ with spectral radius $λ$ satisfies $Δ(G)<m-\frac12(λ-1)(λ-2)$, and hence $Δ(G)<\frac12m+\frac32\sqrt m-1$. Both bounds are sharp up to an additive constant less than $\frac12$: for every $r\ge3$, the complete graph $K_r$ with $\frac12(r^2+r-2)$ pendant vertices attached to one vertex is a Nosal graph with $r^2-1$ edges whose maximum degree lies within $\frac12$ of both bounds. Consequently, the largest maximum degree of a Nosal graph with $r^2-1$ edges is exactly $\frac12(r^2+3r-4)$. The first bound cannot be improved by any positive additive constant: its gap on these graphs is less than $\frac{4}{r+5}$ and tends to zero as $r\to \infty$.

title: Sharp $L^2$ stability for anisotropic radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities
abstract: We establish quantitative stability for radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities involving the anisotropic radial derivative and the Minkowski functional of a smooth, strictly convex body in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. Here, the convex body need not be origin-symmetric. For the $L^2$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, we establish the sharp stability constant $|b+1-a|$ for $a\ne b+1$, and classify all equality cases in the natural weighted completion spaces, by optimizing over the angular coefficients and a common dilation parameter. We also obtain the sharp stability constants $2$ and $4$ for the scale-invariant and scale-noninvariant $L^2$-Heisenberg inequality, respectively. For $2\le p<\infty$, we also establish weighted stability of the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities when $a\neq b+1$ and $(b+1-a)(N-p(b+1))\geq0$, and the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Heisenberg inequalities. As a byproduct, we establish weighted $L^p$-Poincaré inequalities for Gamma measures, which serve as the main tool for our stability estimates.

title: Nonuniqueness and failure of positivity preservation for doubly critical semilinear heat equations
abstract:
At the Fujita exponent $p=1+2/N$ we construct a strictly positive mild solution of $u_t-Δu=|u|^{p-1}u$ in $\mathbb R^N$ whose initial trace in $L^1$ is zero. In similarity variables the solution approaches a Gaussian profile, and $$\|U(t)\|_1\sim C_N(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},\qquad
  \|U(t)\|_\infty\sim c_Nt^{-N/2}(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},$$ with explicit constants $C_N$ and $c_N$. In particular, uniqueness fails at the borderline logarithmic rate, and the solution lies outside every stronger logarithmic uniqueness class; this answers two questions raised by Miyamoto [J. Evol. Equ. 21 (2021), 151--166, Remark~1.6]. We also prove that, up to time translation, this is the only ancient solution of fixed sign of the rescaled equation that decays in a Gaussian weighted supremum norm. On a bounded smooth domain the whole-space solution can be localized at finitely many interior points, with independently chosen signs, on top of an arbitrary bounded initial datum. The resulting solutions are classical for $t>0$ and continuous at $t=0$ in $L^1$. Consequently, uniqueness fails for every bounded datum, and positivity is lost for every bounded nonnegative datum, $u_0\equiv1$ included. These results provide affirmative answers to Open Problems~3 and~4 posed by Brezis and Cazenave in [J. Anal. Math. 68 (1996), 277--304].

title: Enhanced convergence guarantees of score-based generative models in $\mathcal{W}_2$-distance beyond log-concavity
abstract: Although score-based generative models (SGMs) have achieved remarkable success in real-world sample generation tasks, it is still far from sufficient to understand them from a mathematical perspective. In this paper, we aim to provide enhanced convergence guarantees for two existing SGMs in $\mathcal{W}_2$-distance beyond log-concavity. More precisely, we develop a novel framework of {\color{black}discretization} error analysis for Euler-Maruyama (EM) and Poisson midpoint (PM) time discretization schemes for SGMs. Under a non-log-concavity condition, we show that $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{d}/ε)$ iterations suffice to approximate the target distributions in $ε$-accuracy for the classical EM-based SGM, considerably improving upon the existing iteration complexity $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(d/ε^2)$. Notably, the novel framework of error analysis also enables us to establish an $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{d}/ε^{2/3})$ iteration complexity for the PM-based SGM in $ε$-accuracy, significantly outperforming current state-of-the-art Wasserstein convergence guarantees for SDE-based diffusion samplers.

title: The Borodin--Kostochka Conjecture for Two Classes of Diamond-Free Graphs
abstract: We prove the Borodin--Kostochka conjecture for $(\mathrm{diamond},L_4)$-free graphs and $(\mathrm{diamond},K_5^+)$-free graphs, where $L_4$ is obtained from $K_4$ by attaching a path of length two to one clique vertex, and $K_5^+$ is obtained from $K_5$ by adding a vertex adjacent to exactly one clique vertex. The proof uses structural properties of maximum cliques in diamond-free vertex-critical graphs with $χ=Δ$.

title: Berezin--Li--Yau inequalities for Aharonov--Bohm operators
abstract: We prove the sharp Berezin--Li--Yau inequality for Riesz means of order at least one for Aharonov--Bohm operators on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. This confirms a conjecture posed by Frank and Hansson in 2008. We also obtain an improved lower bound for individual eigenvalues and extend it to the case of magnetic potentials with bounded magnetic field. These results are then applied to deduce estimates for Riesz means of orders between zero and one, and for Aharonov--Bohm eigenvalues on product domains.

title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
abstract: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.

title: Inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-Selfless Groups
abstract: We introduce the notion of inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selfless groups and study their structural properties. We prove a Fourier coefficient extraction theorem for invariant subalgebras of crossed products by such groups under a compatibility assumption on the action. Consequently, every inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selfless group has the relative $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-invariant subalgebra rigidity property, and every finite product of such groups has the $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-invariant subalgebra rigidity property. We also introduce another group-theoretic notion, which we call cyclic Powers property. This implies inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selflessness, complete $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selflessness, and the Powers property, among others. We establish it for groups admitting a topologically free extreme boundary action on a compact Hausdorff space with more than two points, and for Zariski-dense discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{PSL}(d,\mathbb K)$ containing a biproximal element, where $\mathbb K$ is a local field and $d\geq2$. In particular, we obtain the Powers property for $\mathrm{PSL}(d,\mathbb Z)$, $d\geq3$, answering a question posed more than twenty years ago by Bridson-de la Harpe. Finally, we show that every non-trivial mixed identity-free discrete group has the relative invariant subalgebra rigidity property for its group von Neumann algebra. This shows that the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ with $|m|,|n|\geq2$ and $|m|\ne|n|$ have the relative ISR property, thereby answering a question of Dudko-Jiang.

title: Packing and covering random trees
abstract:
We study the sizes of optimal packings and coverings of conditioned branching processes by balls with growing radii. We find a universal limiting constant, and thereby establish universality of packing and covering numbers across different scales and different offspring distributions.
  To be precise, for $μ$ an offspring distribution with mean $1$ and finite variance $σ^2$ we let $T_n$ be a Bienaymé tree with offspring distribution $μ$ conditioned to have size $n$. We prove that the packing number (resp. covering number) of $T_n$ with balls of radii $1\ll γ_n \ll n^{1/2}$ is asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C} n /(σ^2 γ_n^2)$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C} n /(4σ^2 γ_n^2)$), for a universal constant $\mathfrak{C}$.
  We also show that the order of limits can be exchanged and that the same limit occurs when we first consider the limiting covering number of $T_n$ by balls of fixed radius $R$, and thereafter let $R$ tend to $\infty$.
  We then extend these results to the Brownian continuum random tree conditioned to have mass $1$. For this model, we prove that the packing (resp. covering) number with balls of radii $\varepsilon$ are asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C}/\varepsilon^2$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C}/(4\varepsilon^2)$), for the same constant $\mathfrak{C}$, in contrast with a conjecture by Aldous.
  Finally, our results answer a question by Devroye, Eide and Pralat on the asymptotic burning number of mean $1$ finite variance Bienaymé trees of size $n$, by showing that it lies between $(c+o(1)) n^{1/3}$ and $(2c+o(1))n^{1/3}$ with high probability, for a constant $c$ that only depends on the offspring variance.

title: Stationary Structures of the Boussinesq equations
abstract: We investigate the steady configurations supported by the inviscid two-dimensional Boussinesq equations in the periodic channel. We show steady laminar velocity fields (closed non-contractible fluid trajectories) coupled to non-decreasing density stratifications are necessarily stratified shear flows. The direction of density monotonicity along level sets is in fact fundamental: in striking contrast with the Euler equations, we exhibit laminar non-stagnant non-shear stationary solutions in the periodic channel. We also provide distinct flexibility and rigidity results (laminar persistence or appearance of islands for nearby non-shear solutions) close to stratified shear flows according to their stagnation points. As a by-product of our analysis, we establish a uniform Crandall-Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem that might be of independent interest.

title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators.

title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications
abstract: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csiszár, Körner, Lovász, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lovász theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tunçel on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph-energy conjecture.

title: Hypersurface and Foliation Isoparametric Transfer for Generalized $(α,β)$-Metrics
abstract: Let $F=αΦ(q,s)$ be a regular generalized $(α,β)$-metric, where $q=\|β\|_α^2$ and $s=β/α$, endowed with the Busemann--Hausdorff or Holmes--Thompson volume. We derive explicit comparison formulas for the induced hypersurface volume and the associated volume mean curvature and use them to study two transfer problems suggested by the Randers case. The first asks whether the same hypersurface is isoparametric for $α$ and $F$; the second asks whether the same regular foliation is isoparametric for both metrics. Exact local and global criteria are obtained. Their Randers specializations recover the corresponding hypersurface transfer and the condition $df(W)=\varphi(f)$. We also prove an all-normal induced-volume rigidity theorem and construct a complete non-Randers example realizing both transfer mechanisms.

title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
abstract: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.

title: Harmonic Analysis on $p$-adic Unipotent Groups
abstract:
Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $χ$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$.
  To the character $χ$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_χ=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $χ$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition
  of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_χ$. We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition. As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.

title: Exponential Convergence of the Lifted Gradient Flow of the Bass Functional
abstract: We establish multidimensional exponential convergence of the lifted Bass gradient flow in martingale optimal transport. Let $μ\le_{cx}ν$ be an irreducible pair, with compact convex target support, source support strictly inside the target support, and target density bounded above and bounded away from zero almost everywhere on its interior. For every bounded $σ(X)$-measurable initial state, the flow converges exponentially in $L^2$ to the global minimizer with the prescribed mean, and the functional value gap decays exponentially. Both bounds hold at every nonnegative time with the exact initial errors as prefactors. The quantitative step is strong convexity on sets with a common $L^\infty$ bound and a fixed mean. We prove it by interpolating entropic endpoint potentials, using two conditional copies to cancel the unknown potential increment, and obtaining a Hessian lower bound uniform in the regularization parameter. Removing the regularization yields curvature for the original functional; the known qualitative theory supplies a common bound for the orbit. This extends the one-dimensional exponential-convergence result of Backhoff-Veraguas, Pammer, and Schachermayer. The main result is formalized in Lean 4. AI was used in preparing the paper (see Section 8).

title: Local Derivations and Local Automorphisms of Arbitrary Finite-Dimensional Nilpotent Lie and Leibniz Algebras
abstract: We study local derivations and local automorphisms of finite-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie and right Leibniz algebras. We prove that every non-abelian Lie algebra in this class admits both a local derivation which is not a derivation and a local automorphism which is not an automorphism. The constructions use a derivation $D$ satisfying $0\ne D([L,L])\subseteq Z(L)$. For non-abelian right Leibniz algebras, both existence statements hold whenever the dimension is at most seven or the nilpotency class is at most four. We construct an eight-dimensional non-Lie algebra of class five satisfying $\LocDer(A)=\Der(A)$ and $\LocAut(A)=\Aut(A)$. Consequently, eight and five are the least possible dimension and nilpotency class, respectively, for either equality.

title: Degeneration of (-1)-shifted symplectic stacks and categorification of Donaldson-Thomas invariants
abstract: We study cohomological Donaldson-Thomas invariants of perfect complexes in a semistable degeneration of projective Calabi-Yau threefolds, with smooth components $X_1,X_2$ meeting along a smooth anticanonical surface $S$. The generic fiber of degeneration family is a $(-1)$-shifted symplectic stack. Over the special fiber, the derived restriction to $S$ is derived Lagrangian, and its homotopy fiber product is also $(-1)$-shifted symplectic. Our goal is to relate the categorical DT invariants of the generic fiber moduli, induced by periodic cyclic homology of matrix factorization category of 0-shifted potential functions over such moduli, to that of the special fiber obtained via derived Lagrangian intersection and geometric quantization. This is achieved via construction of a flat Gauss-Manin connection that relates the generic fiber cohomological DT invariants to that of the special fiber. The geometric framework, universal trace diagrams, and fourfold foliation were developed jointly with Jacob Kryczka in arXiv:2510.20325. Here we construct ordinary critical realizations, oriented cyclic-to-bar comparisons, and Gauss-Manin operators, and verify finite specialization in explicit moduli problems. We workout our construction via several explicit examples such as Grassmannians, Relative Hilbert Schemes and moduli space of pure 2 dimensional sheaves with support moving in a fixed linear system of divisors in the ambient threefold.

title: Relativistic collision geometry and global near-vacuum solutions at critical transverse regularity
abstract: We establish global well-posedness near vacuum for the relativistic Boltzmann equation with soft and hard potentials in the range $γ\in(-2,1]$. The initial data have critical Besov regularity of order $2/r$ in the transverse spatial variables for an admissible range of $r$ depending on $γ$, together with weighted integrability in the longitudinal and momentum variables. The proof combines a fixed-direction div--curl lemma with bilinear collision estimates. In particular, to control the gain term, we combine localization to spherical caps with energy-weighted angular estimates. The key relativistic estimate controls the singularity associated with the first component of the post-collisional relative velocity. These bounds yield the required time decay.

title: Ricci curvature of semigroup walks on graphs and generator representations
abstract: We present an operator-theoretic framework for the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of (one-parameter families of) random walks generated by positive semigroups on graphs. On a metrically complete graph $(G,d)$ that is $d$-locally finite, we introduce a class of admissible semigroup random walks whose infinitesimal first-order approximation is itself a random walk. We prove that the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of an admissible semigroup random walk is well-defined and completely determined by its first-order approximation. We then establish a variational representation of the curvature of random walks in terms of a notion of the initial-time generator. This representation applies in particular to admissible semigroup random walks. Finally, we use this representation to define an operator-theoretic Ollivier--Ricci curvature for operators acting on spaces of functions over general metric spaces and establish sufficient conditions for well-definedness. This framework contains, in particular, Markovian random walks associated with discrete Laplacians.

title: Drift-diffusion equations with saturation on $\mathbb{R}^d$
abstract: We study a class of nonlinear drift--diffusion equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with saturation-type mobilities, not necessarily concave. Under structural assumptions on the mobility and potentials, bounded-domain approximations and local Caccioppoli estimates yield weak solutions for all positive times and an $L^1$-contraction estimate. The same estimates provide local space--time compactness of time translates, whose subsequential limits are weak solutions. Under additional confinement assumptions, uniform mass-tail estimates yield a mass-preserving, free-energy dissipating $C_0$-semigroup of $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$-contractions. In this confining setting, every trajectory converges strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to a stationary state with the same mass, and the resulting time-limit operator is an $L^1$-contraction. Under the same assumptions, we also identify the unique global and $L^1$-local minimiser of the free energy at each fixed mass and prove that it is stationary under the semigroup.

title: Ergodic treeable equivalence relations are richly ergodic
abstract: We study the density of ergodic subrelations in the canonical Polish space of subequivalence relations of a probability-measure-preserving countable Borel equivalence relation. Our main result establishes rich ergodicity for ergodic treeable equivalence relations. The proof combines a strongly increasing exhaustion with relative ergodic hyperfinite decomposition. As an application, for every $2\leq r<\infty$, we show that the product of the dyadic odometer action of $\mathbb{Z}$ with the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_r$ has a richly ergodic orbit relation, whereas the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{F}_r$ does not. Thus rich ergodicity of a free ergodic action is not determined by the acting group.

title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
abstract: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

title: Discrete hermitian groups are FC-hypercentral
abstract: We show that a discrete group is hermitian if and only if it is FC-hypercentral, that is, if and only if it does not have any nontrivial ICC quotients. In particular, a finitely generated group is hermitian if and only if it is virtually nilpotent. The main step is an elementary, self-contained proof that every hermitian ICC group is trivial, based on a finite-set separation property of nontrivial ICC groups.

title: On a class of meromorphic functions with three singular values
abstract: We give a parametrization of the class of real meromorphic functions in the plane for which the preimage of $\{0,1,\infty\}$ is contained in the real line, and all singular values belong to $\{0,1,\infty\}$. As corollaries, we obtain a new parabolic type criterion and prove that all such functions are limits of rational functions of the same class.

title: Polarimetric Low-Rank Imaging of Anisotropic Maxwell Media
abstract: We consider three-dimensional imaging of compactly supported anisotropic electric media from fixed-frequency polarimetric Maxwell far-field data. Maxwell transversality creates an obstruction absent from scalar Born inversion: each measurement determines only a projected action of the tensor-valued Fourier transform. We first resolve this obstruction by a finite-dimensional polarimetric inversion. For a general complex $3\times3$ contrast, three incidence--observation configurations are necessary, and we give an explicit three-configuration design that is sufficient at every nonzero interior Fourier point. Its Gram determinant yields quantitative conditioning information and exhibits the loss of recoverability at the boundary of the accessible Fourier ball. After tensor demixing, the inverse problem reduces componentwise to restricted Fourier inversion on the unit ball, which we regularize by spectral cutoff in three-dimensional ball generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions. For discrete acquisition, a combined reconstruction error estimate separates the effects of measurement noise, polarimetric amplification, off-grid Fourier mismatch, quadrature error, Born modeling error, and spectral truncation. Numerical tests examine polarimetric conditioning and use analytically generated Born data to compare three- and six-configuration recovery and assess off-grid sensitivity. Reconstructions from full-Maxwell volume-integral data assess the effects of noise, wavenumber, and basis choice, as well as the recovery of different tensor components.

title: Optimal subtrees of finite metric graphs
abstract: We consider a metric graph analog of a classical extremal problem for Riemann surfaces studied by Teichmüller, Jenkins, Strebel, and others. In particular, we prove that on any finite metric graph with a marked point, there is a unique open subtree which maximizes a metric graph analog of the reduced modulus, and we also give an equivalent characterization of this optimal subtree in terms of balanced harmonic measures.

title: Numerical Investigation of Soft-to-Hard Convergence: Discretization, Admissibility, and Spectral Regularity
abstract: This paper presents a numerical investigation of soft-to-hard terminal constraint convergence for optimal control problems governed by a second-order ordinary differential equation and the one-dimensional heat equation. The study complements the analytical convergence theory through comparisons with exact solutions and independently computed numerical approximations. For the heat equation, a fully discrete Crank--Nicolson finite-difference formulation is validated against exact modal solutions, exhibiting approximately second-order convergence in the terminal-state and midpoint-sampled control errors under simultaneous space-time mesh refinement. Numerical experiments demonstrate the predicted first-order penalty convergence for benchmark problems and investigate the admissibility threshold governing finite-energy exact terminal controllability.
